This helps reviewers quickly understand your changes. -->

### Description <!-- REQUIRED -->

Bugzilla: Bug-2091035

<!-- Please include a short summary of the changes. More detailed implementation information belongs in commit messages. -->

Moves the Access Connector urlbar button and panel out of `browser/components/enterprise` into `browser/components/ipprotection/enterprise`, next to `IPProtectionToolbarButton`, and restructures it after the toolbar button so upstream IPP changes can easily be applied to both at once, when necessary. The move of this into an `enterprise` directory within the `ipprotection` component mirrors what was done in `toolkit`.

- New `AccessConnector` module creates a button for every browser window via `EveryWindow`, the way `IPProtection` creates the toolbar widget. `UIHelper` now starts and stops it on enterprise builds based on the IP Protection service state, instead of a `browser-window-domcontentloaded` category entry.
- The button now passes `browserId` to `getRule()` and updates on `SiteRuleManager:RuleChanged`, `IPPProxyManager:ModeChanged` and `IPProtectionService:StateChanged`, which it previously missed. Unlike the toolbar button it does not check `canManage()`, since policy-included sites are claimed by a higher-precedence provider.
- Markup, CSS and icons move with it into their own includes and jar manifest. The panel now loads `enterprise.ftl` itself instead of relying on the lockdown mode include. Lockdown mode keeps `#enterprise-urlbar-actions` to itself.
- The `access_connector.proxy_error` telemetry stays in the button for now, but it will be moved in Bug 2091028.

author: seankoji
body:
> [!NOTE]
> _Written by **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** on behalf of @seankoji_

## Summary

The Claude billing page shows `Monthly credit USD 200` and `Next credit Nov 15, 2026`, but FrugalBar v0.24.0 draws no org credit line.

Two things are true:

1. **The app's Claude billing WebKit session is signed out.** Its `~/Library/WebKit/frugalbar` store contains no `claude.ai` cookies, so the opt-in session cannot read `/api/quirky-lollipop/link-state`. The web API rejects the Claude Code OAuth token (`oauth_token_not_accepted`), so this web session is the only source for that figure. Reconnecting in Settings is still required.
2. **The decoder only accepted a string amount.** The billing page's own client reads `monthly_credit_usd` with `Number(value)`, so the live payload can carry it as a JSON number. A numeric amount failed `String?` decoding, was treated as "no entitlement", and left the line blank even for a connected session.

This PR fixes the decoder. It does not, and cannot, restore the user's web login.

## What changed

- `ClaudeMonthlyCredit.Payload` accepts `monthly_credit_usd` as either a JSON number or a numeric string, preserving exact decimals.
- A present amount of any other type (boolean, object, array) throws a `DecodingError` instead of becoming "not published"; the billing session then keeps the last reading and marks it stale rather than clearing it.
- The sibling fields (`status`, `next_grant_at`, `grant_due`, `grants_held_reason`) keep strict decoding, so a malformed response is a failed read, not an absent entitlement.
- Invalid numeric strings (`"1e3"`, `"-1"`, `"200.00.0"`) still yield no entitlement. Whitespace is trimmed, matching the web client's `Number(value)`.
- Tests cover the live `200` value, `123.45`, booleans, negatives, exponent strings, malformed types, whitespace and negative zero.
- `AGENTS.md` records the shape rule.

## Verification

- `swift build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` — passed.
- `scripts/run-swift-tests.sh` — 1157 tests in 106 suites, plus the isolated deadline suite, all passed.
- Reviewer mutation analysis: removing the numeric branch, reverting a sibling field to `try?`, or returning nil instead of throwing each turns the relevant test red.
- Live WebKit store check: no `claude.ai` cookies; the billing page assets are cached but the session is not authenticated.

## Screenshots

The billing page the figure comes from:

![Claude billing page: Linked org, Monthly credit USD 200, Next credit Nov 15, 2026](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5630ccbc-0b2c-4ebd-8957-ba9e41ef4660)

The popover before this fix has no org credit line. After evidence requires the user to reconnect the app's Claude billing session; the decoder fix is verified by tests and the visible line will follow that reconnect.

## Review

Independent cross-lineage review by **Claude Opus 5.5** (Anthropic lineage; coordinating model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash). Final score 94/100 after the strict-field repair; the remaining test-coverage finding was closed in `7996355`. No open SEV1/SEV2/SEV3 findings.

## Agent and author disclosure

Code and prose by **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** (OpenCode / litellm `deepseek-v4.1-flash`), on behalf of @seankoji. Review by **Claude Opus 5.5** (`claude-opus-5-5`) via T3 delegation.

No pull-request template exists in this repository.


## Fable row consistency

The scoped Fable row no longer draws the "Weekly · Resets…" subtitle. It now matches the plan-wide row beside it: the model name on the left, the bar/percentage, and the compact reset on the right. The spoken label still says "Fable weekly … resets in …". Before/after crop attached.

![Before: Fable has a second Weekly · Resets line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe0c874c-c11c-49dc-ae43-9b36aeaa3aa8)

![After: Fable is a single line, matching Claude Code](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4581803-0380-432d-99c7-940574a1146b)

![After (final): Fable is one line with WK 5%, matching Claude Code's WK 60%](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d29e604b-2023-41f6-8b11-fffa12ebdd43)

author: ajroetker
body:
Prepared storage-owner leases are shared by standalone and replicated paths, but contention and publication fencing returned `RaftApplyWriterUnavailable`. They now return the retryable `StorageOwnerAdmissionPending` identity. Native FK callers retry that storage admission result directly; committed Raft apply preserves its existing replay-safe retry contract. Both runtime transports append stable mappings without renumbering released values.

Clean-checkout LangChain validation now resolves example self-imports from source without requiring redundant package output. The PDF metadata-frame allocation-failure sweep retains its original inputs and exhaustive injection coverage while using checked allocation backing with optional stack traces; the measured Debug sweep passes in 3.9 seconds. PDF unit tests also honor focused filters and expose per-test timing through the existing repository runner.

Validation: native owner admission and publication-fencing regressions pass; 51 runtime error tests, 13 storage error-identity tests, and independent native callback transport pass. LangChain clean source typecheck, ESM/CJS/declaration builds, and 60 unit tests pass (eight optional live tests skipped); lint passes with existing warnings. Generated error checks and formatting pass.

Full Debug unit, full PDF, standalone FK, Raft checkpoint, and broader E2E qualification continue; full-suite green is not yet claimed. Follows merged #1606.

author: 164zheng
body:
## 何が問題だったか

`revertTo: 0` で作られる版は v0 を複製するので、`source` が `agent.ts` の全文（decide の本体ではない）になります。`persist()` は v0 本体を除外していましたが、この複製は全文のまま保存していました。次のエポックの復元でそれを executor としてコンパイルし、`Cannot use import statement outside a module` で失敗して `revision_resume_failed` を記録し、版履歴から落としていました。

参加者からの報告（600579e、Docker、`--agent-state-root`、spike#101 → calm#101）:

- 第 1 エポック: v1 = `revertTo: 0`、v2 = ENTRY_MARGIN 10 → 50 bps、v3 = `revertTo: 0`
- 第 2 エポック: v1・v3 が `revision_resume_failed`、`versionsCarried: 1, versionsRefused: 2, runningVersion: 0`

実行される戦略は正しいままでした（最新の版が落ちると v0 にフォールバックし、その版の中身も v0）。壊れていたのは履歴で、LLM には v0・v2 しか渡らず、後のエポックで `revertTo: 1` / `3` は「no such version」で拒否されていました。

Python は改訂も v0 も `strategy.py` の全文という同じ形なので、復元では落ちていませんでした（一時ディレクトリのコピーから実行されていた点だけが違います）。

## 修正

- v0 に `shipped: true` を付けます。巻き戻しは `...target` で対象を複製するので、v0 への巻き戻し（と、それへの巻き戻し）は印を引き継ぎます。
- 保存は印だけで、本文は書きません（`versionResume.ts` の `persistedVersion`）。巻き戻すたびに `agent.ts` 全文が状態に積み上がることもなくなります。
- 復元は印を見てコンパイルせず、そのエポックの `agent.ts` / `strategy.py` から組み立て直します（`resumeVersions`）。**エポックの間に `agent.ts` を書き換えても引き継がれます**（v0 自体と同じ扱い）。Python でも元の `strategy.py` から実行されます。
- 印は状態ディレクトリ（エージェントが書ける場所）から読みますが、選べるのは参加者自身が提出した戦略だけなので、生成コードがコンパイルを飛ばす経路にはなりません。

### 印の無い古い状態ファイル

コンパイルに失敗した版に限り、次のどちらかなら v0 として読みます（`revision_resume_as_shipped` を記録）。

1. 本文が今の `agent.ts` と一致する
2. runtime が書く `reverted to vN: ` の注記で、N が 0 か、すでに v0 と判定した版

コンパイルに失敗した版に限るので、LLM が自分の `notes` に同じ文字列を書いても、動く改訂版を v0 と取り違えることはありません。次に保存するときに印の形式へ移ります。

## 保存形式

`PersistedVersion` は `{ source }` か `{ shipped: true }` のどちらか。`parseState` は `shipped` が `true` 以外の値なら拒否し、`shipped` の無い版には従来どおり `source` を要求します。古い runtime で新しい状態ファイルを読むと `source` の無い版で全体が読めなくなりますが、runtime を戻す運用は想定していません。

## テスト

- `test/versionResume.test.ts`（新規 8 本）: v0 の本文がコンパイルできないこと / 印での保存と読み戻し（本文が書かれない）/ `agent.ts` を書き換えた後の印付き版の復元（コンパイルを呼ばない）/ 報告どおりの古い状態（本文一致）/ `agent.ts` 書き換え後の古い状態（注記の連鎖 v3 → v1 → v0）/ 注記を偽装した動く改訂版は v0 にならない / 無関係な失敗は従来どおり拒否 / `parseState` の検査
- `test/pyBridge.test.ts`: 型の変更に合わせて 1 か所
- `npm run typecheck` / `npm run check:boundaries` 通過。`npm test` は全件通過（Python の 2 本は `ERIS_PYTHON` に venv を指定して確認）

`botMain.ts` の復元ループそのものは単体テストで駆動していません（チェーンが要るため）。判定は `resumeVersions` に切り出して、そちらをテストしています。

author: roanboc
body:
## What the film says

*Protection you can't prove is protection you hope for.* Film 17 of *Data protection and privacy*, the last of *Only what you may see*: 8:34, seven chapters.

It opens on the vaccine vial monitor: a square printed inside a circle on each vial's label. It darkens with heat and never turns light again, so a health worker can see, at the moment of use, whether the cold held. Then the first review of the study's agreement, three months after Mei signed it, asks of each promise: can we prove it held?

- **Who could read it:** grants made from the contract, to the study's group, and the directory's quarterly access review, which removes Elena after she moved to another project.
- **A class and a policy:** a check every morning finds a new `mobile` column on the exam support table, 31 hours with no class.
- **Where it went, and who read it:** lineage shows the column went nowhere; the audit log shows only the night load read it.
- **Until its date:** access ends on the agreement's last day, and Yusuf checks it the day after.

## What's in it

- The film, on the *Night glass* kit (`films/locks-before-the-data/shared/`, unchanged), with its own helpers (`ph_*`), captions in English and Spanish, Pause and think in both, and its pages.
- The example project: three queries in `analyses/governance/` (`morning_check.sql`, `who_read_in_a_window.sql`, `where_a_column_went.sql`) and section *18. Proof it held* in `docs/databricks-governance.md`, after main's sections 12 to 17 and before the sources; its sources follow section 17's at the end of the list, so no line on main moves. The morning check is the daily look for unclassed columns that section 17 asks for, set up as a SQL alert the way section 14's is. Since *Tags that travel* (section 16), a column classed `none` carries no tag, so the check reads the project's YAML for those columns and doesn't count them as unclassed. Nothing runs in the build, and all three compile with dbt.
- With the series complete, the capability *protect who sees what* goes from amber to green, with its evidence; the architecture map's views are written again.
- The film's questions and assumptions, in its own file, marked merged: `docs/assumptions/08-data-protection/2-only-what-you-may-see/8-proof-it-held.md`.
- Pages and lists generated by `build_series.py` and `catalog.py`.
- `"draft": true` in `site.json`, and the Draft label here.

## The soundtrack

`audio.json` points at the prerelease `audio-proof-it-held-423be13ea7a6d8542d0c`, and the MP3 is committed beside it (`git add -f`). *Store audio outside Git* publishes and verifies that release when the film reaches main (#243), so nothing needs a manual run. Until then CI and the deploy use the tracked copy, whose checksum matches.

## Checks

Run on main at c5f9d5a7, and again after each merge of main, the last at 02dcdcc3 (films 1 to 7 of the series all on main):

- `tools/check.py`: all 15,424 moments draw; 282 texts, none under 28 px; contrast at least 4.64 to 1; places and people paint in at most 0.08 s; nothing shown twice, nothing jumps, no arm jump in the 13 people `steady.py` follows, nothing past a person's picture. None of the player's inputs changed on main since.
- `tools/pace.py`: 128 words a minute (118 to 135 by chapter), voice at most 79% of a chapter.
- `tools/quiet.py` passes; the mix is -16.4 LUFS.

## What
I reviewed all 10 agent specs against the repo (graph, evals, the scripts they name). Two agents stood out: `importer` (no evals, imprecise spec) and `documenter` (one shared eval).

**`importer` was wrong in three ways**
- It claimed to rewrite MCP servers and register ports in `.vscode/mcp.json`. `scripts/import-agents.ts` imports no servers, and the convention is one gateway (`mcp-servers/gateway/tools.ts`).
- It listed "agents" as importable. Agents are generated from `prompts/agents/*.ts`; the script only maps chat modes, prompts, instructions, skills, scripts and utils.

- Capability evals for `importer` and `documenter` (documenter must hold `confluence_get_page` and `confluence_update_page`, must not hold `confluence_delete_page` or `jira_transition_issue`).
- Behavior evals `importer-reports-what-it-skipped` and `documenter-previews-before-publish`. The documenter case has automatic call-log checks: page read before update, no delete, no live write.

`mustState` evals only read `flow`, `always` and `never`, so a rule placed in `owns` is invisible to them. My first version of the importer rule failed the eval for exactly that reason; moved to `always`. Recorded in learnings.

The orchestrator still lists `search-across-sources` and `onboard-project` but cannot run their tools; this is 19 of the 40 accepted graph findings. Fixing it changes who owns those skills, so I left it.

author: francisreboucas
body:
## Summary

IFC import made one type per element when an IFC type shared its name with a different type in the project: `find_or_add_type` only reused a project type with the IFC type's name and the same data, so each occurrence created another renamed type (`<name> (IFC)`, `<name> (IFC) 2`, `<name> (IFC) 3`…).

`Importer::find_or_add_type` now:

- remembers the types the import added, per category and requested name (`added_types`), and reuses one whose data matches, so every following occurrence of that IFC type lands on the same `<name> (IFC)`;
- reuses a type that already carries the IFC type's GlobalId as its uid when the data matches (re-importing into a project that already has it);
- gives the IFC GlobalId only to the first type made from an IFC type: when occurrences of one IFC type differ in size and become several types, the others get a fresh uid, so type uids stay unique.

`clashing_type_names_import_as_one_type` (cc_ifc round trip) exports three windows of a 130 cm "Janela 120x120" and imports them into the template, whose type of that name is 120 cm: all three get one `Janela 120x120 (IFC)` type of the right size, and type uids are unique. It fails on `main` with `(IFC)`, `(IFC) 2`, `(IFC) 3`.

Fixes #247

author: joshuasprow
body:
Closes #91.

## Summary

```diff
 route
   "/"          → GET, HEAD  form        (form.go, form.html)
+  "/copy.js"   → GET, HEAD  copyScript  (copy.js, embedded; the page's one script)
 serve
-  d := e.decoder()
+  d, data := e.load()                     # decoder plus the artifact bytes it opened
+  api.errorTexts = errorTexts(data)       # artifact's errorcode table: id → NHTSA's ErrorText
 CSP
-  default-src 'self'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'
+  default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'
```

```text
GET / (no query)
  one-sentence intro, two example VINs (/?vin=…, clean code 0, Honda and Tesla)
  Install (brew, scoop, winget, Docker, go install), MCP (local binary, Docker),
  Verify (README's commands, TAG = this release), Links:
    release page for this exact version, or the releases index for a non-release build
    (devel, pseudo-version, +dirty)
    nitrovin-data release of the embedded month (build info's module version),
    else a release search for the month
    this month's parity report (refresh PR search), docs/parity.md at the tag,
    vPIC home and API docs, NHTSA's decoder

GET /?vin=… (decode)
  error codes, each with the errorcode table's text; the decode's AdditionalErrorText
  VIN and corrected_vin by character, differing positions in <mark>, "differs at position 7"
  JSON on /v1 · this VIN on NHTSA's decoder (VinDecoder?VIN=…&ModelYear=…)
  groups: <details>, General and Engine open, vPIC's group order, Other last
    vpic: empty values hidden by default; show_empty=true (checkbox + link) shows them
    nitrovin: decoded elements only, multi-valued as lists
  copy: decode JSON (json.Marshal, /v1's bytes), page URL, curl, nitrovin decode
```

Choices worth a look:

- **Group order.** The engine's `groupRank` labels put spaces around `/` ("Exterior / Body"); the data's names have none ("Exterior/Body"), so the engine ranks 20 of the 26 groups alike (99). The page uses the CASE's label order and matches each group by name with those spaces removed and case folded (`vpicGroups` in form.go). It agrees with the engine wherever the engine ranks a group (General < Interior < Engine < Passive < Active) and orders the rest the way the labels intend.
- **Error-code text needs the artifact.** No public API exposes the `errorcode` table, so `env.load` returns the bytes `nitrovin.Load` opened and `serve` opens them once more to read the table. Opening checks the arena; it does not copy. `pkg/` is unchanged.
- **README sync is a test.** `TestFormREADME` compares the page with README.md: each install channel's code spans, the `mcpServers` snippet, and the Docker variant built from the README's inline `"command"`/`"args"`. It also checks the verify block with `TAG=` set to the build's version.
- **The `show_empty` parameter belongs to the page.** It is removed before `ParseQuery`, so the JSON link, `curl` and the CLI never see it.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `/` showed one flat two-column table in element-id order (141 rows in `vpic`, most of them empty), error codes as bare numbers, and nothing to copy.
  **After:** `go test ./cmd/nitrovin -run TestForm` (embedded data, `httptest`) passes 4 tests:
  - `TestForm`
    - the empty page links (the devel build gets the releases index and `TAG=vX.Y.Z`; the data release is `…/nitrovin-data/releases/tag/v1.202610.…`; parity report)
    - error text for code 1 (`1HGCM82633A004353`) and code 14 with `Unused position(s): 5,6,7,8.` (`JH2PC40066M200001`)
    - suggested VIN marks for `1FBNF0AA21A111111` (position 7) and `1GTW7NFH5PA077131` (positions 8, 11)
    - NHTSA link with the VIN and model year
    - escaping
    - on every page: the CSP has `script-src 'self'`, there is no `on*=` attribute, and the only `<script>` is `src="/copy.js"`
    - `/copy.js` is served as `text/javascript` with `nosniff`
  - `TestFormGroups`
    - Honda's group order, with General and Engine open
    - `Make` sits under General and `DisplacementL` under Engine (`Displacement (L)` in the nitrovin shape)
    - by default `BusLength` and the Interior group are absent. With `show_empty=true` there are 141 rows, as many empties as were hidden, and Interior appears.
  - `TestFormCopies`
    - all four copyables equal their exact text, and the JSON equals `GET /v1/decode/…` byte for byte
    - the copied `nitrovin decode …` command, run through the built binary, prints the same bytes
    - shell quoting for `*`, a leading `-`, the VIN `-`, and `'`
  - `TestFormREADME`
    - install, MCP and verify text equal the README
    - a `v9.8.7` build links `releases/tag/v9.8.7` and `blob/v9.8.7/docs/parity.md`
    - a pseudo-version or `+dirty` build is treated as no release
- `NITROVIN_ARTIFACT=…/nitrovin-2026_10.artifact go test ./...`: all packages ok, with `TestServeContract` unchanged.
- **Real browser:** headless Chromium (omp `browser`) against `nitrovin serve` on the embedded 2026_10 data.
  - Copy buttons, read back from the clipboard: on the decode page, each of the 4 buttons was focused and pressed with Enter. The clipboard text equalled its copyable, the button said "Copied", and the `role=status` region announced "Copied the decode's JSON" (and likewise for the others). On the empty page, all 7 buttons (Homebrew, Scoop, Docker, go install, both MCP blocks, verify) were clicked; each clipboard read equalled its block.
  - Keyboard and focus: a closed `<summary>` opened with Enter and showed a solid focus outline.
  - Phone width: at 390 px, `/`, a `full` decode and a `show_empty` decode had no horizontal overflow. A long `%APPDATA%` path overflowed at first; fixed with `p code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }`.
  - JavaScript off: there were no buttons and no status region, and every copyable `<pre>` was visible and selectable. General and Engine were open, and `<details>` still toggled. The "Show them" link navigated to `&show_empty=true` and showed 105 empty values. There were no console errors or CSP violations at any point.
  - Every outbound link on `/` returned 200, and the parity-report search finds #80.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** `/` and the new `/copy.js` only

No `/v1` route, status, body, OpenAPI document, contract, artifact or importer change. `--data` loading now reads the file in `cmd/nitrovin` (the same `filepath.Abs`, `os.ReadFile` and `nitrovin.Load` that `nitrovin.Open` runs, with the same error text), so `serve` can keep the bytes.

author: homeowner-agents
body:
Closes #541

## Why

The app's monthly saving suggestion needs one predictable rule a Resident can check by hand. This ships the rule alone, with no database, HTTP or clock, so a later ticket can put it behind the API.

## What changes

Nothing is visible yet: no route calls the new code. `SplitContribution` splits the base between the reserve and the Goals and gives each an expected month. `Extra` shows how many months sooner a leftover above the base gets there. `OverLimit` lists Spending Categories over their limit, largest first.

Read first: `backend/internal/finance/contribution.go` (the rule) and `contribution_test.go` (one table row per criterion).

## Risk

**Risk:** low

New pure code and tests, with no caller, migration or wiring. Nobody can notice it until a later ticket uses it.

### What can go wrong

A rounding or month-count mistake would show as a wrong suggested amount or date once the API uses it. Tests pin that reserve + Goals + unassigned always equals the money given.

## How it was tested

`go vet ./internal/finance/` and `go test ./internal/finance/...` pass, including `purity_test.go`. Table tests cover each criterion and the edge cases in the ticket. They don't check the rule against real user data, and nothing bounds the number of Goals read (#538 is meant to).

## How to revert

Revert the merge commit. It leaves nothing behind: no migration, data or config.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Reserve share rounded half up, parts add up (R$ 9,99 at 33% gives 3,30 and 6,69): the rounding rows of `TestSplitContribution`
- [x] Reserve never takes more than it misses, takes its share again if it falls below: the "reserve reaches its target", "already full" and "fell below" rows
- [x] No reserve target means everything to Goals: "no reserve target" row
- [x] The pot fills dated Goals first, then the rest in order: the "pot fills" rows
- [x] Dated Goal takes missing ÷ months left, rounded up (R$ 1.200 over 4 months gives R$ 300): "R$ 1.200 with 4 months left" and the rounding rows
- [x] Short money pays the earliest date first and marks the others late: "money short for two dated Goals" and "same date" rows
- [x] The rest goes to the first unfilled Goal, overflow flows on: "after dated Goals" and "what passes a target" rows
- [x] Money with no Goal is unassigned: "no Goals", "every Goal full" and "pot larger than every target" rows
- [x] Expected month for the reserve and each Goal, none past 120 months: the "120th month" and "not reached within 120 months" rows
- [x] Leftover above the base gives the extra and months sooner: `TestExtra`
- [x] Leftover below the base lists categories over their limit, largest first: `TestOverLimit`
- [x] Table tests cover every line above: `TestSplitContribution`, `TestExtra`, `TestOverLimit`

author: hypertask-runners[bot]
body:
## Summary for non-engineers
Selecting a whole column and pressing Ctrl+E now empties that column immediately instead of removing tickets one at a time.

## What went wrong
Bulk archive on the board ran one API call per selected ticket in sequence, so the column emptied slowly and sometimes left tickets behind.

## What changes
Multi-select bulk archive applies one optimistic UI update per column, clears the selection, then archives tickets in parallel in the background. Failed archives reconcile back onto the board.

## What you will see
After Ctrl+E on a multi-select, every selected ticket disappears from the column at once. Undo still restores all successfully archived tickets.

## Watch out for
Only applies when two or more tickets are selected and the htpr-8928-bulk-archive-instant-hide flag is on. Single-ticket archive is unchanged.

- [ ] Reload: all archived tickets in archive
- [ ] Undo restores all archived tickets

author: siuo-player
body:
## Segunda Auditoria RedWar - Resolução P0/P1 Rigor Metodológico da IA Ares

### Sumário das Correções:
1. **Formulação Exata de Wald para SPRT (\i/sprt.py\):**
   - Substituição da aproximação de variância que causava inflação artificial de LLR (> 2.944) com apenas 12 vitórias consecutivas.
   - Implementação da razão de log-verossimilhança exata de Wald para ensaios de Bernoulli / pares:
     LLR = (W + 0.5 \cdot D) \ln(p_1 / p_0) + (L + 0.5 \cdot D) \ln((1 - p_1) / (1 - p_0))
   - Adicionado portão de amostra mínima (\min_games = 20\).
2. **Governança Estrita Anti-Involução e Portão de Campeão (\i/ares_hypothesis_testing.py\):**
   - **Tier 0 (< 20 jogos)**: Veredito estritamente \CONTINUE\ (Screening Rápido Exploratório com rótulo \ΔElo_screened\), vedada qualquer promoção a Campeão.
   - **Tier 1 (< 100 jogos)**: Veredito estritamente \CONTINUE\ (em verificação), vedada qualquer promoção a Campeão.
   - **Tier 2 (>= 100 jogos)**: Exclusivo para decisão \PROMOTED\, exigindo cumulativamente aceitação de $ no SPRT e portão \sigma > 0$.
3. **Validação e Testes Matemáticos (\	ests/test_p2_sprt_mathematical_rigor.py\):**
   - Prova empírica de que 12 vitórias consecutivas não alcançam  \ge 2.944$.
   - Teste de bloqueio de promoção em Tier 0 e Tier 1.
   - Teste de promoção autorizada em Tier 2 com portão \sigma > 0$.

author: githubmaster8899
body:
## What this does

He now thinks for himself about how to get better, and tells you. **He only suggests.** Nothing changes until you say yes, and every real change (test run, apply, update, model switch, notes) still asks you first, exactly as before.

### What he notices
Plain counts only. Nothing you said and nothing a tool returned is kept.
- a tool he reached for and doesn't have (2+ times) -> "Build a `<name>` tool"
- a tool that **crashed** (3+ times; a tool just saying "no" doesn't count) -> "Fix my `<name>` tool"
- a model that can't use tools (5+ messages) or that writes tool calls out as text (3+) -> "Try a model that can use tools"
- a newer version upstream -> "Update to the newest version (N new commits)"

He can also file an idea he thought of himself (`upgrade_ideas suggest`). That text is shown to you but is **never put into his system prompt**, so something he read on a web page can't reach his instructions through here.

### When he raises one
- At most one idea per message, and no more often than every 24h (`[ideas] min_hours`, never below 1h whatever the config says).
- The hint tells him to mention it ONCE, briefly, in his own voice, only if it fits the conversation.
- An idea only counts as raised once the model actually received the message.
- Not while he is in the middle of a change of his own.
- A no is permanent for that idea and quiets that kind of idea for a week. An idea nobody answers is raised at most 3 times, a week apart, then parked.

### The tool
`upgrade_ideas`: `list`, `suggest`, `accept`, `dismiss` (no prompt, they change nothing but his list) and `pause` / `resume` (always ask). `accept` only records your yes and says which tool to use next; it does not start, test, apply, pull or switch anything.

### Newer-version check
Once a day, when a front end starts him (never when `BabyAI` is constructed, never in tests, never in a one-shot command), a read-only `git fetch` finds out whether newer commits exist. It does not merge, check out or reset. **On by default;** `[ideas] check_updates = false` turns it off, and `[ideas] enabled = false` turns the whole feature off.

## Guard rails
New `IdeaGuardTests` / `IdeaUpdateGuardTests` in the locked `tests/test_guardrails.py` pin: every idea action leaves the repo, branches, notes, model and journal untouched; accepting unlocks nothing at any safety level; the safety package never reads ideas; the hint wording; one idea per message and per day; a no stays a no; nothing private is stored; paused or switched off means silent; the version look only runs `fetch`/`rev-parse`/`rev-list`. `babyai/upgrade/ideas.py` and `tests/test_ideas.py` are flagged as upgrade code (he can edit them; you are told).

## Verification
- 455 tests pass on Python 3.11, 3.13 and 3.12 with Tk (112 new).
- Mutation check: 56 deliberate weakenings of this feature (hint wording, throttles, quiet periods, privacy filters, the read-only fetch, risk ratings, ...) all caught by the full suite. The locked guard tests alone catch 46 of them; the other 10 are product behaviour rather than guard rails (e.g. counting crashes) or are protected twice (size caps).
- End-to-end demo with a scripted model and a real temp git repo: two missing-tool attempts -> one hint next day -> yes -> accept (no prompt) -> branch + files -> the only prompt is the test run -> live checkout untouched.

## Not verified
The model's replies in the demo are scripted. I could not check how well a real local model (llama3.1:8b / llama3.2:3b) follows the hint, so how naturally and how reliably he brings an idea up is untested. A 3B model may ignore it or phrase it clumsily.

## Stacked, not merged
Base is `feature/learn-habits` (PR #6), because it builds on that branch. Not merged into `main`.

author: ruvnet
body:
Lands the code part of #1119 without that branch's unrelated `.claude/helpers` churn, the full `docs/adr/INDEX.md` rewrite, and its ADR-352 file (that number is now taken by `ADR-352-ruvector-python-sdk-cli-mcp.md`). The commit is cherry-picked unchanged from #1119 (f6ff53665).

**Bug:** `DeterministicLocalKCut::deterministic_bfs` called `calculate_boundary(graph, &visited)`, a full rescan of every edge incident to the visited set, at every depth `0..=radius`. That cost is paid again per (seed, budget) pair in `BoundedInstance::search_for_cuts`. It drove the `partition()` latency blowup measured in ADR-345.

**Fix:** keep `boundary_edges` incrementally, touching only the edges of vertices newly added at each layer. This is `calculate_boundary`'s own definition applied incrementally: an edge is on the boundary iff exactly one endpoint is visited. No public API change.

**Verified locally on this branch (rebased on today's main):**
- `cargo test -p ruvector-mincut`: all suites pass (lib: 518 passed, 0 failed). That includes the new randomized regression test, which checks every witness `search()` returns against an independent from-scratch `calculate_boundary` across 20 random graphs.
- `cargo run --release --example boundary_incremental_bench`: identical cut results at every size, with these speedups:

| n | old ms | new ms | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 1.58 | 1.22 | 1.3x |
| 100 | 7.87 | 5.24 | 1.5x |
| 200 | 44.9 | 19.7 | 2.3x |
| 400 | 195.6 | 61.9 | 3.2x |

This is a real but partial fix for ADR-345's latency gap, matching #1119's own framing.

## Summary

Promotes `develop` to `main`. The only change since the last production build is the Stripe settlement fix from #7.

**Merging this triggers the production deployment to Azure** (`deploy-prod.yml` runs on push to `main`).

## What ships

- Reliable Stripe webhook settlement: inbox bookkeeping that survives failed settlements, paid orders honoured after a lapsed seat hold while a seat is free, and `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` support.
- Stable payment-confirmation polling in the payment modal.
- See #7 for the full description, behaviour changes and test evidence.

## Deployment

- No database migration.
- `Payments__StripeWebhookSecret` is already set on the Azure app, and the Stripe destination is already subscribed to both checkout events.
- Rollback: revert this merge on `main`; nothing persistent changes shape.

## Post-deploy check

1. An unsigned `POST /api/payments/webhook` should answer `400` (the previous build answers `401`).
2. One sandbox payment with card `4242 4242 4242 4242`: the delivery in Stripe should show `200` and the learner should be enrolled.

author: rebelato
body:
Transforma o Passeio Certo num bichinho virtual: as fases dão moedas e as moedas cuidam da Margot.

## O que muda
- **Casa da Margot como tela inicial:** barras de fome e alegria, moedas, balão de fala pelo humor, móveis em 5 espaços, brinquedos e carinho com um toque. Abaixo ficam Passear (com a dificuldade e quanto rende) e o desafio do dia.
- **Necessidades no tempo real:** cerca de 48 h até a fome zerar e 36 h até a alegria zerar, sem castigo. Ela nunca adoece nem foge; só fica tristinha e pede comida ou passeio.
- **Moedas:** base da dificuldade × patinhas (10/25/60/120). Repetir só paga a melhora; o desafio do dia tem bônus de sequência. A vitória mostra as moedas contando e a alegria ganha.
- **Loja:** comida (despensa), 6 acessórios, 8 móveis, 4 paredes, 3 pisos, 3 casinhas e 3 brinquedos, todos com arte vetorial original. A casinha escolhida aparece no fim do caminho nas fases.
- **Lembrete de fome:** notificação local opcional, desligada por padrão.
- **Save v7:** migra quem já jogava (mantém os acessórios liberados e converte patinhas em moedas). O Seu cantinho vira o quarto mais o Álbum.

## Verificação
- `swift test`: 118 testes, zero falhas. Cobrem: queda com o tempo (e relógio voltando), humor, compra, despensa, brinquedos com recarga, decoração, recompensas e antifarm, bônus do desafio do dia, migração v6 → v7, sessão pagando uma vez e persistência.
- Screenshots no simulador: veja `docs/validation/virtual-pet/`.
- **Pendente:** toques reais (comer, brincar, decorar, comprar), a contagem de moedas na vitória e a notificação no iPhone.

author: yungweng
body:
## TL;DR: Was ändert sich für Nutzer?

Keine Änderung für Nutzer. Der E2E-Test für den persönlichen Kalender wählt sein Startdatum nach dem Berliner Schultag. Dadurch vermeidet er montags kurz nach Mitternacht einen Termin in der Vorwoche.

## Warum und Umsetzung

Closes #6419

Der Test leitete das Startdatum bisher vom lokalen Tag des Runners ab. In CI ist das UTC, während `/calendar` die Woche des Berliner Schultags anzeigt. Montags bis 01:00 Uhr Berliner Zeit, während der Sommerzeit bis 02:00 Uhr, ist der UTC-Tag noch Sonntag. Der Test wählte dadurch Freitag der Vorwoche; nach „Nächste Woche“ fehlte der erwartete Serientermin.

Das Startdatum basiert jetzt auf `parseISODate(berlinTodayISO())`. Die weitere Datumsrechnung bleibt in lokalen Kalenderfeldern. Timeouts und Assertions sind unverändert.

Der Timeout aus #6416 wird dadurch nicht erklärt: Das dort betroffene Dienstagsszenario läuft mit fester Uhr stabil grün ([Beleg](https://github.com/moto-nrw/project-phoenix/issues/6419#issuecomment-6755371099)).

## Prüfung

Beleg: Mit fester Uhr ist der Spec vor dem Fix montags um 00:30 Uhr Berlin rot und danach grün (Tabelle).

Lokale E2E-Prüfung auf einem eigenen nativen Stack mit Backend und Seed wie in `e2e.yml`, PostgreSQL mit Berliner Zeitzone sowie Runner und Chromium in `TZ=UTC`. Für die Prüfung mit fester Uhr wurden die Runner-Uhr per Node-Preload und die Browser-Uhr per `page.clock.setFixedTime` gesetzt. Die temporäre Spec-Kopie wurde anschließend gelöscht.

| Feste Uhr | Berlin | Vorher | Nachher |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-11-08T23:30Z` | Mo 00:30 | Rot: Start am 06.11.; Termin nach „Nächste Woche“ fehlt | Grün, Start am 09.11. |
| `2026-11-09T23:30Z` | Di 00:30 | Grün, 6 von 6 Läufen | Grün, Start am 10.11. |

author: pablo-mayrgundter
body:
Hover highlighting on a large batched model was the main thread's biggest cost while the pointer moved. On the owner's M2 trace of PSB (a GLB cache hit), 16 s of pointer movement ran 1.7 s of `DOMWindow.onmousemove`, and one handler took 99 ms. #2117 measured why: three-mesh-bvh's batched raycast walks **every instance** per ray before any per-geometry tree can reject it. This PR gives each batch a tree over its instances, so a ray visits only the instances it can reach, and it makes the hover scheduler spend less on picks.

## What the profile showed

A hover pick is `ShareViewer#highlightIfcItem`: `castRayIfc()` (a raycast against the pickable models, all hits, nearest after the clipping filter), then a preselection recolour that is skipped when the hovered key is unchanged.

- **The raycast dominates.** `acceleratedBatchedMeshRaycast` (`node_modules/three-mesh-bvh/src/utils/ExtensionUtilities.js:86-160`) costs O(instances) on every ray. For each instance it calls `getMatrixAt` (16 floats from the matrix texture), `premultiply`, then `raycastObject3D`, which does a matrix `invert`, a ray transform and `setFromMatrixScale`, and only then the per-geometry tree's root test (`MeshBVH.js:447-464`). The per-geometry trees speed up the triangle tests of the few instances a ray actually crosses; they do nothing for the walk itself.
- **The highlight is cheap.** It is O(1) per move and deduped (`_lastBatchedPreselectKey`).
- **The scheduler picked when nothing had changed.** The listener is on `window`, but the ray's canvas position only updates on the canvas's own `mousemove` (`three/context/mouse.js`). Moving over a drawer or the NavTree therefore re-cast the same ray at full cost for the same answer.

## What this changes

1. **An instance tree per batch** (`src/viewer/ifc/batchedInstanceBvh.js`).
   - It is a median-split BVH over each instance's geometry box under its instance matrix, in batch-local space. The ray is brought into that space per query, so moving the model doesn't invalidate the tree.
   - Boxes are padded, relative to their coordinate magnitude and extent. They only ever **add** candidates, and every candidate is still tested triangle by triangle, as before.
   - `batchedRaycast.js#raycastInstances` runs the library's own per-instance loop, line for line, over the candidate ids in **ascending id order**. The hit list is therefore the library's entry for entry, including the order of equal-distance ties, which decides `filtered[0]`.
   - The tree is built in `deferredBatchedBvh.js`'s idle slices, **before** the per-geometry trees: it costs milliseconds, they cost seconds. Until it is done, picks walk every instance as today. The build is resumable at any instance or node, so a slice can stop at its deadline.
2. **Edits** (design/new/model-edit.md L0). The tree is an `onBatchEdit` listener.
   - An id an edit adds, moves or reshapes, including three's recycled ids, goes on an `extra` list that every ray walks besides the tree's candidates.
   - Deletes need nothing: `isActive` is checked before `getVisibleAt` at query time, which keeps #1915's deleted-id fix. Hidden instances are skipped there too.
   - Ids past the build span are always walked.
   - If the batch's edit revision is ever ahead of what the listener saw, the tree is not used.
   - Past a quarter of the batch on the `extra` list, the tree is dropped.
   - An instance whose box comes out NaN or infinite (one bad vertex) is walked on every ray rather than boxed.
   - Cancelling the build job drops only a tree still building. A finished tree stays until its own batch is disposed, so disposing one batch doesn't cost its siblings their trees.
3. **The hover scheduler** (`src/viewer/hoverPick.js`, wired in `Containers/viewer.js`).
   - Skips the pick while the canvas pointer hasn't moved.
   - Spaces picks by their own cost: the interval is 4× the median of the last 5 picks, clamped to 33–500 ms. However slow a pick gets, hover's own synchronous work takes at most about a fifth of the main thread, and one outlier pick doesn't stall the next.
   - mouseup re-checks, so a pick skipped while the button was down is made where it let go.
   - Adds a trailing pick, so the highlight settles on where the pointer stopped. The old fixed throttle dropped the last move whenever it landed inside the 33 ms window.
4. **`?feature=disableInstanceBvh`.** It is the per-session A/B and, set to `isActive: true`, the prod rollback. The before/after numbers below come from it.
5. **Docs.** glb-export-premium.md §1.1d gains "What a hover pick costs after it", the router row points at it, and model-edit.md L0's raycast entry covers the tree's edit handling.

Why not the other candidates first: scheduling alone (rAF coalescing, skipping during damping) only rations an O(instances) pick; it can't make one hover cheap. The tree removes the cost itself, and the scheduler is the small addition that bounds what's left, including during the build window. A redundant re-highlight was already deduped.

## Review

Codex is out of quota, so review fell back to a Sonnet sub-agent (agent-workflow.md §"Review", Quota), which was pointed at the hazards.
- **Round 1:** no blockers, 3 should-fix (NaN boxes, sibling trees cancelled, single-sample interval) and 4 nits. All fixed in 217887f6 and answered in the thread.
- **Round 2:** on 217887f6. No blockers. The nits are fixed in a6ecfa51: a test that a sibling batch keeps its finished tree, and an E2E that polls for the tree and anchors the walk leg's zero. The rest are answered in the thread.

## Measurements

All numbers come from the same build, A/B'd with `?feature=disableInstanceBvh`, in headless Chromium on SwiftShader on this sandbox's CPU. Absolute times aren't the owner's M2's, so ratios are given too.

**PSB** (23,453 instances, 20,177 geometries, one batch). Measured on a **cold load**: in this harness the GLB cache write never finished within 8 minutes, so the cache-hit legs couldn't run. The owner's trace was a cache hit, whose collapsed batch has ~15.7k geometries, so the instance walk there is the same shape.

Picks, from two alternating runs (before, after, before, after). The rays are aimed at 40 points on the model (instance centroids projected through the camera; all 40 hit). Totals are for the 2nd and 3rd of 3 passes; per pick is median / worst over all three. `performance.now()` is coarsened to 0.1 ms here, so the tree's medians sit at that floor.

| | 40 rays | per pick (`castRayIfc`) | per hover (`highlightIfcItem`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| walk (before) | 348–383 ms / 409–410 ms | 9.2–10 ms / 23–26 ms | 9.3–9.6 ms / 14–19 ms |
| instance tree (after) | 4.5–5.6 ms / 6.3–7.3 ms | 0.2 ms / 3.7–4.4 ms | 0.1 ms / 4.8–5.3 ms |
| **ratio** | **~65×** | **~45× median, ~6× worst** | **~90× median** |

A 5×5 screen grid that mostly misses the model gave 263 ms → 0.3–0.8 ms per 25 rays. The walk costs the same whether a ray hits or not; the tree makes a miss nearly free.

The pointer sweep follows the owner's trace: Playwright moves the real pointer across the canvas, 5,082 `mousemove` events, and every window `mousemove` listener is wrapped to time it. The "old scheduler" legs replay main's exact handler (33 ms throttle, skip while dragging) in place of the new one, so all three legs run the same build:

| | mousemove handler total | worst handler |
|---|---|---|
| main's scheduler + walk (**before**) | **65.0 s** | 75 ms |
| main's scheduler + tree | 0.17 s | 5.1 ms |
| new scheduler + tree (**after**) | **0.09 s** | 4.4 ms |

That is ~720× less handler time, and the worst handler is ~17× shorter. The owner's trace had a 99 ms worst handler and 1.7 s in 16 s. Frame rate in the sweep is **not** comparable here: SwiftShader rasterizes PSB's 11.6 M triangles in software, about 2.5 s a frame. Faster picks change the hover highlight more often, and every change asks for one of those repaints. On a real GPU that repaint is the normal per-frame cost, and the owner's

author: pmoust
body:
The process memory budget takes one evictor, and the server registered it
only for the decoded column-block cache, only when that cache was on. The
catalog's part and postings caches gave memory back only to the catalog's
own refused decode, so a SQL scan, a fetcher or a live reader refused by a
bounded budget failed while those caches still held memory.

The server now registers one pressure evictor whenever the process budget
is bounded, in every mode. It asks the decoded column-block cache first, for
the shortfall plus the admission margin, and then the catalog's decoded
caches for whatever the decoded cache did not free, least-recently-used
across every tenant of both caches. It runs for an accounted refusal and
for a host-memory gate refusal. It is registered with slack 0 and adds the
margin only in its call to the decoded cache. When the decoded cache is on
under an unlimited budget, the cache block installs the same evictor so its
entries keep giving way. The catalog's own refused decode keeps its
evict_until_fits retry.

The catalog gains Catalog::evict_decoded_for_pressure, which evicts until
the evicted entries' reservation bytes reach the amount asked for and
returns that sum, counting each entry in decoded_cache_memory_evictions.
ADR-3326 carries an amendment describing the wiring and naming the tests.

Eviction is not tenant-scoped: a refusal from one tenant's query can evict
catalog entries another tenant's queries use, which then pay a re-decode.
That was chosen over leaving the catalog caches out of pressure eviction,
which would keep refusing requests while those caches hold memory.

Fixes: #4015
Signed-off-by: Panagiotis Moustafellos <pmoust@nofire.ai>

author: krperry
body:
## Problem
In a new document, pressing Enter five times, typing a print page number (e.g. `12`), selecting it and choosing **Styles > Miscellaneous > Page** closed the application with a `NullPointerException` in `WPView.determineWhitespace`. No print page indicator was drawn either.

## Root cause
Blank lines typed with Enter are stored as `utd:newLine` and the formatter holds them as pending spacing until the next content is placed. When it reached the page number those lines had not been laid down, so every line above looked empty and the page number was treated as the first thing on the braille page. That path is for a print page that starts a braille page and draws no indicator line. With no indicator and nothing else in the document, the views held only blank lines, so caret restoration found no element and crashed (also in the `initializeAllViews` recovery path).

## Fix (utd)
- `PageBuilderHelper.handlePageIndicator`: lay down pending user blank lines before handling a page number, and place the braille page's own numbers while the previous print page is still in effect (as when text comes first), so the new number does not also appear in the top corner.
- `PageBuilder.isBelowForcedBlankLines`: the "first thing on the page" checks treat a line reached only through user blank lines as not the top of the page.

The indicator (dots 3-6 across the line, print page number at the right margin) is now drawn on the line after the blank lines in both braille and print views. The page number gets a normal map element, so the caret has a target and the crash is gone without special handling.

This branch has two commits: the first was a caret-side workaround that stopped the crash but drew no indicator; the second reverts it and fixes the formatter. Net diff against `main` is only the `utd` change plus tests.

## Tests
- utd `LiteraryFormatterTest.insertPrintPageIndicatorAfterBlankLines`: indicator on line 6 after five blank lines, with and without text after, page number not at the top. Fails without the fix.
- core `PageStyleAfterBlankLinesTest`: drives the real Page menu item after 5 and 3 blank lines (indicator in both views, blank lines kept, no crash, typing below the indicator works); no blank lines (number still goes to the top corner); text following; text before and after.
- Full suites: utd 728 passed, brailleblaster-core 207 passed.

## Manual check
Not yet verified by hand in the packaged app on Windows.

body: Reactive dependency switches copy intermediate arrays, and compiled constant `style`/`classList` props create effects with no reactive inputs. Include regression tests and patch changesets for core, DOM and compiler. body:
Ticket 276, a window is one project, PR 1: open and switch projects. Today's app (`apps/fabrika`, `packages/fabrika`), never `next/`. Plan: [docs/plan/project-window.md](docs/plan/project-window.md), approved by the owner 2026-11-09.

**Not ready to merge yet.** Two things are left:
1. `pnpm lint` fails after the merge of main. Main's dead-export check finds four lane exports: `Palette` and `PaletteSource` in `window/frame.ts`, `settingsFile` in `host/settings.ts` (only tests call it), and `platform` in `project.test-support.ts`. Those go to build and tests.
2. Review 1 has not run. drive.ts refused it: 15 GB free on the boxes' volume, and it needs 20.

## What it does

A window is one project. Launch shows a welcome page. Cmd-O opens a box of recent projects, with Open Folder last. Summon runs in the window's project, and `FABRIKA_REPO` is gone. Reopening on launch and from the Dock is PR 2.

## Steps and who ran them

All are this repo's hand-run steps through `drive.ts`. Today's fabrika pipeline did not run.

| Step | Ran on | Result |
|---|---|---|
| plan | Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) | approved by the owner |
| tests 1 to 10 | Codex, then Claude Sonnet | laws P1 to P7 (P7's quit-save half), P9 to P30, E1, E2 |
| build 1 to 4 | Claude Sonnet | build 4 `ee2ff75c` |
| mutation 1, 2 | Claude Sonnet | round 1 never got past the dry run, so tests 10 made the Electron and multi-process laws skip inside a Stryker worker. Round 2 is partial (the five-minute cap): 6 killed, 46 survived, 43 no coverage. Narrowing: **none**. One law added (host record rows). Survivors are advice only |
| review | not run | drive refused: low disk |
| lead | Claude (this session) | merged main, Electron captures, shots, field rows |

Step agents' list price so far: **$7.76** (sum of `listUsd` on this lane's 14 new `field/runs.jsonl` rows; Codex rows at OpenAI's standard price, Claude rows at Anthropic's, read 2026-11-08). All of it ran on subscriptions. The lead session's own cost is not in a row yet.

## Shots

100 shots in `apps/fabrika/docs/projects/`, from the real built app at `ee2ff75c` (`node e2e.ts --projects-captures`, exit 0). Each run had its own short test home, the windows were hidden, and every shot came from `page.screenshot`. They cover: welcome (empty, populated, selection, rejected), each at normal and small. Then project opened, long duplicate name, fake agent summoned, second project independent, and the projects box (selection, filtering, already open), each at one, side, stacked, 2x2 and small. Then migration ready (five layouts) and migration failed (normal, small). Every state comes in dark and light.

Every shot was looked at. None shows a machine path, a name or a secret. What looks off:
- **The top bar shows `1 tsh` next to a plain `tsh`, in every project-window shot. The plan does not decide this.**
- The rejected welcome has both "Choose Folder…" and "Open Folder…", two controls for one action.

author: ladd
body:
### Description

Add opt-in `--experimental_disk_cache_deduplicate_outputs` (default false). After local outputs have been validated, reuse their existing digests to find matching disk-cache CAS blobs, make a clone-capable copy to a temporary sibling, and atomically replace the output. Refresh the contents proxy and reinject file or tree metadata before publishing the action result; output contents are not hashed again.

Regular files, tree children, and archived trees are handled. Remote/resolved outputs, symlinks, empty files, outputs without a trustworthy contents proxy, and files changed since validation are skipped. File permissions and timestamps are preserved.

### Motivation

On APFS, locally regenerated output and an existing identical CAS blob can occupy separate allocations. Clone-capable replacement can reestablish sharing while keeping future writes independent. A local macOS experiment reduced unique referenced data by about 110 MiB across 926 replacements; these are single-workload footprint measurements, not a performance claim.

### Build API Changes

Adds one experimental command-line flag, disabled by default. Requires `--disk_cache`; without a disk cache no deduplicator is installed. No Starlark API changes.

### Validation

- Fresh local test run after recovery and rebase passed seven deduplication tests plus 39 existing disk-cache tests on current upstream master.
- APFS smoke builds verified shared physical extents, mutation isolation, readonly tree directories, warm builds, and builds after server restart.
- Java formatting, BUILD formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed again after recovering the original implementation scripts.
- The branch is rebased onto upstream master at `488801805d9ccfc7a110f168802fd8af4cb1239f`. The APFS footprint/smoke evaluation predates this rebase.

### Draft scope

This is an experimental prototype. File copying may fall back to a full copy when cloning is unavailable; it does not currently detect already-shared APFS extents. The replacement counter reports logical bytes processed, not bytes saved. CAS disappearance during copying is treated as a miss, while other I/O errors still propagate. These details need review before broader enablement.

### Checklist

- [x] Added tests for digest reuse without output rereads, changed outputs, cache misses, regular output metadata, tree metadata, remote outputs, and empty files.
- [x] Added command-line help for the experimental flag.

### Release Notes

RELNOTES[NEW]: Add opt-in --experimental_disk_cache_deduplicate_outputs to deduplicate finalized local outputs against existing disk-cache blobs using clone-capable file copies.

author: kvlonge
body:
## Why

When one target of a mixed check cannot run, `fensu check` exits 2 and prints the error, but the report of the targets that did run still ended with `Found 0 faults`. Read on its own, as a log tail or a CI summary, that looks like a clean check of the whole repository. One example is a Rust target without `cargo` next to a Python target with custom rules.

## Changes

- When a target of a mixed check fails, its error still goes to stderr and the exit code stays 2. The faults of the targets that ran are still printed, but the summary now reads:

  ```text
  Check incomplete: found 1 fault in the targets that ran

  It is coloured as unhealthy even when the count is 0.
- A complete check keeps `Found N faults`. A single-target check that cannot run already exits 2 before any report, as before.
- docs/rust.md describes the incomplete summary.

- New CLI test: a Python target with a custom rule and a Rust target, with `cargo` missing. It expects exit 2, the `FPRSL902 … cargo not found` error, the incomplete summary, and no `Found ` line. It fails on `main`, which prints `Found 1 fault`, and passes with this change.

- `cargo test -p fensu-cli --test command`: 141 passed. `test_rule::given_forced_color_…` fails here on `main` too, which looks environmental. `cargo test -p fensu-cli --lib`: 36 passed.

author: benbentwo
body:
## What
`scripts/name-dev-electron.cjs` (runs on `postinstall` and `predev`) now also replaces the icon in the dev `Electron.app` bundle with `resources/icon.icns`, alongside the existing rename to "Choo Choo".

## Why
In dev, macOS takes the app icon from `node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app`, which Notifications settings, Finder and Launch Services use. The script renamed that bundle but left Electron's icon in place, so Notifications settings showed "Choo Choo" with the Electron icon. `app.dock.setIcon` only changes the Dock icon while the app is running. Packaged builds were already correct.

## How
- Finds the bundle's icon file from `CFBundleIconFile` (falls back to `electron.icns`) and copies our `.icns` over it.
- Skips the work when both the name and the icon bytes already match.
- Re-signs ad hoc, updates the bundle's timestamp, and runs `lsregister -f` so the cached icon is dropped.

## Testing
- `node --check` passes.
- Not yet run against a real dev `Electron.app`: this worktree has no `node_modules`.
- To verify: `npm install` or `npm run dev`, then open System Settings > Notifications > Choo Choo. If the old icon persists, quit System Settings and run `killall usernoted NotificationCenter`, or log out and back in.

body:
Phase A of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-orange-project-space-design.md` (the spec is added by this PR; the user approved it on 2026-11-09). Plan and rulings: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-orange-project-space-phase-a.md`.

orange now watches the sessions the user runs themselves, files what wants them into one inbox, and pushes the urgent part. No judge yet (Phase B): attention is rule-based.

## What it adds

- **V19**: `projects`, `project_repos`, `space_items`, `sessions`, `session_events`, `attention_items`; `pg_notify` channels `session_changed` and `attention`.
- **Reporter**: plugin hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, Notification, SessionEnd, and PostToolUse only while a session was waiting) run `plugin/hooks/orange-report.py`. It translates the hook into a neutral event, resolves git on the node, prints nothing, always exits 0 and gives up after 2 s.
- **Ingestion**: `POST /sessions/events` stores the event in the PR 2 inbox (idempotent by event id); `SessionEventHandler` applies it.
- **Rules** (`SessionReactor`, pure): a stop that asks something, or a permission prompt, files a `normal` item that becomes `urgent` after 15 minutes without the user; a stop with nothing to ask is filed after 15 idle minutes; a prompt, activity or the session's end resolves the session's items; archived projects are muted.
- **Projects and the space**: a session's repo decides its project; an unknown repo proposes one. Space items supersede instead of changing; agents only propose; conventions resolve session → project → global.
- **Pushes**: ntfy, urgent and critical only, one push per 10-minute window, quiet hours hold all but critical.
- **Steering**: `/mcp/steering` with 11 tools; REST `GET /sessions`, `GET /attention`, `POST /attention/{id}/ack|resolve`.
- **Auth**: `ORANGE_API_TOKEN` guards the new endpoints when set.

- `./gradlew test`: 354 tests, 0 failures. - Live, Claude Code 2.1.321 (`claude -p --plugin-dir plugin` in a fresh git repo, against a running orange): SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SessionEnd arrived through the real hooks. The repo proposed a project, the prompt became the intent, the stop's real last message was filed as a question, and the session's end resolved it.

- Notification and PostToolUse hooks against a live session (they need an interactive permission prompt). Their payload fixtures follow the hooks reference, not a capture.

- The spec's own exit for this phase, two days of real sessions, starts once the plugin is installed at user scope.

The `runs` → session link and `verdicts` (B), `evidence.session_id` and `session_work` (C), `briefs` and `tasks.project_id` (D / v2 PR 4), ntfy action buttons (B).

author: cfretz244
body:
WP-1158: UBSan type descriptors now spell type names the way clang does.

clang builds each descriptor name with `ConvertArgToString(ak_qualtype)`, the same printer its Sema diagnostics use. kiln now does the same: the diagnostic type printer moved to `kiln_ast::diag_names::DiagNames`, and both sema and codegen use it. kiln_sema still exports it as `SemaNames`.

- Qualification: a type keeps the scope it was written with, and a pointee keeps its sugar (`TypeContext::pointee_sugared`). A nested class prints with its enclosing class scope.
- Template arguments: an implicit specialization drops trailing default arguments (`H<>`). An explicit specialization or instantiation prints its arguments as written (new `Templates::args_as_written` map and `TypeNames::args_as_written` hook), e.g. `coroutine_handle<void>`. The clang 19 and clang 22 differences for redeclarations and `aka` follow the selected oracle.
- Descriptor identity: descriptors are keyed per QualType, so a substituted template parameter gets its own descriptor.
- Side effect: Sema diagnostics also print written specialization arguments and nested scopes now, as clang does.
- Spec: spec/codegen.md §5.2 and the spec/types.md Printing section.
- New test: tests/conformance/driver.sanitize/ubsan-typename-ir.cpp. It passes against the clang 22 oracle, `KILN_ORACLE=19`, and `--compiler clang++-19`.

## What this changes

Adds a set of labeled captions that every test run reads, so a screening change shows on the pull request when it flips an older caption. Two new files and a docs section; nothing in the app changes. Related #226, #199.

**Why.** Screening decides whether a caption reaches the stream. Today each fix has its own hand-written test in `fact-verifier.test.ts` (2,800 lines), eleven screens are tested only by calling their helper and never through `screenClaims`, and there is nowhere to put a wrong caption the evening it is found. author: cjna
body:
### Purpose
`pnpm --filter ./docs build` (`docusaurus build`) fails on `main`. Every page, the blog and 404 included, fails with "Hook useNavbarMobileSidebar is called outside the <NavbarMobileSidebarProvider>" or "Hook useTitleFormatterContext is called outside the <TitleFormatterProvider>". This makes the docs site build again.

### Approach
**Cause:** the minor-and-patch bump in #172 (https://github.com/chamals3n4/OpenATS/pull/172) moved most of the docs tree to `postcss` 8.5.32 but left `@docusaurus/theme-classic` on 8.5.31. pnpm keys a package copy by its peer versions, so it installed two copies of `@docusaurus/core`, `@docusaurus/theme-common` and their plugins, one per `postcss` version. The theme's providers and the swizzled `Navbar` and `Footer` (`docs/src/theme/`) loaded different copies, so React saw two separate contexts.

**Fix:** every package accepts `postcss` ^8, so it is now 8.5.32 throughout (`pnpm update -r --depth Infinity postcss`). Only `pnpm-lock.yaml` changes, and no `package.json`. Two version lines change, and 490 lines of duplicate Docusaurus entries go away.

I didn't use a full `pnpm dedupe`: it would also have changed unrelated backend packages such as `jose` and `express-rate-limit`.

author: blackmesatech
body:
`set_placed_footprint_models` could not change the 3D models of a footprint whose pads carry a fabrication property (`pad_prop_heatsink`, `pad_prop_mechanical`, ...). The live update sends the whole footprint back and KiCad 10 re-creates its pads without the property, so the tool refused, and it had no other path. On the J3-HW-0008 board that blocked U2 and J301.

## Changes

- **Saved-file path.** When KiCad does not serve the board, the tool proves it closed (the same `closed_board::prove_closed` gate the stackup and footprint-graphic editors use) and works on the saved file:
  - `inspect` reads the named footprint's `(model ...)` blocks, including `(hide yes)` and `(opacity ...)`;
  - `append`, `replace` and `remove` rewrite only those blocks, in one atomic write that fails if the file changed.
- **Same contract as the live path.** A mutation still needs the `expected_models_revision` from `inspect`. No new arguments.
- **Checks on the write.** Every byte outside the planned spans is compared with the original, the footprint's other clauses and its pad fabrication properties are compared with what they were, and the persisted file is read back. Results carry `source: "saved"`, `board_closure`, `pad_fabrication_properties` and `write`.
- **Live refusal names the way out.** For a footprint with pad fabrication properties the refusal now says to save, close the board and repeat the request, instead of "make this change in KiCad itself".
- New module `pcb_components/saved_models.rs`; docs in `tool-directory.md`, the PCB skill and `API_MIGRATIONS.md`.

## Behaviour changes

- With KiCad unreachable, or reachable but not holding the board, the tool used to return `editor_unavailable`. It now reads or edits the saved file once the board is proven closed, and otherwise returns the closure gate's refusal.
- A saved model entry with a legacy `(at ...)` offset, or a clause the reader does not know, is refused rather than rewritten.
- Nothing changes for a board open in KiCad except the wording of the fabrication-property refusal.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked --lib --tests` and `cargo test --workspace --locked --doc` pass on the branch tip.
- 9 new unit tests: 6 for planning and verification (remove, replace, append, a one-line footprint, refused clauses, a tampered candidate) and 3 through the tool handler (inspect then remove, append and replace, a board with KiCad's lock present).
- On a copy of `Yoshi_Link_RevA.kicad_pcb` (J3Techs/hardware, `j3-hw-0008-yoshi-link`), through the built binary with KiCad closed: inspect and remove on U2 and on J301. The diff against the original is exactly the two 11-line model blocks. `kicad-cli pcb drc` (KiCad 10.0.7) loads the result and reports the same 9 violations and 0 unconnected items as the original.
- Live, KiCad 10.0.7 standalone PCB editor on another copy: inspect U2 returns `source: "ipc"`; remove on U2 is refused with the new wording; inspect and append on R204 apply in one undo step.

## Not verified

- KiCad 10.0.6. This machine has 10.0.7.
- macOS and Linux, beyond CI.

author: zeenotheinventor
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zeenotheinventor"} -->
_Requested by **Zee**_

Closes KEY-928.

## Why

Zee should not have to tap a button to see more food search results. On mobile, each group had a "See N more" button, and matches past row 25 could not be reached at all.

## What changed

- Mobile food search (log search, plain search, ingredient search) now shows 15 rows, then 15 more each time you near the end, up to 50.
- One running budget fills Yours, then Common, then Branded. Rows only ever append at the bottom, so nothing moves above where you are reading.
- Mobile fetches 50 rows, the most `search_foods` allows. No migration.
- A new search returns to 15 rows and scrolls to the top.
- Open Food Facts rows and recipe rows stay outside the budget and show in full, as before.
- The mobile See more button, its `seeMore` prop, story and `describeSeeMore` copy are removed. `FOOD_SEARCH_GROUP_LIMITS` and `hiddenCount` stay because web still uses them.

Trade-off: the per-group previews go away, so someone with many matching foods of their own sees Common only after scrolling.

## QA / How to test

Manual:
1. In Find food, search for something with more than 15 local matches, such as "chicken".
2. Expect 15 rows in the order Yours, Common, Branded, with no "See N more" button, and no heading for a group with no rows yet.
3. Scroll down. Expect more rows to append at the bottom with no jump, stopping at 50.
4. Type a different search. Expect it to return to 15 rows at the top of the list.
5. Repeat in the Diary add food search and in a recipe's Add ingredient.
6. Check the idle, "No foods found" and error states still sit centred, with normal spacing between groups. Not yet seen on a device.
7. Search for something with few matches and check the Open Food Facts rows still show in full.
8. On a tall device or tablet where 15 rows do not fill the screen, check the next rows still load.

Automated, run locally:
- `pnpm --filter @keylow/core test`, `lint`, `typecheck`
- From `apps/mobile`: `pnpm exec jest test/foods test/ui/GroupedList.test.tsx test/recipes/recipeEditorAddIngredient`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm exec eslint .`

## Out of scope

- Web food search keeps its See more button for now. That is KEY-929.
- More than 50 rows would need paging in `search_foods`.
- The exported design boards still draw the button because web does. `docs/design/food-search/README.md` records the mobile decision.
- Known edge, accepted: on a tablet-sized screen, rows could fail to load if results land at exactly the same content height as a list that had just asked for more while none were available. Changing the search clears it.

author: schindlershadow
body:
## Summary

Makes Communications mode (ad-hoc multiplayer) work in the native build. The PSP ad-hoc stack (`sceNetAdhocctl*`, `sceNetAdhocMatching*`, PDP/PTP) was a set of no-op stubs; it is now emulated over UDP, with a small relay server for internet play and a Network page in the settings menu.

- **Emulation** (`runtime/src/hle/psp_hle_adhoc.cpp`, generic runtime code): peers found by beacons; group/peer/scan events delivered to the game's handlers; the matching lobby state machine; PDP datagrams; PTP as a TCP-like reliable stream (connection ids, retransmission, partial sends); large messages split into single-packet fragments (the 4.7 KB lobby hello is dropped by many routers when IP-fragmented). Guest callbacks run on a game thread (`psp_adhoc_pump`), never on the network thread.
- **Two modes.** *Internet* (default): everything goes through a relay server; no port forwarding. *LAN*: broadcast / loopback / listed peers, no server.
- **Relay** (`psprecomp/tools/adhoc_relay`, C++): rooms, a cookie handshake so a forged source address cannot register, per-client rate limits, MAC-spoof checks, nothing crosses rooms. Protocol tests in `test_relay.py`.
- **Settings > Network page**: mode, server, room, direct peers, live status, and a small text editor (keyboard or letter picker). Saved in `settings.ini`.
- **Frame rate:** a session runs at the lowest rate any player asked for; a 5 s popup shows the agreed rate.
- **Controllers** now only act on the window that has focus (two instances on one machine shared one pad). `PSPRECOMP_PAD_BACKGROUND=1` restores the old behaviour.
- **Menu overlay:** four tiny functions the analysis missed (`0x08A0BED0`, `0x08AB41D8`, `0x08B535B8`, `0x08B535C0`) are added to `overlay_menu.toml`; leaving the lobby jumped into the first and showed a white screen.

Docs: new `docs/multiplayer.md`; `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `frame-rate.md` updated.

## Please read before merging

**The default server is a private host.** Internet mode defaults to `party.schindlershadow.com:27500`, a relay run by schindlershadow on a home server. Anyone running this code with default settings sends their traffic (player name, game messages) through it, so please decide whether that should be the default here, or change `DEFAULT_SERVER` (`psp_hle_adhoc.cpp`) and `NET_DEFAULT_SERVER` (`psp_settings.cpp`) before merging. The relay has no accounts and no encryption; a private room name is the only secret. Anyone can run their own (`tools/adhoc_relay`, README).

## Testing

Run on Linux (x86-64) with the US image:
- A full match between two instances, and a 3-player group battle, all on one machine, through the relay and in LAN mode.
- Relay protocol tests (`tools/adhoc_relay/test_relay.py`): registration, room isolation, directed / broadcast / fragment routing, spoofed MAC, wrong cookie.

Not tested: players on separate machines, over the real internet (from outside the relay's network), on a real LAN with broadcast, on the Steam Deck or macOS (the socket code is POSIX; unbuilt there), mixed US/EU images, and latency (the game is lock-step and nothing here delays or predicts input, so high round-trip times may be unplayable). The in-game text editor was not tried with a controller.

author: drbergman
body:
`Sobolʼ` reported only S1 and ST, with no uncertainty on either. This PR adds pairwise interaction indices (S2) and confidence intervals for all three orders.

**What changes for every Sobol' user.** Each entry of `results` is now a `SobolIndices`, ModelManager's own type, instead of `GlobalSensitivity.SobolResult`. GlobalSensitivity has no abstract result type to subtype. The `S1`/`ST`/`S2` field names are unchanged, so `.S1` and `.ST` reads still work, but code that annotates against `GlobalSensitivity.SobolResult` will break. The bootstrap is on by default (1000 resamples), so every result now carries `S1_CI`/`ST_CI`. The positional `Sobolʼ(sv, methods)` and four-argument `SobolSampling(...)` constructors are kept. This calls for a minor version bump (0.13.0), which this PR does not make.

**Second order.** `Sobolʼ(n; second_order=true)` adds one B_A^i matrix per focus parameter, so a run goes from N(d+2) to N(2d+2) monads. Because monads are reused, turning it on for a design already run costs only the extra N·d. S2 uses the Saltelli 2002 closed-index estimator and subtracts Saltelli 2010 first-order terms whatever `sobol_index_methods.first_order` is set to, since that is the form the closed term is in. `S2` is symmetric with a `NaN` diagonal.

**Confidence intervals.** Rows of the design are resampled with replacement and every index is recomputed; the point estimates still come from all N rows. No extra simulations are run. This is not GlobalSensitivity's `nboot`, which partitions the rows into batches and averages per-batch estimates. Resamples come from a `copy` of `rng`, which defaults to a fixed-seed `Xoshiro`. The intervals are therefore reproducible, and neither the global RNG stream nor the caller's RNG advances. A constant output gives `NaN` bounds rather than an error.

**Scheme columns.** Columns after `A` and `B` in `monad_ids_df` / `sobol_scheme.csv` are now prefixed `A_B:` or `B_A:`. A frame without prefixes is read as the old all-A_B layout; that fallback is meant to be dropped at v1.0. Nothing in ModelManager reads the CSV back.

**Plots.** Bars get asymmetric whiskers from the stored CIs (`show_CI=true`), and `plot(s, :S2; quantity)` draws an interaction heatmap.

author: jkoehler11
body:
lipsinc: a slot is read by name, and a zero is a skip

The four bodies the sampler note nominated are read, and what was left of U4 turns out to be a naming
convention and a sentinel rather than another container field.

**The accessor addresses a slot by name.** `0x000b4710` (215 bytes) copies its caller's `FString`,
resolves it with `0x000b45c0` (329 bytes: a `__wcsicmp` scan of the key block's 28-byte groups, count
`+0x40`, base `+0x3c`, returning `index*0x1c + base` for the first match and 0 otherwise) and evaluates
the group it finds with `Engine_LIPSincSupport`; no match answers the `0x4c8848` zero. All 58,006 groups
in the corpus are unnamed, so the only query this data can resolve is the empty name -- a slot number is
not an address anywhere in the runtime, which is why the file-side measurements could never label one.

**A zero means "no contribution".** `0x000b5f10` (1,244 bytes, the pose-pair blend) enters its sampling
path only at `alpha == 0` exactly -- the first frame of a fade -- where it copies the destination pose
indices, calls `ValuesAtTime` once, resets the pose out of `pDefBonePose` (`0x000b2700`), then writes each
0x48-byte record's named curve into `+0x40` and calls pose assembly `0x000b29a0` **only when that value
is non-zero**; at any other alpha it does no curve work, lerping the three position floats between the
pair and copying four orientation dwords filled by `0x000b19b0`. `0x000b63f0` (1,411 bytes) is the fade
state machine that drives it: state 1 = fade in (duration `[request+0x28]`, alpha = elapsed/duration),
state 2 = play (clock at `+0x20`, `ValuesAtTime` as the bounds check, the same accessor-and-assembly
loop), state 3 = fade out (duration `[request+0x2c]`, then a `+0xec` vtable call and every record's
`+0x40` zeroed), 0 = idle. A negative weight passes the same gate as a positive one, so the 7 signed
columns are ordinary weights, not a second curve type.

**The corpus against that gate** -- `tools/lad-weights.py` (new; `make lipsinc-weights`,
`inventory/lipsinc_weights.csv`, `--check` in `make ci`), 2,231 tracks / 35,031 populated slots:

| measurement | value |
| --- | --- |
| slots non-zero at tick 0 (applied) | **12,080 (34.5%)** |
| slots exactly zero at tick 0 (skipped) | **22,951 (65.5%)** |
| per-track share | median **36.4%**, p10 9.1, p90 66.7 |
| tracks with no contribution at tick 0 | **3** |
| per file | 6.7% (`JAnderson`, 3 tracks) to 36.2% (`carter`, 610) |
| slots non-zero at a track's own end | **26 (0.07%)** |
| 24 == 25 at tick 0 | **2,230 of 2,230** tracks that carry them |
| 19 == -24 by value / key for key | **2,137** / **1,890** (of the 1,890 sharing a grid) |
| range of 19 / 24-25 at tick 0 | 0..8.378 / -8.378..0 |
| range of 20-23 | within +-2.87 |

Docs: `docs/formats/lipsinc-runtime.md` gains the consumer section and the state table, `docs/UNKNOWNS.md`
U4 the resolution, `PLAN.md` 5.5 the item text and an execution note above the newest one. No game data
and no decompiled output: addresses, constants and counts only. No boot and no xemu run -- this is a
static read plus a CSV walk.

author: rafaelmatosdasilva
body:
## What changes

Three Figma rules. Each is based on what most of the library already does, never imposed, and each flags a component for a person to look at, never one the engine removes or merges. Built on #398, now merged.

- `icon-with-label` (`lib/part-rules.mjs`): an icon beside a label is the size most of the library puts beside that text style. The icon's size is read from its size option or the size its name ends in (`arrow-down-m`).
- `component-used` (`lib/need-rules.mjs`): a component is placed on a page of the file or held by another component. It is read with the examples snapshot; without it, a component nothing holds may still be placed on a page, so no rule is made.
- `no-option-twins` (`lib/need-rules.mjs`): a component is not another component plus an option that other already takes (`buttonLarge` beside a `button` whose Size takes `large`).

On a real library:
- 44 of 49 components with an icon beside a label use the usual size (`m` beside `s/strong`, 199 times).
- 21 of 187 components are neither placed on a page nor held by another.
- No component repeats another with an option.

## Checks

- Full suite with Chrome, nothing skipped.
- Skill evaluation for the guide change (`reference/usage.md`), recorded in `test/skill-evals/RESULTS.md`.
