## Summary

Round-5 symposium artifact: a precise, mathematical invariants document with full invariant↔guard↔test traceability, plus an always-on executable assertion suite for the cross-machine invariants.

### docs/FORMAL_INVARIANTS.md
- **145 first-order invariants** (explicit quantifiers) across ceremonyCore, vote, confirmation, signing, DKG, selection, batchAttestation, validator, + 10 cross-machine invariants
- Every invariant carries: ID (INV-<machine>-<n>), formal statement, enforcing guard (file:line), pinning test (file › name)
- Notation section: the CanonicalWriter encoding as a formal grammar (prefix-freeness/injectivity laws), the BAO-Court/* hash domains as a pairwise-disjoint family, machine formalization convention, fail-closed laws
- Full traceability matrix (145 rows)
- **12 findings** — the audit value:
  - F-1 batch membership scope is caller-duty (dedup by verdictHash is convention, not enforcement)
  - F-2 the group-key pin is opt-in AND falsy-fragile (a present-but-empty pin silently disables)
  - F-3 outcomeHistory is not barrier-verified on restore
  - F-4 clawback reason language is open
  - F-5 weightFn purity unenforceable

Executable pins for the cheap global invariants: hash-domain disjointness, typed error family, behavioural terminal absorption on all four machines, deep-freeze discipline, deadline precedence (both sides of F-12), roster closure, threshold/quorum bounds, CanonicalWriter totality + injectivity, compareOutcomeUtf8 vs the UTF-8 byte oracle (supplementary-plane divergence pinned), shared Verdict/v1 domain, commit version bit + legacy-format rejection, RFC-6962 split-point oracle.

author: yeongseon
body:
## Summary

Finishes the historical part of #887. The release-notes tool built each Full Changelog link from the previous GitHub Release by version, so once `v0.17.2` was documented as never published, `v0.18.0` would have linked `v0.17.2...v0.18.0`, which GitHub reports as *diverged* (2 ahead, 66 behind). This adds a `not_a_release` list so such tags are never used as a compare base.

## Changes

- `tools/release_notes.py`: new `not_a_release` config key; those tags are skipped when choosing the previous release (a tag is still rendered against its own predecessor). Regression test added; it fails without the filter.
- `.github/release-notes.json`: `"not_a_release": ["v0.17.2"]`, so `v0.18.0` compares against `v0.17.1`.
- `docs/release_process.md`: one sentence describing the key.

The 33 remaining historical Release bodies are standardized with `tools.release_notes apply --backup`, one at a time, on the existing tags only (the nine already standardized were left alone). author: valleteclab
body:
## Resumo
Dois pedidos do dono, no modelo da BLL: importar a proposta por planilha e entregar ao fornecedor um comprovante de tudo o que ele grava no sistema.

### 1. Importar a proposta por planilha
- **Planilha-modelo** (`GET /propostas/licitacao/:id/planilha-modelo`, pública para licitação divulgada):
  - sai com os itens da licitação: item, lote, descrição, quantidade, unidade e valor de referência;
  - o fornecedor preenche valor unitário, marca e modelo, e só essas células ficam destravadas;
  - o valor de referência fica fora quando o orçamento é sigiloso.
- **Tela da proposta:** botões "Baixar planilha-modelo" e "Importar planilha preenchida" (`.xlsx`, `.xls` ou `.csv`).
- **A importação só preenche o formulário.** O fornecedor confere e envia como antes, e as validações do envio são as mesmas.
- **Avisos na importação:** valor que não é número, item repetido, item que não existe na licitação e item exclusivo de ME/EPP fora da proposta. Aceita valor no formato brasileiro ("1.234,56").

### 2. Comprovantes
- **Quando é emitido:** a cada envio, alteração ou exclusão da proposta, e a cada documento de habilitação anexado, removido ou entregue.
- **O que traz:**
  - número `CP-AAAA-NNNNNN`, data e hora de Brasília e a descrição do que foi feito;
  - o retrato do que ficou gravado naquele instante: itens e valores da proposta, anexos com tamanho e SHA-256;
  - um código de verificação (SHA-256 do conteúdo).
- **PDF:** gerado do retrato gravado, sempre igual. Na exclusão, o retrato é tirado antes de apagar, e o comprovante mostra o que foi excluído.
- **Sigilo:** só o próprio fornecedor lista e baixa os seus comprovantes, porque a proposta é sigilosa até a abertura. Órgão recebe 403 e outro fornecedor recebe 404.
- **Onde aparece:** cartão "Comprovantes" na página da proposta, na tela de cadastro da proposta (para quem excluiu) e na sala do fornecedor.
- **Robustez:** se a emissão falhar, a ação principal não é desfeita; o erro vai para o log.

### Detalhes técnicos
- Módulo novo `backend/src/comprovantes` (global), com a tabela `comprovantes_fornecedor`, criada pelo `synchronize` como as demais.
- A emissão é chamada nos controllers de propostas e de habilitação.
- Módulos por órgão: não se aplica, porque as telas são do portal do fornecedor e não do órgão.

## Plano de testes
- [x] `comprovantes.regras.spec` (3 testes): número, JSON canônico e código de verificação
- [x] e2e `comprovantes-proposta` (5 testes): planilha-modelo com as colunas do contrato e células destravadas; um comprovante por ação; retrato na exclusão; PDF só para o dono
- [x] Leitura da planilha conferida em script: formato brasileiro, item repetido, valor inválido, planilha sem cabeçalho
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` (backend e frontend); os erros de eslint da página da proposta já existiam
- [x] Next local com dados simulados: importação preenche 4 itens e mostra os avisos; cartão de comprovantes aparece
- [ ] Railway: baixar o modelo, importar, enviar a proposta, anexar um documento e baixar os PDFs

author: dain
body:
On aarch64, C2 can't encode the subtraction of `0x0101010101010101` as an immediate. A SWAR word loop that subtracted it as a literal, or from a local holding the literal, rebuilt it with four instructions on every word. Each such loop now reads the constant from a final field once per call, so C2 keeps it in a register. Generated LIKE reads a static field instead. `LiteralSearchKernel`'s contains loops and `RequiredBytes` already work this way.

- The class-run counter's `countUtf8` reads the field on aarch64 only. A class-init `static final` makes the choice, and C2 folds it, so each JVM compiles one form. On x86-64, C2 spilled the field to the stack, and the method's changed branch layout cost about 1,200 more branch misses per call on rebar `letters-ru`, 2.8% slower on r8i. Generated LIKE's literal broadcasts already split the same way ("Generated Trino LIKE Kernels" in REGULATOR_DECISIONS.md). klauspost/compress#1230 made the same split for its hash primes, and golang/go#81755 reported the compiler behaviour.
- Measured on r9g (Graviton 4, aarch64) and r8i (Xeon 6975P-C, x86-64). Other x86-64 hosts keep main's `countUtf8` form. Other aarch64 hosts (Graviton 2 and 3, Apple silicon) get the field form, which hasn't been measured on them.
- `TestBoundedCharacterClassCounterForms` runs each `countUtf8` form in a child JVM with `os.arch` set, so both forms are tested on any host. Each child checks by reflection that it picked the intended form.

| Row | r9g | r8i |
| - | - | - |
| SearchEdges `containsGeneral` `finalLineLiteralNoMatch` 32 KiB (inlined `indexOfSWAR`) | 0.787 | 0.935 |
| Class-run counter, specialized Russian 32 KiB | 0.991 | 0.998 |
| Class-run counter, specialized ASCII 32 KiB | 0.993 | 1.000 |
| rebar `letters-ru` | 1.003 | 0.997 |

The other changed loops already hoisted the constant in their hot code on main, and their rows stayed within noise. Two residues are noise:
- On r8i, TrinoRegexp `extractAll` `captureSparse` measured 1.022 in the first round.
- On r9g, the counter rows read 0.5–0.7% slower than a build that read the field on every platform. On aarch64 the two builds run the same code.

author: 6deadshot9
body:
Step 2 of the takeover work, and the rest of bug #1. While you're in control, the bot's container is now paused, so nothing it runs makes progress: no tool calls, no model calls, and no background processes it started earlier. Step 1 already kept the bot away from your private browser. This step also stops it from doing anything else while you're in.

## What changes for you
- **Take over privately** now pauses the bot before your private browser opens. Other sessions see "Paused while the owner uses a private browser". There's no live view of the frozen screen.
- The two **Advanced** settings from #9 now take effect, and their "takes effect when takeover pausing ships" note is gone.
  - **When the bot is mid-reply** (default: pause immediately). With a wait of 15, 30 or 60 seconds, the pane shows "Scout is finishing a reply…" with a countdown. **Take over now** skips the wait, and **Hand back** cancels the takeover.
  - **When the bot can't be paused** (default: ask). The pane shows "Couldn't pause Scout" with **Try again**, **Take over without pausing** and **Cancel**. *Always refuse* hands control back with "Couldn't pause Scout. Try again." *Always take over without pausing* lets you in and shows a banner saying the bot keeps working but still can't see your browser.
- **Hand back** resumes the bot first. Your logins (cookies) then reach its browser, and only after that does it get control back.

## How it works
- **Takeover runs in three steps,** so the per-bot lock is never held during the wait:
  1. Under the lock: fence admission and take the lease. From here the bot's tools refuse to run.
  2. Without the lock: if the bot is mid-reply and a wait is set, poll until its turn ends, the wait runs out, you press Take over now, or control changes.
  3. Under the lock again: re-check that you still hold control, read the bot's pages and cookies, record the pause and stop the active-time clock, pause through the supervisor, then open the private browser.

  Progress is committed in short separate transactions, so status polls show each step as it happens.
- **Supervisor:**
  - New endpoints `POST /runtimes/{bot}/pause` and `POST /runtimes/{bot}/resume`.
  - They act only on Hermbot's own runtime for that bot, are idempotent, and report a state only once Docker shows it.
  - Stopping or starting a paused runtime thaws it first.
- **Nothing calls a paused bot.** A call would connect and then hang, so the guard answers at once instead:
  - `native.request` returns 409, and `HermesClient` raises `RuntimePaused`. Neither makes a network call.
  - Computer status is served from the database while paused, and the thumbnail is empty.
  - Watchers are refused.
  - The secure-input check now asks the database before the bot.
- **Worker:**
  - `claim_existing`, `probe` and the routine scheduler skip paused bots.
  - A drive interrupted by a pause isn't counted as a failure, and a direction that was never sent goes back to pending.
  - Accounting never restarts the clock while a bot is paused, so a takeover is never charged as active time.
  - Each probe resumes any runtime left paused without a takeover, for example after an interrupted handback.
- **Failure handling:**
  - If the private browser fails to start, or the pause is refused, the bot is resumed and handed back.
  - If a handback can't resume the bot, you keep control and nothing is lost; hand back again.
  - A forced handback always resumes.
  - A takeover interrupted after the pause starts over cleanly.
- **Reclaiming from another session while paused** moves control in the database without waking the bot, and the old session is fenced. Its handback is refused unless forced. Because the bot isn't called, the lease epoch no longer increases on that kind of reclaim. The live `phase3-computer` check now asserts the fencing directly instead of the epoch.
- Migration `030` adds six columns to `computer_controls`, all `IF NOT EXISTS`. The runtime image is unchanged and no bot is reprovisioned.

## Checks run before opening this PR
- **Lint and the full suite:** 815 passed. Of those, 25 are new tests in `tests/test_takeover_pause.py`. They cover:
  - the three-step order, with status available during the wait;
  - Take over now;
  - the wait limit;
  - a handback during the wait cancelling the pause;
  - each failure mode;
  - the resume-first handback order;
  - forced handback;
  - a handback that can't resume;
  - paused reclaim;
  - an interrupted takeover;
  - the guard making no network call;
  - the worker, probe and routine skips;
  - no active time charged across a pause;
  - orphan recovery;
  - the supervisor's checks.
- **Fixture browser tests:**
  - new `takeover-pause.mjs` (9 checks: every pane state at 1440, 768 and 390 px with no overflow, and no live view of a paused bot);
  - `private-takeover`, `settings`, `model-auth` and `timeline` all pass.
- **Disposable end to end, real Docker, this branch's code:**
  - a forking loop inside a throwaway runtime made 0 progress in 4 s while paused, and the adapter connected but never answered;
  - exec was refused (409), and a second pause was a no-op;
  - resume and adapter readiness took 0.06 s, in the same process;
  - cookies applied after resume reached the thawed browser;
  - the fence still blocked the agent user after resume;
  - stopping a paused runtime exited cleanly.
- **Deployed from this branch,** then the live acceptance ran with Scout (`tests/takeover_pause_live_acceptance.py`, real model, local only):

  | Reply wait | Takeover took | Pane showed | Counter while paused (20 s) | Active time while paused | After handback |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0 s | 2.1 s | pausing → paused | 3 → 3 | 18.09 s → 18.09 s | counter resumed; completed `PAUSE_ACCEPTANCE_OK 31` |
  | 15 s | 10.7 s (reply finished early) | finishing → paused | 12 → 12 | 24.20 s → 24.20 s | task was `waiting_computer`, then completed `PAUSE_ACCEPTANCE_OK 37` |

  In both runs, active time after handback stayed within wall time (31.1 s in 33.6 s, and 29.6 s in 31.5 s), so the pause wasn't charged. The test groups were archived afterwards, and Advanced was reset to its defaults. The 15 s run left two entries in Advanced's change history.
- **Live UI scripts:**
  - all pass: `phase3-computer`, `phase3-knowledge`, `ui-regressions`, `execution-monitoring`, `work-controller`, `reconnect` and `ui-taste-audit`;
  - the first `phase3-computer` run failed on the epoch assertion above and left Scout paused. That's how I found that a failed run left the bot paused, so the script now force-hands-back if it fails. Scout was handed back and was healthy again within seconds.

## Rollback
Images `hermbot-app:pre-pause` and `hermbot-hermes:pre-pause`. The new columns are harmless to the previous code.

## New: colony-wide Essencebound Codex
- Five searchable tabs: **Essences (125), Confluences (101 + recorded unique-three recipes), Awakening Stones (30), Abilities (100), Bestiary (observed creatures and astral tiers)**.
- Unfound names remain secret behind a count of unknown entries. Known items, powers and creature details offer descriptions, rarity/affinities or rank-linked drop chances.
- Confluence recipe journal records the *three distinct inputs*, output, and whether the recipe was catalogued, a generated mod synthesis, or a disputed match. Separate triples remain separate even when they have the same confluence output.
- **Per-save GameComponent** stores discovered essence IDs, stone IDs, abilities, species, astral tiers and recipe records via Scribe. It is shared across the colony, not attached to a specific pawn or global mod settings.
- Automatic 600-tick observation finds known colonist abilities and recipes, plus **unfogged** essence crystals, awakening stones, and animals on player home maps. Essence absorption and stone awakening also immediately sync from the pawn's saved state.
- Existing saves automatically reconstruct knowledge held by surviving colony pawns and currently observable map items/creatures, without inventing historical discoveries.
- Accessible through **Essence Codex** gizmo on essence users, **Open Codex** in their profile, or **Essencebound mod settings** even before the first essence.

## Scope and safeguards
- Codex does not alter rank resistance, loot rates, confluence selection, or ability effects.
- Search and detailed views filter to discovered entries so unknown names cannot be enumerated.
- Added documentation in `CODEX_GUIDE.md` plus README note; included `Tests/test_codex.py` in CI.

author: ntucker
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ntucker"} -->
_Requested by **Nathaniel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016euKxQ34TM4LKaPsKxjHB5?thread=cmsg_016euKxQ34TM4LKaPsKxjHB5LuDTmy7ZZXLPkJqLdJQjbB)_

### Motivation

Improvement. The mutation scenarios only time how a view that is already mounted updates. They don't time the browsing that follows.

After a create or an edit, Data Client shows every next view from the store. The response updates each stored list that matches, and the Entity is [Queryable](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/schema#queryable), so other lists and the detail page need no fetch. `move` updates a stored list even while it isn't mounted. Caches keyed by query refetch after each mutation, fetch every view they haven't cached, and serve only back and forward from that cache. The baseline fetches every view.

### Solution

Two React benchmark scenarios. Each one sums its timed steps (`nav-step`, like `list-detail-switch-10`) after an unmeasured warmup round.

**`create-edit-browse-5`.** The open-issues list loads first, then the 1,000-issue list mounts, like two tabs the user visited. Each of 5 rounds times ten steps, and the runner reports the sum of all 50:

1. Create an issue, until the list shows it.
2. Switch to the open list.
3. Open the issue.
4. Go back.
5. Go forward.
6. Edit its title, until the detail shows the new title.
7. Go back to the open list.
8. Go back to the all-issues list.
9. Go forward to the open list.
10. Go forward to the issue.

Each step ends when its view shows the new issue or title. After each mutation step, its reply is handled and painted before the next step starts, so reply processing never lands in a later navigation window. The optimistic edit holds its reply during its own window, as `measureUpdate` does.

Data Client sends only the create and the edit. The scenario has three tiers on purpose, so no single special case closes the gap:
- Data Client renders every view from the store.
- TanStack Query and SWR serve back and forward from cache, but refetch after each mutation and fetch the views they haven't cached.
- The baseline fetches every view.

**`move-switch-list-10`.** The open and closed lists were loaded, and only one is mounted at a time, like tabs. With the open list shown, an issue moves to closed (untimed), and then the view switches to the closed list. Each step is timed until the closed list shows the moved issue.

Each library mutates the way it already does elsewhere in the benchmark, through new untimed `createItem()`, `editTitle()` and `moveToState()` actions:
- Data Client uses Collection `unshift`, `update` and `move`.
- TanStack Query calls the API, then invalidates the list and detail keys.
- SWR calls the API, then `mutate()`s the list and detail keys.
- The baseline calls the API, then refetches.

Both scenarios are mount-like, so the runner resets the store between iterations. `measureNavStep` now also takes a predicate, and can skip recording for a warmup round.

### Assumptions and validation

- `yarn validate`: 66 passed, 0 failed. The new checks pass for all four libraries: the final view, the edited title, no step timed out, and the number of `nav-step` measures (30 for create-edit-browse, 3 for move-switch). Thirty back-to-back create-edit-browse iterations ran without a timeout. High.
- A per-step probe confirmed what each window holds. Data Client's navigation steps take 0.5–8 ms and its create about 15–20 ms. TanStack Query's steps that refetch the 1,000-issue list take 85–150 ms, and its cached back and forward steps take 3–16 ms. High.
- Local runs, network simulation on, Linux container, headless Chromium, in ops/s:

  | Scenario | data-client | tanstack-query | swr | baseline |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | `create-edit-browse-5` | 4.60 ± 9.3% | 0.34 ± 0.7% | 0.33 ± 0.8% | 0.26 ± 0.2% |
  | `move-switch-list-10` | 15.37 ± 7.2% | 1.46 ± 0.5% | 1.50 ± 0.6% | 1.52 ± 0.5% |

  Create, edit and browse runs at 13.5× TanStack Query's speed (217 ms vs 2.9 s for 50 steps), and TanStack Query and SWR run at 1.3× the baseline's. Switching to the list an item moved into runs at 10.5× TanStack Query's speed (65 ms vs 685 ms). This is one run on one machine. Medium: the README's results table comes from a different machine, so I didn't add these numbers to it.
- The create step doesn't hold its reply. Holding it stalled the optimistic create in about 1 of 8 runs. Without the hold, a zero-latency reply can land inside that window, which only adds to Data Client's time. High.
- Both scenarios are classed Volatile, because Data Client's margin was ±8–12% in CI and locally. High.
- TanStack Query could seed the detail and the other lists from each response with `setQueryData`, which takes a handler per mutation per affected query. The scenarios use each library's existing mutation code, not hand-seeded caches. High.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are confined to the benchmark-react example, harness, and docs; no production library API or runtime behavior is modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds two **hot-path** React benchmark scenarios that time UI work *after* mutations and across navigation, not just in-place updates.
> 
> **`create-edit-browse-5`** runs five rounds (plus an unmeasured warmup) of ten summed `nav-step` windows: create issue → browse open list / detail / back-forward → edit title → navigate back through lists. **`move-switch-list-10`** preloads open and closed lists, moves issues to closed off the clock, and times switching to the closed tab until the moved issue appears.
> 
> The shared harness gains tab-style **`stateList`** rendering, **`measureNavStep`** support for selector or predicate “done” checks and optional non-recording warmup rounds, plus orchestration in **`createEditBrowse`** / **`moveThenSwitch`**. Each library port implements untimed **`createItem`**, **`editTitle`**, and **`moveToState`** (data-client via `controller.fetch`; TanStack/SWR via invalidate/mutate; baseline via refetch). Runner/scenario registration treats these as mount-like and **large** convergent scenarios; validation asserts DOM outcomes and `nav-step` counts. Docs classify both scenarios as **volatile** variance.

author: yosuke-wolfssl
body:
### Problem
`sc_reduce()` and `sc_muladd()` in the C Ed25519 scalar code can return a value outside `[0, l)`. The last fold of the reduction leaves a result that is either `l` too low or `l` too high, and nothing corrects it:

Inputs are SHA-512 outputs and the clamped private scalar, so the odds are about 2^-127 per operation and no party can steer them. Although it breaks the documented `s mod l` contract.

### Fix (`wolfcrypt/src/ge_operations.c`)
After the final carry chain, without branching on the value:
- **All four functions** add `l` back when the top limb is negative, using a sign mask, then repeat the carry chain.
- **The `__int128_t` versions** then subtract `l` and add it back under the same mask if the result goes negative, which maps `[-l, 2l)` to `[0, l)`.

Values already in `[0, l)` come out unchanged. Closes f-17452.

### Verification
- `sc_reduce` and `sc_muladd` are `WOLFSSL_LOCAL`, and no public API can steer an input into either range, so I checked them with an out-of-tree harness linked against the static library, compared with exact bignum `% l`. Both versions: 0 wrong out of about 330k vectors (edge values, in-range residues, uniform random, caller-shaped inputs, and targeted top-carry patterns). The unpatched code gets 24,557 of 59,991 targeted vectors wrong.
- `testwolfcrypt` and `unit.test --group ed25519` pass, with and without `NO_CURVED25519_128BIT`. ASan + UBSan clean. GCC `-Werror` clean on Ubuntu 24.04.
- Ed25519 sign/verify throughput changes by -0.4% to +1.1%, within run-to-run noise.

author: hanthor
body:
Fixes #60

## What
- `ccleft serve` now listens on `127.0.0.1:9464` when no `--addr` flag and no `addr` config value are set. The old default `:9464` put the unauthenticated `/readings` and `/metrics` endpoints on all interfaces.
- The order is unchanged: flag, then config `addr`, then the default. A new `serveAddr` helper holds this logic.
- New test `TestServeAddrDefault`. It fails if the default is `:9464`.
- Docs: README, `ccleft.example.yaml`, the `config.go` comment and the usage text show the new default. The README pod examples now pass `--addr :9464`.

## Existing deployments
- The container image is not affected: the Dockerfile `CMD` already passes `--addr :9464`.
- A deployment that overrides `args`/`command` without `--addr`, and has no `addr` in its config file, will now listen on loopback only. A Service will not reach it. Add `--addr :9464` (or `addr: ":9464"`) to keep remote access.
- `tuna-os/hive-operator` only reads ccleft through a URL (`http://ccleft.hive.svc:9464`). It has no ccleft Deployment manifest, so it needs no change. Check the cluster manifest that runs ccleft for the case above.
- `tuna-os/docs` (`docs/ccleft/index.md`) has a copy of the README. It will need the same update if it is not synced.

## Checks
- `gofmt -l .` (no output), `go vet ./...`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /dev/null ./cmd/ccleft`: all pass.

author: barronkid
body:
## What changed and why

Closes #41 and closes #42. These are the last two feature issues on the roadmap.

```sh
turnrow-profile orgchart show  acme.org.json --on 2026-11-07 --compare 2026-01-05 --format html --out chart.html
turnrow-profile orgchart show  acme.org.json --format pdf --out chart.pdf
turnrow-profile orgchart stats acme.org.json --from 2026-01-05 --to 2026-11-07
```

### The view (#41)

Against the issue's "done when":

| Asked for | What this does |
|---|---|
| An accessible interactive chart, keyboard and screen-reader navigable as a tree, light and dark, on any date | `--format html`: one file that fetches nothing. A nested list that scripting turns into a tree (the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: arrows, Home, End, level and position announced). Without scripting it is still the whole list. Colors are the brand tokens (7:1 in both themes). `--on` picks the date. |
| Vacant and planned posts marked distinctly, never by color alone | In words ("Vacant (open, new post), wanted by 2026-12-15") and by border: dashed for vacant, dotted for planned. |
| Two dates can be compared | `--compare <date>`: a table of what opened, closed, was filled or vacated, changed hands, moved or was retitled. |
| The same view exports as a tagged PDF and an accessible table | `--format pdf` (PDF/UA-1 through Typst, now in the CI job that runs veraPDF and the text-order check) and `--format table` / `csv`. The page also carries the table. |

See `examples/out/orgchart/acme.html`.

### The analysis (#42)

`orgchart stats`: posts, people and FTE; filled, vacant and planned per unit; span of control per manager; layers. With `--from` and `--to`: headcount at the start of each month and the change log. With `--budget`: budgeted FTE and cost per unit against the cost of its filled posts. See `examples/out/orgchart/acme.stats.md`. The numbers are counted from the same state as the chart, so they can't disagree with it.

### Three things that differ from what you might expect

1. **It is a tree you move through, not a drawing of boxes and lines** (design decision 8 in #76). That is what lets it meet the keyboard, screen-reader, zoom and small-screen requirements outright. A drawn view can sit on the same data if you want one.
2. **"On any date" is chosen when the page is made, not inside the page.** The page is a snapshot of one date (or a comparison of two). A date picker inside the page would mean shipping the whole file, including history, to whoever opens it.
3. **"WCAG AAA" is what the page was built to, not an audit result.** See below.

## Checks

- [x] `npm test` passes: 419 locally with Typst present (11 new in `test/orgchart-views.test.mjs`).
- [x] Example outputs are regenerated: `examples/out/orgchart/acme.html`, `acme.stats.md`; diffed in CI.
- [x] README, CHANGELOG and SECURITY say what the code now does (no SECURITY change: the page has a `default-src 'none'` policy and holds no addresses).

**Checked in a browser.** I drove the example page in Chromium: no network requests, no script errors; the tree roles and `aria-level` / `aria-posinset` / `aria-setsize` are set; arrow keys, Home and End move as the pattern says; both themes render; at 320 pixels wide there is no sideways scrolling; with scripting off it is a plain list of all six posts.

**The PDF** passed the text-order check locally. veraPDF runs on it in this PR's CI for the first time.

## Privacy

- [x] Nothing a profile marks private, unapproved or unconsented can reach an output or a release through this change. The views show only what is in the organization file; a test checks budget figures appear in no view unless `--budget` is passed, and that a photo's address is never written into the page.
- [x] No real person's data is added to the repository.

## Accessibility checks a tool can't make

- [ ] **Screen reader.** Not done. This is the check that matters most for this PR, and I can't make it.
- [x] **Reading order.** The PDF's text order matches the table (checked by `scripts/check-reading-order.mjs`); the page's order is the list's order.
- [x] **Plain language.** Status and changes are in short plain words, in English only.
- [x] **Not by appearance alone.** Vacant and planned are words plus a border pattern; depth is a "Level" figure in the table and PDF.
- [x] **Contrast.** Every color is a brand token; a test fails on any other color in the page's styles.
- [ ] **Zoom.** Reflow at 320 pixels was checked in a browser; 200% zoom of the PDF was not.

**Not checked, and why:** I am an AI agent without a screen reader, and no automated accessibility scanner (axe or similar) has been run on the page.

**Exceptions.** None.

author: joemattie
body:
Closes #115. This is the criterion left over from #49: the gateway's first listing after a start.

## What changed

- **The broker's stream listing carries each stream's recorded extent.** `Catalog::stream_extent` (both catalogs, conformance-tested) is two reads of the time index: the start of the stream's earliest payload and the end of the one that starts last. `StreamList` sends it as `extent_start_ns` and `extent_end_ns` (schema minor 36).
- **With the broker up, the gateway's listing is the broker's and nothing else.** No chunk file is opened and no chunk directory listed. The warm-up listing thread at start is gone. The chunk directory is listed only while the broker is unreachable, or when the gateway runs without one.
- **A stream summary is its id, name, liveness, format, and extent.** The `chunks` and `frames` counts are removed: the catalog can't give them without a scan, and the dashboard only tested `frames > 0`, which is now `end_us > 0`.
- `GET /streams` answers with the same listing as the socket's `streams` request.
- A range for a stream the broker doesn't know is an error now; it used to fall back to a directory walk to look for it.

## Numbers

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Chunk files opened by the first listing after a start | all of them (37 s and 60 s on two starts with 185,000 files) | 0 |
| Listing six streams' extents with a full 30-day window (259,200 chunk rows, synthetic catalog, debug build) | | 0.49 ms the first time, 0.41 ms after |
| Directory reads per listing while the broker is up | every hour directory still being written | 0 |

Measured with `measure_stream_extents_over_a_full_video_window` (ignored by default) on the Linux machine. Nothing was run against the live services.

## Upgrade

The broker, the gateway, and the frontend have to go together, or the dashboard shows no camera as live. MIGRATING.md has the steps: `mise run continuum-release`, `mise run frontend`, `pack-services restart --cascade`, then `pack-services restart continuum-gateway dashboard`. Nothing is deleted and the catalog's format is unchanged.

## Checks

- `cargo test --no-fail-fast -p continuum-catalog -p continuum-client -p continuum-broker -p continuum-gateway -p continuum-core`: 786 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored (one gateway test asserted the removed `frames` field on the first run; fixed, and the gateway crate rerun: 102 passed).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features continuum-tier/ffmpeg,continuum-capture/ffmpeg -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean, Biome clean on the changed files, `vitest run` on the five changed test files: 104 passed, and the production build (`vite build`) passes.
- New tests: the extent in both catalogs (empty, an instant, several payloads, a chunk, after a purge, an unknown stream), and the gateway against a real broker (extents in the listing, a stream that holds nothing, and a chunk file the broker doesn't know not turning up).

author: harusame64
body:
When a `terminal` run loses its baseline, the reply now says the command may have run and tells the caller to read the terminal, instead of advising a rerun.

## The problem (internal #241)

`terminal(action:'run')` finds its output with a hash of the text that was on screen before the send. If that text is redrawn afterwards, the hash is not found again. This happens in a terminal opened seconds before and still settling, and with a prompt that rewrites itself on Enter. The run then waits out its time and answers `BaselineMarkerLost` with empty output, even though the command ran.

Before this PR, the reply's advice was "use pattern mode / increase timeoutMs", and the tool's caveat said "rerun with until:{mode:'pattern'} or longer timeoutMs". A caller that followed it ran the command a second time.

win2 reproduced this on main 8618b51a with a transient prompt: `reason: timeout` after 15 s, `BaselineMarkerLost`, and the command's output on screen.

## The change

**Reply:** the `BaselineMarkerLost` `readError` now says:
- the command may have run, or still be running;
- its output could not be told apart from earlier text;
- it may not have reached this terminal at all.

It then advises: "Do NOT send the command again until you have read this terminal", with the same windowTitle or paneId as the run.

**Warning and caveat:** both say the same. Neither names a rerun or a different mode.

**Test:** `a-lost-baseline-does-not-say-rerun.test.ts` pins the caveat, the reply and the warning, and rejects rerun, retry, `timeoutMs` or mode advice in them.

## What this PR does not change

The run itself still waits out its time and answers `BaselineMarkerLost` in that case. internal #241 stays open for that, and the CHANGELOG says so.

The first heads tried anchoring on the run's own echoed command. win2 and gate 2 showed that it can pass an earlier run's output off as this one's:
- a pre-send read taken while the terminal is still settling undercounts earlier echoes;
- PSReadLine's list predictions and the error view reprint the command text.

That turns a loud failure into a silent wrong success, so it was dropped. The `ok:false` semantics and an early end when the marker is missing are left for #241.

## Checks

- **Real machine (win2, 91144ec4):**
  - **Transient prompt:** `reason: timeout`, `BaselineMarkerLost`. The new readError, suggest and warning reached the caller verbatim, with no "rerun" anywhere.
  - **Normal prompt:** `pattern_matched`, unchanged.
  - The last commit changes wording only.
- **Full local unit run (serial):** the same 21 failures in the same 12 files as the baseline.

Refs internal #241.

author: mmcdole
body:
Refreshing an unmatched title, Refresh all metadata, or changing a series' episode ordering marked the title's files and then scanned its whole library, checking every directory on disk before the title was looked up again. Now only that title's folder is identified again and nothing is scanned.

- Identification is a task of its own (`identify-media`, on demand). A scan hands it the files it probed as the scan ends, so the scan row now finishes after reading files and Identify media shows under On demand while it works.
- At startup a scan resumes only libraries with unprobed files. Files probed but not yet identified are picked up by the identify task, at startup and hourly.
- identify no longer imports scan. scan reaches identify only through its small interface.
- The `identify` step is gone from ScanStep and TaskStep, since a scan no longer has it.

author: johnynek
body:
## Changes

Implement steps 0c and 0d of the hermetic Bazel rules plan. `tool compile-packages` takes explicit source and signature files and emits a compiled package bundle and a deterministic public signature. Private test entries stay in the implementation.

The file compiler follows the exposure closure before inference, resolves legacy re-exports against their owners, and compiles a local owner first when an external interface needs it. The exposure index is optional on the wire. The whole-file and selected readers handle deep legacy re-export chains and enforce constructor visibility. A full implementation can supply only the owner’s exported types to a foreign signature. For library inputs, `tool check` binds raw re-exports after selecting their source or signature owners.

## Cache behavior

Inference, cache keys, and warm reads use the same public dependency views. An opaque field edit preserves the consumer key. A change to an exposed alias invalidates it. The compiler checks public type schemes against the current owners’ kinds before cache lookup, including when an older signature still names a type whose arity has changed. The compiler fingerprints resolved foreign definitions, rejects conflicting definitions during key generation, and caches only diagnostic-free successes. Cache schema 5 prevents reuse of older entries. An additive import marker preserves the original decoding behavior for older compiled packages.

## Verification

- 2,156 passing JVM core tests and 121 passing CLI tests (one Linux-only skip on macOS), including warm/cold parity, opacity, mixed source and library providers, output preservation, and a 3,000-package legacy re-export chain, and kind checking under 6,000 nested type applications.
- All 13 signature tests on Scala.js, Scala.js CLI compilation, API documentation, and Paradox.
- `./test_cli.sh`, including all 6,118 Bosatsu tests.
- Generated Bosatsu sources from `TypedAst.proto` and type-checked them against the previously released core library.
- Java 17 deploy-jar smoke test for legacy signatures, mixed ownership, and preservation of prior outputs on failure.

body:
## 무엇을 하나

이슈 #345(대표 피드백) — 기억책 순간 면의 도메인 표기·버튼처럼 보이는 칩/'제목 고치기'를 정리하고, 의미를 알 수 없던 '경로 한눈에'를 '여기까지 온 길' 세로 타임라인으로 바꾼다. 기준 `origin/main` `bf894ad`. 저장·스키마·공유/예시의 쓰기 금지 동작은 그대로다.

## A. 기억책 순간 면

- 영상 바로 아래 한 줄 `▶ 영상 제목 · 채널 … YouTube ↗`(원본 링크). 제목은 `mediaMetadata.title`(#344), 없으면 링크만. 도메인 표기 제거.
- 날짜는 제목 위에 작게, 제목이 면의 주인공.
- 감정은 테두리 칩 대신 `● 설렘`(색 점 + 글자). 점 색은 기존 `--lt-group-1..6` 토큰, 글자는 종이 잉크(--lt-ink).
- '제목 고치기' 버튼 제거 → 제목 옆 작은 `✎ 고치기`(데스크톱 hover·포커스, 390 항상) + 제목을 눌러 편집. 키보드 접근 유지. 공유에는 숨김(`editAffordances` 순수 함수).
- 마음 한마디가 비면 흐린 안내 `이 순간에 남기고 싶은 마음을 적어 보세요…` → 누르면 기존 편집 경로. 공유에서는 안내 없이 비움.
- #344 자동 제목(영상 제목과 같은 title)은 큰 제목에서 빼고 출처 줄에만(`withoutAutoTitle` 확장, 표시 단계만·데이터 불변).

## B. '경로 한눈에' → '여기까지 온 길'

- 버튼·창 이름 변경 + 설명 "처음 좋아하게 된 순간부터 지금 보는 순간까지예요. 누르면 그 장으로 넘어가요."
- 세로 타임라인: 칸마다 썸네일(사진·YouTube 썸네일, 없으면 감정 색 사각형)·날짜·제목·감정, 금색 선, 현재는 금색 점 + `지금 보는 순간`.
- 칸 사이 `↳ 연결 이유`(실제 연결 우선, 없으면 생략), 칸 클릭 → 그 장으로 이동+창 닫힘, 아래 `N단계 · N일`.
- 390 세로 스크롤, 공유·예시 동작 유지. 카드·글자는 `--lt-*` 토큰만(닫기 버튼 대비 실측 17.9/11.6:1).

## 계산·시험

- `book-model.js`(LT59Model): `journeyTimeline`(현재까지 자르기·이유 우선/생략·썸네일)·`journeyDays`·`emotionTone`. `book-usability.mjs`: `mediaSourceText`·`editAffordances`·`withoutAutoTitle` 확장.
- 시험: book-model +4, book-usability +2, 공유 1건 갱신. 강도 증명 3회(현재까지만 자르기 제거 1실패 / 공유 편집 손잡이 개방 1실패 / 영상 제목 억제 제거 1실패) 후 `cmp` 원복.
- `npm test` **919건 882 pass / 0 fail / 37 skip**, `npm run build` pass.

## 로컬 실측(가짜 세션=만든 기록을 dist에 재생) — 12/12 PASS

출처 줄·도메인 0·hover ✎(opacity 0→0.72)·390 항상 보임·빈 마음 안내·타임라인 3칸/이유 2줄/현재 표시/'3단계 · 9일'/썸네일 3(ytimg)·칸 클릭 이동+닫힘·12칸 390 세로 스크롤·axe serious·critical 0·pageerror 0. 캡처 `.tmp-261109/shots-345-local/`, 시안 비교 `compare-A.png`·`compare-B.png`.

## 시안과의 차이(보고용)

- 면: 시안의 ▶ 재생·노란 설명 말풍선은 시안 표기용. 실제 영상은 기존처럼 썸네일+`여기서 재생` 단추. 날짜는 저장 문자열 그대로(실기록은 ISO) — 시안은 점 표기.
- 타임라인: 시안 썸네일은 감정 색 사각형(미디어 없음), 구현은 실제 YouTube 썸네일. 연결 이유에 시안은 따옴표를 썼고 구현은 생략. 시안 제목 30px vs 구현 26px(390 카드 높이 고려).
- 감정 글자색은 시안과 달리 잉크색 — 종이 위 대비 4.5:1 확보(점만 감정 색).

## 참고

- 운영 실측(계정 04)은 머지·배포 뒤: 빠른 추가 YouTube 3개+연결 이유 → 면 표시 → 제목 바로 고치기 → 마음 쓰기 → '여기까지 온 길' 이동 → 공유 주소 로그아웃 열람에 편집 요소 없음 → 트리 0·보관 0. 결과는 #345 댓글.

author: ppeble
body:
Follow-up to #41. Fixes the 48 broken internal links left in `content/en/docs/4.1/topics/install/upgrade/` and the dead manifest URLs in the 4.1 docs, so the 4.2 docs (copied from 4.1) start clean.

## Changes

- **Host the manifests.** The docs applied manifests from `app.getambassador.io/yaml/emissary/3.10/...` and `.../v2-docs/3.10/...`. Those short paths now return 403, but the full patch-version paths (`3.10.0`) still serve the originals. Those files are copied byte for byte into `static/yaml/emissary/3.10.0/` and `static/yaml/v2-docs/3.10.0/`, and the docs point at `emissary-ingress.dev/yaml/...`. Shell commands (`kubectl apply -f`) use the full URL; browser links use `/yaml/...`.
- **Trim the upgrade pages.** Remove the Helm and YAML upgrade pages for Emissary 1.14, 2.0 and 2.4 from 4.1. The migration matrix now sends anyone on 2.4 or earlier to the [3.10 migration matrix](https://emissary-ingress.dev/docs/3.10/topics/install/migration-matrix/), where those pages remain. Older doc versions are unchanged.
- **Fix links** in the remaining upgrade pages: relative paths that resolved one directory off, Helm/YAML cross-links between 3.8 and 3.9 that pointed at the wrong version, and a dead `/docs/emissary/latest/` link.

- **Add 3.10 to 4.1 upgrade pages** for Helm (`upgrade/helm/emissary-3.10/`) and YAML (`upgrade/yaml/emissary-3.10/`), linked from the migration matrix. Tested end to end on k3d from three 3.10.0 baselines (OCI charts; kubectl-applied CRDs plus the `datawire/emissary-ingress` chart; YAML manifests) to 4.1.0, with `v2` and `v3alpha1` Mappings returning 200 before and after. Findings not in the CHANGELOG that the pages cover:
  - `enableLegacyVersions=true` is required while `v2` is a CRD stored version; without it the CRD upgrade fails and changes nothing.
  - kubectl-applied CRDs and `emissary-apiext` need Helm ownership labels and annotations before the CRD chart can adopt them.
  - `helm upgrade` needs `--reset-values`, or a pinned 3.x `image.tag` is kept.
  - For a release named `emissary`, the 4.x chart replaces `emissary-emissary-ingress` with `emissary` / `emissary-admin`: new LoadBalancer address and about 40s of downtime. The page documents a tested zero-downtime alternative.
  - YAML users must render with the release name `emissary-ingress` so names and selectors match the 3.10 manifests.

## Not in this PR

- `helm repo add datawire https://app.getambassador.io` is unchanged; that Helm repo still works.

## Testing

Built with `hugo -e dev -DFE` and re-ran the link check: no broken internal links or anchors remain in 4.1. The full-URL `kubectl apply -f https://emissary-ingress.dev/yaml/...` commands can be checked against the deploy preview.

author: chenzc24
body:
## Summary

The China login proxy forwards an internally synthesized `CF-Connecting-IP` to the overseas authority, which Cloudflare rejects with HTTP 403 / error 1000. Strip that header only from the outgoing authority request; retain the local client address for rate limiting and the browser's Origin and cookies.

```text
Regional browser → local address/rate limit → authority proxy (without CF-Connecting-IP)
```

Align the signed-in header with overseas by removing the extra regional Switch account entry. Keep the account page and its sign-out flow. Render the configured ICP filing as a centered, muted footer link. Related to #2060; this PR does not complete the public opening or change DNS.

## Evidence

- Before: the handoff regression with Nginx's client-address header failed with HTTP 403. After: 46 targeted regional tests pass; private Hangzhou redirects reach GitHub/Google with the canonical callbacks.
- Before: the signed-in regional header rendered an additional Switch account link. After: 56 account/Gallery checks pass; the private browser screenshot confirms the revised footer and header. The signed-in UI check uses an API fixture, not a real provider login.
- Typecheck, dead-code check, changed-file formatting and lint pass. The frontend and pinned regional bundle build; generated runtime configuration and test-impact checks pass. Separate Standards and Spec reviews report no findings for both slices.
- Local `verify:pr --base origin/main`: 9,692 tests passed, 167 skipped, 4 failed in unchanged `scripts/gallery-download.test.mjs`. Its URL `.pathname` produces `E:\E:\...` on Windows. No checks or assertions were weakened. Linux merge-candidate checks remain required.
- The private candidate proves drawing, undo/redo, browser recovery, Agent pairing/read and one operator divider simulation (0.5 V). Real canonical login/save acceptance and public routing remain separate deployment checks. Prior full-data replication and off-host restore evidence is retained.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Code-only rollback; no schema or data migration. Preserve regional state and synchronization cursors. Normal Production deployment publishes the shared regional artifact; the host follows the verified release.

**Blast Radius:** regional-auth

The authority proxy fix affects regional browser authentication. The account-header change removes one regional shortcut; existing account settings and provider choices remain. Filing styling applies only when a filing number is supplied. No DNS, firewall, secret or write-switch changes are included.

body:
PR 2 of 4 in the run-cards stack (plan `3ef69c1d-026`, intent `run-passkey`). It stacks on #376.

The glass's page token is in the page any local process can fetch, so a Run is confirmed with a WebAuthn passkey (Touch ID) on this Mac.

## Change
- **Hosts:** the glass answers at `localhost:<port>` as well as `127.0.0.1:<port>`, because a WebAuthn relying party can't be an IP address.
  - Any other Host is refused, a rebound DNS name included, and Origin must match the Host.
  - `/api/show` (the pet's and the CLI's route) stays at 127.0.0.1 only.
- **`apps/cli/src/run-passkey.ts`** verifies ES256 registrations and assertions with `node:crypto`. It checks:
  - the ceremony type, challenge and origin;
  - the RP id hash;
  - that the user was present and verified;
  - the signature;
  - that the counter never goes backwards.

  Challenges are single-use, last two minutes, and are bound to the card and the script hash the page showed. Only public keys are stored, in `~/.lobstah/run/passkeys.json`.
- **Registration gate** (Chris picked "both" in ume `f81321ac-e3d`):
  - macOS's own administrator password dialog runs before any passkey is stored (`osascript … with administrator privileges`, naming the action).
  - Once one passkey exists, registering another also needs an assertion from it.
- **`/requests` kinds:** `run-passkey-challenge`, `run-passkey-register`, `run-challenge` and `run-assert`, all from the localhost page only. PR 3 turns `run-assert` into `run`.
- **Settings:** a "Run cards" section shows the registered passkeys and registers one. The 127.0.0.1 page links to localhost for it.

## Criteria (intent `run-passkey`)
| Criterion | Proven by (`apps/cli/test/run-passkey.test.ts`) |
|---|---|
| `ach-verify`: an assertion from the registered passkey over a fresh challenge is accepted, and the challenge is spent | accepts an assertion from the registered passkey over a fresh challenge, and spends the challenge |
| `ach-replay`: a used challenge, or one older than 120 s, gets 403 | the same test's replay; refuses a challenge older than 120 seconds |
| `pres-rebinding`: any Host but 127.0.0.1 or localhost on the glass's port gets 403 | refuses writes at any name but 127.0.0.1 or localhost on its own port |
| `pres-other-writes`: a decision answer with the page token gets 201 with no passkey | takes a decision answer with the page token alone, at either name, with no passkey |

The registration gate's tests:
- registers another passkey only with consent from a current one;
- asks with macOS's own password dialog, and refuses without the password or off macOS.

A software ES256 authenticator (`apps/cli/test/fixtures/soft-passkey.ts`) builds the browser's exact responses.

## Note
Files outside the intent's `applies-to`:
- `apps/cli/src/run-routes.ts` (the request kinds)
- `packages/core/src/glass.ts` (`runPasskeys` on the snapshot)
- `packages/glass-ui/ui/actions.ts`, `store.ts`, `components/app.ts` and `components/run-card.ts`

The full suite passes on the top of the stack: 268 files, 3363 tests.

author: damianvtran
body:
## Summary

Every recent native proof dispatch of `e2e.yml` died at **"Provision the existing pinned Maestro driver"**, before the app ever launched. One example is run [42581162973](https://github.com/damianvtran/local-operator-mobile/actions/runs/42581162973). Runs 42573553980 and 42571245938 failed the same way:

```
curl: (56) The requested URL returned error: 504
Downloaded zip archive is corrupt. Are you connected to the internet?
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The cause is that `get.maestro.mobile.dev` downloads the ~315 MB release zip with a single `curl --fail` and never retries it. One CDN 504 is enough to fail the lane.

## Change

- **`scripts/ci/install-maestro.sh`** (new). It downloads the same asset the upstream installer uses for a pinned version, `https://github.com/mobile-dev-inc/maestro/releases/download/cli-$MAESTRO_VERSION/maestro.zip`, read from the installer source.
  - curl flags: `--fail --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --connect-timeout 20`.
  - It verifies the **sha256** against a digest pinned in the script. 2.11.0 is pinned to `5384593c…283a`, which matches both the release's `checksums_sha256.txt` and the GitHub asset digest. An unpinned version falls back to the release-published checksum.
  - It runs `unzip -tq`, then installs the upstream layout (`~/.maestro/bin`, `~/.maestro/lib`) and appends `~/.maestro/bin` to `$GITHUB_PATH`. Any failure exits non-zero.
- **`.github/actions/install-maestro`** (new composite action). It runs `actions/cache@v6` on the zip, keyed `maestro-zip-<version>-<os>-<arch>`, then calls the script. A cache hit skips the download, and the sha256 is still re-checked.
- All seven `curl … | bash` steps now call `uses: ./.github/actions/install-maestro` with `version: ${{ env.MAESTRO_VERSION }}`: six in `e2e.yml` and one in `android-oauth-callback-proof.yml`. Step names, `if:` conditions and the `MAESTRO_VERSION` pin are unchanged, and no other step was touched.

## Validation

- `ruby -ryaml` parses all three YAML files (`ok` ×3).
- `actionlint` on both workflows gives exactly one finding, SC2012 info at `e2e.yml:1541`. That finding is pre-existing and identical on base `6d36c22a`.
- `shellcheck scripts/ci/install-maestro.sh` is clean, and `bash -n` passes.
- Real URL: it returns `302 → 200`, `content-length: 314886578`, and the first bytes are `504b0304` (zip magic). `cli-9.9.9` returns 404, and curl exits 56, so the step fails closed.
- Script logic, run against a curl stub that serves a tiny zip:
  - Fresh install: published-checksum fallback → download → sha match → `No errors detected` → installed, `bin/maestro` runs, `GITHUB_PATH` appended, exit 0.
  - Cached rerun: `Reusing cached … archive`, with no zip fetch.
  - Wrong digest: `::error::… sha256 mismatch`, exit 1, bad zip removed.
  - Unset `MAESTRO_VERSION`: exit 1.
- The full 315 MB download was **not** completed locally. The workstation disk was at 100% and curl failed writing (`curl: (56) Failure writing output to destination`), and the script exited non-zero as intended. The dispatched proof run below covers the full download path.
- Proof dispatch: `gh workflow run e2e.yml --ref ci/maestro-provision-retry -f proof_mode=chrome-ios-proof` → run 42757258965.

## What changed?

`MEFF301` now reports a typed `catch (ScopeFailure)` and filters that can be determined to accept `ScopeFailure`, such as `when (ex is not OperationCanceledException)`. Both can let the catch body run after a scope step returns an `Err`.

`MEFF302` uses the same catch classification for scope steps in cleanup. author: jordanbrock
body:
Moves the site off GitHub Pages' built-in Jekyll build to Bridgetown 2.2, deployed by GitHub Actions. This only changes the tech: the design is the same apart from a viewport tag so it scales on phones.

## What changed
- Content moved under `src/`. The layouts, home page (5 posts per page), archive, `atom.xml` and `sitemap.xml` are now Liquid templates.
- Every post now sets its URL explicitly:
  - 170 permalinks changed from `…/slug/index.html` to `…/slug/`. Bridgetown would otherwise build those as `slug.html`.
  - 12 posts from 2012–2023 that relied on Jekyll's default URL pattern now have it written into their front matter.
- The `.github/workflows/gh-pages.yml` workflow builds and deploys on every push to `master`. There's no Node or esbuild step; the CSS is copied as plain files.
- Removed:
  - the tag links, which never rendered anything
  - `comments.yml`, the old WordPress comments, which published commenters' emails
  - the WordPress import script and an empty `*.markdown` file

## Verification
- A production build has all 184 URLs from the live sitemap, with 0 missing. Pages `/page2/`–`/page37/` match the live site.
- `atom.xml` and `sitemap.xml` are well-formed XML. Feed links use the original post URLs.
- Spot-checked the home page and a 2008 post with images in a browser. Every local image a post references is in the build.

## Before merging
Change **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source** to **GitHub Actions**. Otherwise the legacy builder will try to build the site with Jekyll and fail.

## Known differences
- Feed entry IDs stay the same, except for the 2019 "retweet" post. Its file name had a colon and curly quotes, so I renamed the file, which changes the post's feed ID. It may show up once more in feed readers.
- Internal links use extensionless URLs such as `/2023/06/05/new-job`. GitHub Pages already serves these on the live site.

author: eosmin
body:
## What
Step 7.9 A6b-1, the first half of "move the widget into its plugin". The doors of the web widget are pinned, and the parts of the module that need nothing from the api moved into `libs/channels/web-widget`: the schemas of the public doors and of the settings, the message view (`widgetMessageView`, `WIDGET_FILES_SELECT`, `visitorMessagesWhere`) and the typing throttle. Behavior unchanged; the api imports them from the plugin library.

The rest (A6b-2) cannot move yet: it uses `TenancyModule`, `MediaModule`, `ChannelsModule`, `PluginRegistry` (a lib a channel may not import) and `WidgetDelivery`, which `RealtimeModule` and `ConversationsModule` reach. Tracked in the plan, Step 7.9 A6b-2, with the prerequisite steps and the `route-protection.spec.ts` roots to extend before the controllers leave `apps/api`.

## Public routes, tenancy, security
Intact: same paths, methods, `@Public()`, rate limits, statuses, CORS middleware, gateway and validations; no controller, guard or route moved or edited. Tenancy unchanged; no new tenant-scoped resource. New specs: `widget-surface.spec.ts` (path, method, status, public flag, rate limit of each public door; permission and not-public of each settings route; no other door) and `widget.schemas.spec.ts` (what each public body refuses). Integration suite `widget.spec.ts` and `widget-typing-throttle.spec.ts` green on a private database.

## Review lenses
`/code-review high` (correctness, security, tests), demonstrable defects only: 6 findings, no runtime regression. Fixed: the bodies were unpinned (added `widget.schemas.spec.ts`); the settings paths compared a builder with itself (literal paths now); the "not public" check missed a method-level `@Public()` (reads the handler too). Debt written in the plan (A6b-2): the CORS middleware, the visitors' gateway and the binding of each handler to its pipe are not pinned yet and must be before they move. Accepted: the surface spec reads the throttler metadata keys of the library (a key rename fails loudly on every door); the barrel now also exports the moved server-side pieces (they import no env, checked with `DATABASE_URL` unset).

## Decisions
- Split in two instead of one big move: the move needs tenancy and media to be libraries first; rejected moving with a copy of those pieces (two sources of truth on guards).
- Pin first, move after: the surface spec reads decorator metadata, so it holds whichever file declares the controller.

author: grahammmm
body:
## [RF1915-3] Bound ledger_list in-memory snapshots to 64 MiB

`ledger_list._snapshot` (shared by `status --list`, `finding packet`, `sources add-batch` and `--from-request`) read the whole ledger with an unbounded `handle.read()`. It now refuses a ledger over `MAX_LEDGER_BYTES = 64 MiB` (physical size, trailing bytes included) before any copy or SQLite use, with the fixed error `private/ledger.sqlite exceeds the 64 MiB snapshot limit`.

- Gate 1: the descriptor's single `fstat` size is checked before opening a read handle.
- Gate 2: `handle.read(MAX_LEDGER_BYTES + 1)`; if the returned length exceeds the limit (file grew after fstat) it refuses before building the bytearray, connecting to or deserializing into SQLite.
- Sidecar precheck, `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, regular-file check, post-read sidecar check and WAL-header normalization are unchanged. No override flag, truncation or fallback.
- Consumers are untouched; they already propagate the ValueError before any write (status exit 1 with empty stdout; packet before staging; source batches before `_batch_write`; custody keeps its named gap).

### VERIFY-1 finding (spec claim differed from main)
The spec says empty under-cap files "retain unreadable-ledger errors". On main, a 0-byte ledger actually hits `sqlite3.Connection.deserialize(b"")` -> raw `MemoryError` (traceback). I added an `if not raw: raise OSError` so an empty file gets the existing "not a readable ledger" refusal. This is inside `ledger_list.py` (owned) and needed for the spec'd behaviour.

### Tests (all synthetic)
- `tests/test_status_list.py`: exact-cap success / cap+1 refusal with `fdopen` and `sqlite3.connect` never called; empty and malformed under-cap files keep the generic error; growth after a genuine `fstat` (file appended inside the wrapped fstat) -> single `read(size+1)` returning `size+1`, handles and fds closed, no SQLite; real CLI on a sparse 64 MiB+1 file (exit 1, exact stopped text, empty stdout, size/mode/mtime/dir entries unchanged); sidecar precedence and symlink refusal preserved.
- `tests/test_finding_packet.py`, `tests/test_sources_add_batch.py`, `tests/test_sources_add_from_request.py`: oversize ledger refused with no target/staging (packet, also via CLI on sparse file), sources.json and ledger mode/mtime/bytes unchanged including dry run.
- RED check: with only the constants added (old reader), the 7 new tests fail; with the fix, 58 tests across the four modules pass.
- `docs/RECORDS-INTAKE.md`: one additive paragraph under "Listing ingested receipts".

No outside-owned files, no pins/digests changed. Not changed: findings-guide date failures on main (pre-existing, per spec).

PREPUSH-TESTS PASS repo=DeFlock-Campaign-Tool head=822e6df5913d526668551968b58e48cb0c0902b0 base=9289b168f093365d493b6bd43149de014628e167 (4 narrowed shards PREEXISTING failures compared with main). `node scripts/scan-secrets.mjs` PASS.

Acceptance command: `python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_status_list tests.test_sources_add_batch tests.test_sources_add_from_request tests.test_finding_packet -q` -> `Ran 58 tests ... OK`.

author: laserkelvin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013-->
# ALCHEMI Toolkit-Ops Pull Request

## Description

The nightly `CI` workflow failed on `main` on every run since 2026-09-21. This PR fixes four root causes found while triaging those failures. It is a draft so that CI can run the full suite: please add the `ciflow:all` label.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] CI/CD or infrastructure change

## Related Issues

Relates to the nightly `CI` failures on `main` (for example run 42576641740).

## Changes Made

- `fix(dynamics)`: in `batch_idx` mode, `remove_com_motion` and `remove_com_motion_out` launched the COM kernel with `dim=num_systems`. That value defaults to 1, and `initialize_velocities` passes it through unchanged. Systems after the first then subtracted stale values from `com_velocities`. The launch now uses `com_velocities.shape[0]`. This caused `test_initialize_velocities_different_temps[vec3d-float64-float64-cuda:0]` to fail on every job: the measured T was 2.705 for a target of 2.0. When the L-BFGS tests from #166 run first, they leave that memory dirty and the test fails. Run alone, it passes. The test tolerance is now six standard deviations of the temperature estimate, and a new regression test fills the scratch array before the call.
- `test(jax)`: `test_jitted_reference_setup_rejects_invalid_input` triggers an expected error in an ordered `io_callback`. On GPU, jax 0.10 keeps the failed effect token, so later barriers, the conftest GPU cleanup, and the atexit hook re-raise `JaxRuntimeError: INTERNAL: CpuCallback error calling callback`. The test input now lives on the CPU device. Upstream jax fixed the token handling in jax-ml/jax#41109 (jax 0.12.0).
- `test(neighbors)`: `test_cluster_tile_tile_fullgraph_explicit_capacity` compared the tile lists from eager and compiled calls in order. The kernel appends tiles through `wp.atomic_add`, so the order depends on block scheduling. The test now compares the active tiles as a set, as the batched test already does. It failed in 3 of 79 CI jobs in the logs checked.
- `fix(torch)`: `scoped_warp_stream` is now decorated with `torch.compiler.disable`. When a compiled call falls back to eager inside a trace, Dynamo builds `wp.Stream` objects without running `__init__`, and Warp's `Stream.__del__` raises `AttributeError: 'Stream' object has no attribute 'cuda_stream'`. This change stops that warning.

## Known failures this PR does not fix

`make test-full` stops at the first failing group, so the groups after `dynamics` have not run on `main` since the 0.5.0 rc. In local runs, two more failures show up. CI on this PR will show whether they also fail there.

- `test/torch/test_warp_boundary_audit.py::test_raw_warp_setup_is_boundary_or_classified` fails from c1fa79a (#170). The new raw Warp setup in the cluster-tile and electrostatics modules is not in `APPROVED_RAW_WARP_FUNCTIONS`.
- About 40 electrostatics tests fail from 80b7492 (0.5.0 rc), in `test_multipole_kernels.py::TestMonopoleCollapse`, `test_factory.py::TestFactoryEnergyParity`, and `test_factory_ewald_recip.py`. The errors are about 2e-8 against `atol=1e-15` or exact-equality checks. They fail on both CPU and GPU.

These need a decision from the module owners, so they are out of scope here.

## Testing

Targeted tests were run locally on a CUDA 13 GPU and on CPU:

- `pytest test/dynamics --slow`: 1076 passed. No `CpuCallback` error at cleanup or exit.
- The velocity test, run after the jax L-BFGS file 50 times in one process: 50 of 50 passed. Before the fix it failed every time in that order.
- `pytest test/neighbors/bindings/torch --slow -W error::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning`: 2543 passed. The one failure, `test_qr_height_certificate_sheared_translated_pair[...-rotated]`, also fails on `main` locally and passes in CI, so it looks specific to this machine.

- [ ] Unit tests pass locally (`make pytest`)
- [x] Linting passes (`make lint`), checked with pre-commit on the changed files
- [x] New tests added for new functionality meets coverage expectations?

author: lucas-flatwhite
body:
Rebased onto `main` now that #36 is in.

## What this adds

People who scan the QR on my card land on `/hi/`. Before they reach the board, they get a short intro to play with:

1. **The card drops in.** My card falls onto the screen and rests at a slight tilt, under "Lucas just handed you his card." It lands only once the type has loaded.
2. **The card flips.** A tap flips it over to "Nice to meet you." The back has two buttons:
   - **Wave back at Lucas** turns the screen yellow with a waving hand and "Hi, Lucas!", for them to show me. The hand is Phosphor's `hand-waving`, filled, rather than an emoji that draws differently on every phone. A tap goes back to the card.
   - **Open the board** unfolds the card into the homepage.
3. **The card unfolds into the board.** The real board has been under the intro all along, so nothing loads and nothing navigates:
   - The card stands straight, and its QR, address, role and dot step back.
   - A sheet of paper opens out from the card to the screen with `clip-path`.
   - The board's own handle, name and Korean name travel from their places on the card (FLIP).
   - The rest of the board rises in.
   - The address becomes `/`, focus moves to my name, and the name swap and the moving pictures start.
4. **Skip** is always there. It is a real link home, so it works even before the intro's script arrives. Once the script has loaded, Skip unfolds the card instead.

**Guards:**
- An inline script marks `<html>` before the board is parsed, so the board never flashes first. Without scripts, only the board shows.
- While the intro is up, the board is `inert`, and neither ⌘K nor `#card` opens anything.
- Under reduced motion, the card lands without dropping, flips at once, and the board fades in over 0.2s.
- While the name travels, the board clips its overflow, so a phone does not zoom out mid-unfold.
- As soon as the board is parsed, an inline script makes it `inert`. A slow intro script therefore never leaves the hidden board's links in the Tab order. Before this, with the scripts 3s late, 15 of 20 Tab stops landed on the hidden board; now none do.
- `/hi/#book` no longer opens the book over the intro, the same way `#card` and ⌘K already wait.

## Checked

- `npx vitest run`: 213 tests pass. `npx astro check`: 0 errors. `npm run build` passes.
- In Chrome:
  - I recorded frames of the unfold at 390×844 (from the back) and 1440×900 (Skip from the front). The name keeps its size at the swap.
  - The end state is `/`, with focus on `#name` and nothing left over.
  - Reduced motion shows the board after about 0.25s.
- With JS off, `/hi/` is the plain board.
- With the scripts blocked, Skip lands on `/` with the board showing.
- With the scripts 3s late, no Tab stop lands on the hidden board. `/hi/#book` keeps the book shut. `/#book` and the book card still open it after the unfold.

## To check on the preview, from a real scan

- [ ] The intro in iPhone Safari, Android Chrome and the KakaoTalk in-app browser
- [ ] The drop and the unfold look smooth on the slowest phone at hand
- [ ] Skip from the front, the back and the wave screen
- [ ] A reload in the middle of the intro shows it again
- [ ] Back after the unfold leaves the site
- [ ] The Card button works after the unfold
- [ ] `/hi/` on a slow connection: Skip works at once

body:
## Summary
- `PUSH_PROVEEDOR=fcm` now sends real push notifications through Firebase Cloud Messaging. Until now `FcmNotificadorAdapter` was a skeleton that threw `NoImplementadoException`, so HU 8.3 ("el sistema debe enviar una notificación push al dispositivo del usuario") was not met.
- The console provider stays the default, so CI and local runs without credentials behave exactly as before.
- The service-account key never enters git or the image. Local docker gets it through an opt-in overlay.

Merge this before the app PR (Walturx/CrowdRadar-FrontEnd, `feat/push-fcm`).

## Approach and discarded options
**Chosen: Firebase Cloud Messaging (free on the Spark plan, no card).** The backend was already designed for it: the `dispositivo_push.token_fcm` column, the `ClienteFcm` interface and the invalid-token cleanup. Only the client was missing.

Discarded:
- **OneSignal / Pusher Beams.** On Android they still need our own Firebase project credentials.
- **Pushy.** Works without FCM, but means a new adapter and changing the `token_fcm` semantics and the diagrams.
- **UnifiedPush / ntfy.** Every user would have to install a second app.
- **Local notifications only.** Not a push: nothing arrives with the app closed.

## Changes
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/adapter/push/impl/FirebaseAdminClienteFcmAdapter.ts` | New `ClienteFcm`. It loads `firebase-admin` lazily on the first send, reads the key at that point (a bad file gives a Spanish error that never echoes its content), uses a named app `crowdradar-push` and calls `sendEachForMulticast` in batches of 500 with `android.priority: 'high'` and `data.lugarId` |
| `src/adapter/push/impl/FcmNotificadorAdapter.ts` | Uses the real client when FCM is on. Still refuses to send when FCM is off |
| `src/adapter/push/NotificadorPush.ts`, `src/container/favoritoAlerta.ts` | Doc comments |
| `package.json`, `package-lock.json` | `firebase-admin` ^14.5.0 (lock kept CRLF) |
| `docker-compose.fcm.yml` | New opt-in overlay. It mounts `./firebase-crowdradar-sa.json` read-only and sets `PUSH_PROVEEDOR=fcm`. The base compose is untouched |
| `test/adapter/FirebaseAdminClienteFcm.unit.test.ts` | New, 15 cases: payload, per-token mapping, 500 chunking, lazy load, unreadable key |
| `test/adapter/FcmNotificadorAdapter.unit.test.ts`, `test/favoritoAlerta/*.unit.test.ts` | The skeleton assertions now expect the real client. Console mode is proven never to load `firebase-admin` |
| `README.md` | Push section, env table, overlay command, Render secret file |

The file is named `...Adapter.ts` because convention test R2-401 requires that suffix under `src/adapter/**/impl`.

## How to run it locally
```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.fcm.yml up -d --build
```
The key `firebase-crowdradar-sa.json` goes in the repo root. It is ignored by `.gitignore` (`firebase-*.json`) and `.dockerignore`.

## Verification
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`: pass.
- `npm test`: 2050 passed, 234 skipped (baseline 2034).
- Independent verifier: no blockers. It ran the real `firebase-admin` 14.5.0 offline with only `sendEachForMulticast` replaced: 1001 tokens went out as 500 + 500 + 1, one named app, no double init. Console mode still works with `firebase-admin` removed from `node_modules`.
- Native review (risk, resilience, reliability): approved.
- E2E on an Android emulator with Google Play: a favorite place changed from "Sin información" to "Saturado", the phone showed "Parque de la Exposición · Ahora está Saturado (antes: Sin información).", and the tap opened the place.

## Known limitations
- iOS: there is no APNs key (it needs a paid Apple Developer account), so iOS receives no push.
- The app re-registers its token on every launch with a session, but not on an FCM token refresh while it is running.

author: brunogutierre
body:
## Summary

Adds the runtime theming API: `provideTessera()`, the `TesseraTheme` service, the `tesTheme` scope directive and injectable built-in labels. Stacked on #2.

## Changes

- `TesseraTheme` (root service):
  - `theme` and `mode` are writable signals; `resolvedMode` resolves `system` through `prefers-color-scheme`.
  - An `effect` writes `data-tes-theme` / `data-tes-mode` on `<html>`.
  - The `matchMedia` listener is removed on destroy, and the service is SSR-safe.
- `provideTessera({ theme, mode, labels })`: environment providers. An environment initializer applies the theme at startup even if nothing injects the service.
- `TesThemeScope` (`[tesTheme]`, optional `tesMode`) for subtrees.
- `TES_LABELS` / `DEFAULT_LABELS` / `TesLabels`: every built-in string, English by default. Strings that contain numbers are functions (`pageRange`, `remove`).
- 11 unit tests, plus README usage and decisions.

## Decisions

- **Initial value precedence:**
  1. explicit config;
  2. attributes already in `index.html` (no flash of the wrong theme);
  3. `enterprise` + `system`.
- **The service only writes attributes; CSS does the theming.** A theme switch costs no change detection in components.
- **`EnvironmentProviders`, so `provideTessera()` cannot be misused in component providers.**
- **Dialogs and toasts follow the page theme; anchored popovers keep the scoped theme.** This is documented on the directive.

## How to test

```bash
npm test   # theme.spec.ts
```

author: moreih29
body:
## Problem

The line under a chat tab's composer (context, session and week usage, profile) hid its details at fixed container-query widths. Those widths counted neither the profile chip, nor the number of meters, nor the language, so:

- With a longer profile name ("Personal") the line overflowed just above each width (584–600, 520–532, 392–416, 328–352, 264–276px and below 220px) and was cut off on the right.
- It hid the week's reset time before the session's, even with the week at 98% and the session at 0%.

## Fix

The line measures itself and takes only as many steps as it needs to fit on one line. `usageViews` in `services/chat/usage-line.ts` lists the steps, most detailed first:

1. The token counts go.
2. The reset times of meters below 80% go.
3. The words shorten: the context keeps its ring, "현재 세션"/"이번 주" become "세션"/"주간", and reset times become "↺ 목 09:59".
4. The bars go.
5. The profile chip keeps its dot; its name moves to the tooltip.
6. Meters below 80% are counted ("+1") instead of shown.
7. The context is counted too, while some meter is near its limit.
8. Last, the reset times of meters near their limit go.

A step that would show the same as the one before is skipped. A context at 80% or more, or one with nothing near its limit, is never hidden. Hovering "+N" lists what it hides.

The composer's fitting hook moved to `hooks/use-fit-step.ts` so both rows share it. It takes the next step on each render that overflows, before paint, and starts over on a new width or new content. `UsageLineView`'s `trailing` is now a render prop, so the profile chip can be compact.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test tests/unit`: 2583 pass, including the new `usage-line.test.ts`. It covers the step order, the no-near-limit case, a context near its limit, and skipped duplicate steps.
- [x] `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`
- [x] Dev app at viewport widths from 1280 down to 700 (line widths 744 → 164px), on Claude tabs with the 기본 and Personal profiles and on a Codex tab: never overflows, steps follow the order above, and the "+2" and compact-chip tooltips are right.

## Problem
When a Skill tool declares a root object schema with `additionalProperties: false`, its generated Pydantic model silently ignores unknown arguments. That accepts inputs the schema explicitly forbids and drops those values before tool execution. Empty closed objects also bypass the rule because they take an early return while the model is created.
