author: chrishsu
body:
PR 3 of 4 in the run-cards stack (plan `3ef69c1d-026`, intent `run-execute`). It stacks on PR 2.

## Change
- **The `run` request does every check before anything runs:**
  - the passkey assertion over a fresh challenge for this card;
  - that the script hash it signed equals the card's hash and the stored copy's hash;
  - that the inputs are exactly the card's, one line each.
- **How it runs:** `/bin/bash --noprofile --norc <copy>`, in the card's cwd and its own process group, with only `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LANG` and `TMPDIR` in the environment.
  - Inputs go to stdin, and stdin then closes.
  - They never go in argv, the environment, a file or a log.
- **`OutputScrubber`** (`packages/core/src/run-scrub.ts`) replaces each input value with `‹NAME›` before any byte leaves the glass.
  - It covers the value's base64, base64url, URL-encoded and JSON-escaped forms too.
  - It holds back enough text to catch a value split across chunks.
- **Time limit:** the process group gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 3 s later, and the run records exit 124.
- **The run answers the card** with its exit code and duration, plus the scrubbed output's last 64 KB unless the card was posted with `--output exit`.
- **Audit:** each run appends a hash-chained line to `~/.lobstah/run/audit.jsonl` (`packages/core/src/run-audit.ts`). It holds the card, script hash, cwd, passkey, exit code and counts, and never an input or output.
- **On the card:**
  - Run asks for the passkey, starts the run and streams the scrubbed output (`run-output`).
  - The card stays on screen with its result after its run answers it.
  - The 127.0.0.1 page links to localhost to run.
  - Typed values live only in the card until Run sends them, then they're cleared.

## Criteria (intent `run-execute`)
| Criterion | Proven by (`apps/cli/test/run-execute.test.ts`) |
|---|---|
| `ach-no-trace`: a secret input is in no file under the lobstah home, not in the glass log, and not in the child's argv or environment | leaves no trace of a secret input… (reads every file under the home, captures console output, and has the script dump its own `env` and `ps` args) |
| `ach-scrub`: a value split across two chunks shows `‹NAME›` in the answer | scrubs a secret printed across two chunks, and its base64 form, from the answer; plus `packages/core/test/run-scrub.test.ts` (every cut point, byte by byte) |
| `ach-hash-refuse`: a stored copy that no longer matches gets 409 and spawns nothing | refuses to run a stored copy that no longer hashes to the card, and spawns nothing |
| `ach-exit-only`: `--output exit` answers with the exit code and no output | answers a card posted with --output exit… |
| `ach-audit`: one chained audit line per run with the card key, SHA-256 and exit code | appends one audit line per run, chained to the one before… |
| `pres-no-token-run`: a valid page token and Origin but no assertion gets 403 and spawns nothing | refuses a Run with a valid page token and Origin but no passkey assertion… (a missing and a forged assertion both get 403) |
| `pres-timeout`: past its time limit the process group is killed within 5 s, exit 124 | kills a run past its time limit, process group and all, within 5 seconds… (the script ignores SIGTERM) |

These tests run real scripts under `/bin/bash`, so they skip on Windows.

## Note
Files outside `applies-to`:
- `packages/core/src/run-scrub.ts`
- `apps/cli/src/run-routes.ts`
- `packages/glass-ui/ui/actions.ts`, `store.ts` and `components/run-card.ts`
- `packages/glass-ui/ui/glass.css`

## Screenshots
These are end to end. The real glass server ran on a temporary home at `http://localhost`, with Chromium's virtual passkey standing in for Touch ID. The macOS password dialog was stubbed for the demo; everything else is real.

| Desktop | |

| Settings after registering a passkey | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aequitas-labs/lobstah/f8c57667764dd62def1d21b24e65d21409153fc3/pr-381/run-settings-registered-desktop.png) |
| A run card with its secret typed (masked) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aequitas-labs/lobstah/f8c57667764dd62def1d21b24e65d21409153fc3/pr-381/run-card-desktop.png) |
| After Run: `CRON_SECRET` scrubbed in the output, and the card answered by its run | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aequitas-labs/lobstah/f8c57667764dd62def1d21b24e65d21409153fc3/pr-381/run-card-ran-desktop.png) |

| Phone width (interactive card) | | |

| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aequitas-labs/lobstah/f8c57667764dd62def1d21b24e65d21409153fc3/pr-381/run-card-phone.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aequitas-labs/lobstah/f8c57667764dd62def1d21b24e65d21409153fc3/pr-381/run-console-phone.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aequitas-labs/lobstah/f8c57667764dd62def1d21b24e65d21409153fc3/pr-381/run-console-done-phone.png) |

## Output wraps on phones (dispatch c33b3ca5)

The run's output rows (the exit line and the log) take `min-width: 0` alongside the card's other rows, so a long URL or JSON line wraps inside the card at 375px. The page never scrolls sideways.

body:
Fixes #197

## What was wrong

`awakener-invoke` is one-shot, and since #217 it holds the cross-process attach lock for the whole press, so the close-sweep collector `:wm` starts is never listening when a user closes a window. A closed surface's panel stood until someone ran `reap`, while `wm.repair.sweep_on_close`, `wm.dock.orphan_policy` and the `AwakenerInvokeCli` KDoc said the close event handled it. Separately, a surface that closed while `attach` waited for its dock to map still reported `dock N beside surface M` with exit 0.

## Design: option (a), sweep on every press

- **`invoke.sweep_first`** (new, default `true`): `Awakening.invoke` calls the sweep the composition root already passes in (`wm::reapOrphans`) before it acts. It already holds the attach lock, so this costs one tree read when nothing is orphaned. What gets swept still follows `wm.dock.orphan_policy` / `wm.dock.reap_evidence`, the same as `reap`.
- **The press is aimed before the sweep, not after.** That includes #221's `pressedFrom`, which is also read off focus. The orphan fills its tab, so it is usually what has focus. Sweeping it hands focus to whatever sway picks next, and a press aimed after that would stand a panel up on a window the user never pressed in. I checked this by mutation: moving the sweep above the aim makes `a press from a panel whose surface has gone is refused` fail with `Animated` where it should get `NoSurface`.
- **A failed sweep doesn't fail the press.** It is kept on `Awakening.sweepFailure` and printed as a `warning:` on stderr. Otherwise one wedged panel would break the hotkey. `reap` still raises, because there the sweep is the whole command. The cost is that a frozen orphan adds about 5.5s to every press until it is killed (the reviewer measured this). The flag description says so and names `invoke.sweep_first=false` as the way out.
- **Mid-attach close:** `attach` re-reads the tree as the last step inside its tree edit. If the surface is gone, it fails, `unwindAttach` kills the dock, and the attach's own bind does not run. The surface's identity is still minted beforehand by `Awakening`, which is existing behaviour on `main`. This is hard-coded rather than flagged because I can't see a reason anyone would want success reported for a dead surface. A close after that read is the orphan the next press sweeps.

**Why this respects "no daemon / no polling / no schedule":** nothing new runs between presses. The sweep is one synchronous tree read and repair inside a press the user just made.

**Option (b), the dock process watching for its own surface, was not built.** It could be argued in-rules, since it is the panel's own lifetime rather than an awakener process. But it would add a long-lived IPC subscriber per panel, and it would have to re-implement `orphan_policy` / `reap_evidence` outside `:wm`. That is a larger and separate design step, so I left it out.

**Text corrected:** the `wm.repair.sweep_on_close` and `wm.dock.orphan_policy` descriptions, the `AwakenerInvokeCli` KDoc ("nothing runs between presses", which includes the collector), and `docs/desktop-setup.md`.

## Tests (headless sway 1.12, `foot`, on kaladin)

Red first. Each of these failed on `origin/main` `3bf7498` with only the flag declared:
- `AwakeningSwayTest.a press takes down a panel whose surface has gone`: expected `[10]` but was `[8, 10]`, so the orphan was still standing.
- `AwakeningSwayTest.a press from a panel whose surface has gone is refused` (the existing #216 test, plus a `docks()` assertion): expected `[]` but was `[8]`.
- `SwayBindingTest.a surface that closes while its dock is mapping fails the attach`: the attach "completed successfully". The dock is delayed by `slowDock` (2s) and the surface is killed at 1s from the test's own connection, which is not behind the lock.

Control: `sweeping on every press is switchable off` passes both before and after, with the orphan standing beside the new panel.

Added in round 2, after rebasing onto `c95db69` (#221):
- `AwakeningTest.a failed sweep is kept and the press still stands its panel`, `a failed sweep fails reap`, `a press sweeps before it acts`, and `a press sweeps nothing with invoke sweep_first off`. I checked the first by breaking it: letting the sweep's exception escape the press makes it fail.
- `AwakeningSwayTest.a press from a panel acts on that panel while its sweep takes an orphan down` shows that #221's from-panel press and the sweep compose. It does **not** test the ordering: it still passes with the sweep moved above the aim, because sweeping that orphan doesn't move focus. The ordering is held by `a press from a panel whose surface has gone is refused`, which fails (`Animated`) under that mutation. I re-measured this after the rebase.
- The stderr line itself is wired in `main` and has no process-level test. The reviewer verified it live through the launcher.

Green, at head `a4f0520` on `origin/main` `c95db69`: `AWAKENER_REQUIRE_SWAY=1 AWAKENER_REQUIRE_SPANREED=1 JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk ./gradlew clean build --no-build-cache` gave BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m16s. Counts read from `*/build/test-results/jvmTest/*.xml` (results dirs deleted first): **640 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failures, 0 errors**, split cli 120 / config 74 / connector 76 / registry 166 / wm 204. `.github/scripts/check-staleness.sh` → `current`.

`Awakening.invoke`'s surface-resolution block was restructured (aim, then sweep, then refuse), now on top of #221's `pressedFrom`.

author: michaelportale
body:
Phase 8 of the native iPhone app: a read-only WHOOP card on Progress, served by your own server. The server does WHOOP's OAuth, token refresh, fetching and normalising; the phone reads one endpoint and never sees a WHOOP secret.

This PR touches `api/` (three new modules and the WHOOP routes), `native/`, `docs/`, `.env.example`, `docker-compose.yml`, `api/Dockerfile`, and two admin-dashboard labels in `frontend/src/lib/audit.js`. It adds no dependency anywhere; `api/` still has its existing dependency list.

## What's in it
- **`api/whoop-vault.js`.** It stores tokens per profile in `DATA_DIR/whoop-<uid>.json`:
  - encrypted with AES-256-GCM, using a key from HKDF-SHA256 over the existing `DATA_DIR/secret`;
  - written atomically, mode 0600;
  - a file that won't decrypt reads as "not connected".
- **`api/whoop-client.js`.** The token endpoint and the four v2 collections (cycle, recovery, sleep, workout):
  - one queue per profile serialises every token operation, and a rotated pair is saved before it is used;
  - `invalid_client` keeps the tokens (a wrong `WHOOP_CLIENT_SECRET` must not disconnect everyone); any other refused refresh deletes them and asks to reconnect;
  - `redirect: 'error'`, a 20 s timeout and at most 20 pages;
  - revoke always removes the local file.
- **`api/whoop-view.js`.** A pure port of the owner's dashboard `data.js`:
  - days are dated by wake date;
  - only SCORED values count;
  - null stays null;
  - a 14-day window.

  A 9,000-case differential fuzz against the dashboard's `normalize` found 0 differences.
- **Routes in `api/server.js`:**
  - `POST /api/whoop/connect-link` returns a one-use, 10-minute link.
  - `GET /api/whoop/connect` shows a confirmation page that names the profile. It can't be framed, has no script, and spends nothing.
  - `POST /api/whoop/connect` checks same-origin, spends the code, sets a `__Host-` state-binding cookie, then sends the browser to WHOOP.
  - `GET /api/whoop/callback` spends the state first and requires the same browser.
  - `GET /api/whoop` keeps a 10-minute cache per profile. After a failure it waits 60 s before asking WHOOP again and serves the last good data marked stale.
  - `POST /api/whoop/disconnect` revokes at WHOOP and deletes the local file even if WHOOP is down.
  - Connect and disconnect are written to the audit log as `auth.whoop.connect` and `auth.whoop.disconnect`, with dashboard labels. An admin profile delete also revokes WHOOP.
  - `WHOOP_BASE_URL` (a test hook) is honoured on loopback only.
- **Phone (`native/src/whoop/`):**
  - `whoop-view.js` is the pure card model: unpaired, not set up, not connected, nothing scored, stale "as of", error with last data kept, and connected (today's recovery, HRV, resting HR and strain; a 7-day recovery chart; the last 5 cardio workouts).
  - `whoop-source.js` holds the pure read logic. A good read is held until the server's copy is 10 minutes old, a failure waits a minute, and "not set up" or "not connected" is asked again on every visit.
  - `whoop-cache.js` keeps one cached row, keyed by server and profile id. The sync engine clears it in `pair()` and `forget()`.
  - `WhoopCard.js`: Connect opens the link in Safari after checking its origin matches the paired address; Disconnect asks first.
- **Docs:**
  - `SELF_HOSTING.md` section 8 "WHOOP (optional)": register the app, set the env vars, connect, and a troubleshooting table;
  - `.env.example` and `docker-compose.yml` gain `WHOOP_CLIENT_ID` and `WHOOP_CLIENT_SECRET`;
  - `openapi.yaml` covers the six routes;
  - the device checklist gains WHOOP rows;
  - PRD row 8.

## Verification
**Local test runs** (Actions are off on the fork, so these are the gate):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `api` | 743/743 |
| `native` | 2301/2301 |
| `native` contract test (real API) | 26/26 |
| `npm run check:shared` | clean |
| `frontend` | 5793/5793 (it includes the audit-label guard that reads `api/server.js`) |
| `mcp` | 100/100 |

The fake WHOOP (`api/test/fake-whoop.mjs`) covers:
- token rotation and concurrent refreshes;
- a 401, then a refresh, then a retry;
- `invalid_client` at 400 and at 401;
- paging, 429 and 5xx serving stale data;
- misused state and code;
- the browser-bound cookie;
- a wrong secret reading as not connected;
- a vault-write failure.

Leak scans check every response, log line and the audit log for tokens, codes and the client secret.

**Reviews:**
- Six tasks, each with its own review and fix rounds. Token rotation, the routes and the phone source were reviewed on the most capable model. Bugs the reviews caught and fixed:
  - `invalid_client` arriving as a 400 would have deleted every profile's tokens.
  - A connect link could be used to phish a profile. It is now closed by the confirmation page and the browser-bound state.
  - The phone's cached card outlived its pairing, and could show server A's numbers with a live Disconnect acting on server B.
- **Final whole-branch review** (most capable model): no critical findings and one important one. The phone's 10-minute throttle held failed and not-connected reads, which broke three device-checklist rows. A differential fuzz of 9,000 random data sets against the dashboard's own `normalize` found 0 differences.
- **One fix wave:**
  - the throttle;
  - the callback failure page;
  - a retry wait after any failure;
  - the GCM tag length;
  - cookie expiry;
  - the pairing read;
  - audit events;
  - troubleshooting docs.

  Its scoped re-review found every finding addressed, plus two minor issues that were also fixed: a failure line wiped by the now more frequent re-reads, and a no-op disconnect being audited.

**Ponytail review:** its verdict was Ship. I fixed its three should-fix items and one can-wait item before merging:
- **Disconnect waited too briefly.** The phone gave up after 15 s, but the server's revoke can take about 80 s against a hung WHOOP. The phone then said "Couldn't disconnect" after the tokens were already gone, and a second tap hid the advice to revoke in the WHOOP app. Disconnect now gets 120 s; every other call keeps 15 s. A fake-timer test covers both.
- **The two troubleshooting rows** now name a wrong or rotated `WHOOP_CLIENT_SECRET`.
- **The checklist's "Couldn't open WHOOP's sign-in" causes** were corrected.
- **The setup row** now says `docker compose up -d --build`.

The scoped re-check said Ship (fb2dac726..3af6351e9).

**Simulator** (Release build; a local `api/server.js` talking to a fake WHOOP behind a loopback stub; no real WHOOP call):
- The connected card matches the seeded data:
  - 67% recovery, 56 ms HRV, 52 bpm resting HR, 12.3 strain;
  - the 7-day chart skips the unscored day;
  - five cardio rows, newest first, with dashes for the unscored workout.
- Disconnect asks first, then the card shows "Connect WHOOP".
- Connect runs end to end: Safari opens the confirmation page naming the profile, Continue goes through the stub sign-in to "WHOOP is connected", and back in the app the card fills on return. The browser-binding cookie works in Safari.
- Paired at an address other than `ORIGIN`, Connect says so ("Connect works when this phone is paired with localhost:3917. …").
  - That line survives a tab switch and a Sync now.
  - Once the profile is connected, the next tab switch shows the card at once and the line clears.

## Owner steps (not done here)
1. Register a separate openGym app in WHOOP's developer dashboard with the redirect `https://<your host>/api/whoop/callback` and the scopes `read:recovery read:cycles read:sleep read:workout offline`.
2. Put `WHOOP_CLIENT_ID` and `WHOOP_CLIENT_SECRET` in `.env`, then run `docker compose up -d`.
3. On the phone, paired at your server's `ORIGIN`, go to Progress, then WHOOP, then Connect. Finish the WHOOP sign-in in the same Safari, then go back to the app.
4. Run the checklist's WHOOP rows: today's recovery and strain and the recent cardio against the WHOOP app, Offline, then Disconnect and reconnect.

## Known limitations
- A real WHO

author: pedrobtz
body:
Closes #238, the `mutation` gap in `.agents/assurance.md` (#260).

**Why:** mutation testing lists the statements no check notices. In the 2026-11-09 reviews, 14 of the 16 bugs were in code the suite ran and didn't check, which is exactly what surviving mutants show. Mull re-parses every file from its recorded command line, and `zuh_ctest` compiled all 46 sources in one command.

**What changes:**
- **`ctest/Makefile`:**
  - `zuh_ctest` links one object per source, under `build/own/`, each from its own compile command, with header dependencies (`-MMD -MP`). Before this, a header change didn't rebuild anything.
  - A stamp records the `CC` and `CFLAGS` that built the objects, and every object is rebuilt when they change. Without it, `tools/coverage/ctest-lcov.sh` or Mull, which pass their own `CC`, could link a plain build's objects and report nothing, without any error.
  - `strict` and `asan` behave as before.
- **`.github/workflows/mutation.yaml`:** calls r-actions' `mutation.yml` (v1.32.0) over `src/zuh_*.c`, excluding vendored code, against `ctest/zuh_ctest`. It runs weekly, on dispatch, and on a pull request that changes `ctest/Makefile` or the caller. It reports and never gates.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** the command to run it.

**Checked locally:**
- `make -C ctest strict` and `asan`: 2901 checks each, 0 failures.
- Rebuild behaviour:
  - the same flags rebuild 0 objects;
  - a new `CC` rebuilds all 46;
  - touching `zuh_body.h` rebuilds only the files that include it;
  - `strict` after `clean` works.
- `tools/coverage/ctest-lcov.sh` writes lcov for all 32 files.
- `make -C fuzz replay-run` and `tools/check-code-lines` pass.

This pull request's own `mutation` run is the first time Mull meets this build, so it's the check that matters. A single `zuh_ctest` run takes 2.5 s.

**Found along the way, not fixed here:** `make asan` puts the vendored objects in `build/`, not `build-asan/`. `BUILD := build$(BUILD_SUFFIX)` is expanded when the Makefile is parsed, before the target-specific `BUILD_SUFFIX` applies, so ASan builds reuse uninstrumented vendored objects. It's filed as an issue.

body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] New numerical APIs and kernel changes follow the [determinism skill](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/skills/determinism_tests/SKILL.md): add/run L0 forward/backward checks and update [API support](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/docs/operations/determinism.md), with unsupported or unverified paths stated. Golden changes include a numerical reason and independent reference results (see [coverage](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/test/python/determinism_goldens/README.md)).
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

Move the host side of the QSA backward out of `kernels/bprop_sm100.py` into `QSA/_backward.py`, as `QSA/_forward.py` does for the forward.

- No functional change: kernels, plans and outputs match develop. Only the import path of the host-side functions moves to `cudnn.QSA._backward`.
- `QSA/_backward.py` holds `LaunchPlan`, `plan_for`, `compile_kernels`, `launch`, `backward`, the sequence modes and the host-side constants, moved verbatim.
- The SM107 dispatch and the compiled cache key (digests of both kernel files) live there, so `bprop_sm100.py` and `bprop_sm107.py` are peer kernel files.
- Callers import `cudnn.QSA._backward`: `QSA/api.py`, `QSA/indexed/api.py`, the QSA tests, `benchmark/qsa`, docs and the tracker row.

## Why

- `kernels/bprop_sm100.py` mixed the SM100 kernels with the launch sequence of every architecture, SM107 dispatch included.

## Related issues

- Follow-up to #2364.

## API and compatibility impact

- No public API change. Code outside this repo that imports the host-side functions from `cudnn.QSA.kernels.bprop_sm100` must import them from `cudnn.QSA._backward`.
- The compiled cache key changes, so the backward kernels compile once more.

## Testing

- The moved code matches develop except four import and cache-key lines.
- `LaunchPlan` fields and workspace sizes match develop over 1008 plans (lengths, head layouts, sequence modes, dS precisions, SM counts, SM107 dispatch).
- The sm_107a PTX of all 12 SM107 configurations is byte-identical to develop.
- `pytest test/python/QSA -m "L0 or L1"` on SM107 (DSL 4.8.0, CUDA 13 build): 287 passed, 16 skipped.
- Same suite on SM100 (DSL 4.8.0): 244 passed, 1 failed, `test_neighbor_isolation[bprop]`, the same failure as develop.

author: ken-jo
body:
**Blocked draft — implementation stopped under the owner's explicit deny-semantics stop condition. Do not land.**

## Owner resume rule (2026-11-10)

Transient restore and recovery never remove a deny that the pre-change code retained, including a moved target found by file ID. Only explicit durable retirement removes one: list change, sandbox disable or uninstall. This rule applies when work resumes. This PR stays a draft while the object-only parent guard is delivered separately.

## Blocking findings

Source review confirmed that ordinary transient restore/recovery now changes moved-deny semantics after a persistent principal marker exists. Minimal path: initialize durable state, transient-stamp T, owner moves T to M, then normal restore journals the removed hold, locates M by file ID and removes its deny. The original mismatch path deliberately retained moved denies. `journal_holder_change` / `apply_pending` bypass that old branch for ordinary release and orphan recovery. This is outside the authority to retire explicitly unlisted durable targets. No old writer or principal migration is needed to trigger it. This finding is based on the concrete source call path, not a newly executed native reproducer.

Preserving the original behavior requires distinguishing explicit durable retirement from ordinary transient release/recovery before identity relocation. That design has not been implemented or approved. Work stopped as requested; no merge or ready-for-review transition was made.

The final Windows helper build and native tests passed, but the subsequent platform permission suite failed **23 cases** after deleted-object recovery used an unsupported ExtendedFileId descriptor on NTFS (`0x80070057`), causing recovery/release cascades. A checked filesystem-specific lookup correction was being prepared off-tree when work stopped; it is not in this PR.

## Motivation and scope

#545 removes boot waiting but does not shorten parent-subtree ACL propagation. This retains completed base deny stamps between sessions and makes parent deletion guards object-only while keeping the same protected targets and permission decisions.

- Persist the complete base set under owner `ave`, including empty sets. Reconcile principal and resolved target/parent identities; unchanged completed protection performs no target ACL writes. Changed sets apply the effective delta while live sessions retain their obligations. Completed physical-format proof must cover the requested deny strength; opaque working labels are insufficient.
- Journal effects before mutation and keep failed work retryable. Recovery preserves completed durable denies. A separate tree-write intent repairs descendants only when an inheritable write began. Live or unverifiable older-format holders refuse mutation before effects; close older hosts before upgrade/recovery.
- Port [#523](https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/pull/523): parent FILE_DELETE_CHILD guards are object-only, and full denies include inheritable FILE_DELETE_CHILD. Local writes preserve exact controls. Full subtree writes use an identity-verified, no-follow security handle and retain owner/unrelated ACEs and protection mode.
- Emit debug target JSON `{path,parent,kind}` before stamping and `elapsedMs` afterward. Keep the actual account profile from `userInfo().homedir` as an independent credential-protection anchor. Isolated HOME/USERPROFILE do not replace the account identity; four synthetic profile regressions establish this intended behavior.

A real Windows matrix isolated the propagation bug: on both NTFS volumes, all 18 cases with the extra MAXIMUM_ALLOWED handle held suppressed child inheritance; all 18 cases with it released propagated correctly, across three APIs and three flag combinations. The final fix drops only that extra handle after the narrower tree handle matches the original file identity, before reread/journal/effect. The verified tree handle remains open throughout. Existing kernel denial, sibling, owner-access and crash-recovery assertions remain intact.

The current upstream local descriptor writer preserves control bits via GetSecurityInfo/SetKernelObjectSecurity. [API guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-setkernelobjectsecurity) recommends filesystem-specific APIs for files; this bounded port follows the current reference to retain exact local controls, while descendant writes use [SetSecurityInfo](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/aclapi/nf-aclapi-setsecurityinfo). File full-deny presence accepts Windows-normalized non-inheriting file ACEs; directories still require OICI, with exact SID and full deny-mask checks in both cases.

## Source build and teardown

The pin remains **0.0.80** after reading both npm distributions and native sources. [0.0.82's retained grants](https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/v0.0.82/README.md#the-child-token-and-kept-write-grants) are coupled to a different restricted-token/capability model, which would expand permission scope. This patch retains the existing model.

The npm package lacks Rust sources. Windows builds verify an immutable source archive and native patch hash, build x64/arm64 with the pinned toolchain, and embed exact binary receipts in the host bundle. Runtime/packaging reject missing, stale or mismatched receipts. Mutable sidecars cannot establish trust. Atomic publication breaks package-cache hardlinks; verified upstream input is retained only for builds and omitted from installers.

Normal reset/exit releases live holds and grants while retaining durable base protection. Turning both confinement scopes off removes durable ownership on the next boot. `acl forget-denies --persistent-owner ave --json` provides explicit teardown; `acl recover --json` completes pending work without disabling durable protection. Uninstall cleans durable owners before deleting the verifiable account. Live/unverifiable holders refuse account-removing uninstall. Canceled elevation changes nothing; cross-account elevation refuses before effects and requires original-account cleanup first.

Permission decision order, target selection, materialization, profile-child projection and default-deny behavior are unchanged. Only the dedicated sandbox principal's managed entries change. A changed identity with a live old hold refuses; retired-account allows use identity-bound retry state, while conservative denies on the absent principal may remain.

## Risk and validation

Initial full-target stamping and one-time legacy descendant cleanup can still be expensive. The existing 60-second budget is unchanged. A crash between full subtree writing and local control restoration can lose historical AUTO_INHERITED provenance; the explicit protection mode remains preserved. No real-host timing improvement is claimed.

- Targeted permission/boot/profile consumers: **297 passed**, 252 existing platform-gated cases not executed on macOS. Final affected host tests: **29 passed**, 17 existing Windows-only skips.
- Required packaging/script lock command: **1767 passed**, 19 existing skips across 88 files after affected failures were fixed and rechecked. `node --import ./scripts/lib/document-consumer-guard.mjs --test test/scripts/*.test.mjs`: **145 passed**, including 23 build-integrity cases.
- Production typecheck passed; test-typecheck baseline held. Final normal pre-push **global-input passed**, all 10 lock suites, **2982 passed / 20 existing skips** across 118 files. No hook bypass, new skip, retry configuration, timeout increase or relaxed product assertion.
- **57 added native regressions** compile for the Windows target; check, Clippy -D warnings and formatting passed. Windows-target checking used host SQLite metadata only, not native linking/execution.

## Salgsmotor
- **Natt (01–05):** finner AS i hele Norge i Enhetsregisteret (de 12 bransjene fra lead-finneren), men bare de som har rolleadresse (post@, firmapost@ …). Firmaer med nettside får egen demo-sekretær (lever 60 dager). Grok skriver fire e-poster per firma (dag 0, 4, 9, 14).
- **Hverdager 08–16:** sender `SALG_PER_DAG` nye firmaer (standard 30, maks 50) og forfalte oppfølginger. Sperrelisten sjekkes rett før hver e-post. Kl. 16 får Preben en oversikt.
- **Lovkrav:** bare AS og bare rolleadresser. Avsender med org.nr, avmeldingslenke `/avmeld` (HMAC) og `List-Unsubscribe` med ett-klikk. Den som melder seg av, sperres for godt.

## Svaragent
- Leser svar via Cloudflare Email Routing (`svar@orvelo.no` → workerens `email()`). Til det er satt opp, kan Preben lime inn svar fra Gmail på /drift.
- Sorterer svaret som interessert, spørsmål, nei, avmeld eller autosvar.
- Svarer selv ut fra faste fakta (`SALG_FAKTA`): pakker, priser, prøveperiode, binding, demo og booking. Den lover aldri telefonsvar, rabatt eller egne priser, og sender svaret i samme tråd med kopi til Preben.
- Nei og avmeld settes på sperrelisten. Autosvar lar sekvensen fortsette.

## Fanen «Salgsmotor» på /drift
- Status og tall, pause og antall per dag.
- Alle fire e-poster per firma, «send test til meg» og samtalen med kunden.
- Merke firmaet som svart, møte, kunde eller stopp, lime inn svar og fylle sperrelisten.

- `RESEND_API_KEY` må være satt, og domenet i `SALG_FRA` (standard `preben@orvelo.no`) må være godkjent i Resend. Til da finner og skriver motoren, men sender ingenting.
- Svar rett til agenten krever Email Routing på orvelo.no og `SALG_SVAR_TIL = svar@orvelo.no`.
- `SALG_AV = ja` slår alt av.

- `node tools/test-salgsmotor.mjs`: 43 sjekker OK, alt etterlignet. Testen dekker MIME/quoted-printable, sitattekst, løkkevern og grensen på 3 svar.

author: shiuh-yaw
body:
## What this does
On the next deploy of the `admin` service, the seed runs once. `SEED_ON_DEPLOY=true` and `APPROVE_STARTER_RECOMMENDATIONS=true` are already set on Railway. It will:
1. **Add 11 real products** sold in Malaysia, covering all 7 supplements, and **remove the sample products** for each supplement that now has a real one.
2. **Approve the 11 pending starter recommendations.** The owner asked for this. Each approval is written to the audit log under the owner's account with the note *"Approved on the owner's instruction … Not yet reviewed by a qualified professional."*
3. **Set vitamin D3 to 1,000 IU a day**, the most Malaysia's NPRA allows in a health supplement. This only changes the live value if it is still the original starter value.

Every step is idempotent, never overwrites backoffice edits, and is recorded in the audit log.

## Catalog (researched 2026-11-10)
| Supplement | Products |
|---|---|
| Protein | ON Gold Standard 100% Whey 5 lb; ON Gold Standard Plant Protein 480 g (vegan) |
| Creatine | Myprotein Impact Creatine Monohydrate 250 g |
| Vitamin D | Blackmores D3 1000 IU (halal, JAKIM); Vitalita D3 1000 IU (vegan, from algae) |
| Omega-3 | Blackmores Omega-3 Fish Oil 1000 mg (300 mg EPA+DHA; halal, JAKIM) |
| B12 | Nature's Bounty 500 µg; LAC 600 µg (only high-strength B12 is sold in Malaysia) |
| Iron | Mega Ferrovit (53 mg iron, plus folic acid and B12) |
| Electrolytes | SiS GO Hydro tablets (sugar-free, Informed Sport); Aspen JusteLyte sachets (with sugar) |

How the data was checked:
- Facts come from retailer and brand pages via search results; the marketplaces themselves couldn't be opened from the build environment.
- Halal, third-party testing and vegan status are marked only where a named certifier or an explicit statement was found. Everything else is left unconfirmed.
- Each product's notes list its sources and caveats. **Prices should be re-checked** in the backoffice; some were sale prices.
- Left out because the data couldn't be verified: whey isolates, Informed Sport-certified creatine in Malaysia, and vegan algae omega-3.

## Engine changes
- **Whole capsules and tablets:** they're counted in whole units, e.g. "1–2 capsules", never "1½".
- **Strong products:** where one serving already covers the dose, it shows 1 serving with a note when that's more than needed. Products over twice the dose are left out, except B12, which has no upper limit.
- **Wording:** a product is described as "not confirmed vegan / halal" instead of "not vegan / halal".
- **Backoffice:** serving weight is now optional for capsules and tablets, and still required for powders.

## Testing
- 56 engine tests and 20 web tests pass. Typecheck and production builds pass.
- Seed run locally against a database in the production state (old vitamin D dose, samples, rules pending):
  - 11 products added, 13 samples removed, vitamin D corrected, 11 rules approved with audit entries.
  - Re-running changes nothing.
- Recommendations checked against the real catalog for a vegan woman with low vitamin D and ferritin, and a halal-only endurance runner.

## Known gaps after this
- **Vegan and halal users see fewer products.** Wherever vegan or halal status wasn't confirmed, the product is hidden from those users. For example, vegans get no creatine, B12 or iron product, and halal users get no protein or electrolytes. Confirming it from the actual labels in the backoffice will make those products appear.
- **Outside Malaysia:** products only have Malaysian prices, so users in other countries will see "not sold in your country".

## After deploying
Set `SEED_ON_DEPLOY=false` and `APPROVE_STARTER_RECOMMENDATIONS=false` on the `admin` service.

author: phillipbritain
body:
Closes #339. **No behavior change is intended.**

## Summary

The pin source and the outer pin source now have one owner, **the pin sources** (`web/src/globe/pinSources.ts`), which is added when the style loads. GlobeMap tells it what changed and reads back what it needs:

```diff
 GlobeMap
-  addPins        → addSource ×2, pin footprint, outerPinsKey, showOuterPins
-  recluster      → setClusterOptions ×2 (pin source left alone at card zoom)
-  showPins / showOuterPins → pinsKey / outerPinsKey, hasCard + isBehindGlobe
-  select         → setFilter on 3 selected-pin layers
-  setTheme       → swap pin footprint, recluster, showPins
-  animate        → pick source, querySourceFeatures, getClusterLeaves
-  zoomToPinCluster → getClusterExpansionZoom
-  pinsLoaded     → isSourceLoaded ×2
+  pins.showGames(games)      games or colors changed
+  pins.cameraMoved() → bool  camera moved / card zoom changed; true = pin size changed → switchLayers
+  pins.themeChanged(theme)
+  pins.select(gameId)
+  pins.loaded()              for the settling
+  pins.layout()              pin size + cluster radius, for gameLayers and city names
+  pins.pulseSource(venue)    the source and features a pulse looks in
+  pins.clusterExpansionZoom(id)
```

The rule for which games are outer pins is now a pure function, `outerPinGames(games, { size, center }, isBehindGlobe)`, with its own unit tests. `addBlankImage` moved into `blankImage.ts` so both modules can share it. Layer order, layer visibility, the city names, click and hover wiring, the card layout source and the card and cluster footprints all stay in GlobeMap.

**Readers left outside the pin sources** (agreed with the coordinator, since the issue overstated "the only code that touches"):
- `ScoreCardMarkers.sync` still reads the pin source to place cards. It is the card layout's adapter, which is out of scope here (#333).
- `fadeNearHorizon` is still given both source ids and sets feature state on them each frame. That is drawing, not the sources' lifecycle.

## Evidence

- `npx tsc -b`, `npm run lint`: clean. `npm test`: 60 files, 655 passed (including 4 new `outerPinGames` tests).
- `npm run test:browser`: 10 files, 131 passed, 1 skipped (77s, one full run). Existing browser tests are unchanged.

Coverage of the behaviors the issue lists:

| Behavior | Browser test |
| --- | --- |
| Cards appear only after the pin source loads | **new**: shows no score card until the pin source has loaded the games |
| A score or clock change alone doesn't reload the pin source | **new**: spies on `setData`. A clock and score change: no call. A status change: one call |
| A theme change reclusters | existing: clusters small pins by the new theme's glows |
| The outer pins follow the globe as it turns | existing: gives a game a card once the globe turns its venue within the card radius. **New**: becomes an outer pin when turned out of the card radius, and is dropped when turned behind the globe |
| Selecting a game rings its pin in every pin set | existing: rings the selected small pin (zoomed out). **New**: the outer pin set, and the cardless small pin set |

Mutation check: each new test failed against a broken pin sources (reload on every change, no behind-globe check, filter set on one layer only), then passed once it was restored.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A refactor with no data, API or config change, so a revert undoes it.

**Blast Radius:** globe

If an ordering fact were lost, it would show as pins, clusters or rings on the globe, or as cards held back. The browser suite covers each of these.

body:
## Objective

Require Founder decision expiry timestamps to be unambiguous across hosts. Current-main `makeDecisionPayload()` and `verifyFounderDecision()` used `Date.parse()` alone, which accepts date-only, timezone-less local date-times, and calendar-rollover strings. A timezone-less signed expiry can therefore resolve to different instants on different hosts.

## Change

Draft child of PR #444, based on exact base `2c7fbde260a0ab568f9522a4cde498190e4eaa53`.

- Added `game/strict-timestamp.mjs` as the shared pure ISO 8601/RFC 3339 validator.
- Kept `game/timestamps.mjs` as a compatibility re-export from its sibling, preserving the existing import API and standalone browser bundle boundary.
- Changed `src/authority/decision.js` so both payload creation and cryptographic verification require an explicit-zone, calendar-valid expiry.
- Added regressions for date-only, timezone-less, calendar-rollover, invalid-hour and invalid-offset values, plus a valid explicit-offset case.
- Added an authority-entrypoint regression proving an expired signed decision emits no authorization event and consumes no nonce.
- Updated both isolated authority fixtures to copy the helper into their temporary `game/` tree.
- Added both game timestamp paths to the hosted preflight target inventory.
- Appended Run 39 and CI-driven corrections to `docs/operations/LATEST_CHECKPOINT.md`.

## CI-driven correction history

- First code head `df122e8` contained a double-escaped regex; diff review caught it and the regex was corrected at `49a25a1`.
- Verify on `49a25a1` failed 6/895 because isolated authority fixtures did not copy the new dependency; Browser Acceptance failed because the game bundle correctly rejects imports outside `game/`. Genesis passed.
- The correction moved the helper inside `game/`, made the re-export bundle-local, and added the helper to both isolated fixtures.
- A subsequent test-only improvement added the expired-authority/no-nonce-consumption regression. Earlier failed/pending runs are not counted as final-head evidence.

## Exact branch and current head

- Branch: `fix/founder-expiry-strict-timestamp-20261109-run3`
- Current PR head: `ca6a0ac4b2518cd41caa364bb47eb015e7b9ca2c`
- Code includes checkpoint history from commit `416138a16b6f8d523c5295ba8397e368935eeb4f` and the final authority-entrypoint regression in `ca6a0ac4b2518cd41caa364bb47eb015e7b9ca2c`.
- PR remains draft; no merge or retargeting is requested.

## Exact-head verification

- Browser Acceptance run `42758221614`: in progress at last poll.

## Authority and product limits

No Founder key was generated, enrolled, exported, or provisioned. The trust anchor remains `NOT_ENROLLED`; this does not integrate signed authority into `game/server.mjs`, establish hardware-backed key custody, merge, release, deploy, or change canonical game state. Worker B retains the active server/game paths. No additional cash cost.

author: dcccrypto
body:
## What
Follow-up to #3778 (Council round 4, N2). The leverage selector's floor is 1x: `selectorMaxLeverage = max(1, cap)`. If the live growth cap for this size ("Max leverage now", `fillMaxLeverage`) were below 1x, the ticket would still offer 1x and allow submit. No leverage the selector can offer would pass the wrapper's growth gate.

## Change (`app/components/trade/OrderTicket.tsx`)
- A new flag, `growthCapBelowOne`, is true when `ticketLimits.growth.fillMaxLeverage < 1`. That value is null on a reduce, a close or a non-growth market, so those cases are unaffected.
- When the flag is set:
  - **Selector:** "1x (fixed)" is replaced by *"Max leverage now: 0.8x for this size, below the 1x minimum. Use a smaller size."*, and the leverage input is disabled.
  - **Submit:** disabled, labelled *"Max leverage below 1x: use a smaller size"*.
  - **Confirm:** if the cap falls below 1x after the dialog opened, confirming sends nothing.

## Reachability (stated plainly)
This state cannot be reached on the deployed wrapper. In percolator-prog 3ba5bc37, `growth_v19::MAX_IMR_BPS = 10_000` caps the dynamic IMR at 100%, so the cap bottoms out at exactly 1.00x. A fixture scan from 10 to 400 lots across ceilings of 8x, 2x, 1.5x and 1.2x never went below 1.00. Test (1) pins this. The guard is fail-closed defence in depth, for example against a future program or a garbled view.

## Tests (`app/__tests__/components/trade/OrderTicket.n2-sub1x-growth-cap.test.tsx`)
Each test mounts the real OrderTicket.
1. Unreachability: at half the room, the room minus one lot and the full room, the cap is ≥ 1.
2. Control: with the real cap the ticket is submittable and shows no note.
3. A cap of 0.8x (the decision's `fillMaxLeverage` forced below 1):
   - the note is shown;
   - the input is disabled;
   - no presets and no "1x (fixed)" text;
   - submit is disabled with the reason;
   - clicking it opens no dialog and sends no trade.
4. A cap that falls below 1x after the dialog opened: confirming sends nothing.

Results:
- **RED** on 58acdd0f (component reverted): 2/4 fail.
- **GREEN:** 4/4, and the #3778 N2 suite is 4/4.
- **Mutants:** 4/4 killed: no submit block, no confirm guard, input left enabled, threshold changed to 0.5.
- **Typecheck:** `tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

## Second commit: fixes from fresh reviews of #3778
Fresh security and code reviews of #3778 both APPROVED at 0f696053. Their verdicts are stored outside the repo. They raised these Lows, fixed here:
- **Code Low-1:** the growth gate compares equity after the fill fee, so `extraEquityNeeded` already includes the fee, and the bundled deposit added `fundFee` on top.
  - The floor is now net of `min(gateFee, fundFee)`, so floor + `fundFee` still covers `extraEquityNeeded` in full and the fee is no longer asked twice.
  - Measured: 156.41 before, 153.47 after.
- **Security Low:** before, only the clamp effect enforced the cap. Now:
  - submit also refuses a leverage above the cap for this size (`leverageOverCap`);
  - the confirm handler sends nothing in that state.
- **Code Low-2:** tests now pin the conservative-equity terms: negative pnl and negative fee credits.
- **Security Info:** the slider bound in the N2 test is asserted unconditionally.

New tests in `OrderTicket.n2-growth-lev-cap.test.tsx`:
- (5) the fee is not doubled;
- (5b) a typed deposit one cent under `extraEquityNeeded` keeps submit disabled, and the quoted amount enables it;
- (6) negative fee credits and negative pnl.

Mutants killed: fee double-count, pnl term dropped, fee-credit term dropped, over-netting (both fees subtracted).

**Not pinned:** `leverageOverCap` has no test. In jsdom the clamp effect flushes before any discrete event, so the over-cap render cannot be produced. It is defence in depth only.

_Requested by **David** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011Q4GKDWkvJWgwKCtfTmW5V?thread=cmsg_011Q4GKDWkvJWgwKCtfTmW5VH9vkhiERtaZE2ua9yZX4Md)_

## What

- A new scene, `model_lighting`, in `KisakCOD-vulkan-d3d9-check` (after `shadow_map`), its name in the runner's scene list, and its row in `docs/vulkan-d3d9-front.md`. No change to the front or the adapter.
- The guide's line on the model lighting difference against DXVK now carries the verdict: it is not the Vulkan back end's.

## Why

The renderer keeps model lighting in a 256-wide, 4-deep volume of 4x4x4-texel cells and rewrites a few cells a frame in one of two ways, chosen by `r_altModelLightingUpdate`:

- 0: one MANAGED volume, locked whole with no flags, cells written in place.
- 1 (the default): a SYSTEMMEM volume locked with `D3DLOCK_NO_DIRTY_UPDATE`, `AddDirtyBox` per cell, then `UpdateTexture` into a DEFAULT volume, which is the one drawn with.

Only the first had a check (the adapter's `cube_volume` scene, after the dark models of laptop run 5). The second is the path on which laptop run 7 measured models 2.7 to 6.7 luma darker than through DXVK. The scene shows that, through the front, both paths leave the same texels.

## The scene

It makes the three volumes with the renderer's sizes, pools and usage, patches them with the renderer's addressing and call order for two frames, and after each frame draws every slice of four cells from both drawn volumes and reads the pixels back. Cells written in that frame, a cell written in both frames, a cell the second frame leaves alone, and a cell never written must hold the same texels on both paths. 1033 points.

## Where the lighting question stands

Closed: no rendering difference was found on any back end at either setting.

- **Vulkan matches real Direct3D 9 on both paths.** Vulkan PC run 6 Part 4 (Windows PC, RTX 2080 SUPER, Win32 Debug build of 8aee1d43): five launches (Direct3D 9 at 0, at 1, at 1 again; Vulkan at 0 and at 1), three screenshots each. Mean luma of all 15 shots is 63.50 to 63.90, and no cell of a 4x4 grid differs between any two settings by more than it moves inside one launch. A local result on one machine, not CI evidence.
- **One screenshot pair from that view misleads.** A plain repeat launch of Direct3D 9 was 31.06 dB from its twin, while two shots inside one launch are about 50 dB apart: each launch lands in one of a few states. Run 7's 33.56 dB was one pair.
- **DXVK matches itself and Vulkan on the laptop too.** Model lighting laptop run 1 (Intel RPL-U, same build, received after this PR's last commit): DXVK at 0, at 1, at 1 again and Vulkan at 0 and at 1, three shots each: no cell beyond its spread on a 4x4 or an 8x8 grid; Vulkan against DXVK at 1 is 39.5 dB, DXVK against its own repeat 36.8 dB. One launch's three shots read mean luma 65.70, 65.84 and 67.05, which is run 7's "67.5". A standalone Direct3D 9 program that patches both paths at random leaves the same texels on DXVK 2.7.1 (9.8 million texels on the laptop's Intel driver, also on lavapipe). Local results, not CI evidence. The guide gets these figures in a docs-only follow-up.

## Validation

Local cloud container, x86_64, Mesa lavapipe through SDL's offscreen driver, no GPU and no game data, on the branch with master 6e11f2b merged in:

- `test_vulkan_d3d9_front.py` and `test_vulkan_legacy_adapter.py` pass with validation required in Debug and RelWithDebInfo; the front check also in Debug with the MoltenVK-path switches.
- The `model_lighting` scene alone passes with the record thread off (`KISAK_VK_RECORD_THREAD=0`, `KISAK_VK_FENCE_FLUSH=0`, `KISAK_VK_GPU_FEED=0`) and with `KISAK_VK_GPU_FEED=always`.
- With `lg::UpdateTexture` changed to copy half a level, the scene fails with 160 mismatches (that change is not in the PR).
- `build-linux.sh` builds `bin/KisakCOD-dedi`; `test_linux_bootstrap.py`, `run_linux_checks.py` (25 checks), the runner self-tests, `test_linux_window_workflow.py` and `run_world_surface_checks.py` in Debug and RelWithDebInfo pass.

Hosted CI is green on the last commit (7a9ceb0, with master 6e11f2b merged in): every job passed, 2 skipped by design ("MSVC x64 build", "macOS universal app bundle size"). Master has since gained PRs 169 and 168, which touch none of this PR's files; the branch merges cleanly with master 0bc504c.

Not run locally: MSVC, macOS, any real GPU. Local results are not CI evidence.

body:
## What this PR does

This is **PR 1 of issue #1** (`#1`): establish a stable notification identity and target contract so later click navigation never has to parse titles or bodies. It intentionally does **not** wire native clicks or client navigation yet.

### Changes

- Add `lib/toast-registry.js`: a bounded, TTL-aware `id -> { sessionId, target, sessionIds, interactionKey }` registry.
- Every `show()` payload now carries `sessionId`, `target`, optional `sessionIds` and `interactionKey`; the Typert schema preserves them.
- Stable ids:
  - pending approval: `pending:<seq>`
  - summary: `summary:<waveSeq>`
  - ordinary event: `<sessionId>:<kind>:<serial>`
- The host remembers each id's target in the registry and clears it when the native host stops, crashes, is restarted, or all toasts close.
- Summary notifications now track the sessions that actually aggregated (side-line only). The body count and `sessionIds` no longer include the main-line session.
- Defer the summary until the finishing session's `settleRun` has completed, so the last side-line session is included in `sessionIds` and the count.
- Guard stale host-child events so an old process exiting after a restart cannot clear the new registry.
- Version bumped to `0.2.2-desktop.14`.

### Tests

```bash
node tests/manifest.test.mjs          # 5
node tests/approval-ledger.test.mjs   # 6
node tests/toast-registry.test.mjs    # 4
node tests/client-logic.test.mjs      # 13
```

All 28 pass. The registry test covers id normalization, defaults, duplicate `sessionIds`, TTL eviction, size eviction, `drop` and `clear`. The client-engine tests verify that a main-line session is excluded from the summary and that the last side-line session is included.

### Follow-ups

- PR 2: native `clicked`/`closed` event unification for GTK/WPF.
- PR 3: host → client click queue and `ctx.sessions.open(sessionId)` navigation.
- PR 4: focus the pending question/approval area.
- PR 5: summary session picker.

Closes nothing yet; part of #1.

body:
## Scope

ADS-FOUNDATION (Amendment D + Amendment G item 3, wave3-status ADS-FOUNDATION row / §G3). Three deliverables, nothing else:

1. **app-ads.txt route**
2. **Real-ID env wiring** for the mobile build
3. **Remote flag plumbing** — server-driven, DEFAULT OFF — plus the config contract the S6 slice-1 slot will consume

**Explicitly NOT in this slice:** no ad UI/slot is placed anywhere (the single Today slot, in-flow under Today's guidance, belongs to S6 slice 1 under the fusion rule); no placement/route change to the existing banner policy (it still names the legacy "more" route — S6 slice 1 re-points it when it builds the slot); no migrations.

## 1. app-ads.txt

- `public/app-ads.txt` contains exactly one line: `google.com, pub-2708638041809482, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0`
- `src/index.ts` serves it at `GET /app-ads.txt` as `text/plain` (public, max-age=86400), following the existing `robots.txt`/`llms.txt` pattern in the same file.
- Smoke lists updated: `scripts/ui-surface-smoke.ts` now requires the file, pins its exact content, and requires the `"/app-ads.txt"` route wiring in `src/index.ts`.

## 2. Real-ID env wiring

Real IDs (public — app-ads.txt publishes the publisher ID): app `ca-app-pub-2708638041809482~4540309917`, banner unit `ca-app-pub-2708638041809482/4316948636` ("munch_android_home_banner").

- `.github/workflows/android-play-internal-bundle.yml` previously **pinned Google's SAMPLE IDs as env values** — signed release bundles silently carried sample ad configuration. It now sets the real IDs.
- `.github/workflows/mobile-android.yml` now sets `MUNCH_ADMOB_APP_ID` / `MUNCH_ADMOB_BANNER_AD_UNIT_ID` to the real IDs in both the validate and boot jobs.
- `android/app/build.gradle`: the envs (or the `munchAdMobAppId` / `munchAdMobBannerAdUnitId` project properties) now feed both build types. Debug uses configured-or-sample; **release uses the configured IDs only and hard-fails at configuration time when they are missing or equal to the sample IDs** — a release build can never silently ship sample IDs. Google sample IDs remain ONLY as the debug/local-dev fallback when the envs are unset.
- Asserted in `scripts/mobile-shell-smoke.ts` (runs in both Android workflows): both workflows carry the real IDs and contain no sample publisher ID; build.gradle reads both envs, keeps the sample fallback shape, and contains the release guard.

## 3. Remote flag — the contract S6 slice 1 consumes

| Piece | Value |
|---|---|
| Server env (Railway, Munch API service) | `MUNCH_ADS_ENABLED` — unset/empty/anything but `true` = OFF. **Default OFF; nothing to set for this merge.** Slots ship dark until Michael flips it after AdMob reactivation + per-app review clear. |
| Server module | `src/ads-config.ts` — `adsEnabledFromEnv()` / `getAdsConfig()` |
| Bootstrap config field | `GET /api/app/bootstrap` → `ads: { enabled: boolean }` (added in `getAppBootstrap`, `src/app/repository.ts`, beside `androidEntitlements`) — the same bootstrap/config path the packaged app already uses |
| JS policy | `public/ads-policy.js` `shouldShowAndroidBanner({...})` now requires `adsEnabled === true`; missing/undefined fails closed |
| App shell | `public/app.js` `syncAndroidAdPlacement()` reads `state.bootstrap?.ads?.enabled` and forwards `adsEnabled: adsEnabled === true` to the plugin on every `setBannerVisible` call |
| Native plugin | `MunchAdsPlugin.setBannerVisible` (both copies: `mobile/android/` source + the generated `android/` copy, kept identical) reads `adsEnabled` with default **false**: `bannerRequested = visible && adsEnabled && !adFree && adUnitId present`. When the flag is off the plugin makes **no ad load attempt** (no consent-form flow toward a banner, no `MobileAds.initialize`, no `loadAd`) |
| Premium | Preserved and verified: the plugin already fail-closes on Premium — `adFree` defaults to `true` when absent, the app passes `adFree: adFree !== false`, and the policy requires `adFree === false`. A Premium account cannot load ads even with the flag on. |

`mobile/runtime.js` needed no change: its frozen `window.MunchAds.setBannerVisible(options)` bridge forwards the options object (now including `adsEnabled`) verbatim. The e2e parity fixture bootstrap gains `ads: { enabled: false }` to match the production shape.

## Tests

Added:

- `src/app-ads.test.ts` — the public file contains exactly the publisher line (byte-for-byte incl. trailing newline); `src/index.ts` registers the route as text/plain.
- `src/ads-config.test.ts` — flag DEFAULT OFF when unset; OFF for empty/`false`/`0`/`no`/`off`/`yes`/`1`; only explicit `true` (trimmed, case-insensitive) enables; `getAdsConfig()` tracks the live env.
- `src/mobile-ads-policy.test.ts` — new case: flag off or flag missing hides the banner for an otherwise-eligible account.
- `scripts/mobile-shell-smoke.ts` + `scripts/ui-surface-smoke.ts` assertions as above.

Local verification before push: `bun test` **966 pass / 0 fail** (7 new tests over the 959 baseline); typecheck clean; Prettier clean (run via the local prettier binary — `bunx` is absent on this VM); capability-manifest, commerce-boundary, submission, connect-route, pantry, widget-contract, mobile-shell, and UI-surface smokes all pass; `bun run mobile:web` + `cap sync android` + `configure-mobile-android.ts` reproduce the committed `android/` tree with no extra diff.

CI run IDs are reported in the PR thread once the runs complete.

## Known evidence limits (recorded, not silent)

- **Release-AAB evidence on a PR is impossible by the repo's existing design**: the only release lane (`android-play-internal-bundle.yml`) is `workflow_dispatch`-only and main-only, and release builds require the protected upload keystore, which PRs never receive. The PR-lane proxies are the Gradle release guard (configuration-time hard-fail on missing/sample IDs), the mobile-shell-smoke assertions, and the debug lanes exercising the same env wiring. The first post-merge dispatch of the bundle workflow is the real release evidence. The Firebase distribution job was **not** dispatched (manual-only by rule).
- Local Gradle execution is unavailable on this VM (wrapper download blocked); Gradle behaviour is proven by the Actions Android lanes on this PR.

author: danmaciel
body:
## Problema
Criação, atualização e aprovação checavam conflito antes de salvar sem serializar requisições paralelas. Duas transações podiam observar o mesmo horário livre.

## Solução conservadora
- Migração Flyway V8 cria uma linha de lock da agenda.
- `AgendaWriteLock.acquire()` utiliza `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` em transação obrigatória.
- Criação normal, atualização e aprovação adquirem o lock antes das verificações e gravação.
- A criação forçada continua sendo exceção administrativa e **não** é bloqueada (pode criar sobreposições intencionalmente).
- Teste PostgreSQL/Testcontainers com duas requisições simultâneas e somente um sucesso.
- README descreve throughput, limites e comportamento.

## Limitações
Este bloqueio serializa todas as datas e pode ser gargalo. É proposital para a agenda única demonstrativa e depende de todos os caminhos normais de escrita usarem a trava. Não é uma solução para múltiplos recursos/profissionais. Não substituir o teste concorrente por testes unitários.

Aguardar CI antes de integrar. Sem alterações destrutivas, sem reescrita do histórico Git.

body:
PR 4 of 4 in the run-cards stack (plan `3ef69c1d-026`, intent `run-console`). It stacks on PR 3.

The plan named macOS's `script(1)` for the terminal. Building it showed that `script(1)` needs its own stdin to be a terminal, and under the glass it's a pipe (`tcgetattr/ioctl: Operation not supported on socket`). That was raised in ume `7ccec454-d66`, and Chris picked `expect(1)`, which ships with macOS.

## Change
- **`man ask --run <script> --interactive`** posts a card whose script gets a terminal.
  - `/usr/bin/expect` runs a short relay (`RUN_RELAY_SCRIPT` in `apps/cli/src/run-exec.ts`). It spawns the script under a pseudo-terminal, sends each line of its stdin to it, and exits with the script's status.
  - On the time limit it kills the script's session and exits 124.
  - Posting `--interactive` is refused where `expect` is missing.
- **Output default:** an interactive card defaults to `--output exit`, because its transcript can hold anything Chris typed.
- **The console line** sits under the live output on the card. Chris answers at the prompt and Enter sends the line (`run-line`).
  - The secret toggle masks the line and adds its value to the scrubber, so its echo and any later print show `‹secret›`.
  - A line only reaches that card's live run.
- **Plain cards are unchanged:** a card without `--interactive` still reads end-of-file after its inputs.

## Criteria (intent `run-console`)
| Criterion | Proven by (`apps/cli/test/run-console.test.ts`) |
|---|---|
| `ach-prompt-answer`: a line sent from the card answers the script's prompt and the run exits 0 | answers a prompt with a line sent from the card, and the run exits 0 (the script also checks `[ -t 0 ]`) |
| `ach-secret-line`: a secret line the script echoes shows `‹secret›` in the card output and the answer | scrubs a secret line, its echo included, from the card output and the answer |
| `ach-exit-default`: `--interactive` with no `--output` answers with the exit code only | gives the agent only the exit code from an interactive card posted without --output |
| `pres-no-line-after-end`: a line for an ended run, or another card, gets 409 and reaches no process | refuses a line for a run that has ended, or for another card's run, and writes nothing |
| `pres-plain-stdin`: a card without `--interactive` reads end-of-file after its inputs | still gives a card without --interactive end-of-file after its declared inputs |

These tests need `/usr/bin/expect`, so they skip where it's missing (Windows CI, and Ubuntu unless it's installed).

## Notes
- **Plan text:** the approved plan's PR 4 still says `script(1)`; the ume ask records the change.
- **Files outside `applies-to`:**
  - `packages/core/src/run-cards.ts` (`interactive`)
  - `packages/core/src/run-scrub.ts` (`add`)
  - `apps/cli/src/main.ts`, `usage.ts` and `run-routes.ts`
  - `packages/glass-ui/ui/actions.ts` and `components/run-card.ts`

The full suite passes: 268 files, 3363 tests.

author: seashell86
body:
Random programs now use the local `ref name = place` from #1221 and compare it with the reference evaluator.

- **What a ref names.** An item of a list, a field of a struct, an item of a holder's list, a holder's whole list or its tag, and an item of a `list[Node]`, which is then changed through `match` with `ref` in its cases.
- **Changes through it.** `+=` and `=` on an int, `append` and `pop` on a list, a tree reshaped, and the ref passed on as `bump(ref r, by)`.
- **Reads while it lives.** The ref and its container are printed between changes, so a read that misses a change shows. The index is worked out once, at the `ref`, and the evaluator holds the program to that.
- **One ref after another.** A second ref into the same container comes after the first one's last use, and sometimes the container is changed directly afterwards.
- **In loops and lock bodies.** Refs come up in any block, loops included. Inside `lock bag as ref held:` the body takes `ref slot = held.items[at]` and adds to it, and a place outside the list crashes, which undoes the lock's changes.
- **Places outside the list.** Outside risky programs the index is kept inside the list under `if len > 0`. A risky program can name a place outside it, which fails at the `ref`.

Reading a ref under a lock doesn't build yet ("`Bag` has no `value`"). That bug went to its lane with a repro, so lock bodies only use `+=` through a ref for now.

Also fixed: a loop over `holder.items` now holds `holder`, so nothing in the body changes it, as the checker requires.

**This fixes main's red `asan` job.** That job built no threads runtime, so random programs that launch a task, through the `sent` helper, didn't build there. It wasn't a memory bug. The job now builds the threads runtime with AddressSanitizer, as the workers' job does, so tasks, locks and rollback across threads run under the sanitizer. It also fails outright if that runtime is missing. Where there's no threads runtime, as in some local setups, the target now skips `sent` programs, as it already skipped `tally` ones.

Closes #3369.

The owner's clipped standing bird was not a fresh regression: the PNGs bake in a cream card and an embossed ring, the code hid the ring by zooming the icon in (#1815, retuned in #2750), and the standing bird overlaps its own ring, so no zoom could hide the ring without cutting the bird. - `src/shop/flightMovement.js`, `src/app.css`: the zoom, transform-origin and `overflow: hidden` are gone; the icon is `object-fit: contain`. The button's own background (white idle, brand green active) is the one circle.

author: talstilkol
body:
## What and why

Plan **1.7 step 5**: the "model credits" screen with ivrit.ai and Dicta attribution. Audit 1.8 found it missing on #200 and on every PR.

**Base: `feat/live-dictation` (#255).** It already contains #200: `fix/model-catalog` is an ancestor of it, so no merge was needed. `CreditsDialog.tsx` is byte-identical on every branch that has it: `feat/live-dictation`, `feat/ivrit-whisper` (#383), `feat/meeting-speakers` (#398), `verify/train`, `verify/train-bisect-1`, `research/usability-hebrew`. I used #255, the branch the dialog was written on. The newer ones are stacked on it (#383 targets it) or busy (verify/train is lane D's).

What was there: `CreditsDialog` listed only the registry entries that *already had* an attribution, so a model without one was silently left out.

What changed:
- **`src/ai/modelCredits.ts`.** For every model in `models/registry.json` that is not forbidden and that reaches the user (bundled, download, ollama-pull, user-pull or user-download), it builds:
  - the name;
  - the licence, and its URL;
  - the source;
  - the attribution;
  - the licence family, with what that licence requires: CC BY (credit, link, note changes), Apache-2.0 / MIT (keep the notices), MPL-2.0, the Llama licences ("Built with Llama", the AUP), and Gemma (the Terms, the Prohibited Use Policy).
  - Hebrew models (ivrit.ai, Dicta) are marked and sorted first.
  - `creditProblems` names what is missing from an entry: attribution, a known licence, an https source, a CC BY or Llama attribution that names its licence.
- **The dialog** gets a **"Model credits"** section, with "Hebrew models (ivrit.ai, Dicta)" first and then "Other models and data". Each entry shows its name, linked licence, source, attribution and the licence's requirement. The old `creditEntries` export is unchanged, because `dictation-segmenter.test.ts` uses it.
- **Strings:** 11 keys, in English and all 7 locales.
  - This base has no lazy-English mechanism: `registerEnglish` and `src/i18n/lazy/` came later, on other branches. So the keys go into the English table next to the existing `credits.*` keys, about 1 KB gzip at startup by estimate.
  - When the lazy mechanism reaches this stack, they can move to `src/i18n/lazy/credits.json` with the dialog.
- **Docs:** `ai/model-credits` in English and Hebrew, with a sidebar entry.

## Definition of done (plan 0.7)

Proposed `dod` for step 5:
```
npx vitest run src/__tests__/modelCredits.test.ts src/__tests__/creditsDialog.test.tsx src/__tests__/dictation-segmenter.test.ts
```
**dodMock: no.** "Every bundled or downloadable model has a credits entry" is `modelCredits.test.ts` → "every bundled or downloadable model that is not forbidden has a complete entry". Today that is 37 models, all complete.

## Local verification

Plain-Node mode: the Vercel Sandbox is blocked by the Hobby limit, and Vercel deployments are rate-limited.

- **`modelCredits.test.ts` under the vitest shim: 5/5.** It covers:
  - complete entries for every shipped model, matched against the registry;
  - forbidden and `delivery: none` entries are excluded;
  - ivrit.ai (CC BY 4.0, linked) and DictaLM are marked Hebrew and come first;
  - a missing attribution or an unknown licence is reported as a problem, not left out silently;
  - the licence families (CC-BY-NC maps to none).
- **`creditsDialog.test.tsx` in the offline Chromium harness: 1/1.** Every model is rendered. The ivrit.ai entry has its licence and source links and the CC BY requirement. The first list is ivrit.ai + DictaLM only. Llama shows "Built with Llama".
- **`dictation-segmenter.test.ts` (it uses `creditEntries`) in the harness: 7/7.**
- **i18n:** `i18n` 14/14, `i18nDrift` 14/14, `i18nValues` 8/8, `i18nPlaceholders` 3/3, `i18nStrings` 4/4.
- **`check-code-hygiene`:** clean.
- **Offline TypeScript:** only missing-react-types diagnostics.
- **Pre-existing failures, the same on the base:** `hebrewModels` 18/19 and `licenses` 70/82 give identical counts on a clean `feat/live-dictation` checkout under the shim, so they are not from this change.

## Not verified here

- The full Sandbox run (`npx vitest run`, `tsc -b`, build and size budget).
- The dialog opened by hand from the command palette, in both languages.

```
gh pr checkout <this PR> && npm ci
npx vitest run src/__tests__/modelCredits.test.ts src/__tests__/creditsDialog.test.tsx src/__tests__/dictation-segmenter.test.ts
npm run dev   # ⌘K → Credits
```
