author: molina211
body:
## Story

`code-corhuila/multi-tour-docs#213` (HU-WFL-005, task WF5-05 of spec `001-hu-wfl-005-change-the-vehicles-of-a-departure`, [PR 870](https://github.com/code-corhuila/multi-tour-docs/pull/870)). AC-WF5-01.6 and .7; plan D-04 and D-07.

## What changes and why

The entry of the saga over the use case of the orchestrator, written to the `openapi/openapi.yaml` of WF5-01.

- `POST /api/v1/sagas/change-departure-vehicles` (`Idempotency-Key` of 8 to 128 characters; `201` with `Location`, `200` for a repeated key) and `GET /api/v1/sagas/change-departure-vehicles/{id}`, plus `/health`. A departure that does not exist is a `404`.
- The token is checked here: RS256 only, `exp`, `sub`, issuer and audience, and the caller must be a **Tenant Administrator** with an ordinary token (not a single-purpose one) and a `tenantId` claim that is an id. The tenant comes from that claim and goes to the use case; a body that carries a `tenantId`, or any field the contract does not declare, is refused. A saga is read only for the tenant of the token.
- The body is read as one JSON object of at most 16 KiB; `departureCode` must be plain (the same pattern the clients of the participants require) and `vehicleIds` 1 to 50 distinct ids, with one detail per invalid field naming the field and never the value.
- One error envelope with the correlation id as `traceId`; the cause of a failure goes to the log, never to the answer. A panic below is the generic `500`. A saga that is still `RUNNING` because a participant gave no clear answer is answered as such with `201`; the description of the contract now says so.
- `TestC_every_contract_operation_is_exercised` validates every answer against the published contract and fails when a response the contract declares was never produced (ADR-004 D7).

`completedSteps` is documented in the contract as the steps that ended, including one undone afterwards. Declared: `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` and the 405 are answered but are not in the contract (as in the sibling saga); the verifier accepts an empty issuer or audience, which would turn that check off, so the composition root of WF5-06 must refuse an empty one at start.

Model: the entry of `multi-tour-workflow-onboard-tenant`. `ParsePublicKey` is for the composition root of WF5-06.

## How it was tested

`test(http)` was committed first and seen failing (the entry did not exist), then `feat(http)` makes it pass. The CI is red because the organization's Actions is locked by billing, not because of this change: [last failed job of a sibling repository](https://github.com/code-corhuila/multi-tour-worker-departure-deadlines/actions/runs/42584426688), "The job was not started because your account is locked due to a billing issue." Local checks that replace `ci.yml`:

- `gofmt -l .`: empty
- `go vet ./...`: passes
- `go test -count=1 ./...`: passes

It will be run again in CI when Actions is back.

## Checklist

- [x] No secret or credential
- [x] No schema change outside a `-db`
- [x] Contract written before the code and exercised by a gate

author: oscarlaw
body:
## Summary

Add login confirmation and a retained, single-consumer account-state subscription so applications can render session review, sign-out reason, and cleanup progress without polling. Reconcile session lists automatically on authenticated connection lifecycle events and typed refresh hints. Preserve transport ownership until shutdown joins complete, including cancelled handovers and cleanup retries. Update published dependency pins, generated native bindings, consumer fixtures, and self-contained SDK documentation.

## Related issues

No separate tracking issue supplied.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking)
- [x] Breaking change (major version / public API / wire behaviour)
- [ ] Protocol change (Syntra framing, handshake, ids, reconnect, realtime grammar)
- [x] Platform binding change (UniFFI Swift/Kotlin, wasm-bindgen JS)
- [ ] Docs / examples only
- [ ] CI / tooling / deps only

## Crates / areas touched

- [ ] `syntra-core` (codec, state, handshake, ids, pending, timeouts, reconnect)
- [ ] `syntra-net` (encrypted native TCP)
- [x] `tinkle-schema` (methods, realtime validation)
- [x] `libtinkle` (public `Client`, facades, `CursorStore`)
- [x] `tinkle-ffi` (UniFFI — iOS Swift / Android Kotlin)
- [ ] `libtinkle-web` (wasm-bindgen — browser/WASM)
- [x] Docs (`docs/`, `README.md`, examples)
- [x] CI / release (`.github/workflows`, `release-plz`, BSR pinning)

Upstream transport implementations are not edited. All three published Syntra crates move together to exact rc.5, with TCP-only networking. The public schema is pinned to BSR `d85fcc4fe5924b57a8def89284d91ed5`. Portable web validation changes transitively through the shared schema decoder.

## Platform impact

- [ ] No platform-specific behaviour (pure Rust core)
- [x] iOS (Swift via UniFFI: runtime threading, `Task.cancel()`, Core Data/GRDB/Keychain store, APNs `sync_after_wake`)
- [x] Android (Kotlin via UniFFI/JNI: coroutines, Room/EncryptedSharedPreferences, FCM/WorkManager/Doze)
- [x] Web / WASM portable schema checks (network unsupported)
- [x] `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` boundary preserved (no browser APIs in native, no `std::net`/raw sockets in `wasm.rs`)

### Platform notes

Native generated bindings expose confirmation, `unconfirmed`, and account-state subscription handles. Kotlin cancellation/shutdown smoke reads enter `next()` with `CoroutineStart.UNDISPATCHED`; that does not prove a suspended Rust waiter was registered. Kotlin binding/initializer/sample compilation passes, but installed Android runtime and final-AAR validation remain unverified because the required NDK and emulator prerequisites are absent. A prior fresh-library iOS simulator run passed 17 XCTest tests; it predates the final Rust corrections and is not qualification of this final commit. Minimum-OS, physical-device, protected-storage, and renewed final-artifact Swift checks remain release gates.

## Protocol / compatibility

- [x] No Syntra wire change (frame, handshake, `request_id`, `RpcResult`, notifications, reconnect)
- [ ] Syntra change is spec-aligned and covered by `CONF-CORE-*` vectors in `syntra-core/tests/conformance.rs`
- [x] Tinkle app change keeps `tinkle-schema` single-decoder (`RealtimeNotification`, complete-batch grammar, cursor rules)
- [x] No change to public API, or public API change is documented below
- [ ] BSR / `tinkle-proto` pin unchanged, or `PROTO_PINNING.md` updated with `buf registry sdk version` output

The first checkbox concerns the upstream transport envelope, not application payload compatibility. Application notifications now dispatch by exact `google.protobuf.Any` type URLs: bare `ConnectivityChanged` and `SessionChanged`. Published schema coordinates and checksums are recorded in `PROTO_PINNING.md` and Cargo.lock; a new literal `buf registry sdk version` command transcript was not committed, so that template box remains unchecked. No source overrides or candidate artifacts are used.

## Security considerations

- [x] No secrets in logs, errors, panics, `Debug`, URLs, query, headers, or event callbacks
- [x] Enrollment material remains redacted, zeroized and separate from application storage
- [x] No `ClientHello` / raw `Frame` bytes logged (prost `Debug` can leak)
- [x] TCP 443/80 use the same pin/scope/key ID/mode; no fallback after socket selection
- [ ] Authorization keys use protected platform storage only

Hosts still supply the protected-store implementation; these changes do not qualify Keychain/Keystore security. Generic authorization denials withdraw knowledge without authorizing erasure. Ordinary per-RPC PermissionDenied preserves a healthy Returning transport; exact current retirement evidence is required for automatic clearing. Review hints never grant access, populate a session list, or advance a message checkpoint. Unknown mutation outcomes are not replayed automatically. Gitleaks scanned the complete staged diff with full redaction and found no leaks.

## How tested

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features --no-deps -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features --verbose` (incl. `client_integration` live mock gateway if touched)
- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v` (release, consumer preflight, and binding-patch tests)
- [x] `bash scripts/generate-bindings.sh --check` (bindings parity, if `tinkle-ffi` touched)
- [x] `cargo check --locked -p tinkle-schema -p libtinkle-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (if portable schema/web touched)
- [ ] UniFFI bindings regen / Swift+Kotlin smoke (if `tinkle-ffi` touched)
- [x] Portable WASM schema checks (if `libtinkle-web` touched)

### Test evidence

The locked Rust workspace suite passes, including 125 core unit tests. Ordinary workspace execution keeps existing opt-in acceptance tests ignored; separate executed fixture lanes are not added to workspace totals. MSRV 1.91.1 and all-target/all-feature checks pass. The new confirmation-generation and denial-state regressions failed before their fixes and pass afterward; transport ownership, review-demand fencing, retained state, and uncertain revocation have focused regressions.

External real-service acceptance passed with race detection and strict direct/wrapped Logout assertions, invocation `5456f238-e88c-44c9-b2c6-fdfb343a1500`, selected stack execution 2026-11-10 04:10:28–04:11:38 UTC. Its selected application executable SHA-256 was `6d935303ce41f54cc930711d1734176b3e94fe91b818af00cfce0074140320ad`; subsequent changes were documentation-only. Raw logs and published dependency provenance are retained by the run owner, not committed to the SDK. This is not installed-mobile, capacity, or deployment qualification.

Python tooling: 136 tests pass. Kotlin compilation and seven package tests pass. Binding parity was freshly rerun before committing and matches the compiled FFI contract; staged diff checks and secret scanning pass. Hosted CI results are pending.

## Breaking changes / migration

`AccountSession` gains required `unconfirmed` data in Rust/native records, generated client interfaces gain confirmation and state-subscription methods, and connectivity validation requires the typed Any envelope instead of bare connectivity bytes. Update struct construction and custom interface conformers/fakes, and ship the matching regenerated bindings with their native library. ConfirmSession returns a commit-point projection, never a replacement session list. A second active state consumer is rejected; explicitly stop the current subscription before replacing it.

This PR does not publish SDK packages or change host protected-storage implementations. Roll back by reverting the application/library upgrade as a compatible unit, not by mixing old bindings with new native binaries or restoring invalidated credentials.

body:
# RE-001: lockwait caller 1site resolver noloader dead duff q50x9328

One-hundred-sixty-second packet of the lock-wait-helper-caller frontier (344 survivors; the lu-miss frontier is exhausted 16/16 with #314–#329). FDE 0x638afe0..0x638b2a0 (704 B, 191 strict) has one lock-wait site, resolves its entry through a separate resolver callee (0x6388310) WITHOUT loading the entry through the trivial 8-byte load helper (0x63bfb90 is NOT called) and WITHOUT a fixed inline adjust (the resolver-fixed chain, adjusts +0xb8 through +0x380 over #341–#364, ENDS at #364; #365/#366/#367/#368/#369/#370/#371/#372/#373/#374/#375/#376/#377/#378/#379/#380/#381/#382/#383/#384/#385/#386/#387/#388/#389/#390/#391/#392/#393/#394/#395/#396/#397/#398/#399/#400/#401/#402/#403/#404/#405/#406/#407/#408/#409/#410/#411/#412/#413/#414/#415/#416/#417/#418/#419/#420/#421/#422/#423/#424/#425/#426/#427/#428/#429/#430/#431/#432/#433/#434/#435/#436/#437/#438/#439/#440/#441/#442/#443/#444/#445/#446/#447/#448/#449/#450/#451/#452/#453/#454/#455/#456/#457/#458/#459/#460/#461/#462/#463/#464/#465/#466/#467/#468/#469/#470/#471/#472/#473/#474/#475/#476/#477/#478/#479/#480/#481/#482/#483/#484/#485/#486/#487/#488/#489/#490/#491 add no adjust entry), a 3-value exit 0/1/22, and a Duff's-device copy loop that is FULLY DEAD (its dispatch tail is never entered and its 8-at-a-time body is never entered; the loop-entry jb is always taken because r12d == 0). It rejoins at the trylock-SUCCESS block after lock-wait (like #332/#333/#334/#336/#338/#339/#340/#341/#342/#343/#344/#345/#346/#347/#348/#349/#350/#351/#352/#353/#354/#355/#356/#357/#358/#359/#360/#361/#362/#363/#364/#365/#366/#367/#368/#369/#370/#371/#372/#373/#374/#375/#376/#377/#378/#379/#380/#381/#382/#383/#384/#385/#386/#387/#388/#389/#390/#391/#392/#393/#394/#395/#396/#397/#398/#399/#400/#401/#402/#403/#404/#405/#406/#407/#408/#409/#410/#411/#412/#413/#414/#415/#416/#417/#418/#419/#420/#421/#422/#423/#424/#425/#426/#427/#428/#429/#430/#431/#432/#433/#434/#435/#436/#437/#438/#439/#440/#441/#442/#443/#444/#445/#446/#447/#448/#449/#450/#451/#452/#453/#454/#455/#456/#457/#458/#459/#460/#461/#462/#463/#464/#465/#466/#467/#468/#469/#470/#471/#472/#473/#474/#475/#476/#477/#478/#479/#480/#481/#482/#483/#484/#485/#486/#487/#488/#489/#490, unlike #330/#331/#335/#337).

Thin packet: README + records.json + MANIFEST + window bytes + disassembly only. No verifier tool, no unit tests, no `make verify`, no `make catalogue`, no full `make test` — every claim is a direct check over the disassembly and bytes, quoted with addresses in the README.

## Window

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FDE | 0x638afe0..0x638b2a0 |
| Bytes | 704 |
| Strict | 191 |
| Lock-wait site | 0x638b0cc |
| Rets | 1 (0x638b087) |
| bsr | 0 |
| shr | 1 (shr $0x3 at 0x638b137) |
| shl | 0 |
| endbr64 | 1 (entry at 0x638afe0) |
| Canary | present (2 %fs:0x28 lines; __stack_chk_fail@plt at 0x638b29b) |
| Jumps | 28 |
| PLT | 3 |
| Prefetch/tzcnt/btc | 0 / 0 / 0 |

## Lock-wait site

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Site | 0x638b0cc |
| Setup | lea -0x40(%r15),%rdi at 0x638b0c8 |
| rdi def | {0x638b0c8} (mutex node 0x6712160) |
| Other argument registers | rsi/rdx/rcx/r8/r9/r10/r11/rax = {CALL(0x638b01b)} (the trylock clobber); rbx = {0x638b004} (entry r9 save); rbp = {0x638affd} (entry rdi save); r12 = {0x638aff9} (entry rcx save); r14 = {0x638afef} (entry rsi save); r13 = {0x638aff4} (entry r8 save); r15 = {0x638afe6} (mutex lea) |
| Predecessors | {0x638b022} (trylock failed; the nopl at 0x638b0dd is padding after the jmp at 0x638b0d8, not a real path) |
| After the call | movb $0x1,0x67121c8 at 0x638b0d1 (waited flag set); jmp 0x638b028 (trylock-SUCCESS block; trylock NOT re-run) |
| Flag clear | movb $0x0,0x67121c8 at 0x638b054 (while lock held, before unlock) |
| Unlock | pthread_mutex_unlock@plt at 0x638b05e |
| Rejoin | trylock-SUCCESS block at 0x638b028 |

## Resolver

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Callee | 0x6388310 (#338's next FDE, 0x6388310..0x6388372, 98 B) |
| Call site | 0x638b094 |
| Input | *(entry rsi + 0x10) (mov 0x10(%r14),%rdi at 0x638b090) |
| Result | direct double-dereference: rax = qword at +0x50 of the resolver result (`mov 0x50(%rax),%rax` at 0x638b099); then qword at +0x9328 of that qword (`mov 0x9328(%rax),%rsi` at 0x638b09d, disp32), stored to (%rsp) at 0x638b0a4 |
| Loader | NONE — 0x63bfb90 is NOT called |
| Adjust | NONE — no fixed inline adjust (no index scale in this window: no lea, no shl; no add $imm,%rdi anywhere) |
| Count call | NONE — 0x634eba0 is NOT called; the count logic lives inside the resolver |
| Resolver internals | Per #373's read of the resolver body: TLS check at 0x638831b (init via 0x63ef8e0 if unset); reads count struct 0x6712130; returns table[index] where index is 0 for rbx == 0x1000 or rbx == 0x1001 or rbx == count, else rbx+2 |

## Selector and copy

The copy IS a Duff's-device loop (0x638b0e0..0x638b247), but it is FULLY DEAD — its dispatch tail is never entered and its 8-at-a-time body is never entered. The length is *r8 (`mov 0x0(%r13),%rdx` at 0x638b0b2, r13 = entry r8); if the length is exactly 8, the qword from the stack temp (%rsp) is stored whole to *rcx (`mov %rsi,(%r12)` at 0x638b0bc, r12 = entry rcx) and the window exits 0 (`xor %ebp,%ebp` at 0x638b0c0). A null dest or null length pointer also exits 0 (`je 0x638b0c0` at 0x638b0ab / 0x638b0b0). Otherwise n = min(len,8) (`mov $0x8,%ecx` at 0x638b0e0, `mov %rsp,%r9` at 0x638b0e5, `cmp %rcx,%rdx` at 0x638b0e8, `cmova %rcx,%rdx` at 0x638b0eb); n < 8 goes to the small tail (`cmp $0x8,%edx` at 0x638b0ef, `jb 0x638b250` at 0x638b0f2), which copies n bytes by 4/2/1 decomposition (0x638b250..0x638b299) and exits 22 with *r8 = n. For n == 8, the first qword is stored to *rcx (`mov %rsi,(%r12)` at 0x638b0fa), re-loaded from the source (`mov -0x8(%r9,%rax,1),%rsi` at 0x638b103, rax == n == 8, set by `mov %edx,%eax` at 0x638b0f8) and stored again to *rcx (`mov %rsi,-0x8(%r12,%rax,1)` at 0x638b10c); then the loop-entry check computes r12d == 0 always (dest-alignment arithmetic at 0x638b0fe..0x638b11a: rcx = (dest+8)&~7, r12 = dest − rcx ∈ [−8,−1], r12d += n (n == 8) ∈ [0,7], r12d &= ~7 → 0) and the `jb 0x638b267` at 0x638b122 is ALWAYS taken to the writeback — the dispatch tail (0x638b128..0x638b1e1, dispatch on (r12d−1)>>3 & 7 via `shr $0x3,%edi` at 0x638b137 and `and $0x7,%edi` at 0x638b13e, `jae 0x638b267` at 0x638b144, seven je entries for edi 0..6) and the 8-at-a-time body (0x638b1e1..0x638b247, back-edge `jb 0x638b1e1` at 0x638b247) are never entered. The writeback stores *r8 = n (`mov %rdx,0x0(%r13)` at 0x638b267) and exits 22 (`mov $0x16,%ebp` at 0x638b26b).

## Calls

| Target | Site | PLT |
|---|---|---|
| 0x63f17b0 (pthread_mutex_trylock) | 0x638b01b | yes |
| 0x6388310 (index resolver) | 0x638b094 | no |
| 0x63f0b70 (pthread_mutex_unlock) | 0x638b05e | yes |
| 0x63bf680 (lock-wait helper) | 0x638b0cc | no |
| 0x63f0d70 (__stack_chk_fail) | 0x638b29b | yes |

No lu-miss, bin_table_init, second-handler, resolver (0x6365150), count call, loader call, or #314–#490 window calls. PLT determination is by `@plt` suffix only: the internal `.text` calls (0x6388310, 0x63bf680) are NOT PLT stubs.

## Shape

The single ret at 0x638b087 returns eax via a single reaching def, `mov %ebp,%eax` at 0x638b07b; ebp's reaching defs are exactly {0x638b048 (1 — lock acquired, caller condition failed), 0x638b0c0 (0 — success), 0x638b26b (22 — copy with length writeback)}, so the three exit values are 0 (success), 1 (lock acquired, caller-side condition failed) and 22 (copy of n = min(len,8) bytes with *r8 = n writeback: len == 8 copies the qword whole and exits 0, n = 8; len < 8 copies via the small tail, n = len; len > 8 copies the first qword, then the loop-entry jb exits to the writeback, n = 8). The small tail's 1-byte copy uses `movzbl (%rsp),%r11d` at 0x638b259, not `%ebp` — there is no `movzbl (%rsp),%ebp` anywhere in this window. author: dbbaskette
body:
## What changes

Every studio's desk is reorganised around the person's work and next move, instead of the pipeline's steps.

- **One arc.** Brief, Plan, Make, Ship is the first thing said about a project in every studio. Each studio's detailed steps stay, one press down.
- **Work first.** The document, deck or page is the middle of the screen. Training Studio and Presentation Studio's slide-text review use three columns: parts, work, and an assistant rail. Blog Studio, Infographic Studio and the slide desk keep their side panels and show the arc in a band above.
- **One move.** A single card says what waits for the person and offers one action, or says that nothing does.
- **Shell kit.** `StudioShell` (`core/studio_core/deck_web/shell.js`) gives every page a command palette (Cmd or Ctrl+K), a Light / Dark / Auto appearance, the progress track, a finish card, and reading mode (F on a desk).
- **Appearance is a shared setting.** `appearance` in the studios config, validated in `studio_core.preferences` with the usual stale-form refusal, and written on each page as it is served.
- **Marketing Studio home** marks saved work as the person's move or as in progress.
- **Blog Studio** renames Full desk to Edit everything and says under the view switch what each view is for.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-golden-gate-3-design.md` and `docs/design/golden-gate.md`.

## Verification

Run locally on synthetic data only:

- Root suite: 1,081 tests pass.
- Training Studio: 3,237 tests pass.
- Blog Studio: 1,901 tests and its page check pass.
- Infographic Studio suite passes.
- Presentation Studio: 2,189 tests; `test_cancel_keeps_the_draft_for_the_session` fails, as it does on `main`.
- Browser: Training Studio's workbench, reading mode and appearance; Presentation Studio's slide-text workbench and slide desk; Blog Studio's desk and review mode; Marketing Studio's appearance save.

Not run: the Playwright journeys and the Tart macOS runner. Infographic Studio's new layout was not seen in a browser. The page harnesses do not load the shell kit, so the arc, move and track are covered by `tests/test_shell_kit.py` and the browser checks, not by the studio page tests.

## Not built

- Answering a decision from Marketing Studio's home, and starting work from there.
- The finish card is in the kit but not yet shown by any studio.

body:
## Why
The mood thread asked for its latest work to go into feat/lofi-app.

Redwood's Claude mood track changes mood 333 times, and the director follows every change in the track. That would make the music change about 24 times an hour.

## What changed
This merges feat/lofiscorekit-mood up to 2705b09 into feat/lofi-app (aabe68b). There were no conflicts. All the code is the mood thread's.

- **MoodSettling (2705b09).** At playback, `TrackedMoodEngine` settles a track into scene-length moods.
  - On Redwood that gives about 6 changes an hour, on a mood the track's own reading lists 95% of the time.
  - A scene only starts on an entry whose own mood it is, so no music plays before its own text.
  - `TrackedMoodEngine(store:fallback:)` settles by default; `settling: nil` turns it off.
  - Track files are unchanged, so no book needs rescoring.
- **`Tools/eval/track_stats.py` (6050ec2).** Shows how restless a track makes the music, and what settling would do.
- **`make-tracks.sh`** gains an optional `--refine-budget`.

The atmosphere side isn't affected. lofi-atmosphere and `LofiAtmosphere` don't read mood readings from `TrackedMoodEngine`. Only `LofiMusicHost` and the mood tools use it.

## Testing
- Docker, Swift 6.4.2: `swift build --build-tests` passes, and `swift test` passes (all XCTest suites, plus 23 + 77 swift-testing tests).
- `node tools/fork/check-fork.mjs` passes.
- No Mac or Xcode build has been run on this head yet. There's no CI on PRs into feat/lofi-app.

body:
Adds the CLV check to the NFL (and college football) model, and a replay of the NFL model against ESPN's openers.

**Code**
- Every spread and total pick carries `clv`: points the line moved toward it since ESPN's opener (`homeSpreadOpen` / `totalOpen`, already parsed).
- `summarizeModel` returns a CLV summary; the model page gets a **★ Line moved our way** card.

**What the replay found (site model, 2023-26, 665 games with ESPN openers, `research/football/scripts/nfl_open_replay.test.ts`)**

| Picks | At the close | At the open | Line moved toward / against |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every spread pick | 51.2% | 50.3% | 39% / 35% (made at the open) |
| ★ spreads (home dog 7+, bounce-back, QB style) | 58.2% (n=146) | 54.0% | 29% / 49% |
| ★ wind unders | 53.8% (n=143) | 56.2% | 59% / 21% |

- The everyday picks hug the line (edges under 1.5 pts) and don't beat the opener: no change.
- **★ wind unders: bet early.** Books lower the total as the wind forecast firms up.
- **★ spread rules: bet late.** The line drifts away from those sides during the week, so the closing number is better.
- Samples are small (~140 each); treat the timing as a lean, and the CLV card will show whether it holds.

author: jonringer
body:
## Problem

`ekaos/modules/module-list.nix` listed 708 modules, but 580 of those files didn't exist. Any EkaOS system built through `ekaos/default.nix`, or through the ekaos tests, failed immediately:

```
error: path '.../ekaos/modules/programs/_0xffff.nix' does not exist
```

**Where they went:** 4a7ad8252 ("modules: remove trivial enable+package-only modules") deliberately deleted 580 generated modules that only exposed `enable` and `package` (`git log --diff-filter=D`). That commit didn't update `module-list.nix`. The deletion was intended, so this PR prunes the list rather than restoring the files.

With the list pruned, evaluation got further and hit a second error. corepkgs (at the pinned rev) now ships `ekaos/modules/virtualisation/docker.nix`, which declares `services.docker` for its service plumbing. That collides with ekapkgs' own `services/docker.nix`:

```
error: The option `services.docker.enable' in `.../corepkgs/ekaos/modules/virtualisation/docker.nix' is already declared in `.../ekaos/modules/services/docker.nix'.
```

## Fix

- **`ekaos/module-list`:** drop the 580 dangling entries. The remaining entries all exist, and their order and section comments are unchanged.
- **`ekaos/docker`:** remove the ekapkgs module. The corepkgs `virtualisation.docker` module covers the same ground (`package`, `storageDriver`, `liveRestore`, `extraOptions`, `autoPrune`) and adds `logDriver`, `enableOnBoot` and `rootless`. The only option that goes away is `dataRoot`.
- **`ci`:** add `ci/module-lists.sh`, a builtins-only check (no package set is evaluated) that fails if `module-list.nix` or `home-module-list.nix` names a missing file. It runs in the `eval` job before `ci/eval.sh`.

## Verification

- **Before (master):** `(import ./ekaos { configuration = <minimal config>; }).config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath` failed with the missing-path error above.
- **After:** a minimal config (systemd-boot, a root filesystem, `programs.steam.enable`, `hello`) evaluates to `/nix/store/b122kigz…-ekaos-system-ekaos.drv`, and the same config with `virtualisation.docker.enable = true` evaluates too.
- **`ci/module-lists.sh`:** passes on this branch. Run against master's list, it fails and names the missing paths.
- **`ci/eval.sh`:** All 9921 packages evaluate.
- **Formatting:** `nixfmt-rs --check` and `nixfmt --check` pass on the changed files.

## Open questions

- **ekaos tests still fail to evaluate:** `ekaos/tests` (`alsa`, `jack`, `pipewire`) now get past the module list but stop on option drift against corepkgs:
  - `services/alsa.nix` uses `systemd.services.*.unitConfig`.
  - `services/jack.nix` uses `systemd.services.*.partOf`.
  - The pipewire test sets `users.users.*.password`.

  This is left for a follow-up.
- **`ekaos/modules/languages/{dart,elm,helm}.nix` aren't listed:** they import a `./lib.nix` that doesn't exist, so I left them out.
- **corepkgs `virtualisation.docker` drops `extraOptions`:** it declares the option but doesn't pass it to `dockerd`. That's a corepkgs follow-up.
- **`doc/options.nix` workaround:** it filters the list with `builtins.pathExists`, which is no longer needed. I left it as is.

author: wieslawsoltes
body:
Follows #436 (merged).

## Why

A profile of a text-heavy scene (about 800 glyph runs a frame, a small set of glyphs) shows 62 % of the render thread in the byte-wise content hash: the outline segments of every run travel through the scene stream each frame and are hashed about four times (scene content identity, glyph resource identity, glyph payload, raster identity of every glyph). The work per frame was proportional to outline size, not to the number of glyph instances.

## What changes

**Glyph outlines by key.** An outline is registered with the engine once and a frame names it with a few words.

- `progpu_native_engine_register_glyph_outlines(engine, outlines, outline_count, segments, segment_count)`: registers outlines under `progpu_native_glyph_outline_key { face, glyph, variant }`. All of a call or none. A key held with the same bounds and segments is left as it is; other content under a held key is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- `progpu_native_engine_release_glyph_face(engine, face)`: forgets the outlines of a face. The face number is refused afterwards, so a key names the same content for as long as the engine lives.
- `progpu_native_scene_builder_add_glyph_keys(builder, keys, key_count, resource_index)`: a glyph resource that is a table of `progpu_native_scene_glyph_key { outline, raster_scale, subpixel_x }` (24 bytes), flagged `PROGPU_NATIVE_SCENE_GLYPH_OUTLINE_KEYS`. Glyph run draws take it; resources that carry their outlines work as before.
- The registry resolves a key to a serial that is never given a second time. The glyph atlas keys a keyed glyph by (serial, raster scale, subpixel phase), so no outline byte is read or hashed for a glyph the atlas holds.
- Keys are resolved when a frame is rendered: a frame that names a key the engine does not hold fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Whether the engine holds an outline is not a property of the stream, so `update_scene` accepts it.
- The registry needs no device and survives device loss.

**Word-wise content hash.** `append_content_hash64` replaces the byte-wise `append_fnv1a64` for the content identities that stay. Audit before the change: no hash value is written to a file format and no test compares one against a fixed vector. The `payload_hash` values of the frame metrics change; `tests/ProGPU.Native.PackageConsumer/PathCoverageProbe.cs` prints them and `docs/native-path-first-frame-isolation.md` quotes values from an earlier run, both as diagnostics only.

The ABI change is additive; `PROGPU_NATIVE_ABI_VERSION` is unchanged.

## The glyph sharing fixture

The fixture is the one of `main`: a scene drawn at another DPI scale drops the retained glyph coverage and rasterizes it again (variants 7 and 8), as the engine does since #436. An earlier commit of this branch changed the fixture to require reuse across a DPI change; the last commit takes that back, so this PR does not change the fixture.

## Tests

- `ctest`: 48 of 48 pass (macOS arm64, Release, Metal).
- New in `progpu_native_internal_tests` and the scene builder tests: registry (all or nothing, same content, other content, released face), keyed atlas map, key and stream validation, the word-wise hash, the keyed builder.
- New `bindings/rust/progpu-native-sys/tests/glyph_keys.rs` (GPU): a keyed run draws exactly the pixels of the run with its outlines in the frame; a glyph many runs name is rasterized once and a later frame that moves glyphs stages no coverage; a frame draws only keys the engine holds (unregistered, other content, released face).
- `eng/progpu-verify-native-exports.sh` passes for `progpu_native`.

## Not verified here

- The managed P/Invoke declarations and contract tests are not regenerated for the three new entry points.
- `eng/progpu-native-dawn-exports.txt` is updated by hand; the Dawn library and `eng/progpu-verify-native-dawn-header.sh` were not built or run.
- Only plain glyph run draws take a keyed resource: the builder and the stream validation refuse it for RGB and painted glyph draws. A test covers the refusal of a keyed record with the color bitmap flag; no test covers a painted or RGB draw that names a keyed resource.
- The atlas keeps the tiles of a released face until it restarts; nothing reclaims them earlier.

author: poitee
body: Fixes GRE-1227 Ports Node's add-to-queue route to Rust as `POST /api/v2/printer-send-queue`, behind `desktop_rebuild` and `PP_DESKTOP_REBUILD`. The route stages one sliced file and writes a `queued` row. It creates no upload job and wakes no worker, so nothing reaches a printer until the user presses Send now or Send ready. ## What changed - `pp-storage` `send_queue::writes`: - `Request::Admit` authenticates before the route reads the upload. - `Request::Add` checks that the Plan is the user's (404 `Profile not found`), applies the existing Farm refusal, and inserts the item last in stored order. It runs in one writer transaction. - `writes/enqueue.rs` holds `NewItem::parse`, which reads Node's form fields and refusals in Node's order, and Node's file-name sanitizer. - `pp-core` `QueueTargets`: - `host` refuses every host that isn't `Host::Read`. It uses Node's enqueue texts, including `Queue is not supported for `. - `stage` writes `exports/printer-uploads//` and refuses any name that is more than one path component. - Send now's printer check now goes through the same `readable` helper. - `pp-api`: - The new `add` handler runs, in order: credential, 10-per-minute rate window, form, host, stage, storage. The route takes bodies up to 64 MiB + 1 MiB. - The staged directory is deleted unless the item was written or storage's outcome is unknown. - The multipart reader moved from `file_assignments.rs` to `multipart_form.rs` with per-route limits, so both upload routes share it. About 300 of the changed lines are this move; the file-assignment upload behaves the same. - `docs/send-queue.md` gains an Add to queue section with every answer and the known differences from Node. `docs/desktop-rebuild.md` rewords one bullet and doesn't grow. **Provisional (reversible):** Rust checks the printer before the Plan, while Node checks the Plan first. Rust always answers 400 for a Bambu host, where Node answers 403 while the Bambu Module is off. Rust refuses a disabled linked host; Node queues for it. Both lists are in the doc. **Size.** 1,085 lines added and 211 removed against `origin/main`. That is over the 300–600 target and under the 1,500 ceiling. About 310 lines move the multipart reader, about 560 are tests, and about 90 are docs; new production code is about 350 lines. Splitting the reader move into its own PR would add a merge wait and leave a refactor with no user. I kept one PR (provisional; the coordinator can ask for a split). **Overlap.** #1648 renames `tests/ticket_t_26_send_queue_http.rs` to `send_queue_http.rs` with no content change. Git carries this PR's edits across the rename whichever merges first. **Not sensitive.** The PR adds no schema, migration, storage-format, auth or secret change. It inserts into the existing `printer_send_queue` table and reuses the existing credential admission. **GRE-1267 is not folded in.** This PR is already past the brief's ~600-line target. GRE-1267's `wait_for_idle` cases still need a way to build `pp_gateway::MoonrakerStatus` in tests. The host refusal it asks about ("anything that isn't Host::Read") is now tested through the real `queue_host`, including bambu, octoprint and unlinked printers. `operations.json` is unchanged: the `/api/v1` route stays `compat` (Node), like dispatch, drain and remove. The route is not in the generated rust-client either; neither are the other send queue writes, and a multipart body doesn't fit the JSON contract. ## Evidence - `cargo clippy --locked -p pp-api -p pp-core -p pp-storage --features pp-api/desktop_rebuild,pp-core/desktop_rebuild,pp-storage/desktop_rebuild --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - `cargo nextest run --locked -p pp-api -p pp-core -p pp-storage --features -E 'test(ticket_t_26) | test(add_to_queue) | test(the_form) | test(file_assignment) | test(upload) | binary(file_assignments_http)'`: `106 tests run: 106 passed (2 slow), 1846 skipped`. - New tests: - `add_to_queue_stages_the_file_and_queues_an_item_without_sending`: 200 `queued`, no durable job, no worker wake. It also covers a 3 MiB file (past axum's 2 MB default) and checks the item is ordered after the stored one. - `add_to_queue_refuses_a_bad_form_or_printer_before_staging`: seven refusals, and nothing is staged. - `add_to_queue_deletes_the_staged_file_when_storage_refuses_the_item`: the staged file is deleted after a Plan or Farm refusal. - `add_to_queue_needs_a_valid_session_before_it_reads_the_upload`: 401 with nothing staged, and 415 for a body that isn't multipart. - `add_to_queue_takes_only_a_read_host_and_stages_inside_printer_uploads` (pp-core, real `queue_host` and `stage`): bambu, octoprint, unlinked and unknown printers; hostile names; Remove deletes the staged directory. - `the_form_is_refused_in_node_order` and `the_form_keeps_node_defaults_and_base_names`: `../../x.gcode`, `..\..\x.gcode` and `C:x.gcode` all stay one file name. - No test contacts a printer. The HTTP tests use a fake `SendTargets`, and the pp-core test points the host at `127.0.0.1:9` and never sends. - `pp-check pr` (`local-ci.py --fast`, `PP_SCHEMA_PARITY_NODE` = Node v22.23.3) at a1bb14b0: 21 passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped. - `nextest-affected`: 2,566 tests run, 2,566 passed. - The failure was `clippy-limits`: `too_many_lines` with `desktop_rebuild` on was 196 against a baseline of 195. The new refusal test was 103 lines, so I split it in two. - After merging `origin/main` (16704f10, docs and guidance only), `pp-check iter clippy-limits,agent-guidance,fmt,duplication` at 0472c35d: 4 passed, 0 failed. `too_many_lines` is back to 195 of 195. The send-queue and file-assignment HTTP binaries: 23 tests run, 23 passed. - SKIP `rust-windows`: needs a Windows runner, so CI runs it. - SKIP `rust-macos`: needs a macOS runner. - SKIP `pr-evidence`: reads the PR body, so CI checks it. - Review: a fresh-context subagent reviewed the diff and found no P0 or P1 issues. Both P2s are fixed in this head: - On Windows, a drive-relative name could put the staged file outside `exports`. `:` is now replaced and `stage` requires a single path component. - Any storage error left the staged file behind. It is now kept only when `may_have_written` says the outcome is unknown. Its P3 parity notes (multipart limit texts, disabled host, the order of the blank-name refusal) are documented as known differences. - `python3 scripts/maintainability-report.py --rev HEAD`, compared with `--rev origin/main` (`--base` isn't on main). Rows that differ: | Measure | origin/main | HEAD | | --- | --- | --- | | Rust lines, tracked | 302,164 | 302,988 | | pp-storage lines (src / tests / files) | 103,098 / 41,146 / 236 | 103,414 / 41,146 / 237 | | pp-storage `pub fn` / `pub struct\|enum\|trait` | 456 / 603 | 459 / 604 | | `desktop_rebuild` cfg attributes in src | pp-api 47, all 832 / 1,150 | pp-api 48, all 833 / 1,151 (on `mod multipart_form;`) | Files named after tickets (63), `tenant`/`profile` lines (67/159), cross-crate `#[path]` includes (67) and pp-api rusqlite files (11) are unchanged. author: wladku
body:
## Summary

Fixes the code-level follow-ups of #221 (review findings of PR #210, E08-S02 staff rentals). The issue stays open: the remaining items need an approval, a dependency or a product decision (see below).

- **Closure undo and redo (Low).** The undo of `facilities.closures.update` and `.delete` takes the occupancy lock first, like execute. An undo that puts a closure back (undo of delete, undo of an update that moved it) and a redo of create or of a moving update flag the sessions, rentals and internal bookings under it **after the replay transaction commits** (`onTransactionLifetimeComplete`, the pattern from lesson `undo-event-waits-for-replay-commit`). A rolled-back replay flags nothing. Before this change, a closure restored by undo over a rental entered in the meantime never flagged it `needs_reschedule`.
- **Lifecycle `updatedAt` (Nit).** `facilities.rentals.advance_lifecycle` sets `updatedAt: new Date()`. The CLI's `--now` still decides which rentals have ended.
- **Dead check (Nit).** Removed `row.chargeId == null` on rental create.

## Left open on #221

| Item | Why |
|---|---|
| M1: `em` on the foundation `OccupancyContext` | Contract change (Ask First), no recorded approval |
| L2: a move does not re-date the charge | Waits for `payments` DD-19 |
| L3: rental dialog uses the browser's time zone | Every facilities admin screen converts wall times in the browser (`rentals-client.ts`). A fix needs the club time zone on the client for all of them; same class as #231 |
| L4: existing clubs get the schedule only on setup re-run | Applies to every `seedDefaults` schedule in every module; needs a generic backfill |
| L5: week preview omits parent-place rentals | Needs a place-family filter on the rentals list API |
| Move keeps the old amount | Product owner decision |
| `lockSchedule` key change and rolling deploys | No code change helps the one overlap window. Going back to the old key would split the lock again |

## Tests

- `yarn verify`: `all 14 step(s) passed`.
- `yarn test:integration:vereino --filter TEST-027`: `4 passed`. The new case covers undo of delete, undo of update and redo of create; each flags a rental entered on the freed slot. The redo step gives the admin's platform role `audit_logs.redo_self`, as TEST-F01 does, because no Vereino role grants redo.

UI: n/a (commands only). Run log: `.ai/runs/2026-11-10-issue-221-rental-follow-ups.md`.

body:
Five fit-side bugs, one commit each, red→green (each commit message carries the red and green output).

- **gh#1016** Every failing method exit records its findings and report. `abandon_method` takes `&Out`, which knows the method's leaf, and writes `diagnostics.json`, then a `failed` `method_report` in `events.jsonl`, then the error. IF2's watchdog, chain-worker and loglik-eval exits and NLopt's runner exits used to write neither. `abandon_method_on`, `fail_recording_findings` and four runner-side `write_diagnostics_then_fail` calls are gone. Test: `gh1016_runner_exits_record_findings.rs`.
- **Resumed PGAS NUTS counters** (divergences, max tree depth, post-burn-in and total) restarted at 0 while being judged against the whole chain: a resume printed 86/200 sweeps (43%, warning) where the chain had 172/200 (86%, error). `NutsCounts` is carried in `ChainResumeState`. Fixed-seed draws and traces byte-identical (`cmp`). **Breaking:** an older PGAS `resume_state.bin` cannot be resumed.
- **Resumed progress** counted from 1 (`1/2500` after resuming from step 2000) on the plain line and in `events.jsonl`; it now reports the chain's own step. The run spec had documented the bug and is corrected.
- **A second identical `--resume`** failed with "artifact already completed"; it is now a cache hit, as the spec's same-inputs-same-leaf rule says (the reuse check had been skipped for resumes on reasoning gh#1015 made obsolete).
- **`mh` recorded its log-likelihood as `marginal`** in `fit_state.toml`, the report, `fit summary` and `fit table`, while progress said `ode_marginal`. It is `ode_marginal` everywhere now (it scores the ODE skeleton).

Gate: full `make test` green (lint, OCaml, goldens, Rust, inference, integration, docs, cli-docs, install); clippy clean per commit; `facts.tsv` unchanged.

Fixes #1016

author: beatzball
body:
Part of #252. Phase 6, pull request 1 of 2: the shell learns what a real App Store app needs, with qdoku as the first. Pull request 2 will make qdoku call the bridge and matrix CI over both apps.

## Why

The demo could never ship. It starts on localhost, which is correct for development. But nothing in the shell could carry an icon, a per-app version or a per-app build number. An upload with no icon is refused by App Store Connect, and nothing before the upload would have said so.

## What changed

- **`native/Apps/qdoku/`**: `com.qdoku.app`, start URL `https://qdoku.com/`, one allowed origin. The origin is confirmed in qdoku's `docs/DEPLOY.md` and live (`/api/health` answers ok).
  - Capabilities are `haptics`, `share` and `review`. qdoku will call all three in pull request 2: haptics where it already uses the Vibration API (which iOS ignores), share from the level-complete screen, review after a milestone.
  - Notifications, badging and secure storage are off. A capability the page never calls shows a reviewer nothing.
- **The icon** is one 1024x1024 image in `Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset`, rendered from qdoku's own vector art: square, with no alpha channel.
  - `select-app.sh` copies the catalog into `Build/Resources/` and sets `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME`.
  - Measured, not assumed: Xcode runs `actool` on it there. The built app has `Assets.car`, its Info.plist has `CFBundleIconName = AppIcon`, and the simulator home screen shows the crown.
- **`version` and `build` are per app, required in `app.json`**, and must be one to three whole numbers. They are no longer shared in `Shell.xcconfig`.
  - They live in `app.json` so the number that shipped is in the history. A command-line setting still overrides either for one build.
- **Only `app.json` and `Assets.xcassets` reach the bundle.** Anything else in the app folder is named and left out. `select-app.sh` validates everything before it clears `Build/`.
  - New `select-app.sh --self-test`, run in CI.
- **The release guard refuses an app with no icon.** It checks existence by stat only, because the build phase is sandboxed and declaring the icon set as an input would break the demo.
  - A Release build of qdoku passes. The demo still fails: on its start URL, its allowed origin, and its icon.
- **`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false`**: the shell uses only system HTTPS.
- **CI** now builds qdoku for Release instead of patching the demo's `app.json`. It asserts the icon, `Assets.car` and the encryption key, and requires the demo's refusal to name the missing icon.
- **NATIVE-019** records the icon trap. The stale comment in `check-release-config.sh` about `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` in Release is fixed.

## Verified

- `select-app.sh --self-test`: 17 checks OK. `check-release-config.sh --self-test`: OK, including 4 new icon cases.
- Release build of qdoku: `check-release-config: OK - https://qdoku.com/, 1 allowed origin(s)`, BUILD SUCCEEDED.
  - Built Info.plist: `CFBundleShortVersionString 1.0.0`, `CFBundleVersion 1`, `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption false`, `CFBundleIconName AppIcon`, no `NSAppTransportSecurity`.
- The same build with its icon set removed fails: `error: this Release build cannot be uploaded: the icon set AppIcon.appiconset is not in Build/Resources/Assets.xcassets.`
- Release build of the demo fails with three guard errors: start URL, allowed origin, no icon.
- Debug build of qdoku on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator loads qdoku.com in the shell, and the home screen shows its icon.
- `swift test --package-path native`: 181 tests, 0 failures. Spelling and doc-reference checks pass.

## Seen, not changed

qdoku's how-to-play dialog runs off the right edge on this screen size. Mobile Safari on the same simulator shows the same, so it is qdoku's layout, not the shell's.

author: mihazs
body:
## What changed

Fix the v1.28.0 report where Agent view said “No agent conversation for this terminal” while Claude and Codex were running in Herdr. It now reads live agents from the attached server. Users select a running session to open the matching reported conversation or enter its exact Herdr pane; Agent view no longer offers a transcript-file picker. Herdr’s reported pane association is disclosed as unverified and grants no terminal input authority.

Android finger swipes no longer become terminal wheel/arrow input inside Herdr agent questions. A separate guarded host operation changes retained history after checking the original attached client, exact runtime and viewport. Unsupported hosts/panes report unavailable without sending input. Ordinary mouse wheels keep their behavior.

## Why

Part of #1120 and #7. The affected host was verified to run stock Herdr 0.9.3 on the development machine. Its live agent list sees both agents, but Agent view previously consulted only tmux hook identity. Finger-generated wheel events could reach alternate-scroll handling and change menu selections.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] Native client clippy with all targets passed with warnings denied.
- [ ] Full workspace tests are not run locally; focused owning suites below.
- [x] 233 focused client tests; client typecheck.
- [x] Native guard suite: 15 passed, including strict unknown-field rejection, target/generation/bounds validation and binding preservation.
- [x] Current-source isolated Herdr host: 25 guard tests passed.
- [x] Actual isolated server/PTY acceptance: history moved both directions, foreign credentials/targets and out-of-viewport requests rejected, receiver stayed empty, original input binding remained usable.
- [x] Android instrumentation compiled; 39 host/oracle tests passed.
- [ ] Android device execution requires CI/KVM. The new fixture paints a synthetic question and checks trusted finger delivery, unchanged selection and the existing exact receiver ledger.
- [x] Herdr provenance/contracts: 7 passed, 9 environment-gated skips.
- [x] Zero-clone pre-commit gate.
- [x] Independent bounded source review found no additional supported defect.

## Commit attribution

- [x] Verified intended author name/email on the commit.

## Release impact

- [x] **Patch**: restores detection and prevents swipe-generated question input.
- [ ] **Minor**
- [ ] **Major (breaking)**
- [x] Branch started from current main and targets main; no stacked branch.
- [x] Open PR search found no duplicate fix.

## CHANGELOG (merge gate)

- [x] Added Unreleased entry.
- [x] Changed default: Herdr finger scrolling requests history only and never falls back to wheel/arrow input; ordinary mouse wheels unchanged.
- [x] Added patch changeset.

## Notes for reviewers

Stock Herdr 0.9.3 can use agent detection; reading a selected session requires the updated companion. Inner pane history needs the optional guarded host with the new methods. The first history route supports the owned display's focused pane; other panes fail closed. Installing a binary does not update an already-running server. The live development server was not restarted or replaced. Cancellation is observational: an already-dispatched operation cannot be recalled.

Temporarily closed prepared test-only #1163, preserving its branch, to prioritize this regression within the ten-open-PR limit.


## Selected running-session integration

A current-source isolated Linux GUI → SSH → Herdr → native resolver → companion test passed, opening a synthetic Codex session while verifying zero original receiver bytes and no transcript picker. The source-built companion read 10/10 live Herdr references on the development host. Seven resolver tests cover duplicate/missing IDs, size limits, retained-directory swaps and fork lineage; native identity matching, frontend race tests, focused browser cases, typechecks and duplicate gate passed. Selected conversations disclose that Herdr's pane association is unverified. Large recordings are reread per serialized poll; the sampled 34.6 MB session used approximately 144 MB peak RSS and 0.88 seconds locally. Physical Android and real Codex UI acceptance remain pending.

   - **`reproduce_mesa_ii.py` (`#117`, Paxton et al. 2013, ApJS, 208, 4)**:
     - `mesa_ii_giant_planets.png`: Irradiated $1\,M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$ radius contraction $R_p(t)/R_{\mathrm{Jup}}$ (`star.e2e.eval_planetary_irradiation_heating`) and interior $T(P)$ profiles.

   - **`reproduce_mesa_iii.py` (`#118`, Paxton et al. 2015, ApJS, 220, 15)**:
     - `mesa_iii_binary_rlof_and_jdot.png`: Ritter (1988) optically thin (`binary.eval_ritter_mdot_thin`) vs. Kolb & Ritter (1990) optically thick (`binary.eval_kolb_mdot_thick`) Roche-lobe overflow rates and Peters (1964) GW / Tauris & van den Heuvel (2003) orbital evolution.
     - `mesa_iii_weak_rates_urca.png`: Degenerate $A = 23, 25$ weak electron-capture/$\beta^-$ rates and Urca shell thermal neutrino cooling spikes.
     - `mesa_iii_hllc_shock_and_ccsn.png`: HLLC Riemann shock-tube profiles (`StarModel.eval_riemann_profile`, `star.eval_hllc_face_jax`) and Type II-P supernova Duffell (2016) Rayleigh-Taylor mixing (`star.e2e.eval_duffell_rti_shock_state`).
   - **`reproduce_mesa_iv.py` (`#119`, Paxton et al. 2018, ApJS, 234, 34)**:
     - `mesa_iv_conv_premix_and_predictive.png`: Convective premixing (`StarModel.do_conv_premix`) neutral-buoyancy alignment $\nabla_{\mathrm{rad}}/\nabla_{\mathrm{ad}} \to 1$ and core-helium burning (`CHeB`) core mass evolution.
     - `mesa_iv_diffusion_and_levitation.png`: Burgers multi-component atomic diffusion (`StarModel.do_element_diffusion`), ${}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$/${}^{58}\mathrm{Ni}$ radiative levitation $g_{\mathrm{rad},i}$ vs. $g$, and surface abundance shifts.
     - `mesa_iv_rsp_periods_and_lightcurves.png`: Linear non-adiabatic (`LINA`) double-mode Petersen diagram (`star.eval_rsp_lina_modes`) and nonlinear Cepheid light and radial velocity curves.
   - **`reproduce_mesa_v.py` (`#120`, Paxton et al. 2019, ApJS, 243, 10)**:

author: zidage
body:
Phase S2 of the [storage query boundary plan](docs/roadmap/alcedo_studio/storage/storage_query_boundary_plan.md#phase-s2-typed-key-mapper-and-one-transaction-style) (tracking #785). Stacked on #794 (S1); the base is `refactor/duckorm-typed-statements-786`.

Closes #787

## Why

The Mapper API took text WHERE clauses and key format strings, so stores interpolated values into SQL text (`commit_hash='{}'`). Mapper batch methods opened their own transaction, so a store could not call them inside its own transaction, and storage had three transaction styles. `CommitGraphStore` called the DuckDB C API 73 times and built 13 statements with `std::format`. `ImageStore::RemoveImageByPath` pasted an unquoted path into its statement.

## Change

- **Typed keys.** Each Derived mapper names its `primary_key_column_`. `GetById`, `RemoveById`, and `UpdateParams` build `(key = ?)` with a bound value (`MapperKey`: integers that fit `int64_t`, or `std::string`). WHERE input is `SqlFragment` only (`GetWhere`, `RemoveWhere`, `GetRowsByQuery`). The text overloads of Mapper and of `duckorm::select/update/remove` are deleted.
- **One transaction style.** Mapper methods open no transaction. The public `begin_transaction`, `commit_transaction`, and `rollback_transaction` are deleted; `ElementStore`, `ImageStore`, and `CommitGraphStore` use `duckorm::Transaction`.
- **CommitGraphStore on duckorm.** Every statement runs on `Statement`, `execute`, `scalar<T>`, `query<Row>`, `query_one<Row>`, or Mapper key methods, with row structs for the label, root state, attribution, id, and history JSON reads. `commit_graph_store.cpp` has zero `duckdb_` symbols outside its includes.
- **Bound values in the sleeve and image mappers.** `FolderMapper`, `FileMapper`, `ElementMapper`, `ImageMapper`, `PipelineMapper`, and `ImageStore` bind names, paths, and types. `GetElementByName`, `GetImageByName`, and `GetImageByPath` pasted their text unquoted before this change; each call failed in DuckDB, and now each one returns the matching rows. `RemoveImageByPath` is deleted.
- duckorm additions: `expr::in_list` for text values (bound), and `duckorm::Connection`.

Persisted rows and SQL results are unchanged.

## Tests (debug build)

- `MapperCrtpRoundtripTest` 8/8, new: `GetByIdReturnsNulloptForMissingKey`, `RemoveByIdBindsTextKeyWithQuote`, `BatchInsertJoinsCallerTransaction`, `GetImageByPathBindsPathWithQuote`.
- `CommitGraphTest` 49/49, new: `MaterializeFailureRollsBackVersionRefDelete` (an ImageEditState upsert fails after the VersionRef delete; the prior rows remain).
- `DuckormStatementTest` 24/24, `DuckormExprTest` 10/10, `MaskAssetStoreTest` 5/5.
- Caller suites (`PipelineMapperTest`, `ProjectCompatibilityTest`, `LibraryHistoryAndExportTest`, `AlbumQueryTest`, `FilterServiceTest`, `SemanticStorageControllerTest`, `AiStorageControllerTest`, `ProjectPackageBackendTest`, `LibrarySearch*`, `SleeveFilter*`): 224 passed, 1 skipped, 1 disabled, 1 failed. The failure is `SemanticStoreTest.ExistingSemanticModelWithoutActiveColumnPromotesLatestModel`, which also fails on `main` (#793).
- `alcedo_main` builds.

## Found during the work

#795: `ElementStore::UpdateElementRows` calls `FileMapper::Update`, which runs `ON CONFLICT` on `FileImage`. That table has no key, so the statement fails for every file element. This PR keeps the statement as it was, with the key now bound.

The plan section has the completion record: call chains, detail decisions, and commands.

author: spuder
body:
> 🤖 This pull request was written by Claude (Claude Code), opened on behalf of the repo owner.

## Problem

From a Cameo 3 log over Bluetooth (a 6-sticker sheet):

1. The first mark search answered `   -1` (not found), and the cutter showed a registration error on its screen.
2. The app retried 2 mm lower. The cutter answered `    0` (found) with the error still on its screen, and the app sent the cut.
3. **Abort** sent `ESC EOT`, but the whole sheet had gone to the cutter as **one packet**. The Cameo 3 kept cutting what it had until it was unplugged.

## Change

- **No retry after a real miss on the Cameo 3.** Models get `retryAfterMissedMarks`. The Cameo 3 now stops at the first answered miss, and the error says to unload the mat with the cutter's own button. A search that gets no answer is still retried. The Cameo 4 keeps retrying, because a retry lower down is what finds its square (tuned on hardware). `RegmarkNotFoundError` gains `answered`.
- **One outline per packet.** `ESC EOT` doesn't stop a packet the cutter already has, so the cut is now sent one outline per packet (a long outline still splits at 1024 bytes). Abort then takes effect after the outline being cut. The command stream itself is unchanged, so the golden tests still match upstream exactly.
- **Honest Abort text.** After Abort, the status and the button's tooltip say the cutter finishes the outline it's cutting, and that switching it off stops it at once.
- **Docs:** CLAUDE.md and `docs/cutter-setup.md` record both hardware findings, plus the Bluetooth movement-event behaviour from #20.

## Testing

- New tests: a Cameo 3 stops at an answered miss without retrying or cutting; a retrying model still retries; six squares go as six single-outline packets. The retry and cancel-on-cutter tests were updated for the new behaviour.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (173 passing) and `npm run build` pass.
- Not yet confirmed on hardware: Abort should now stop the cutter after the current outline.

author: nublox
body:
## Goal
Expand native MySQL prepared-cache performance qualification beyond isolated-local loopback to verified TLS and higher concurrent session counts, while strictly limiting scope to a disposable CI MySQL fixture.

## Implementation
- Preserve the original 4-connection/4-global-handle MySQL 8.4.11 test, but strictly admit only recognized GitHub Actions/fixture identities.
- Add a separate pinned MySQL 8.4.13 TLS-required job with an ephemeral CA, 8 concurrent native sessions, global `max_prepared_stmt_count=8`, **256 measured SQL operations per mode across 3 alternating rounds**, and cached hot, uncached and SQL-key-churn scenarios.
- Before measuring, verify native TLS transport, a negotiated session cipher, `require_secure_transport=1`, and rejection of an independent unrelated CA; close any unexpectedly admitted session.
- Independently census SQL-specific prepared handles (0 uncached, exactly 8 cached/churn, 0 after close), confirm correct bound values, and retain redacted latency and handle evidence in a TLS-specific 60-day CI artifact.
- Add deterministic tests for identity admission, wrong ports/versions/flags, distinct CA requirements, missing TLS cipher, server security policy and negative certificate authentication.
- Document differences between TLS and local fixture measurements and their diagnostic limitations.

## Limits
This uses no new runtime dependencies, production driver changes, migrations, retries, or application server config changes. The quota setting is applied only inside the disposable CI MySQL container. Do not treat cross-fixture latency differences as isolated TLS overhead or commercial performance claims.

author: gmeag01
body:
## 변경 내용

- **⑥ 미세조정에 2배 오버샘플링 적용** (`ampcap/optimize.py`)
  - `losses_for`가 이제 `G(..., mode="fft", oversample=True)`를 부릅니다.
  - ⑦ 렌더링(`G.render` = lfilter + 2배 오버샘플링)과 같은 조건이 됩니다.
  - 설계 문서 4.4절(구현 결정 5)과 부록 표를 고쳤습니다. 오버샘플링은 ⑥과 ⑦에서 켜고, ④ 합성 데이터와 ⑤ 인코더 학습은 속도 때문에 48kHz로 둡니다.
- **scipy 1.18 호환** (`ampcap/evaluate.py`)
  - scipy 1.18에서 `disp` 인자가 없어져 `linalg.sqrtm(..., disp=False)`가 `TypeError`를 냈습니다.
  - 인자 없이 부르면 예전 scipy에서도 행렬만 돌려줍니다.

## 이유

⑥이 오버샘플링 없이 48kHz로 맞추면 클리핑 블록의 앨리어싱이 θ*에 섞입니다. 같은 θ*를 ⑦에서 96kHz로 렌더링하면 다른 소리가 납니다.

| 조건 | 장기 평균 스펙트럼 L1 차이 (48kHz vs 96kHz) | 대역별 차이 (48 − 96) |
|---|---|---|
| british 하이게인 | 2.5 | 40~250Hz +5.5dB, 6~16kHz −4.3dB |
| 비교용: 트레블 +0.5dB | 0.08 | |

- 같은 96kHz에서는 FFT 필터와 lfilter의 차이가 0.06뿐입니다. 차이의 원인은 필터 방식이 아니라 샘플레이트입니다.
- FFT 꼬리 감김도 확인했습니다. 꼬리 여유를 8192에서 65536으로 늘려도 결과가 같습니다.

## 리뷰 참고

- ⑥은 스텝당 약 2배 느려집니다.
- 측정에는 실제 곡이나 EGDB가 아닌 합성 기타 DI(Karplus-Strong)와 θ 설정 2개만 썼습니다.
- 실험 1의 가짜 곡은 `G.render`로 만듭니다. 이 변경 뒤에는 θ 되찾기 수치가 달라질 수 있습니다.

## 테스트

Windows CPU(torch 2.15)에서 scipy를 고치기 전에 `pytest tests/`를 돌렸습니다.

- 결과: 97개 통과, 1개 실패, 6개 건너뜀.
- 실패한 1개는 scipy 문제인 `test_metrics_basic`입니다. scipy를 고친 뒤에는 이 테스트가 통과합니다.
- 건너뛴 6개는 다음과 같고, 이번에 돌려 보지 않았습니다.
  - `nam` 2개, `demucs`, `anthropic`, `pedalboard`: 해당 패키지가 설치되어 있지 않음
  - `AMPCAP_NAM_INPUT`이 필요한 Colab 전용 테스트 1개

author: walledmahmoud
body:
## What this changes

**Website pages showing up inside the app.** On a real phone the app sometimes got the website's version of a page: the billing page after switching language on the Account page, a website menu with Home, a footer. The server recognised the app only by its name in the user agent, and a request that arrives without that name got the website.

The app now also carries its own cookie (`listen_app`), set on its first page. Either sign is enough, so every request from the app gets the app's page. The phone's browser has a separate cookie jar and is not affected; the website is unchanged.

**Rows of tabs that slide sideways** (the studio's sections, an agent's pages, the voice filters), in the app:

- the edge fades where more tabs are waiting;
- the tab that is tapped, or lit as the page scrolls, moves to the middle, so the next tabs come into view without having to know the row slides.

## Tests

Full suite: 2,711 passing, 13 skipped. New test: a request with the app's cookie but a plain browser user agent gets the Account page, is redirected away from billing, and has the tab bar with no website menu or footer; a browser without the cookie gets the website. Sliding rows checked on screen at 360×800 in Arabic and English by tapping the last visible tab repeatedly.

## Not verified

The exact request on the phone that arrives without the app's name could not be reproduced here (no Android WebView in this environment). The cookie covers that whole class of request whatever its source.

## After merging

Live: `inspect`, then `deploy`. No migration, no settings change, no new APK.

author: dmetzner
body:
## Problem

We can't tell why uploads fail. On 2026-11-09, 10 of 17 `POST /api/projects` answered 422, and nothing explains why:

- **Format errors** are logged with `warning()`, but prod's main handler is `fingers_crossed` with `action_level: error`. A warning is only written when an error happens in the same request, so these never reach disk.
- **Request validation** (size, checksum, missing file) answers 422 without logging anything.
- **Files over 100 MB** never reach PHP. Cloudflare or nginx answers 413, and the web uploader only finds out after the user waited for the whole upload.

## Fix

**Logging.** A new `upload` Monolog channel, with `upload/upload.log`, 30 rotated files in prod, at info level so it bypasses `fingers_crossed`. `ProjectsApi::projectsPost()` writes one line per attempt with:

- `outcome`: `created` / `rejected` / `failed` / `unauthorized` / `rate_limited`
- `reason`: the validation message or exception class
- `bytes`, `flavor`
- `client`: `app` / `browser`
- `ms`: duration

The custom formatter already adds the IP and user. The logger is injected via the `$uploadLogger` autowiring alias, with a `NullLogger` default for hand-built instances.

**Browser check.** The upload page gets `data-max-bytes` from `ProjectsRequestValidator::MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES`. The uploader shows the existing "file too large" text with the file size and the limit before uploading.

## Tests

`ProjectsApiTest::testARejectedUploadIsLoggedWithItsReason` asserts the info record with outcome, reason, size and flavor. The suite passes 29/29. phpstan and full-project psalm are clean, as are Biome and both Twig linters. I also checked that the container injects the `upload` channel logger.

body:
Fixes the layout on phones. The big one was the scrolling Artist Alley banner: since the text is wider than a phone screen, it was making the whole page way wider than the screen. On iPhone you could scroll sideways, and on Android Chrome it zoomed the whole site out.

**What changed** (CSS only)
- The banner is clipped to the screen on phones so it can't make the page wider. It still scrolls all the way across.
- If someone has reduced motion turned on, the banner doesn't scroll, so on phones it just wraps onto a couple of lines so you can still see and tap "Apply Here".
- The main content box uses the full width on phones with smaller side padding (it had 5em of padding on each side, which was most of the screen, and it was hanging off the left edge on the home page).
- The countdown columns can shrink on phones so the table fits.
- The invisible intro caption image was sitting on top of the banner and blocking the "Apply Here" link part of the time (on desktop too). It ignores clicks now.

Desktop (768px and up) looks the same as before.

**How to test**
- Open every page on your phone: no sideways scrolling, nothing hanging off the edge.
- Tap "Apply Here" when it scrolls by.
- Check desktop looks the same.

Tested in Chrome and Safari (WebKit) from 320 to 414px plus iPhone 13 / Pixel 5 sizes, with and without reduced motion, and together with the mobile nav PR. Merges cleanly with the other PRs.

body:
pwsafe (wxWidgets on GTK 3) isn't wrapped, so it can't find GTK 3's GSettings
schemas and aborts as soon as it opens a GTK file chooser (e.g. "Browse..." in the
open-database dialog) unless the desktop session happens to provide them. On GNOME
on NixOS 26.05, whose session has the GTK 4 schemas but not GTK 3's:

```
$ pwsafe        # then "Browse..."
(pwsafe:122366): GLib-GIO-ERROR **: 20:45:38.470: Settings schema 'org.gtk.Settings.FileChooser' is not installed
Aborted
```

Adding `wrapGAppsHook3` wraps the binary with the GTK 3 schemas and the usual
GIO/GDK environment, as for other GTK 3 apps.

body:
Closes #269

Part of bet #204. **Pains:** S-3 information spread over SIU, campus, Discord and WhatsApp (J 14:33); S-7 SIU has no quick access and feels outdated (I 00:43); P-10 course work split across SIU, campus and Discord (J 08:35, J 14:33). **KR:** bet #204, at least 2 of 3 users of each role finish their main task unaided, and every role path (now including the campus) passes `npm run test:browser` at 390 and 1440 px.

Plan: [`specs/269-campus-shell-frame/plan.md`](https://github.com/HackAI2026/AUREA/blob/269-campus-shell-frame/specs/269-campus-shell-frame/plan.md)

## What changes

- **Shell frame to the campus.** `src/campus/shell-frame.ts` (new) turns the shell's own frame for the request (`shellFrame`, `src/shell/routes.ts`) into the contract `{ v: 1, home, role, roles, who, signOutPath, nav }`, with Campus `current: true, external: false`. `src/campus/proxy.ts` always drops an incoming `x-aurea-shell`, then sets AUREA's (base64url of UTF-8 JSON) when the request has a valid AUREA session. Role by area: `/campus/profesor` and below → teacher, else student. A frame over 4096 bytes is not sent (one warning, without the value); the campus then falls back to its own shell.
- **One sign-out.** `POST /auth/sign-out` also sends `campus_session=; Path=/campus; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=0` (`; Secure` when AUREA's cookies are), the name, path and attributes `campus/app/sso/route.ts` sets. The next `/campus` request goes through the campus middleware to `/go/campus`, and from there to `/sign-in`.
- **Contract fixture** `campus/tests/fixtures/aurea-shell-vector.json` (`{ frame, header }`) for #270 (B3) to decode.

## Done when

| Item | Check |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` passes, one test per Behaviour scenario (proxy tests against a stub upstream that records the headers it got) | `npm test` (172 files passed locally). Scenarios: `test/campus/shell-frame-proxy.test.ts` (student, both roles, forged header, no session, accents and ñ), `test/campus/shell-frame.test.ts` (4 KB limit, encoding, `campusRoleOf`), `test/identity/sign-out.test.ts` (303, both cookies, then `/campus` → `/go/campus` → `/sign-in` with no campus page rendered) |
| The fixture's `header` decodes to its `frame` | `npx vitest run test/campus/shell-frame.test.ts` ("the contract fixture"); or `node -e 'const v=require("./campus/tests/fixtures/aurea-shell-vector.json");console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(Buffer.from(v.header,"base64url"))) === JSON.stringify(v.frame))'` prints `true` |
| `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass | both, locally |

A guard test reads `campus/lib/session-token.ts`, `campus/lib/base-path.ts` and `campus/app/sso/route.ts`, so a change to the campus cookie's name, path or attributes breaks this test, not sign-out in production.

## Adapters

No SIU, Moodle or Zoom call is added or changed. The campus is a stub HTTP server in the tests (records headers; mimics `campus/middleware.ts` without a session). SIU is still reached only through `InMemorySiu` in tests.

## Cuts

- Rendering the frame in the campus: #270 (B3), next.
- Server-side revocation of an already-copied `campus_session` (it expires on its own; **Unverified** whether that is enough for Austral).
- Return-to-page after sign-in: #273 (B2).

## Demo

`just campus-up` and AUREA with `CAMPUS_UPSTREAM_URL` and `CAMPUS_SSO_SECRET` set; sign in as a synthetic student, open Campus, then post Cerrar sesión: the browser lands on `/sign-in`, and opening `/campus` again lands on `/sign-in` too. The header itself is visible once #270 renders it.

## Used in

No UI in this PR (no design-system row); #270 adds the campus's "Used in" row.

author: holm10
body:
## AIUE-226: refuse Braams impurity rates when no table was read

Fixes the out-of-bounds read of `rtlt(1)` in `api/fimp.m:108` (and `:459`) found by the AIUE-95 `--checkbounds`
audit (d_c variant `bbb.newapi`).

**Cause.** `ueinit` resets the Multicharge tables (`rtnt = rtnn = rtnsd = 0`) on every call and fills them only through
`readmc`. With `ismctab = 2`, impurity species and `newapi = 0` (or `nzdf = 0`), no table is read, and the first
`mcrates`/`radmc` call reads `rtlt(1)` of an empty table, then stops in its species search (`*** mcrates could not find
za= 0 zn= 6`).

**Fix (owner decision D1′).** One check in `ueinit` after the impurity block (`bbb/odesetup.m`): when `isimpon` is 4-7,
`ismctab = 2`, `nzspt > 0` and `rtnsd = 0`, stop with `xerrab('*** ueinit: ismctab=2 but no impurity rate tables were
read (newapi=0 or nzdf=0); set newapi=1 and nzdf, mcfilename ***')`. Runs that read tables by another route
(`istabon = 16` through `aphread`) or need none (`isimpon = 7` with `nzspt = 0`) are not refused. `newapi`'s doc line
(`bbb/bbb.v`) says so. The `istabon = 16` / `newaph = 0` path is AIUE-227.

**Default results: unchanged.** Serial bitwise check against the base, complete gate, plus imp7 and large_dd2c by
name: AGREE (serial and OpenMP builds). Only the three INVALID yldot entries `bbb.newapi` of d_c, large_dd2c and imp7
change their `reason` text (kind stays `error`); they are regenerated through `regenerate-references.yml` (run
[42760918518](https://github.com/holm10/UEDGE_v9_dev/actions/runs/42760918518), `--only bbb.newapi`, from 8b6c04d)
and committed as a data-only commit on this PR (owner decision D2), with release
[yldot-data-v18](https://github.com/holm10/UEDGE_v9_dev/releases/tag/yldot-data-v18). The run's `--checkbounds`
audit found no Fortran runtime error in the three variants (before: the `rtlt` out-of-bounds read). imp7's old
reason (`RuntimeError (log: *** For isimpon=7, set afracs, not afrac ***)`) named the wrong line: that is a `remark`
every `isimpon = 7` run prints (`bbb/odesetup.m:1155`). The run failed on the same bare-`RuntimeError` `mcrates`
stop as d_c and large_dd2c (probe on base d6e7f04), and the generator's log heuristic took the last `***` line. The new
reasons carry the `xerrab` text in the exception, so no heuristic is involved.

**Ticket record:** [Plan: AIUE-226 (Confluence page 22183937)](https://holm10uedge.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SD/pages/22183937): plan, validation, reviews
(plan: REVISE then APPROVE; implementation round 1: APPROVE, 0/0/1 MINOR) and owner decisions.

**Not independently verified by the reviewer:** the CI regeneration and Linux results; the full yldot, serial_check and
pytests runs (the reviewer read the logs).

**Known limit (review I1-m1):** no test distinguishes the new refusal from the old `mcrates` failure: the tests
compare only the reason kind (`error`). The regenerated manifests do record the difference (the reason text is now the
`ueinit` refusal), and the checkbounds audit at each regeneration is the guard.

**After merge:** update the `newgeo` reset citation on the Confluence page `UEDGE gotchas` (9437185) to
`bbb/odesetup.m:1185-1187`, as in `.claude/context/uedge-gotchas.md`.

author: parth-surve2007
body:
## Summary

This adds a governed experience-to-skill loop inspired by Hermes Agent's separation of procedural skills, persistent memory and operator-curated learning.

### Learning engine
- Extracts a proposal only from a settled task with at least three completed tool actions across at least two distinct tools.
- Stores argument schemas and result-field names, not run-specific argument values, file paths, document content or raw transcripts.
- Records generalized failure lessons when present in a trace and deduplicates repeated procedures using a deterministic fingerprint.
- Repeated evidence updates an existing proposal rather than creating duplicate skills.

### Governance and reliability
- New skills always begin as `proposed`; only explicit operator approval makes them discoverable to the agent.
- Approved skill content is immutable in place. Content revisions and rollbacks are reviewable; locks prevent edits.
- Usage outcomes are recorded. Two failures flag the skill for review and hide it from the agent's catalog until the operator resolves the review.
- Skill changes and lifecycle actions are recorded in an append-only JSONL history.

### Workbench
- Adds a Learning page for pending proposals, approved skills, review flags, pinning and locking.
- Documents the learning loop and its current limits in README.

### Validation
- Adds regression coverage for multi-action thresholds, privacy sanitization, deduplication, approval, review gates, usage feedback, locking and rollback.
- CI is running on Ubuntu and Windows; the Windows packaging job follows the test matrix.

## Safety scope

This is event-driven procedural learning with human review, not an autonomous background LLM curator. Skills remain guidance, never permission grants. Existing runtime permissions, fresh application observations and postcondition verification remain authoritative for every execution.

author: grahammmm
body:
## [RF1925-10] strip-metadata publishes the cleaned copy only after a complete, synced write

**Defect (reproduced per spec):** `content strip-metadata` opened the final target with `O_EXCL` and wrote straight into it. A write/flush/close error (e.g. ENOSPC) left a truncated file under the requested name, and the retry was refused with "already exists; nothing written".

**Fix (`campaign_tool/image_meta.py`, `strip_file` only):**
- Parse/strip and every existing refusal (suffix, source symlink, existing/dangling target, public/ folder, unreadable image) run first and create no staging.
- Cleaned bytes are written into a private 0700 sibling staging directory (`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=target.parent)`), payload created with `0o644` (umask-filtered, no-follow), all bytes written (short writes looped, zero progress is an error), `fsync`ed and closed.
- Publication is `os.link(payload, target)` (atomic, no-replace). A target that arrives first (file, symlink, dangling symlink, directory) wins untouched and gives the existing `already exists; nothing written` ValueError. A filesystem without hard links fails with no final file.
- Only this call's staging directory is removed; the target is never unlinked in a handler. Abrupt exit before publication may leave a private stage but never a final partial copy; no sweeping.
- Return shape `{"removed": kinds, "written": str(target)}`, default/explicit target names, cleaned bytes and modes unchanged. No cli.py edit.

**Tests (`tests/test_strip_metadata_atomic.py`, 13 tests):** prefix write + ENOSPC then retry; fsync/close failure; fsync→close→link order; short writes and zero-progress write; KeyboardInterrupt; child process `os._exit` at fsync (private remnant, retry works); target arrival (regular, competing clean copy, symlink, dangling, directory); link unsupported; post-commit cleanup failure keeps final; unrelated entries/stage inode-identical; JPEG/PNG/WebP default+explicit+idempotent controls; umask modes; refusals create no stage.

Red on old source: the new module fails (15 failures/errors); old code does not use the os-level write seam, so the prefix test fails there by not raising rather than by observing the 11-byte final file. Green on the fix.

**Outside owned files:** none. `tests/test_personal_data.py` / `test_publish_path_coverage.py` run unchanged (strip_file identity preserved, no new function).

**Checks run:** `python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_strip_metadata_atomic` (13 OK), test_image_meta, test_png_structure, test_personal_data, test_publish_path_coverage, test_site_news OK; `node scripts/scan-secrets.mjs` PASS; prepush PREPUSH-TESTS PASS.

Review routing: independent reviewer per card (codex-reviewer per spec).
