author: vitalykl
body:
## Summary

Stacked on [PR #92 — Revisioned content history and restore API (P1)](https://github.com/vitalyKl/ProjectBeacon/pull/92). This PR remains Draft and unmerged. Do not merge until the complete P1–P7 scope is verified on the final HEAD.

### P1–P2 — revisioned content and proposal lifecycle
- Tenant-scoped immutable content history, optimistic writes and restore API.
- Revision/hash-bound proposals with idempotency, expiry, pending limits, supersession and optimistic lifecycle concurrency.
- Human-only accept/reject, original-author withdrawal, stale-base conflict handling and audit events.
- Atomic acceptance of ordinary content: target mutation, ContentVersion, proposal state and audit are committed together.
- Update is supported for ProjectDescription, ContextSection, Decision, Constraint, Milestone, TaskDescription and RepoPatch.
- Create is supported only for a new Milestone. The server reserves its target ID, uses BaseRevision 0, and creates the Milestone plus initial history atomically on acceptance. Replays with the same idempotency key return the same reserved ID.
- Delete is supported for reviewed ContextSection/Milestone and accepted Decision/active Constraint. ContextSection/Milestone write tombstones and are physically removed; Decision becomes Deprecated; Constraint becomes Rejected.
- Deleted ContextSection/Milestone can be recreated from a prior immutable snapshot only while the latest revision is the matching tombstone. It reuses the target ID and appends a new revision. New tombstones supply lifecycle metadata for older source snapshots that predate review/close fields.
- Decision/Constraint history restore restores recorded lifecycle status as a new revision. For legacy snapshots missing status, restore preserves the current lifecycle state rather than implicitly accepting or activating the target.
- Manual Decision Accept/Deprecate/Supersede and Constraint Activate/Reject transitions append history. Legacy ContextSection approval advances its revision and writes the reviewed snapshot atomically with audit.

### P3 — Actor/MCP proposal workflow
- knowledge_propose, knowledge_proposals and knowledge_withdraw are bound to the live task/subtask/session and project-bound Harness token.
- MCP accepts only supported target/operation pairs; Delete requires an empty payload and exact current baseRevision; Milestone Create omits targetId and uses BaseRevision 0.
- docs-writer remains RepoPatch Update-only with exact-file/text SHA-256 tools and documentation-only path grants.
- knowledge-curator instructions distinguish Update, new Milestone Create and reviewed Delete from legacy Proposed/NeedsReview creation flows.

### P4 — proposal Inbox and content history UI
- Project Inbox counts and review UI for Pending, Conflicted, Applying and completed proposals.
- Shows operation, rationale/author context, editable Update/Create payloads, immutable Delete payloads, structured field diffs (including null/cleared and numeric values) and base-snapshot comparison.
- Create shows the proposed new content rather than a nonexistent base revision.
- Context and Roadmap expose deleted ContextSection/Milestone tombstones and allow restore from the prior snapshot.
- Context exposes ContextSection/Constraint history and restore; Decisions exposes Decision lifecycle history/restore.
- Roadmap milestone details expose every Milestone revision and restore older snapshots without losing linked task associations.
- Project Settings exposes ProjectDescription history and restores nullable descriptions as a new revision.
- Proposal Create renders its proposed content; Delete payload is immutable and Update/Create diffs show structured fields, cleared/null values and numeric metadata.
- Batch acceptance reports each result and refreshes persisted conflict/expiry state.

### P5 — review and Auto policy
- Project decision matrix defaults to Manual and is concurrency-versioned/audited.
- Auto remains restricted to RepoPatch Update, requiring both project policy Auto and docs-writer profile ApplyPolicy Auto.
- Create/Delete and governance changes always require human review; Decision/Constraint changes require Owner/Admin.

### P6 — documentation RepoPatch
- Docs-writer submits immutable unified diff plus per-file base/result SHA-256 manifest; no direct workspace edits.
- Server validates allowed docs/README paths, profile grants, patch headers and manifest before queueing.
- Human approval atomically queues ApplyProposalPatch and marks the proposal Applying. Auto uses the same validated queue only when both Auto switches are enabled.
- Workstation rechecks hashes, applies only remaining patch sections on retry, verifies results and restores pre-attempt state on apply/verification failure.
- Completion is accepted only for matching ProposalId and ApplyCommandId with verified file results; generic device-command enqueue cannot queue ApplyProposalPatch.

### P7 — docs and security
- Authorization matrix, SECURITY.md and AGENTS.md document route policies, Actor binding, untrusted proposal content, secret handling, supported operation pairs and tombstone restore rules.
- GET /proposals/mine is API-token-only at the route and in the authorization inventory.
- PostgreSQL RLS coverage verifies Proposals are isolated by ProjectId. Deleted-target listing and restore are Human-only and project-member-scoped.
- Generic content-version history reads now independently enforce Human project membership/inherited Owner/Admin or a project-bound ApiToken with ContextRead/Admin; TaskDescription is excluded from this generic route.
- Milestone list/get routes now also require project membership (or inherited Org Owner/Admin), validate the route ProjectId, and query by that explicit scope only after authorization; API tests cover outsider denial and cross-project NotFound.

## Verification status

- CI #1081 passed Linux, macOS and Windows at HEAD 5d814b3; it predates the Inbox and Create/Delete work.
- CI #1093 found two earlier issues, both fixed: missing Domain.Entities.Identity import in Milestone lifecycle tests and a stale/fictitious base revision/hash in the Inbox Delete fixture.
- CI #1094 ran on old HEAD 215d28b and exposed a Web bUnit assertion issue, subsequently corrected.
- CI #1124 passed Linux, macOS and Windows at HEAD 0d17423; it predates the final milestone read/mutation authorization updates.
- CI #1128 identified three missing Actor arguments in Backlog, Board and TaskDetail milestone reads. All call sites were updated and the authorization allowlist was reviewed.
- CI #1132 passed Linux, macOS and Windows at HEAD 98d9959.
- CI #1138 passed Linux, macOS and Windows at HEAD 1c0b790. It includes the Owner/Admin requirement for restoring Decision/Constraint history but predates the generic ContentVersion read scope fix.
- CI #1153 passed Linux, macOS and Windows at HEAD 82a9d4f.
- CI #1160 compiled and passed the test modules on its HEAD c2e781f; its only reported failure was the existing whitespace-format guard in the Milestone Delete switch block. That indentation was corrected in commit c6fc030.
- CI #1163 is the current full matrix on HEAD c6fc030. It includes the Milestone and ProjectDescription history UI, their bUnit coverage, and TRX minimum 1547; all platforms are in progress with no failures reported so far.
- PR #93 remains Draft and unmerged. Do not merge until CI on the latest HEAD is green.
## Remaining contract boundaries

Unsupported pairs remain rejected: Create for targets other than Milestone; Delete for ProjectDescription, TaskDescription and RepoPatch; RepoPatch operations other than Update. New Decision/Constraint records and new ContextSection drafts continue to use their existing Proposed/NeedsReview flows. No merge until all jobs and test-result guards pass on the latest HEAD.

body:
## TL;DR

Restrict GHCR publication to the release workflow and exclude competing publishers.

## How it works

The main release workflow runs this command from `apps/infra`:

```bash
npm run mbuild publish -- --ghcr boxlite-ai/boxlite --tag <full-sha> --version v1.2.3
```

The CLI requires that workflow’s publish job. Other invocations fail before registry access and print a dispatch command.

Per-artifact locks exclude competing processes; workflow concurrency owns cross-run exclusion. The dependent workflow integration enables this path.

Verification: `make coverage:infra` → passed, including competing-process and partial-retry tests. This entry point adds a new contract; full-revert defect proof is inapplicable. Live publication untested.

Documentation: [GHCR publication](https://github.com/boxlite-ai/boxlite/blob/ci/ghcr-release-publication/apps/infra/mbuild/README.md#reading-release-images-in-ghcr).

Design doc: https://linear.app/polygala/issue/BUI-1483/design-publish-release-images-to-ghcr-and-deploy-existing-tags

author: dirkwa
body:
## What problem does this solve?

The radar picture took its spoke geometry (spokes per revolution, spoke length, legend) from the radar whose details are loaded, but opened the spoke stream for the selected radar id. On a boat with two radars, the two differ for a moment after switching: the new radar is selected while its details are still loading. If the stream restarts in that window, for example when the tab comes back into view, Freeboard draws one radar's spokes with the other radar's geometry. Raised by CodeRabbit on #1219 and tracked in #1272.

## How does it work?

The stream URL now uses the id of the loaded radar, the same one the geometry comes from, as the acquire request in #1219 does. When the new radar's details arrive, the radar layer's id input changes and it restarts the stream for that radar, as it already did.

## What changes for the user?

Switching between two radars no longer risks a scrambled picture: Freeboard keeps showing the previous radar until the new one has loaded, then switches to the new radar's picture. Single-radar setups see no change.

## How was this tested?

A new spec in `radar-render.service.spec.ts` connects while radar A is loaded and radar B is selected, and expects A's stream URL. It fails without the fix. `npm run format`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build:all` and `npm run test:ci` (3440 tests) pass.

## Checklist

- [x] One logical change; version numbers untouched.
- [x] `features/` untouched — the user-facing change is described above instead.
- [x] Skimmed [`DEV-LESSONS-LEARNED.md`](../docs/freeboard/DEV-LESSONS-LEARNED.md) for traps relevant to this change.
- [x] Tests added/updated for new behaviour and `npm run test:ci` passes.
- [ ] CodeRabbit review completed (re-requested with `@coderabbitai review` after
      the stated wait if it was rate-limited) and every finding acknowledged — fixed,
      or rebutted on its thread.

Fixes #1272

Round 896 1T for #747 (lane BA). It is built on 9d653a5d4 (#946) and committed onto main 80e32763, which moved only in shared-field. DLW build ruling 2026-11-09.

**What it does**
- **Host authority (items 8–21).**
  - Every native command admits its webview first.

- **Field and engine.**
  - A hidden document's field plays on by real time while its sound is open (1W).

- **Git env ruling.** Every test that makes a git repository clears GIT_* from its children. This is pinned by `git-env-isolation-896`.

**Item 23, met by 1T.0.** A frame that is shown again is drawn first, and the held time goes one sub-step per draw. The first cut drew fewer shown-again frames than 08721ea3: per-copy medians of 1T 8 against 10, over runs at load 19–31, which could not judge the pin. Measured again on 1T.0, by item 23's protocol (five rounds, each started at a one-minute load under 8), the per-copy medians are:

| Engine | Copy 1 | Copy 2 |
|---|---|---|
| 08721ea3 | 10 | 10 |
| 1T.0 | 8 | 10 |
| 1T.0 + V2 (flush only where the next step polls) | 10 | 8 |
| 1T.0, cap-take polled only | 8 | 8 |

That is within the pin's 2 frames, so 1T.1 needs no patch of its own. V2 gains nothing on 1T.0 and is not carried.

**Checks (lane BA, on 9d653a5d4 + 1T)**
- Candidate job, every step: test-all 5549, engine 1140, conformance 45, expressions-app 1784, browser harnesses 11/11.
- Kernel 1020; host 73; three tsc roots green.

The Central half is EpiLogos/Central#341, merged.

**1T.0 (this branch, 453c4838, then main merged in twice).** It fixes what #956's two reviews (956a, 956b) and its CI found. DLW build ruling 2026-11-09, items 1–15 and three CI items:
- **The two regressions are fixed.**

  - A hidden field keeps real time. Each timer fire is one wake of at most 2 s of field time, in the engine's capped steps. The backlog stops at 10 s, and the skip is said once when the field is shown again. It is pinned at 1 Hz and 10 Hz within 5% over 60 s.
- **The reviews' pins and nits:**
  - `shownAgain` is required and pinned.

  - Item 22's pins bite. `vendor --verify` compiles and compares.

  - wry is pinned at 0.55.1 with `Started`'s timing.
  - The git census reads more forms.

- **#956's CI:**
  - WebKit's "7 steps in 2 s" was the hidden clock (fixed above).
  - The landing tier's kernel test is two gates (unit 15 min, integration 30 min), and the landing job's limit is 120 min. Measured: #956 adds no work there (instructions retired: lib +0.34%, `expression_act_world` −0.25%). Main's own suite has outgrown 15 min.

    - The legacy capture check now asks every inspection in one task.
    - A cadence beat whose answer comes late is unknown, not refused, and the rejoin's late answer settles it.
- **The host's tests now run in CI** (the macOS native-shell job). Running them locally found that the PTY test was red under bash 3.2, which is macOS's /bin/bash and /bin/sh. bash 3.2 runs the rest of a line after an interrupt. The line now prints the child's status. Green 3 of 3 under SHELL unset, /bin/bash and /bin/zsh, and 30 of 30 with SHELL unset.
  - A second race, a line lost when it is typed at a resize, was reproduced outside the test (1 line in 100–300). The test guards against it, but it was not what made the test red (corrected after review).

- Host fmt, check and clippy ×2; host tests 148/0/2 on the lane's Mac. **On the macOS runner the new step is red (147/1)**, see below.

author: ohadraz
body:
The investigation found CPU rising in step with request volume until it hit the fixed 3.0-core limit, and nothing deployed or changed. That makes CPU cost per request the thing this code controls. Both functions in the account page's figure path do quadratic work for each request:

- `average_spend_per_item` in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` is the default figure, rendered for every request outside the rollouts. For each purchase it re-sums the whole prefix `account.purchases[:index + 1]`, then throws away every sum except the last. That is n(n+1)/2 price reads plus n slice copies to get one total, which a single `sum` over the purchases gives. The fix sums once. The result is unchanged: it is still derived from the purchases, not from the carried `total_cents`. An empty history still raises `ZeroDivisionError` (0 // 0), which the existing boundary test relies on.
- `typical_spend_per_item` in `src/io_shop/typical_spend.py` (behind `typical-purchase-feature`) runs `min` and `remove` over the remaining list about n/2 times, which is also O(n²). The fix sorts once and indexes the lower middle, `(n - 1) // 2`. That picks the same element the old loop did, including repeated prices and the lower middle of an even-length history. An empty history still raises `ValueError`, as the old `min([])` did.

The more history a shopper has, the faster per-request cost grew, so the pods hit the CPU limit at a much lower request rate than the work needs. This change doesn't remove the fixed limit or the autoscaling settings in `deploy/values-production.yaml`. It cuts how much CPU each page costs, so the same cores serve more requests before they queue. Nothing has run these changes or the tests; the claims below come from reading the code.

Tests:
- `tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py` adds a case that counts reads of `price_cents` over a 1000-purchase history and asserts at most 2n. The old prefix re-summing does about 500,000 reads.
- `tests/io_shop/test_typical_spend.py` adds a case that counts `<` comparisons between prices over a shuffled 1000-purchase history and asserts fewer than 50,000. A single sort needs about n log n (roughly 10,000); the old repeated `min` needs several hundred thousand. Both new tests also check that the answer is still right, and the existing correctness tests are kept unchanged.

---

Proposed by Argus for incident `85584d81-8502-4c7e-8086-84d92d2a3b26`.
The investigation concluded: Request volume ramped from 1200/min starting 2026-11-10T04:58:00Z to 5400/min, about 4.5 times baseline. CPU use rose with it and hit the fixed 3.0-core limit at 2026-11-10T05:06:00Z. Requests then queued for CPU, and p95 rose from about 210 ms to over 1800 ms. Nothing was deployed or changed, and the rollout had converged.

This is a draft. Argus cannot merge it - review it as you would any change from somebody who has not run the service.

author: fi3w0
body:
## What this does

**Native retest status (2026-11-10):** the `0.91.32` retest exposed a real Steam toast that maps near the centre and then moves to the edge immediately afterwards. `0.91.33` follows those post-map owner moves through optional X11 RECORD support. A native `0.91.33` retest is still pending, so native acceptance is not complete and this PR must remain unmerged.

Brings the local queue from master 0.91.23 to 0.91.33: 14 signed commits covering Ebb Phase 3, Scroll camera/input fixes, window picking, fullscreen notifications and diagnostics, X11 overlay placement, the observer review fixes, and post-map overlay movement.

Fixes #6. The Steam wheel fix was confirmed on a native session. This PR is not a claim that fullscreen direct scanout or every X11 overlay edge case is solved.

| Area | Resulting behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Ebb Phase 3 | `tidectl ebb stats` adds per-app cache/buffer estimates and client PSS read by the CLI. Shells can subscribe to rate-limited `ebb-pressure`; report-only findings identify repeated empty redraws and costly pointer motion. |
| Kernel pressure delivery | Correct the nested-epoll handling that consumed PSI readiness before Ebb could observe it. Pressure events are reported in every mode; only balanced/aggressive queue automatic pressure passes. |
| Scroll view restoration | Closing a newly opened window restores the strip view it displaced when the user has not since changed the view or focus. |
| Steam wheel / Scroll pointer focus | Suppress repeated synthetic pointer motion at an unchanged surface-local position before wheel steps and clicks, while retaining refreshes when the strip changes the target. |
| Fullscreen state events | Client-requested fullscreen/maximize transitions emit `window-changed`, allowing external shells to react without polling. Duplicate/denied requests emit no event. |
| Scanout diagnostics | Native render statistics report why a fullscreen surface is not scanned out. This adds diagnostics; it does not fix scanout rejection. |
| Window picking | `tidectl pick-window [--timeout <seconds>]` and IPC return the next clicked window. Includes cancellation, replacement, timeout, disconnected-client handling, consumed input and a native crosshair. |
| X11 overlays | A read-only observer recovers X11 geometry for override-redirect windows that satellite exposes as toplevels. Matching windows float without taking focus on map or receiving compositor decoration/depth. When the server supports RECORD, TideWM follows ConfigureWindow requests from the owning X11 client after mapping while ignoring satellite's placement feedback. No application, corner or monitor policy is hardcoded. |
| Observer review fixes | Remove size-only provisional matching, reject conflicting/tied identities, handle reused XIDs and disappearing windows, preserve split UTF-8, clear stale records on EOF, and snapshot ordered geometry events rather than a later `GetGeometry` reply. |
| Cleanup / documentation | Remove unused Ocean helpers, gate test-only accessors, narrow spatial field visibility, and update the reference, technical report and both changelogs. |

## How it was verified

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo test --locked --all-features --all-targets -- --test-threads=1` — **793 passed**: 759 compositor, 25 tidectl, 9 wavefmt.
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo build --locked --release --all-features`
- [x] Real-client nested checks, described below.
- [x] Native 0.91.33 acceptance — native 0.91.32 failed the toast regression; `0.91.33` needs a rebuild/relog retest.

The tested source is commit `3cf9a43`. Tests and nested checks ran against that implementation.

Nested verification used an isolated KWin host, private runtime/config directories, real clients and TideWM IPC:

- Ebb app rows and CLI client PSS, real kernel/cgroup pressure: low produces one event without a cache pass; balanced produces one event and a cache pass/heap trim.
- Client-requested fullscreen/unfullscreen/maximize events and Scroll close/view restoration.
- Window-pick timeout/replacement over the real socket, plus protocol tests for selection, cancellation and disconnected clients. Physical click/Escape/crosshair acceptance remains owed.
- Five overlay regressions pass on the final 0.91.33 release binary: a normal window colliding with a provisional popup record; reuse after unmap; rapid popup creation/destruction; geometry changed immediately after mapping; and a generic client that maps at (300,200) then requests (1000,650) 20 ms later. The last case fails on 0.91.32 and passes on 0.91.33. Unit tests additionally cover split UTF-8, identity conflicts, ambiguity, EOF, scale/origin conversion, owner-versus-foreign ConfigureWindow requests and partial/signed coordinates.

Native confirmations already recorded: Steam wheel scrolling on 0.91.29 and the reported toast placement on 0.91.31. The native 0.91.32 toast retest failed after the client moved the window post-map; 0.91.33 addresses that sequence through RECORD.

### Known limitations / follow-ups

- Overlay association remains best-effort: satellite's xdg_toplevel exposes no X11 window ID. A deliberately delayed observer record misses first-map classification and is not reconciled later; identical ordinary/overlay identities cannot be reliably distinguished by metadata alone.
- In panned Ocean, the overlay first-map path treats recovered screen coordinates as world coordinates. This is reproduced and remains open. Overlay anchoring under Ocean navigation/Scroll strip-floating and participation in ordinary physics/buoyancy also need follow-up.
- RECORD is optional. Without it, only the first-map geometry is available. Owner moves stay on the overlay's original output; cross-output owner moves are not mirrored. Rendered multi-output/rotated overlay acceptance and hotplug are not established by the single-output nested fixture.
- Native scanout blocker evidence, physical window-pick interaction, and long Ebb soak/pressure acceptance remain pending. No direct-scanout, leak-elimination or general memory-saving claim is made.

## Anything touching the RAM budget?

Ebb retains bounded monitoring/report state; app reports are generated on request and capped at 32 rows. The CLI reads client PSS outside the compositor event loop. X11 apps share satellite's Wayland client PID, so that PSS is not independent attribution to each underlying X11 application.

The overlay compatibility path adds a separate observer process when XWayland is enabled, keeping synchronous X11 property queries off the compositor loop. `x11rb` is now a direct dependency; it was already present through winit's X11 backend. Its `record` feature adds no package version change. The compositor's pending matching and owner-position queues are capped. The follow-up observer fixes add no process/thread or frame-path work to the compositor; the optional RECORD reader thread and connection live in the observer child.

No controlled release PSS before/after measurement was taken for the complete queue, so no aggregate RAM/VRAM reduction is claimed.

## Objetivo
Conter a amplificação de leituras do Firestore sem perder a atualização em tempo real, a segurança entre unidades nem a integridade das operações. Ref #192.

## Correções implementadas
- `src/api-fetch.js`: cache em memória de 12 segundos para `dayList`, `list` e `notifications` (além das consultas pesadas anteriores). Chave inclui URL, payload, autorização e escopo; qualquer mutação invalida o cache. Respostas 503 não são guardadas.
- `src/api-fetch.js`: `setApiScope` só invalida quando identidade/unidade/papel/status mudam de verdade.
- `src/Production.jsx`: a atualização apenas de `stock` ou `catalog` não chama `dayList` se não houve mudança do domínio `production`. Os carregamentos de produtos/receitas continuam onde necessários.
- `src/live-hub.js` / `src/useUnitLive.js`: o evento de listener compartilhado invalida o cache uma única vez, em vez de uma vez por componente.
- `src/StorageManager.jsx`: distingue primeira consulta ainda não confirmada de estado realmente vazio; não mostra falso zero após falha inicial.
- `src/PhysicalStock.jsx`: atualização de resumo/lotes após mudanças mantida para preservar exatidão.

## Testes adicionados
- Isolamento do cache por endpoint, payload e token.
- Expiração do cache de leituras pesadas e `dayList`.
- Invalidação imediata após mutação de notificações.
- Uma invalidação por evento live, com um listener compartilhado e cleanup.
- Workflow `storage-spaces.yml` passa a executar novos testes, além do build.

## Validação necessária
- GitHub ainda não retornou checks ou execuções de workflow no último commit no momento desta atualização; tentativa de clonar diretamente bloqueada por DNS do ambiente. Não marcar testes como aprovados.
- Validar build e testes de regras, depois executar cenários de 1, 5 e 10 sessões em staging Firebase isolado.
- Medir QUERY e LOOKUP antes/depois, correlacionando ações `list`, `dayList`, `v3Alerts`, `v3Dashboard` e eventos em tempo real.

**PR permanece como draft. Não integrar à main até CI e medições.**

author: luciazgagliardi
body:
## Fallo real reproducido en Azure
`/api/acervo/estado` devuelve una versión antigua e informa `ENOENT` al renombrar `/home/datos/acervo/acervo-<version>.db.tmp` a `acervo.db`. Dos procesos que importan la misma versión compartían el mismo archivo temporal y podían borrárselo mutuamente.

## Solución
- Crear un nombre temporal único por proceso y ejecución para importar SQLite.
- No cerrar la base anterior hasta verificar que existe una base nueva íntegra, y no promover versiones obsoletas.
- Separar las copias de lectura por PID y eliminar el barrido de `/tmp` que podía borrar archivos de otra instancia.
- Prueba con **dos importadores FTS5 concurrentes** de la misma versión, más pruebas de rutas y contenido.

## Verificación posterior
Comprobar versión publicada en Azure y búsquedas de sentencias civil/laboral, daño moral y daño punitivo. PR preparado en borrador para pasar CI antes de desplegar.

author: papaya2003
body:
## Why

Jialei decided on 2026-11-10 that there is no reactor translator. The brain speaks the vdW reactor's own Lab Console API (reactor ADR 0010), and the simulated reactor window imitates that API, so the sim and the real reactor stay symmetric. Spec: `notes/vdw-reactor-20261110/reactor-native-spec.md` (section 3).

## What

New `qumus_simlab/simlab/reactor_console.py`, mounted under `/lab/` on the reactor window (both its normal and its remote listener, sharing one simulated reactor). The contract v1 routes on 8783 are unchanged, so the Hall-bar bench is not affected.

- Console:
  - `api/console/state`, `state/<device>`, `describe/<device>`, `events`
  - `heartbeat`, `control/<device>/take|release`, `release-page`
  - `command/<device>` (202/409/422)
  - `stop/<device>`, `api/dashboard/motion|heat`
- Orchestrator: lease (`api/heartbeat|renew|release`); `api/runs` with `borrow: true` (refused until the caller holds every device the recipe uses); `api/state`; `api/runs/<id>`; abort.
- Recipes: `slot-state`, `crucible-load` (refused at 100 °C or more), `crucible-unload` (waits until the crucible region is below 60 °C), `microscope-record`. A motion stop, or losing the lease, holds the run.
- Furnace: `start_sequence` with steps, gas % per MFC, `end_gas` and `end_gas_until_c`. It follows the program in fast sim time: 600 sim seconds per real second by default. The furnace stop turns heat and gas off.
- Sim only:
  - a generated microscope frame at `sim/microscope/api/camera/microscope/frame.jpg`
  - `POST sim/handover {slot, chip_id|null}`: the person's hand
  - `GET sim/world`
  - Tray slots are A1 to A4.

`server.py` is touched in one place: `start()` adds these routes for the reactor module. It also prints the `/lab/` URL.

The real reactor's code is AGPL, so nothing was copied from it. This module was written from the reactor's public docs.

## Tests

- `tests/test_simlab_reactor_console.py`: 6 tests pass (reads, control refusals, a full round trip, loading refused when hot, gas rule plus furnace stop, motion stop holds a run and abort closes it).
- `tests/test_simlab_records.py` and `tests/test_simlab_contract.py` still pass (18).
- End to end: the brain's `python -m qumus2.reactor.roundtrip` (qumus-agent branch `claude/project-thread-xdfzay`) completed handover_in → load → heat → snapshot → unload → handover_out against this console in about 2 s.

author: dimmur
body:
Closes #6655. Changelog entry included. No migration.

The periodic check that keeps date-filtered views ("is today", "is within X days") up to date for subscribers used to run as one big transaction over every subscribed view. On instances with many linked tables it could deadlock with ordinary row edits or run out of memory, and then the whole pass rolled back, so `view.rows_entered` webhooks for those views never fired.

## What changes
- Each table is checked and committed on its own, so a row edit on one table no longer deadlocks with the check, and finished tables keep their results.
- A table that fails is logged and skipped; the other tables still commit and send their webhooks, and the failed table is checked again on the next run.
- Generated table models are no longer kept for the whole pass; memory stays flat as the number of tables grows (400 tables: ~72 MB peak growth vs ~148 MB before).
- After deploy, the first pass can send a burst of late `rows_entered` events for rows that should have entered while the check kept failing. They are valid.

## Worth checking by hand
1. **Deadlock gone.** While the check waits on the second table, a row edit that locks the first table goes through. On `develop` it fails with `deadlock detected`.
2. **One failing table doesn't stop the rest.** Cancel the check's query on the second table: the first table stays committed and its webhook is sent.
3. **Large instance.** At 400 small tables a pass took 9.9 s (was 9.1 s) and memory stayed flat (72 MB peak growth vs 148 MB). The soft limit is 300 s.

<details><summary>How to check 1 and 2</summary>

**Setup**
1. Run a Celery worker (webhooks are sent from it).
2. Create table A, then table B, so A has the lower id; the check goes in table id order. In each:
   - a date field;
   - a grid view filtered on `date is today`;
   - a webhook with the "Rows enter view" event on that view. The webhook's call log shows each call, so no receiver is needed.
3. Add one row dated tomorrow to each table.
4. Run the check once to record the starting state. The shell imports the checked-out code, so switching between `develop` and this branch needs no restart:
   ```
   just b manage shell -c "from baserow.contrib.database.views.tasks import periodic_check_for_views_with_time_sensitive_filters as t; t()"
   ```
5. Simulate midnight passing. Updating the row in SQL skips the row signals, so the saved view rows go stale just like when the date changes:
   ```sql
   UPDATE database_table_<A> SET field_<date A> = current_date;
   UPDATE database_table_<B> SET field_<date B> = current_date;
   ```

**1. Deadlock**
1. In psql session S1, act as a row edit on B that holds B's lock:
   ```sql
   BEGIN;
   SELECT 1 FROM database_viewrows WHERE view_id = <view B> FOR UPDATE;
   ```
2. Run the check from step 4. It waits for B.
3. In psql session S2, run `SELECT row_ids FROM database_viewrows WHERE view_id = <view A>;`
   - This branch: A's row id is saved and A's webhook is in the call log.
   - `develop`: still empty, and no webhook.
4. In S1, lock A the way the edit locks its linked table:
   ```sql
   SELECT 1 FROM database_viewrows WHERE view_id = <view A> FOR UPDATE;
   ```
   - This branch: returns at once.
   - `develop`: `deadlock detected` after about 1 s.
5. Run `COMMIT;` in S1. On this branch the check finishes and B's webhook is sent.

**2. One failing table**

Repeat setup steps 3 to 5, and steps 1 and 2 of the deadlock check. Then cancel the check's waiting query from S2:
```sql
SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE wait_event_type = 'Lock' AND query ILIKE '%database_viewrows%';
```
- This branch: the log shows `Checking the time-sensitive views of table <B> failed`, and A stays committed with its webhook sent. Run `ROLLBACK;` in S1 and run the check again: B's webhook is sent.
- `develop`: the whole pass rolls back and A's webhook is never sent.
</details>

The new test covers per-table commit (read from a second connection), failure isolation with retry on the next run, the per-table cache, and the soft time limit stopping the pass.

## Also
- Each table costs two extra queries (its own transaction and re-fetching cached state), about 4-8% more pass time.
- A database outage logs one error per table, so one pass can produce many Sentry events.
- A failure inside a commit callback (e.g. the broker is down when a webhook is queued) happens after the table committed; it is logged, and that event is not retried. It was lost before too.
- Freed models are released by Python's garbage collector, so memory is bounded by GC cadence rather than by the largest table.
- Remaining gaps (checking only views whose date window moved, row edits not locking view states, deadlocks between edits on linked tables, errors per table during an outage, events lost when queueing fails) are tracked in #6657.

<details><summary>Why this approach</summary>

A transaction and cache scope per table inside the existing loop: the smallest change that removes the cross-table lock chain and the unbounded cache, with no change to the schedule or what gets sent.

**Not a sub-task per table:** more moving parts (queue, ordering, overlap) for a patch release; the plain loop already isolates tables.
**Not the loop in the Celery task:** it would duplicate the loop out of the handler, which has another caller; keeping it in the handler keeps that caller working and mirrors the per-table shape already used in `fields/tasks.py`.
**Not a forced `gc.collect()`:** extra cost per pass for a bound that already holds at the measured sizes; easy to add if workers run tight.
</details>

author: iamacoffeepot
body:
Slice 9a of the dev overlay (ADR-0053): the band's left column under the frame chart. The right column (memory meters, adapter; slice 9b) is untouched.

## What changes

- **GPU graph** (`gpu/`): `GpuTimes` is subscribed and unsubscribed alongside `FrameStats` at the same stop transitions. Each frame's passes are kept on the frame chart's 60 s axis by their `elapsed_nanos`, cut into the frame chart's columns (same span, same x via the shared `chart::left_of`). A column is a stack of the passes, bottom-up in the order their labels were first heard. Each pass sits at its **median** over the column's frames, from a bounded stride sample. The scale is linear and **auto-ranged**, as Tracy and PIX do it: the top is the tallest stack in the 60 s window, rounded up to 1, 2 or 5 x 10^n ns (0.083 ms becomes 0.1 ms, 3.1 ms becomes 5 ms), never below 10 µs, so an idle GPU's noise is not drawn full height. The top only moves between those steps, which keeps it from flickering. Each pass that took any time is at least 1 px tall, and a stack over the top is clamped. The budget's dashed bone line is drawn only when the budget is at or below the top. The gutter beside the graph shows `gpu` with `top 0.1 ms` right-aligned. A 2x-budget top had left eve's 0.08 ms frames (240 Hz, 4.17 ms budget) under a pixel. Under it, one Mono line: each pass's label (with `aether.render.` dropped) and its median ms over the window, in its pass colour so the line is the legend, then `gpu busy NN%` (median GPU frame total over the median frame time). On `GpuTimes::Unsupported` the graph's place shows only `GPU timing not supported on this device` in stone.
- **Pass colours**: slate blue `#6f8aa6`, muted violet `#8a7ca8`, mauve `#a88aa0`, cycling by first-seen label. None is lichen, sand or slate-teal.
- **Four lines** (`lines/`): draws, triangles, bytes uploaded and GPU memory (the sum of every `GpuMemory` kind). Each is a thin row of stone bars over the same columns. A column is the **max** of its frames, scaled linearly from 0 to the max shown. Each row's label and latest value sit in a gutter at the column's right. Bytes use the `memory` tool's `bytes_shown` (KiB/MiB/GiB), and counts switch to k/M past 10 000.
- **Shared binning** (`binned/`): one generic `Binned<A: Accrue>` keeps samples for 3 windows and recuts on resize, as `frames` does. The frame chart's stride sample moved into `binned::Thinned`, and `frames::Bin` uses it.
- **Layout**: the band now grows to fit its sections: frame chart (6% of height), its figures, GPU graph (2/3 of the chart), GPU figures, four text-line-tall rows. That is 263 px at 1080. Every graph ends at a 20-character gutter, so the frame chart narrows to 191 columns at 1080 (was 226).
- **ADR-0053**: colour table rows and the pass-colour sentence replaced; the band bullets describe the graph, the lines and the gutter.

## Record room

`MOST_RECORDS` = 5 + 1 + 3002 x (3 + 6 passes + 4 lines) + 2 x 1000 dashes + 64 marks + 3 = **41 099** records = **1 315 168 bytes** of instance capacity (was 10 079 / 322 528). At 1920x1080 one write is at most 2 902 records = 92 864 bytes.

## State fields added (R-0048)

- `Overlay.gpu: GpuTiming`: an enum, `Timed(PassTimes)` or `Unsupported`.
- `Overlay.gpu_figures: GpuFigures`: last computed figures; busy is an enum `Busy { Unknown, Share { percent } }`.
- `Overlay.lines: FrameLines`: binned frames, plus `latest`, which is zeros before any stats are heard.
- `binned::Open<A>`: `Nothing | Filling { span, bin }`.
- `Overlay.gpu_top: GraphTop`: the top the GPU graph was last drawn to, which its gutter line shows. It starts at the 10 µs floor and is never optional.

No `Option` field and no `.take()` in non-test code. The one `Option` the diff adds is `Labels::slot`'s `position` lookup, used inline. `GraphTop::of` takes `.max()` over the columns, also a lookup, and treats no columns as 0. The slot itself is an enum, `Pass(index) | Past`.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt -- --check`: passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: passed
- `cargo xtask check browser` (wasm32 clippy): passed
- `cargo test -p aethereal-overlay`: 50 passed

author: kblack0610
body:
P5 of the codex-parity plan: a fleet Codex run now gets the same session rules a Claude one does.

## What changed

- Hooks. `codex exec` fires hooks once they are trusted, and a rewritten `hooks.json` is untrusted again. That is why they went quiet after the last sync. Fleet launches now pass `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`; an interactive `codex` still asks. `.config/codex/hooks.json` gains the block-pkill-f, forge-guard and checkout-guard PreToolUse guards, plus a Stop hook, `.claude/hooks/codex-item-stop.sh`. When a run tries to stop while its queue item is still running with no PR, the hook blocks that one Stop with the ways to close the item. That gives ar-1124's "ended before it closed the item" one more turn, and only the item's own claimed thread is held.
- Blocked on the human. A headless brief now says to file the ask, then run `agent-queue requeue <slug> --ask <id>` and stop. The new `requeue --ask` puts the item back behind the ask, and the answer restarts it with the decision in its brief. Before, the brief said "say why and stop", which reap filed as failed.
- Forgejo. On a repo whose canonical forge is Forgejo (the mirror workflow marker), the brief points at one-shot's `references/landing.md` "Forgejo repo" instead of agent-land, headless runs included.
- ar-1087. On a Codex item, reap no longer trusts the tmux session as a witness, since wt can hand that name to a Claude item. `codex_gone` reads whether an `agent-codex run` process still carries `AGENT_QUEUE_ITEM=<slug>`. As with claude_gone it is one witness, so `reap_confirm` settles only on a second read.
- Config. `config.managed.toml` (dead) becomes `config.owned.toml`. Its keys head `~/.codex/config.toml` and replace the human's copies: `model = "gpt-6.1-sol"`, plus `project_doc_fallback_filenames = ["CLAUDE.md"]`. The managed MCP block loses the `type`/`description` keys behind "Codex is ignoring 7 unrecognized configuration settings" on every run.
- Session views. agent-panel lists a pane that runs Codex and no Claude: busy, the thread id of the rollout file the process holds open, and `codex: <item>`. Most list readers treat every `session_id` as a Claude conversation, so `list` shows these rows only with `--codex` / `AGENT_PANEL_CODEX=1`. fleet-sessions sets the env form, which a binary not yet rebuilt ignores instead of refusing. The chooser always shows them; `dialog` and `answer` skip them.
- Docs. Rows were added to `.config/codex/README.md` (guards, Stop check, owned keys, hook trust, three troubleshooting rows) and to `agent-panel/README.md`.

Removed: the stale `gpt-5.6-sol` default, the dead `config.managed.toml`, the brief's claim that a headless harness has no hooks, the "Skip what this harness lacks (final-pass, wind-down)" line, and "say why and stop" for a blocked headless run.

The HTTP 401 at `codex exec` startup does not come from an MCP server. All 342 rows in Codex's log come from one process: a `codex app-server --managed-daemon` started Nov 6, before the Nov 9 re-login, which reports `codex_models_manager token_expired`. Every MCP server is stdio, and none logged an error. Restarting that daemon is a human step, since agents do not touch auth state, so it is a README troubleshooting row and not a code change.

This PR addresses board rows ar-1124 (narrowed to real no-close cases) and ar-1087. Neither row was touched by hand.

## Assumed

- assumed: a headless run blocked on the human uses `requeue --ask`, because a waiting item has no session left to hear the answer.
- assumed: the Stop hook acts only on the thread the item claimed, because a Claude session's AGENT_QUEUE_ITEM is in the env of any codex it runs.
- assumed: only the launcher's own processes witness a live Codex run, because a daemon a Codex command starts inherits the env and can outlive the run.
- assumed: Codex rows are opt-in for `agent-panel list`, because `fleet-dispatch record` would otherwise save a Codex thread as a Claude conversation and `restore` would `claude --resume` it.

## Evidence

- Hook probes (`/usr/bin/codex` 0.164, `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, live `~/.codex/hooks.json` restored and `cmp`-checked after each): SessionStart fires; PreToolUse and Stop payloads captured (threads 01a1c3ac-40c2-7282-bafa-0adf7d5ff0a0, 01a1c3ac-f54c-7201-8176-9857f5ec4159); a Stop block forces a second turn; a PreToolUse deny is honored ("A PreToolUse hook blocked it with: probe: denied").
- Doc fallback probe: a dir with only CLAUDE.md answered from it; a dir with AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md answered from AGENTS.md.
- Guards fed Codex-shaped payloads: block-pkill-f, forge-guard (a home-config push) and checkout-guard (a ~/.dotfiles checkout) each deny; `ls` passes.
- Config sync dry run on a copy of the live `~/.codex/config.toml` (temp homes, rulesync stubbed): exit 0, owned keys at the head, 0 `type`/`description` keys left, the rest identical line for line, a second run byte-identical, and `codex mcp list` parses it.
- agent-panel built from this branch lists the 4 live Codex runs on this machine. Each thread id equals its queue item's `sessions:`. The plain `list --json` count (32) matches the installed binary.

## Tests

- Bats files the Stop hook picks for the changed files (`test_picked`, 76 files): 2724 ok, 2 not ok on the first run. One was the ar-1087 reap test, which ran while I had a fix reverted for a negative control. The other asserted that a headless brief never names `agent-ask post`, which this PR changes on purpose; the test now asserts the requeue rule and that "ask it here" is absent. After both: `fleet_dispatch.bats`, `codex_config_sync.bats` and `codex_item_stop.bats` re-run in full on the final tree, 383/383 ok.

- `cargo test` in `.local/src/agent-panel`: 118 passed, 0 failed; `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.

Review: /code-review high, 9 findings. Fixed 7: a Forgejo headless brief no longer says to run agent-land; codex_run_live reads only this user's processes (`pgrep -u`) and skips a pid that exited since pgrep listed it; a human's multi-line copy of an owned key goes whole; an owned file with no keys no longer kills the sync, and the key regex takes digits and dashes; `codex_below` picks the lowest pid of two sibling runs, so refreshes agree; the dialog lookup skips Codex rows; the Stop hook names the proof and doc+ask closes. Answered 2: `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` was proven on the installed codex 0.164 by the hook probes (Evidence); rulesync writes plain MCP names and one-line descriptions, so the strip needs no quoted-name or multi-line case. Each fix has a test, and each test fails with its fix reverted.

author: jovanhartono
body:
## Summary

`volume::judge` guessed disk images from mount flags. A writable .dmg, a .sparsebundle or an .iso got indexed, and a Mac drive locked read-only was left out. It now asks Disk Arbitration for the device's model and refuses "Disk Image". The old flag rule is kept for when Disk Arbitration can't say. Closes #134.

## Changes

- `crates/argus-core/src/volume.rs`:
  - `mac::disk_image(from)` asks Disk Arbitration for `kDADiskDescriptionDeviceModelKey` and compares it with "Disk Image" using `CFEqual`. Every CF object is held in a wrapper that releases it on drop.
  - `judge` takes the question as a closure and asks it last, after the startup, backup, network, hidden, quarantine and outside-/Volumes checks, so those mounts never pay for the call.
  - A quarantined mount is still always an image.
  - No C ABI change.
- `ARGUS_DRIVE_IMAGE`, already set by the opt-in `DriveImageTests`, makes `check_volume` skip Disk Arbitration. That keeps a writable disk image usable as a stand-in USB drive in those tests (`DrivesTests.swift` doc comment updated).
- `crates/argus-ffi/src/lib.rs`, `check_volume` doc: `tl_volume_added` now makes one call to a system service. It costs 0.1-0.4 ms (up to 2 ms the first time), against ~15 µs before. It still never reads the volume itself.
- `docs/m3-beats-spotlight.html`: the "writable disk image is still listed" gap is closed, and the line says how the drive tests use an image.

## Testing

Run on macOS 26.6, Apple silicon. Five images were attached normally (visible in Finder) and checked with the ignored `judge_what_is_mounted` test:

| Image | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| writable APFS .dmg | indexed | DiskImage |
| read-only UDZO .dmg | DiskImage | DiskImage |
| APFS .sparsebundle | indexed | DiskImage |
| .iso (cd9660) | indexed | DiskImage |
| writable exFAT .dmg | indexed | DiskImage |

- All five report the model "Disk Image". The internal SSD reports its own model, so it isn't taken for an image.
- New tests:
  - a locked Mac drive (APFS and HFS) with "not an image" is indexed;
  - images of each kind are refused;
  - quarantine wins over a "not an image" answer;
  - Disk Arbitration is never asked before the cheaper checks;
  - the real call never calls the "/" device an image (`Some(false)` here; `None` on the GitHub macOS runner, whose virtual startup disk has no model, so the old flag rule applies there) and answers `None` for a file server or an unknown device.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, and clippy with `-D warnings` on the host and on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.
- `cargo test -p argus-core -p argus-ffi`: 274 and 150 passed.
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos`: 323 tests, 0 failures.
- `ARGUS_DRIVE_IMAGE=<drive.dmg> swift test --filter DriveImageTests`: 6/6 passed.

## Notes

- The call stays on the window's main thread. Moving `tl_volume_added` off it would mean one ordered queue shared with `tl_volume_removed`, or a quick mount-then-eject could add a drive that's already gone.
- A real USB stick locked read-only is covered by a unit test only; there was no stick to try by hand.

author: alapaque
body:
## What and why

Fixes #93. On the Mac, with the sidebar hidden completely and the address row hidden too
("Hide the address row with the sidebar"), the page runs to the window's top edge and the
traffic lights sat on it, over the site's own controls at its top left.

Patch 0177 adds `stedding::WindowButtonsOverPageMac`, owned by `BrowserNativeWidgetMac`. In
that one state (sidebar hidden completely and not slid in, row hidden, not full screen) it
hides the three traffic lights, and shows them while the pointer is within 8 points of their
place. It watches pointer moves in the window with a window `EventMonitor`, as the hidden
sidebar's reveal edge does, and the strip's bounds and the row's visibility. Everywhere else
the lights show as now (sidebar Y53). Spec: sidebar Y55, and a line in toolbar T8.

It is its own patch so it is easy to review; folding it into the hidden sidebar's patch is a
`tooling/fold-fix` on a checkout, if you prefer.

## How it was tested

On a MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, built-in display with a camera housing), macOS 26.5.2:

- `tooling/build-chromium release chrome stedding_browser_tests` on the series with 0177.
- `WindowButtonsTest.HiddenWithTheRowHiddenTheLightsShowOnHover` (new) passes.
- `WindowButtonsTest.*`, `WindowTopTest.*`, `SidebarFormsTest.*`, `SidebarAddressTest.*`,
  `SidebarRailTest.*`: 50 of 52 pass. The two that fail,
  `WindowButtonsTest.HoveringTheRailInFullScreenLeavesTheRowAlone` (the full-screen row is
  70 DIP lower after the hover) and `WindowButtonsTest.FullScreenTitleBarDrawsNoDivider` (an
  `NSScrollPocket` line under the title bar, trap 97), fail the same way on a build without
  0177, with the cursor parked, so they fail on this machine before this change.
- By hand, with the issue's settings: the lights are gone over the page, come back near the
  top-left corner and go again, and show as before with the row back, the sidebar open or
  slid in.
- `tooling/check-repo`: all checks passed.
- Not run: `mac-checks`.

## AI assistance

- [ ] No AI tool helped with this pull request.
- [x] An AI tool helped. Tool, model, and what it did: Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5. It
  found the cause in the series, wrote the fix, the browser test and the spec rows, and
  drafted this description. I built and tested it on my Mac.

author: elahayman
body:
## What
- **Music:** a new original home tune. It is dreamy and slow, with a soft melody, plucked arpeggio chords and a warm bass.
- **Bedtime:** the default is now 4 minutes, with options 4, 6 or 10 minutes, or off. A stored 5 (the old default) is read as 4.
- **Place words:**
  - The "on the table" picture now sits on the tabletop instead of overlapping it, both in the quiz card and in the drag game.

author: mattmook
body:
## Summary

SipHash keeps its state as four `Long` words. On Kotlin/JS, every add, rotate and xor in a SipRound creates a new `Long` object. Profiling `SipHashBoringSslTest` on Hermes put 44% of its time in `Long` arithmetic.

The state is now an `expect class`, as Ascon's (#139) and Keccak's (#142) are:

| | JS | JVM, Apple, `nativeLongMain` |
|---|---|---|
| `SipHashState` | `actual class` with the four words as eight `Int` fields | `actual typealias SipHashState = SipHashStateLong` |

**`SipHashStateLong` (common)** holds the code `SipHash` had, unchanged: the key setup from `reset`, `processWord`, `sipRounds`, and the final-word packing and finalisation from `digest`.

**What changes in `SipHash`:**
- It keeps the buffering and hands whole words to the state. Full words in the input now go to the state as one `compress` call rather than one call per word.
- The total length is now counted in an `Int`. Only its low byte goes into the final word, so wrapping is harmless, and adding to it no longer allocates a `Long` on JS.

**The JS version:** each SipRound is written out on `Int` halves.
- Adds carry from the low half into the high half.
- Rotates by 13, 16, 17 and 21 move bits between the halves.
- Rotates by 32 swap the halves.

**On JVM and Native**, SipHash runs the same arithmetic as before. The one difference is the extra `SipHashStateLong` object between `SipHash` and its four words.

## Results

Hermes, `main` against this branch, 3 alternating runs (ms):

| Test class | `main` | This PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---:|
| SipHashBoringSslTest | 465 / 520 / 348 | 98 / 162 / 168 | **about 3× faster** |
| SipHashTest | 84 / 47 / 61 | 28 / 40 / 42 | about 1.6× faster |

## Testing

- **Checks:** detekt is clean; the JVM, JS and linuxX64 compiles succeed.
- **JVM:** the SipHash tests pass.
- **JS:** the SipHash tests and the `Algorithm` equality and parameter-copy tests pass on Hermes and Node. They cover:
  - the reference implementation's SipHash-2-4 and SipHash128-2-4 vectors for every length from 0 to 63 bytes;
  - copying a digest mid-stream and reusing one after reset;
  - BoringSSL's vectors.
- **CI** runs the full suites.

author: xuangong
body:
One invalid but attributable worktree can block all Worker acquisition. Separate complete enumeration from per-resource validation: retain proven quarantined resources in capacity and same-task fences while allowing unrelated work to use remaining capacity. Unknown ownership, unreadable registration pointers or incomplete enumeration still block acquisition. Registration uniqueness uses physical targets, including manual registrations and case aliases; symbolic or multiply linked targets cannot establish uniqueness. Forward, reverse and common-directory pointers preserve raw filesystem traversal before physical comparison; missing parent traversal, unresolved Windows volumes and missing-target case ambiguity remain unknown. Only explicit static validation failures from stable observations can be quarantined. Changes to markers, sidecars, current directory identities or Git pointers remain unknown. Even early branch/sidecar failures recheck the indexed marker before quarantine, so cached ownership cannot hide an observed conflict. Native query/parse errors and unclassified failures also remain unknown.

Cross-check full claim/worktree identity against registered physical repository paths and original Web/Herdr bindings. Pending-stop owners and their original execution paths remain evidence after a workspace closes; conflicting worktree identities or paths keep acquisition fenced. Preserve the strict list API and pending fences. Quarantined resources never gain execution or deletion authority.

Validation: Node 24.22.1 typecheck/build and 452 tests across eleven related files passed for the ownership-observation repair, with 25 final targeted checks after the validation-order adjustment. Main-integrated typecheck and all 374 tests across the four combination files passed. The preceding Windows traversal repair passed native Windows with 9,950 tests and 179 existing platform skips; the new observation regressions still require native CI. Real Git/metadata fixtures verify unknown coverage and no claim after observed ownership changes, while stable local damage remains quarantined. Production Worker, remount and reboot acceptance have not been run. Dependencies use the Tencent npm registry.

This PR contains nine production files. New regression tests are in #984; specifications and mechanism documentation have separate PRs.

author: andrewkern
body:
Fixes #85: no example YAML set the major selection and gene conversion options, so the YAML/CLI parity check in `testing/yaml_validation_suite.sh` did not cover them.

## New fixtures

Each fixture has an `# Equivalent to: discoal ...` line, so the suite runs both forms and compares their output.

| fixture | option |
|---|---|
| `hard_sweep_example.yaml` | `-ws` (hard sweep) |
| `deterministic_sweep_example.yaml` | `-wd` |
| `neutral_sweep_example.yaml` | `-wn`; `selection_coefficient: 0` (on the command line, `-wn` ignores `-a`) |
| `recurrent_mutation_sweep_example.yaml` | `-uA` |
| `recurrent_sweeps_example.yaml` | `-R` |
| `gene_conversion_example.yaml` | `-g` |
| `gene_conversion_ratio_example.yaml` | `-gr` |

## Changed fixtures

- **`sweep_example.yaml`** now sets `hide_partial_snp` (`-h`), because it is the only partial sweep. Its sweep is moved from 1.0 to 0.1 x 4N generations ago. At 1.0, all lineages had coalesced before the sweep, so no selected site was added and `-h` had no effect.
- **`neutral_sweep_example.yaml`** uses N = 10^4, so its trajectory takes 0.05 s, not 3.5 s.

The README of `config_examples`:
- lists the new fixtures and `tree_sequence_example.yaml`;
- no longer says that `demographic_example.yaml` has gene conversion;
- runs `build/discoal` in its commands, without the removed `-T`, and without `-p` sizes that disagree with the file.

## Checks

- **Review.** An instrumented build checked that each fixture's feature takes effect. With `uA = 0.5`, both replicates of the `-uA` fixture descend from more than one origin. (A first value, 0.0005, gave one origin.)

- **All 20 fixtures pass.** The suite takes about 30 s.
- **The check sees each key.** I changed one key in a copy of each new fixture, and the output then differed from the command line. The keys were `fixation_time_ago`, `sweep_mode`, `sweep_position`, `beneficial_mutation_rate`, `recurrent_sweep_rate`, `gene_conversion_tract_length` and `crossover_ratio`. The same is true for `hide_partial_snp: false` and a changed `effective_population_size`.
- **The comments match the docs and the code:** times in 4N generations, alpha = 2Ns, the `-R` rate per 2N individuals per generation, gamma scaled for the whole locus as rho is, and the `-gr` rate = rho x ratio.

## Not covered

`unsimplified_tree_sequence` (`-F`). It needs a second tree-sequence fixture and tskit.

Close #85 by hand after merge, because this PR targets `demes`.

author: retronym
body:
Since the scheduler arrived in eb2ec8c78 (2011), every task completion has retried every pending task: `cleanup` drains the `pending` queue, calls `tags.add` and `tags.valid` on each entry, and re-queues the ones still blocked. `tags.add` for `tagged` restrictions builds a fresh immutable `TagMap` (one `update` per tag, plus `Untagged` and `All`), through megamorphic `Map` and `Function2` calls. So the cost is O(completions × pending), and in a large build almost all of those retries fail for the same reason, usually the `All` cap.

On a whole-build `clean; compile` of Apache Pekko 1.7.1 on sbt 1.12.15, a caller audit counted about 36.8k tasks per build, about 200 pending tasks retried per completion, 7.3M `tags.add` and 14.7M `ConcurrentRestrictions.update` calls per build. In a kperf profile of that JVM (all threads), the stacks under `update`/`merge`, `Tags.getInt` and `EvaluateTask.tagMap` were about 2% of cycles, 1.3 points of it in itable stubs. Those threads are mostly off the critical path, so I don't expect wall time to move much; the point is to stop doing the work.

This commit groups pending tasks by a new `private[sbt] def restrictionKey(a)` on `ConcurrentRestrictions`: tasks with equal keys are interchangeable to `add`. `tagged` uses the task's tags, `limitTotal` and `unrestricted` a constant, and the default is the task itself, which claims nothing and keeps the old behaviour for third-party restrictions. A scan polls group heads from a priority queue ordered by submission sequence, so tasks are still tried in global FIFO order, and drops a group at its first refusal. Law 5 on the trait (`!valid(add(g, a)) => !valid(add(add(g, b), a))`) says a refused task stays refused while the state only grows, which is all a scan does, so the skipped tasks would have been refused anyway and tasks start in exactly the same order as before. Each completion now calls `tags.add` once per started task plus once per blocked group.

Started tasks are handed to the executor after the scan rather than during it, so a caller-runs `Executor` re-entering `cleanup` can't see a half-finished scan.

Evidence, from a synthetic build (80 Java-only projects in a binary-tree dependency graph, 3 × `clean; Test/compile` in one JVM) on the 1.x backport, base `1.13.x` vs this change, counted with a perflab-agent caller audit (`tags.add` is the real method, not its bridge):

```
                       base         fix
submits/completions    156,220      156,220
tags.add               13,506,530   415,027     (32x)
update                 27,391,112   1,182,993   (23x)
```

The base retried about 85 pending tasks per completion; with this change it is 2.7 `add` calls per completion. Pekko has more pending tasks per completion (about 200), so I'd expect a larger ratio there, but I haven't measured it yet.

The new `PendingTasksTest` has a Hedgehog property that drives the completion service on a single-threaded executor with random tag sets, weights, limits and completion order, and checks that tasks start in the same order as a model of the old retry-everything scan. A mutation that reorders the scan is caught. A second test submits 400 tasks under an `All` limit of 2 and asserts at most 4N `add` calls; the old scheduler makes 79,801. `tasks-standard` tests, MiMa (vs 2.1.0-RC3) and `scalafmtCheckAll` pass.

Risks: the change leans on law 5. The built-in `Tags` rules obey it for valid states; a `Tags.customLimit` that doesn't could now see a task start at the next completion instead of later in the same scan. A further step would be an allocation-free `canAdd`, or skipping the scan while the `All` cap is saturated; I've left those out to keep this small.

A backport to 1.x (off `1.13.x`, which contains v1.12.15) is on `perf/sched-pending-groups-1.x`, not pushed yet.

I used an LLM (Claude) to help write this change, its tests and this description; I've reviewed and run them as described above.

body:
# Summary

Adds a one-sentence routing pointer to six skill descriptions. Two pairs among the ten most
lexically similar descriptions name neither partner (`scikit-learn` / `umap-learn`,
`polars-bio` / `pysam`), and three pairs point in one direction only (`matplotlib` → `seaborn`,
`cirq` → `qiskit`, `pennylane` → `qiskit`). Each new sentence reuses the target skill's own
scope wording, in the style the library already uses ("For X, use Y.").

If the project now prefers fewer cross-references in descriptions, please close this; several
were removed between v2.65.0 and v2.72.0, and this PR does not assume that was unintended.

## Type of change

- [x] Update to an existing skill

## Skills touched

- polars-bio
- pysam
- qiskit
- scikit-learn
- seaborn
- umap-learn

## How this was tested

Similarity uses the method in Section 4 of the library's paper (arXiv:2609.00065v2): lower-cased
alphanumeric tokens of at least 3 characters, a function-word stop-list, log-TF × IDF, and cosine
over all description pairs. A pointer is a description that names another skill. Measured on
`main` at `2d2065f`, before and after this change:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Pairs at cosine ≥ 0.25 without pointers both ways | 4 | 0 |
| Top-20 most similar pairs with a pointer | 14 | 17 |

| Pair | Cosine before → after | Pointers before | Added |
|---|---|---|---|
| scikit-learn ~ umap-learn | 0.276 → 0.488 | none | both ways |
| polars-bio ~ pysam | 0.262 → 0.411 | none | both ways |
| matplotlib ~ seaborn | 0.332 → 0.384 | matplotlib → seaborn | seaborn → matplotlib |
| cirq ~ qiskit | 0.250 → 0.514 | cirq → qiskit | qiskit → cirq |
| pennylane ~ qiskit | 0.289 (after) | pennylane → qiskit | qiskit → pennylane |

The pointer text itself raises lexical similarity, so the cosine column goes up by
construction. The measure is a lexical proxy for confusability, not observed agent selection.

```
python -m pytest tests/_meta -q
```

Same result before and after this change: 18 passed, 4,222 subtests passed. On Windows the two
`shell_scripts` executable-bit subtests (`latex-posters`, `scientific-schematics`) also fail on
unmodified `main`; that is a Windows filesystem artifact, and they pass on Linux.

Not run locally: `uv run skills-ref validate` and the per-skill suites on Python 3.13. None of
the six suites reads description text. Please rely on this PR's CI for both.

## Related issues and references

- Method: arXiv:2609.00065v2, Section 4 and Appendix G.
- Earlier link-contract work: #258.

---

## Checklist

**Skill format**

- [x] The skill directory name and the `name` frontmatter match exactly.
- [x] The skill directory contains only `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`, and `assets/`; no files added.
- [x] `SKILL.md` has valid YAML frontmatter and a Markdown body.
- [x] Only the six spec-defined top-level fields are present.
- [x] `metadata` is a block mapping; unchanged apart from the version.
- [x] No `metadata.openclaw` or `metadata.hermes` block changed.
- [x] `metadata.version` bumped by a minor step in all six skills.
- [x] Each `description` still says what the skill does and when to use it (all under 460 characters).

**Validation and tests**

- [ ] `uv run skills-ref validate ./skills/<name>`: not run locally, see above.
- [x] No tests added or moved.
- [x] `tests/_meta` passes as on `main`; per-skill suites not run, see above.

author: piyumisandunika
body:
<!--
The TITLE of this pull request becomes the commit on main (squash merge), so write it as a
conventional commit: type(scope): what changed
  feat(m1): register an entity      fix(kernel): ...      docs: ...      chore(deps): ...
A check fails when the title does not have that form.

## Summary

Install and test formulae by their fully qualified tap name (`open-telemetry/tap/<name>`) instead of by file path.

Previously, brew fell back to loading `Formula/ocb.rb` as a formula from the path (it logged `Treating Formula/ocb.rb as a formula`). Homebrew/brew#24442 ("Require explicit internal package source loading") restricted default formula and cask lookup to names.

The Linux job picks this up because `setup-homebrew` pulls the latest brew. The macOS job uses the runner's preinstalled brew, so it will likely hit the same error once that updates.

author: tomash
body:
## What this changes

Three compile-time switches for targets where the runtime's flash and static RAM are the budget: 32-bit microcontrollers. I found them while porting spinel to the ESP32-C3, where Ruby runs as a FreeRTOS task with ~300 KB of DRAM. Each one is off by default, and the generated C does not change.

- **`SP_NO_ALLOC_REPORT`** compiles the `SPINEL_ALLOC_REPORT` machinery out of the runtime and the program. Even when it is off at run time, the report kept its stats and type-name tables in `.bss` and its constructor (which reads the environment and arms the report signal) in every binary. Through the tags `sp_tu_init` registers, it also kept every container kind's scan function in the link. With the define, `sp_alloc_report_on` is the constant 0, `sp_alloc_report_tag` is a no-op that drops its arguments, and `sp_alloc.c` defines none of the reporter. On amd64, hello.rb links 12 KB less text and 270 KB less bss; on the ESP32-C3 it saves 16 KB of static RAM. `make no-alloc-report-test` checks both halves: a program compiled with the define references no reporter symbol, and `sp_alloc.c` compiled with it defines none.
- **`--no-bigint`**: no value may be a Bignum. The loop-growth detectors leave accumulators at Integer, so their overflow raises `RangeError` like any other raise-mode arithmetic. A value that can only be a Bignum is refused at its line, with a hint for the 32-bit case (`0xdeadbeef` on a 32-bit target). `--no-bigint` is refused together with `--int-overflow=promote`. On the C3 this keeps the bigint runtime, and the float formatting and libm it reaches, out of an integer-only program. Just as important there, a silent Bignum becomes a loud error. `make no-bigint-test` covers the loop, the refusal, and that no `sp_bigint_*` symbol is linked.
- **`SP_FIBER_STACK_CACHE_MAX`**: the fiber stack cache keeps 32 stacks, but its two arrays were sized for 1024 slots (8 KB of bss on 32-bit, 16 KB on 64-bit). The bound can now be overridden like the runtime's other static tables, and a default above it is a compile error.

Docs: `docs/int-overflow.md` (`--no-bigint`) and `docs/profiling.md` (`SP_NO_ALLOC_REPORT`).

On hardware (ESP32-C3 running a WiFi status server with OTA updates), these plus the existing capacity macros take the runtime's static RAM from 98 KB to 32 KB, and the program's free heap at idle from 36 KB to 103 KB.

body:
## Summary

Profiling execution now belongs to Engineering's pipeline configuration. Data Contract Authoring retains governance definitions and Guardrails without requiring saved profiles.

- Add `setup_pipeline(profiling_enabled=True, profiling_interval_days=1, profiling_max_rows=None, grain_discovery_enabled=False, frequency_enabled=False)`. Booleans are strict; integer settings reject booleans and nonpositive/noninteger values. Read/Write inherit the active session settings.
- Standard runs first when eligible, then on each pipeline's configured interval against the latest shared confirmed physical workspace/item/table completion. Grain discovery and Frequency are independent opt-ins, each first-completion-only. Standalone `profile_table()` also defaults both to False.
- Remove contract profiling controls and new-payload `profiling` objects. Retain historical frozen Contracts unchanged; their old profiling objects have no execution authority. Missing profiles remain “Not yet profiled.” Schema, Grain, DQ, Freshness, Source Drift, Sensitive Data and Processing requirements retain their enforcement.
- Include profiling settings in saved notebook submission/promotion parameters and compare them during Governed setup. Existing promotions without approved settings require a newly tested submission and promotion.

## Bounded profiling and metadata

`profiling_max_rows=None` retains complete-table profiling. A positive value applies Spark `limit` before statistics, Grain search and distributions; Warehouse selects `TOP (n)` and profiles the bounded selection in Spark. The selected DataFrame is cached for that activity and released afterward. This arbitrary selection is not representative sampling and does not guarantee reading only n physical rows.

Existing profile and Frequency tables gain nullable `profile_scope` / `profiling_max_rows` columns through normal additive metadata setup. Activity JSON and Catalogue Grain-candidate JSON also retain scope; no new tables are added. Full snapshots remain separately stored. Counts, uniqueness and distributions from bounded selections are sample-only facts, clearly labelled in Data Contract Authoring and AI authoring context. Sampled candidates cannot automatically supply table-wide key suggestions. Full-table Read/Write totals remain unknown when only bounded counts exist. Samples never drive mandatory Guardrails, Source Observation, checkpoints or publication.

Failed/skipped/nonpublishing Writes do not consume eligibility. Dry Run does not persist completion claims. Historical Run JSON without the new scope members retains its logical content/hash semantics.

SQL routing from #1809 is unchanged. Restricted query results never masquerade as complete-source profiling or Source Observation; due full-table profiling reports its physical scope and possible full-scan cost.

## Validation

- Full local unit run: 2,474 passed initially; eight obsolete signature/schema/approval assertions were updated and their affected modules reran successfully (292 passed, 1 skipped). Two unchanged dashboard CLI-browser tests still time out locally; a separate `chromium --dump-dom about:blank` probe also hangs in this environment.
- Combined contract/template/integration run: 201 passed, 129 skipped initially; the two template assertions were updated, with template/metadata rerun passing (47 tests).
- Final core profiling, promotion, metadata, Guardrail independence, SQL-routing and template run: **214 passed**, including real Spark aggregates. Rebased template/SQL run: **80 passed**. Sampled Grain UI cases: **4 passed**.
- Actual ipywidget browser check passes across every tab at 1440/1050/700 px; captured screenshots inspected.
- Ruff, compileall, strict MkDocs build, wheel/sdist build and Twine checks pass.
- API/call-flow/metadata references regenerated; the second reference run produces no diff. Architecture JSON and its matching timestamp are retained; historical release artifacts and dashboard HTML are unchanged.

Signed-in Microsoft Fabric execution and optional Delta runtime integration remain maintainer validation steps. Governed admission retains its existing Fabric validation gate. GitHub CI passed on the original implementation commit `da1615955`: all three unit shards, integration, contract/template, lint/docs/package and the required `validate` check. [CI run](https://github.com/Voycepeh/FabricOps-Starter-Kit/actions/runs/42781961589).

Base: latest main (`4b7624e3c`), including merged #1809 and its #1810 SQL examples. Do not merge automatically.

## Review follow-up (`098a695e9`)

- Respect orchestration verbosity and report scope only when an activity is actually due; disabled and not-due work stay quiet.
- Filter confirmed completion history by sufficient scope before choosing its latest timestamp. Full-table requests ignore bounded completions. Full completions satisfy bounded requests, and bounded completions satisfy equal or smaller requested limits. This includes first-only Grain/Frequency work and Standard intervals, across pipelines.
- Add real Spark history tests, bounded/full transitions, quiet-output cases, and older-full/newer-sample coverage.
- Correct the approval handoff to retain and compare the complete executed pipeline parameters during durable Dry Run capture and submission export; add a real setup-to-export regression.
- Local verification: 148 scheduling/observation/metrics tests, 60 history/session/configuration tests and 71 approval tests passed. Ruff and strict documentation pass; reference generation remains deterministic. All CI checks passed on this follow-up: [run 42784123198](https://github.com/Voycepeh/FabricOps-Starter-Kit/actions/runs/42784123198).

Introduced by ORB-23898 at frozen commit bbb4a7d7d1f4d7ca6efcdaea79c6b798942288eb (PR #9006), verified against that exact source.

In crates/orbit-engine/src/activity_job/cli_runner/orchestrator/completion/projection.rs:89-99, truncated_terminal_envelope_message falls back whenever the projected answer has no envelope, without checking whether a later terminal result was retained. latest_assistant_message (crates/orbit-agent/src/providers/mod.rs:194-229) skips a result with null/empty result and no structured_output, and returns an earlier assistant's envelope instead. Thus an exit-0 truncated stream ending in {"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","is_error":false,"terminal_reason":"max_turns","result":null} can select an earlier success envelope. project_completion:176-239 validates that older envelope; the success predicate at :274-283 has no generic terminal/max-turns rejection. The existing public dispatch fixture response_correction.rs:676-680 establishes this exit-zero max-turn terminal as a real failure shape.

Deterministic reproduction: a retained Claude JSONL tail containing an assistant text block with a valid success envelope followed by that max-turns result. The exact new helper, linked against the unchanged pinned orbit-agent/ParsedStdout public readers, returned recovered=true, selected_status=success, selected_frame_valid=true; ordinary projection has no envelope. The same happened with a later empty result and with structured-output-exhaustion lacking result text. Evidence and executable scratch probe are attached to ORB-23923. This is source/helper-level reproduction, not a full engine dispatch run. Before this commit the retained terminal remains the projected answer and the missing-envelope checks fail.

Preserve the intended recovery when no later terminal result exists, but do not replace a retained later terminal with earlier assistant text. Add a focused public dispatch regression alongside truncated_envelope.rs for the later exit-zero max-turns/empty-result cases. Keep error, refusal, and timeout behavior authoritative and reconcile the fail-closed documentation in docs/runbooks/executor-onboarding.md if recovery semantics change.

Escape: no_test. At the culprit revision, truncated_envelope.rs covers valid final assistant/no terminal, no envelope, and contradictory status; response_correction.rs covers max-turns and truncation separately, but no test combines a retained older success envelope, truncation, and a later empty terminal. No covering test was merely omitted by gates.
Severity: medium: a completion feature incorrectly accepts an incomplete turn; retaining an untruncated capture is a workaround. No data-loss consequence is asserted.
Duplicate checks: orbit.search kind=task all=true for truncated_terminal_envelope_message returned no hits; error_max_turns returned only completed ORB-10746; stale assistant envelope returned prior resolved defects in other providers, not this new Claude fallback.

### Acceptance Criteria

- A truncated Claude capture with an earlier assistant success envelope and a later retained exit-zero max-turns or empty terminal result fails completion instead of selecting the earlier envelope, demonstrated through the public dispatch boundary.
- The intended truncated capture ending on a valid final assistant envelope without a later terminal still succeeds, and contradictory envelope/error validation remains enforced.

## Execution Summary
