author: mathusanm6
body:
### Summary
Implements the core RaftKV distributed cache service built on top of `github.com/jathurchan/raft`.

### Key Components
- **Protobuf Schema (`proto/raftkv/v1/raftkv.proto`)**: Client gRPC interface, internal Raft state-machine commands (`Set`, `Delete`, `EvictBatch`), and snapshot format.
- **Deterministic Memory Accounting (`pkg/cache`)**: Exact 648-byte accounting per entry (`len(k) + len(v) + 72`) with 557,056 bytes reserved upfront for a 4,096-slot circular `TombstoneRing`.
- **Wrap-Around Delete Safety**: Overwrites in the tombstone ring only delete from the lookup map if the version matches the slot entry, preventing double-delete bugs.
- **Pluggable Evictions (`pkg/eviction`)**: Thread-safe `LRU`, `LFU`, `W-TinyLFU` (Window LRU + Count-Min Sketch + SLRU), and `ColdStartWrapper` (warmup by apply index).
- **Raft State Machine & Node (`pkg/raftnode`)**:
  - `Applier`: Deterministic idempotent log replay and atomic snapshot encoding/decoding.
  - `ReadIndexCoalescer`: Coalesces concurrent reads into linearizable next-round batches.
  - `ProposalManager`: Enforces pre-consensus 100% hard limit rejection and 90% soft limit batched evictions.
- **Servers (`pkg/server`)**: gRPC server on `:9000` with follower redirection hints, and HTTP management server on `:8080` (`/status`, `/livez`, `/readyz`, `/debug/reset-policy`).

---
*Part 1 of 7 in the raftkv stack.*

author: sp3rick
body:
## What changes for the user

**User:** an allowed `.eth`, IPFS or Swarm site that keeps its own service worker (an offline-first app) works on every reload again. Its page is answered by its worker, and `window.orivon` and the site's grants are there, on a reload, on a start and with the gateway gone. Since the site started running in the session websites run in, such an app lost them on every reload once its worker was installed.

**Dev:** an app may register a service worker that answers its navigations and still call `orivon.*` on those pages. Its worker script must come from the app's own files: a script Orivon did not serve is refused at registration.

## Changes

### Keep the grants of a page an allowed site's own service worker answers

**Goal.** A document is the app's if the shell answered it or if the app's own worker did, and the worker's bytes are the app's.

**What it achieves.**
- A page with no response seen by the session, committed while the shell served the origin, in the app's tab, whose top frame reports a controlling worker, is attributed, once the origin has settled.
- A worker script (or an import: `importScripts` and module-worker imports are `script` requests with no page, measured) of a served origin that the shell did not serve is cancelled when its headers arrive, from before the website's old workers are removed, so every worker at that origin is the app's. A request another origin issued (its worker importing from this one) is let go when Electron names the initiator. The preparer lives in `website-workers-subsystem.ts`, listed above the loader, because the loader restores pinned apps at a start and each needs it.
- **Settling (review fix F2).** A website page open or loaded before the host knew the site is served can write Cache Storage, which the app's worker would then answer with. The origin now settles in order: the shell announces what it serves and waits for the host's acknowledgement (`shell-serves-applied`); every website page open then, in every session, loads again; once those have committed, the origin's workers and Cache Storage are removed; only documents that commit after that count for a worker's answer. A worker script the shell served is held until the origin settles, so the app's first registration cannot race the removal. Each wait is bounded; a timeout fails closed (no grants for worker answers, worker scripts cancelled) and retries with a doubling delay. A first visit waits, within a bound, for the host's word, loads its tab as the app, and the settling waits for the tab to show the shell's document.
- **Versioned marks (F3).** The "workers cleared" marks live in `website-workers-cleared-v2/`; marks of an earlier rule are not read, so a pinned app has its origin cleared once more with the guard armed.
- **Extensions (F5).** The extension webRequest dispatch and the declarative rules refuse to add, change or remove any `x-orivon-*` header, on a request or a response, and the shell-mark watch reads the mark where the headers arrive, before an extension's change.
- Still denied: a document from the HTTP cache or the network (whatever controls it), a document nothing is known of, a page committed before serving began or before the origin settled, any other view or session.

**How it works.** Read `src/main/sessions/worker-settle.ts` (the order, Electron-free) and `src/main/sessions/session-attribution.ts` first. Main cannot tell which worker controls a document (Electron names none), so the tab's preload reads `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` in its isolated world and reports it (`src/preload/worker-control.ts`); main takes it only from the top frame, for the committed address. Why not track registrations or script addresses: [`ADR-0113`](docs/decisions/ADR-0113-a-page-an-allowed-sites-own-service-worker-answers-keeps-the-sites-grants-because-no-other-worker-script-can-be-registered-there.md) (amends ADR-0108).

## Streams, paths and merge order

- **Streams:** main, verifier host protocol, preload, test, docs
- **Paths touched:** `src/main/sessions/`, `src/main/verifier/`, `src/protocols/verifier-host/` (one message and its acknowledgement), `src/main/extensions/` (protected headers), `src/main/install/` (first visit waits for the host's word), `src/main/subsystems.ts`, `src/preload/`, `src/main/channels.ts`, `test/web3/`, `test/app-behaviours/catalogue.md`, docs -- all mine
- **App behaviours:** rows `allowed-app-worker-keeps-grants`, `allowed-app-unchecked-worker-never-installs` (spec `e2e-allowed-app-worker-answers`), reworded; changelog line updated
- **Contracts:** none changed
- **Merge order:** independent

## Decisions and open questions

ADR-0113 and `d-0787`; numbered past the ADR-0112 and d-0786 main holds; whichever PR merges later renumbers. Open questions: none. Written in the ADR as limits: a website page opened and closed wholly between two looks of the settling is not seen (*provisional*); and a content script of an extension on the app tab can write Cache Storage on the origin and so have the app's worker serve a page the shell never checked, the same class of risk ADR-0108 accepts for extensions on an allowed site, now reaching any extension with host access to the site rather than only those with webRequest.

## How it was verified

- Unit tests written first and shown failing, then passing: settle order and bounds (`worker-settle.test.ts`), the attribution gate (removing the settled check fails three attribution tests), the first visit's blank-settle-enter order (fails without the wait), acknowledgement counting, the versioned marks, the initiator exemption, protected headers (an extension's added mark does not attribute), and the subsystem wiring.
- E2E `e2e-allowed-app-worker-answers`: first test covers a reload, another address, Back, the gateway gone and a restart; second holds the host's word back, shows a refused worker and no grants, then releases it and shows the shell's page, the app's worker and its grants.
- Also run: `e2e-first-visit-service-worker`, `e2e-first-visit-order`, `e2e-tunnelled-app-answered-by-the-shell`, `e2e-website-page-never-becomes-the-app`, `e2e-eth-app-update-boundary`, `e2e-eth-app-update-open-tab`, `e2e-app-origin-platform`, `e2e-extensions-webrequest`.
- `npm run typecheck`, `test:changed` (302 files) and the guards pass locally; `e2e-allowed-app-worker-answers`, `e2e-tunnelled-app-answered-by-the-shell` and `e2e-website-page-never-becomes-the-app` pass locally. CI: green and CLEAN on the last head. Earlier runs failed once each on `e2e-app-oauth-popup` and `e2e-eth-system-proxy-environment` (specs this change cannot reach) and passed on rerun: flakes. The first CI failures of the settling spec were real and fixed (the host protocol validator dropped the acknowledgement; the tunnelled site's first page can take longer than the first visit's bound).

## Risk and rollback

Security boundary (who gets grants). Every new wait fails closed to "no grants for worker answers"; the shell's own answers are unaffected. Rollback: remove the guard, the settling and the report, and a worker-answered page is denied again.

author: treydone
body:
## Story
`[S62-03] choregos a2a: start and follow a workflow over the A2A door` — `docs/plan/08-backlog.yaml`

## Change
A `choregos a2a` command group, so a person or a script starts a Choregos workflow over the A2A door, hands it its data and files, and follows it to its result without writing JSON-RPC (`packages/cli/src/choregos_cli/a2a.py`).

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `choregos a2a skills [--json]` | the card's skills, with their fields from the `skill-fields/v1` extension (`*` = required) |
| `choregos a2a send <skill> [--text …] [--field k=v …] [--fields-json file] [--file PATH[;type=…] …] [--message-id …] [--title …] [--wait] [--out DIR] [--json]` | `message/send`: text parts = body, one data part = fields, files in base64 with a media type guessed from the extension |
| `choregos a2a get <task> [--out DIR] [--json]` | `tasks/get` |
| `choregos a2a follow <task> [--out DIR] [--json]` | `tasks/resubscribe` until a final state, reopened after the hour cut |
| `choregos a2a cancel <task> [--json]` | `tasks/cancel` |

Choices:
- **Token**: `--token` / `CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN`, else the profile's token. A `403` whose `WWW-Authenticate` says `insufficient_scope` prints the door's message plus `choregos tokens create --scope a2a …` and `choregos machines token …`.
- **Default `--message-id`**: `cli-` + a sha256 digest of the message (skill, title, texts, fields, files). It is printed on stderr before the call. The same command sent again after a timeout finds the same task, and nothing starts twice. To start the same request again on purpose, pass a new `--message-id`.
- **`--wait` / `follow`**: `message/send` (or nothing), then `tasks/resubscribe`. A stream that ends without a final status (the door's hour cut), or a connection that breaks after the stream started, is opened again after one second. A door that cannot be reached, or a refusal, is not retried. On `input-required`, `decision_url` is printed once per request, and the command keeps waiting. At the end, `tasks/get` reads the final task. **Exit codes**: 0 completed, 3 failed (or rejected), 4 canceled, 1 refused or unreachable, 2 usage, 130 interrupted.
- **`--out`**: the artefacts of a completed task, written as text (`.md` when the name has no extension), JSON (`.json`) or file bytes. An artefact the task only describes (too large, withheld) is named, not written. Names are reduced to their base name.
- **`--json`**: stdout carries only the task as the door answers it (the final one with `--wait`). Progress goes to stderr.
- **Own client, not `choregos_adapters.a2a.A2aClient`**: `choregos-cli` depends on `choregos-core` + httpx only. Adapters would bring cryptography, PyJWT, structlog and pydantic into the CLI. Its client also parses a task into dataclasses that drop what a script needs here (the raw task for `--json`, `error.data.errors`, `metadata.choregos`), and it has neither the card nor `tasks/resubscribe`. The CLI's client is async (`httpx.AsyncClient`, `asyncio.run` per command), so a test can hand it an ASGI transport.

Docs: `docs/starting-a-workflow-from-outside.md` gives a CLI way at each step of "The A2A door, step by step" (the curl blocks `test_a2a_guide.py` replays are unchanged). The "No CLI verb for the A2A door" bullet is gone. `docs/cli.md` is regenerated. The two A2A entries of `MACHINE_ONLY_ROUTES` (`tests/web/test_api_routes_have_a_client.py`) now say that `choregos a2a` also calls them. No ceiling or allowlist moved: no crossing import, no API path added.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `choregos a2a skills` lists the card's skills and their fields from the extension
- [x] `send` with `--text`, `--field`, `--fields-json`, `--file`, `--title`, `--message-id`; the default message id is stable and printed
- [x] `--wait` follows until a final state, prints the decision URL on input-required and keeps waiting, exits 0 only on completed, `--out` writes the artefacts
- [x] `get`, `follow` (resubscribes on the hour cut), `cancel`
- [x] `--json` on skills/send/get/follow/cancel
- [x] `--token` / `CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN` with a fallback to the profile; a clear message on `403 insufficient_scope`
- [x] Guide updated, "No CLI verb" bullet removed, `docs/cli.md` regenerated, STATUS row after S62-01, `**Total**` = 619/299/9
- [x] End-to-end test against the real door through ASGI with the CLI's client code

## Proof
- `uv run pytest packages/cli/tests tests/docs tests/architecture tests/web/test_api_routes_have_a_client.py tests/language apps/api/tests/test_a2a*.py`: **925 passed, 2 skipped**
- `uv run ruff check` + `ruff format --check` on `packages/cli`, `tests/web`, `apps/api/tests/test_a2a_cli.py`: clean
- `uv run mypy packages/*/src` (strict): no issues in 320 files
- `make docs-cli`: regenerated and committed. `tools/check_english.py` and `--all`: 0 findings
- Guards turned red by removing them one at a time:
  - no reconnection after a stream without a final status: `test_send_wait_follows_through_a_decision_and_the_hour_cut…`, `test_a_stream_that_breaks_is_opened_again`, and the end-to-end `test_the_cli_starts_a_workflow_with_a_file_and_follows_it_across_the_hour_cut` go red
  - no scope hint: `test_a_star_token_is_refused…` and the end-to-end `test_the_cli_says_a_star_token_does_not_open_the_door` go red
  - a random default message id: `test_send_puts_text_fields_and_files_in_one_message`, `test_send_wait_json…` and the end-to-end idempotency assertion go red
  - a broken stream not retried: `test_a_stream_that_breaks_is_opened_again` goes red
  - the decision URL printed on every frame: `test_send_wait_follows_through_a_decision…` goes red

## Contracts

## Findings filed
- None.

## STATUS row
S62-03 ✅. **Proves**: `apps/api/tests/test_a2a_cli.py` drives the real door through ASGI with the CLI's client. It covers the card's fields, a message with fields and a file, the same command twice giving one task, a follow across a cut stream to `failed`, a `*` token refused with the hint, and refused fields with their reasons. `packages/cli/tests/test_a2a.py` (respx) covers the message the commands build, the stable id, `--wait` through a decision and the cut to the written artefacts, the exit codes, a broken stream reopened and an unreachable door not retried, the token's precedence, and `--json` on stdout. **Does not prove**: the typer commands against the real door. The CLI runs `asyncio.run` per command and the ASGI app lives in the test's event loop, so the end-to-end test calls the client functions the commands call. author: brandondurandpro
body:
## Problem
\`AgentQuotaRefreshE2eTest\` › \`the silent question never shows in the conversation, even while it is asked\` timed out after 60 s on Linux 22.04 · x11 (PR #191), while passing on the other 5 Linux configurations. The PR did not touch the agent.

It waited for \`conversation.timedTurns >= 3\`. That counter skips a turn that ends while the silent probe is marked (\`probeFrom != null\`, \`syncWorkingClock\`), so depending on the agent's pace it can stay at 2 and never reach 3.

## Fix
Wait for what the test is about: the quota reached the echo's turn (\`percent >= THIRD_TURN_PERCENT\`, the probe was answered), the agent is idle and no probe is in flight. The assertion that no \`probe-\` item was shown is unchanged.

## Tests
Test-only change (no feature, no UI behavior): \`./kotlin test -m agent --include-classes='*AgentQuotaRefreshE2eTest'\` passes, \`./lint\` passes. \`./ci\` was not run locally; the CI will.

author: powerbot-1
body:
## What this changes

Per-site Website Studio route audit: two defects found and fixed, plus regression coverage for the v1 / format-2 compatibility work that merged in #106.

### 1. Save accepted a document that switched the site's business category — fixed

`PUT /api/studio/websites/content` validated the draft against the business's category and then stored whatever `categoryKey` the request body carried. A document naming another category was silently accepted, which changes the sections, catalogue rules and storefront flow the site renders with.

The site's own business is now the authority:

- a mismatched `categoryKey` is refused with **422** + `experience_schema_invalid`;
- a missing `categoryKey` is pinned to the business's own;
- a payload that is not a document at all (`null`, string, array, number) is refused with **400** rather than repaired into a *default* website and overwriting the owner's draft with placeholder content.

### 2. Refusals for an unsupported document disagreed between routes — fixed

`publish` answered a refused document with `code: "experience_schema_invalid"`. `save`, `rollback` and `restore` sent the same refusal with **no code**, so a client could not tell an unsupported document from a database failure without parsing prose. All four now send the code and the `issues` list.

## Audit result for the rest of the per-site surface

Reviewed `studio/websites/{route,content,publish,revisions,rollback}.ts` and the `/api/experience/*` routes. Tenant checks (`assertStudioWebsiteAccess` / `assertStudioPublicationAccess`) resolve the business from the website record, never from the request body; every write is a compare-and-swap on the version the client read; suspended tenants and sites, stale versions and inline media are each refused before any write. No further unguarded throw was found.

I specifically tested the hypothesis that `validateExperienceJson` could return `ok` and then let normalization throw (a 500). **It cannot** — `validateExperienceDocument` normalizes internally, so the refusal is always reported as issues. A 20-case probe over art-direction, version and shape variants found 0 cases that validate-ok-then-throw. This is recorded so the wrong hypothesis is not carried forward as a defect.

## Legacy-draft compatibility (v1 and format 2)

- **Fixture defect fixed.** The "legacy v1" fixture was `const v1 = () => baseDocument()`, format 1 only by coincidence — the moment the default document emits a newer format, every legacy test would have silently exercised the current format. It is now a literal format-1 document, and the block asserts it carries no format-2 field.
- **Load (GET) coverage added** for format-1, format-2, version-less and malformed stored drafts, plus an unsupported stored version — none may 500, and none may modify the stored bytes.
- **Malformed vs unsupported** documents now have separate tests with distinct expectations.
- **Explicit current-format (2) coverage** added alongside the v1 regression.
- **Preview resolution** for a legacy draft: the owner sees the draft, the public keeps the published snapshot.

## Evidence

Both defects are **mutation-verified**: reintroducing either one fails the new tests.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | **0 errors** |
| `npm run lint` | **0 errors**, 51 pre-existing warnings |
| `npm run build` | **succeeded** |
| Full `vitest run` | **4473 passed, 0 failed**, 375 files passed, 38 skipped |
| New route-hardening suite | **28/28** |
| `experience-version-guard` | **54/54** |
| Studio/experience targeted set (8 files) | **134/134** |

The 38 skipped files are database-gated suites (`realPrismaConfigured`); no PostgreSQL is available in this environment, so they were not executed and are **not** claimed as passing.

## Not claimed

- No production deployment was triggered.
- Production evidence (contrast, template selection, publish/history/rollback in a real browser, R2 media) is unchanged and still **BLOCKED / NOT TESTED** — no owner session and no R2 credentials in production.
- This is **not** full Website Studio 2.0 acceptance.

## Note on the branch name

The directive named `arena/dd512593-jata-aftercall`, but this session's active branch is `arena/f523ef51-jata-aftercall` (already at the #106 merge commit, with this work on top). It was not renamed or recreated.

body:
## Problem

On a Mac whose system language is neither English nor Simplified Chinese (e.g. German, French, Korean), Birth shows Chinese. `zh-Hans` is the package's `defaultLocalization` and the app's `CFBundleDevelopmentRegion`, so every unmatched system falls back to Chinese — even though a complete English translation ships.

## Changes

- **English is the fallback**: `defaultLocalization` and `CFBundleDevelopmentRegion` are now `en`; the Info.plist usage string is English, with Chinese moved into `zh-Hans.lproj/InfoPlist.strings`. `resolvedSystemLanguage` mirrors the new fallback.
- **New languages: German, French, Spanish, Japanese.** Full `Localizable.strings` for BirthUI and BirthCore, using Apple's own macOS terminology in each language (e.g. Systemeinstellungen / Réglages Système / Ajustes del Sistema / システム設定), plus a localized `NSAppleEventsUsageDescription` for each.
- **Settings**: new options Deutsch, Español, Français, 日本語. The relaunch notice and button speak the target language. The row label reads "Language / <current language's word>" so it stays readable in any language.
- **About window**: the copyright and "Built with ❤️ by" lines were hard-coded English; they now go through `L()`.
- **README / README_CN**: new Languages section, including how to add a translation.
- **Tests**: the core lockstep test lists all six languages; the UI lockstep test picks them up via `AppLanguage.allCases`.

Chinese and English systems behave exactly as before.

## Verification

- `swift test`: all tests pass, including both localization lockstep tests (identical key sets and format specifiers across all six languages).
- `./scripts/make-app.sh` builds; the packaged bundle resolves `de-DE → de`, `fr-FR → fr`, `ko-KR → en`, `zh-Hans-CN → zh-Hans`, `en-US → en`.

Translations other than German were machine-assisted and have not yet been reviewed by native speakers — corrections welcome.

author: prastoin
body: Follow-up to twentyhq/core-team-issues#3011: test that an OIDC login only completes in the browser that started it. At login, openid-client stores the PKCE verifier and the `state` in the browser's session. The callback checks both, and Okta only exchanges the code for the verifier it was issued with. Twenty sends no nonce, since it uses the code flow and PKCE fills that role. The suite already covered a callback with no session and a `state` naming another provider. It didn't cover these two: | Case | Error | |---|---| | `state` altered at the callback (same provider, an added invite hash) | Authentication error: Unauthorized | | Code from one login completed with another login's session | Authentication error: invalid_grant (PKCE verification failed.) | A state mismatch reads as "Unauthorized" because openid-client fails it without passing its message on. Without the check, the altered state would have gone through and failed later as "Workspace not found". ## Testing Both cases pass alone against the Okta tenant, and the whole `failing-sso-login` suite passes (23 tests) with no provider or SSO connected account left behind.

This follows #226 and #227. Once it's deployed, Tomifin can only be reached through Caddy on the tailnet (`https://down.tn.tomdixon.uk` → `127.0.0.1:8791`). No internet-facing path reaches any Tomifin code or data.

## Changes
**Worker**
- Removed `TOMIFIN_HOSTNAME` from `wrangler.toml` and `worker/env.ts`.
- Deleted `worker/routes/tomifin.ts`, `worker/routes/tomifin-site.ts`, their wiring in `worker/index.ts`, and `scripts/tomifin-worker.node-test.mjs`. No shared helper was used only by them.

**Agent**
- The Recovery listener (port 8788, the one the tunnel reaches) answers `404 {"error":"not-found"}` to every `/v1/tomifin*` path. It does this before the token check, so the answer is the same with or without a token. The Tomifin handlers are now only called by the local listener.
- The local listener's behaviour is unchanged: same sign-in, session, Origin check and routes.
- If the local port is already taken, the agent logs one line and Recovery keeps running: `Tomifin local listener is off: 127.0.0.1:<port> is already in use by another service. Set TOMIFY_TOMIFIN_LOCAL_PORT to a free port (8791 on the box), update Caddy's reverse_proxy to match, and restart tomify-recovery. Recovery keeps running.`
- The listener has no default port; it stays off until `TOMIFY_TOMIFIN_LOCAL_PORT` is set. The env example, docs and tests now use 8791.

**Docs**
- `docs/TOMIFIN.md` is rewritten for the tailnet-only setup: down.tn, Caddy, `127.0.0.1:8791`, a table of settings, the port-clash message, checks and rollback.

## Tests
- New `recovery-agent/recovery-listener.node-test.mjs` starts the real `index.mjs`.
  - GET and POST to six `/v1/tomifin*` paths return 404 with the right token, with no token and with a wrong token.
  - `/health` and `/v1/status` are unchanged.
  - The Tomifin listener still answers: 200 for the page and 401 for the API without a session.
  - A taken Tomifin port logs the one-line error and Recovery stays up.
- Worker:
  - New test: on Host `tomifin.tomdixon.uk` and on Tomify's host, `/api/tomifin/*` returns `404 {"error":"not-found"}` and never calls the agent.

1. **Merge.**
2. **Worker:** Cloudflare deploys it from `main` on merge. Wait for that deploy to finish. The public Tomifin site and API are then gone.
3. **Agent:** in the Windows checkout, run `git checkout main; git pull; pnpm install; .\scripts\deploy-agent.ps1`. This removes `/v1/tomifin/*` from the Recovery listener. Before running it, check that `TOMIFY_TOMIFIN_LOCAL_PORT=8791` is still in the env file.

5. **Verify:**

   | Command | Expected result |
   | --- | --- |
   | `nslookup tomifin.tomdixon.uk` | `NXDOMAIN` (after step 4) |
   | `curl -sS https://tomifin.tomdixon.uk/` | Can't resolve the host. Between steps 2 and 4 the host still resolves, but `curl -s https://tomifin.tomdixon.uk/api/tomifin/session` returns `{"error":"not-found"}` and no page contains "Tomifin". |

body:
Fixes found running #931's ACP driver against a real **OpenCode 2.2.6** (`opencode acp`) on the free model `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`.

- **Missing `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`.** OpenCode silently dropped our requests, and `initialize` timed out. `JsonRpcPeer` can now tag every message; ACP turns use that, Codex's app-server stays untagged.
- **Model selection.** OpenCode offers models as a session config option of category `model`, set with `session/set_config_option` (`configId`, `value`). The runner uses that and falls back to `session/set_model` only for agents without such an option.
- **Models reported to the platform.** At start the runner opens one session on an ACP harness, reads the offered models, and sends them in `hello` like Codex does. The client's Runner tab can then pick the model, a free one included.
- If OpenCode is configured through `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` (Orca sets it), the runner needs `--pass-env OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. Without it OpenCode answers `session/new` with `ServiceUnavailable`.

## Verified against real OpenCode
- Turn 1 sets the model and calls OpenCode's own `write` tool, which creates `hello.txt` containing `pong`. The run ends with `tool.result` success, the message `done`, then `completed` with a session id.
- Turn 2 resumes that session through `session/load` and answers `hello.txt` without replaying turn 1's events.
- The model report lists OpenCode's models, the free ones included.

CLI: prettier and tsc clean, ava 126 passed (new test: the session's model option and its models).

author: eraviart
body:
`prime_partage_valeur_exoneree` — la part de la PPV exonérée de cotisations — est ajoutée au `salaire_imposable` (cerfa 1AJ) et à l'`assiette_csg_abattue` sans la condition de rémunération qui borne pourtant l'exonération d'IR, de CSG et de CRDS (article 81 du CGI ; loi n° 2022-1158 du 16/08/2022, art. 1.V ; BOSS, « mesures exceptionnelles / protection du pouvoir d'achat ») : pour les primes versées jusqu'au 31/12/2023 aux salariés dont la rémunération des 12 derniers mois est inférieure à 3 Smic, cette part est non imposable — elle se déclare en case 1AD de la 2042 (DSN type 904), hors rémunération nette fiscale — et n'est prise en compte que pour le revenu fiscal de référence. Le modèle la taxe donc à l'IR, y prélève CSG/CRDS, et sa part pérenne n'atteint le RFR que par son passage dans le 1AJ.

Reproduction (2023, salaire 20 966,40 €/an, PPV 3 000 €) : 1AJ 19 993,77 € au lieu de 17 194,20 €, impôt 198 € au lieu de 0 €, RNI gonflé de 2 520 €. Sur la déclaration doctrinale (1AJ sans la prime, case 1AD), la calculette DGFiP (oracle Mlang, millésime 2023) calcule IRN 0 € et RNI 15 475 €. `tests/formulas/prime_partage_valeur.yaml` encodait ce comportement comme attendu pour les salaires < 3 Smic ; ses lignes sont corrigées et un nouveau `tests/formulas/prime_partage_valeur_non_imposable.yaml` couvre PPV 780 € et 3 000 € sous 3 Smic, le témoin sans prime, et le cas > 3 Smic (inchangé : prime imposable, DSN 905).

Correctif : deux variables datées jusqu'au 31/12/2023 — `ppv_eligibilite` (symétrique de `ppv_eligibilite_exceptionnelle`, même fenêtre glissante des 12 mois) et `prime_partage_valeur_non_imposable` (part exonérée × éligibilité) — sont sorties du `salaire_imposable` et de l'`assiette_csg_abattue`, ajoutées au `salaire_net` et au RFR (× 0,9, symétrique de la part exceptionnelle). Après correctif : sous 3 Smic, 1AJ et impôt identiques au témoin sans prime, CSG/CRDS inchangées, RFR + 90 % de la prime ; au-dessus de 3 Smic, comportement inchangé. La part pérenne sous 3 Smic rejoint le traitement déjà correct de la part exceptionnelle (rfr, impôt, prestations identiques). Sous 3 Smic la part exonérée de cotisations reste exonérée comme avant ; en 2024+ le comportement est inchangé (l'exonération d'IR dépend alors de la taille de l'entreprise, non modélisée).

Revue demandée : @clallemand @b-michaud

author: lszomoru
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up of #347275 and #347287, for #345429: the two jobs of `component-fixtures.yml` that install the dependencies, **Playwright Fixture Tests** and **Screenshots**, start from the workspace image of `main`, like the jobs of `pr.yml`.

## What changes

- **Image steps:** both jobs download the image scripts, set up Node.js and restore the Linux image before the checkout, exactly like the jobs of `pr.yml` (the steps are defined in Playwright Fixture Tests and reused with YAML anchors), and check out with `clean: false` when they mounted one. The install steps are unchanged, and install only what changed since the commit of the image.
- **Pull requests and pushes:** the workflow also runs on pushes to `main` and `release/*`. Pull requests use the images of their base branch, and pushes those of their branch, so pushes to `main` also start from an image, while release branches, which have no images, install everything.
- **No pnpm store cache:** without an image, or on any error or timeout of the restore, the jobs install everything with a plain `pnpm install`, like the jobs of `pr.yml`. The workflow no longer restores or saves `pnpm-store-component-fixtures`, which only these jobs used.
- **Playwright browsers:** the jobs keep restoring the Playwright browsers cache, also with an image. They install full Chromium, while the image only holds Chromium's headless shell, so `restore-playwright` points `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` at the cached browsers in the workspace instead of the image's. Pushes to `main` keep saving that cache.
- **Permissions:** the workflow gets `actions: read` to find and download the image artifacts.
- **Guard test and docs:** `workspaceImage.test.ts` checks that both jobs download the image scripts like the jobs that build the images, and the workspace image README, the CI caches README and the header of `pr-workspace-images.yml` list them.

## Reviewers should know

- **Playwright Fixture Tests** gains little, if anything: with the store cache, its checkout, store restore and install take about 20 s in recent runs, and restoring the Linux image takes about 12–20 s on its own. It moves to the image mostly so that the workflow no longer depends on the pnpm store.
- **Screenshots** should gain more: its 150-commit checkout, store restore and `build` install (which builds native modules) take about 55–75 s in recent runs.
- Without an image, both jobs now download every package instead of restoring the store cache, so they set up more slowly in that case.
- Merging this pull request builds new images, since it changes `pr-workspace-images.yml`.

## How to test

This pull request's own run of Component Fixtures runs both jobs: each one reports in its job summary that it restored an image, or a `Workspace image` warning when it installed everything instead.

- `cd build && node --test lib/test/workspaceImage.test.ts lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts lib/test/detectMissingCaches.test.ts lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts`: passed, 36 tests.
- `cd build && pnpm run typecheck`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint build/lib/test/workspaceImage.test.ts`: passed.
- `actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/component-fixtures.yml .github/workflows/pr-workspace-images.yml` (actionlint 1.7.12): passed, apart from the custom runner labels.
- Not run locally: the jobs themselves, with and without an image, and a push to `main`, which runs after merging.

author: ddtcorex
body:
## The problem

The `key` track was unreachable from a Claude-only session. `memory_add` refused it with:

```
key is gated — use memory_suggest target=key with reason (direct memory add for key is CLI-only)
```

There is no CLI. So the only real path was the queue, and the queue can only be decided in the DSH Memory view. On a machine without DSH open, a suggestion waits forever, and nothing in the session even reports that it is waiting.

## What changed

- **`memory_add` accepts `target:key` with `approved:true`.** The model shows the exact entry, asks with `AskUserQuestion` (write it, edit it, skip), and sends the flag only after an explicit yes. Without the flag nothing is written and the refusal names both real paths: ask in the session, or defer with `memory_suggest`.
- **A key write still requires `cwd`**, because key entries are per project.
- **The tool schema now advertises both**: `key` in the enum and `approved` as a boolean. Without that the call was invalid at the schema boundary, so the handler change alone would have been dead code.
- **The session-start context reports a non-empty queue**, one line, before the snapshot: `[maestro-memory] 2 suggestions are waiting for approval; review them in the DSH Memory view.` Nothing else in a session can see that queue, which is how suggestions filled up unseen.
- The skill, `/remember`, README and CHANGELOG describe the ask-first flow; version 5.2.0.

## Honest note on the gate

It changes nature. Before, a model could not write `key` at all. Now it can, and whether it asks first depends on following the skill. On a machine where the agent has a shell, no local mechanism can prevent that; the difference between "impossible" and "depends on compliance" is real and this PR moves to the second. What still holds: a key entry is visible in the Memory view, editable and removable, and the queue path still exists for anything deferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/mcp-tools.spec.ts`: refusal without the flag writes nothing; write succeeds with it; key without `cwd` is refused; the old test that pinned the dead-end message now pins both real paths
- [x] `tests/mcp-definitions.spec.ts`: `key` in the enum, `approved` boolean, description names the ask
- [x] `tests/hook-session-start.spec.ts`: two queued entries produce the notice, an empty queue produces none
- [x] 569 tests, `pnpm verify`, `pnpm build`
- [x] Real bin, temp store: one queued entry prints the singular line, two print the plural, empty queue prints nothing
- [x] `node scripts/check-public-blacklist.mjs`: 0 hits

## Release note

The plugin pins 5.2.0 in `.mcp.json` and `hooks/hooks.json`, so publish before updating the plugin, as always.

author: karlnaumann
body:
## Summary

Give each model built without `parameters` its own `Parameters` object, so a hyperparameter set on one model no longer changes the others.

## Type

`fix`

## What changed

Python evaluates a default argument once, when the class is defined. `Model.__init__` then updates `parameters.hyper` in place. As a result, `GL06SIM(hyperparameters={"dtype": "float64"})` switched every GL06SIM built without `parameters` to float64, including models built earlier.

- Change the `parameters` default from `ParametersX()` to `None` in 13 model constructors. Each constructor already builds a fresh `ParametersX()` when `parameters` is `None`. KirmansAnts, Mark0COVID and PichlerEtAl2022DIO use the same pattern.
- Add `test_default_parameters_not_shared` to `BaseModelTest` (`tests/models/common_test.py`), so it runs for every model.

## Quality assurance

- Tests: the new test fails on the 13 models without the fix and passes on all 16 with it. Non-slow core and model tests pass.

author: kjgbot
body:
When a native upload credential expires, Desktop posts to `/v1/auth/token/refresh`. In Control-only reader mode the ingress omitted that exact path, so the reader returned 405. Desktop classified refresh as an outage and kept retrying the expired credential instead of renewing from its healthy Control sign-in.

Route that exact path to native ingest in both reader modes. Ingest already returns `401 refresh_not_supported`, which triggers the existing Desktop renewal flow. Keep descendant paths on the reader and internal issuer routes private. Update the Kind ownership guard to require the same route and reject a missing, widened or misdirected path. Bump sessions-pipeline to 0.8.17 and agent-relay to 0.6.26; no image or admission mode changes.

Validation: 9 chart routing tests and 38 Kind network tests pass; the old template fails the new refresh-route regression. Two-chart static checks, the full umbrella render contract and pinned Helm goldens, the requirements registry (139 entries / 27 profiles), and version/whitespace checks pass. A guarded live route repair changed the public refresh result from 405 to the expected 401 over verified HTTPS. Separate runtime checks confirmed bidirectional native messaging, 85 acknowledged uploads, authenticated event readback, and newly generated summaries. Search remains a separate failing acceptance check (501); this PR does not claim full end-to-end completion.

  - 순응 타이어 팔: 좌우 하중 균등, 왼쪽 고정 편향 없음, 전진 평균 0.99–1.00(120 Hz 저속은 안쪽 바퀴 부족·0.97–0.98 잔차).
  - 대각 하중은 공통 매개일 가능성이 있지만 특정하지 못함(순응 타이어가 강성과 분배를 함께 바꿈). 적재는 필요조건 아님(빈차에서도 발생), 추가 기여는 배제 못 함(A4a 고속 우회전 악화, A4b 무효). 앞바퀴 구동 무관(A11).
  - dt 민감도 별도 절: 강체 120 → 240 Hz 에서 0.912 → 0.958, e_L 36 → 20 mrad. dt 를 실시간화 수단에서 빼고, dt 다른 실행끼리 섞어 비교하지 말 것. 이산화·접촉 모형 기여는 분리 못 함.
  - 다음 조치 후보: F2 재검토(총괄, 새 Isaac 필요), 실차 회전·조향 추종 측정(사용자 결정), 계획 곡률 여유는 콘솔·총괄 판단.
- 검토: Codex 3 회차에서 새 P1/P2 없음(수렴). 1 차 P2 3(적재 범위, 평균 상쇄, 원인 특정), 2 차 P2 1(dt 해석) 반영.

author: chayan-bit
body:
Fixes #295

## What was wrong

`ArkivProvider::unadopted` decides what to serve for a block hash that reth knows but the store never tagged.
Its doc comment says a block behind the store's head is refused, but the guard was `number <= next` (with `next = adopted + 1`), so every older untagged block passed it and was answered with `store.head()`.
Trigger: `eth_getBalance` or `eth_call` at the hash of a gap block, or a block from before the node started tagging.
Impact: the caller gets head state presented as that block's state, the "confident lie" the module is written to avoid; a wrong balance reads exactly like a right one.

## Fix

The check is now `maps_to_head(number, adopted)`: an untagged block resolves to head only when it is the adopted head itself or the block built on it (`number == adopted + 1`, or genesis when nothing is adopted).
Everything else returns the existing `ProviderError::StateForHashNotFound`.
Block building and validation read the parent, which is the tagged head, and `best_hash` is handled before this check, so neither path changes.

## Testing

Unit tests for `maps_to_head`: untagged older block is refused (red before the fix), head and next-to-build block resolve, a block further ahead is refused, and genesis with nothing adopted resolves.
`cargo test -p arkiv-reth-golemdbprovider`, `cargo clippy -p arkiv-reth-golemdbprovider --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` pass.
The decision is tested as a pure function because the crate has no harness for building a full `BlockchainProvider`.

## Alternative

An untagged hash at exactly the adopted height is a sibling fork block, not the head, so it could be refused too.
It is kept as served here, as a conservative reading of the intended window; tightening it is a one-line change if the maintainers prefer.

## Demo

The new test on the test-only commit (fails), then on the fix commit (passes).

author: n3puiol
body:
## Description

The backend refused to start with `Storage migration failed: Cannot automatically migrate Physical AI Studio storage because the new storage directory already contains files` for users whose data already lives in the new storage directory (`~/.local/share/physicalai`).

The legacy location `~/.cache/physicalai` is shared with the Physical AI Runtime, which keeps isolated model-execution environments under `isolate/` (several GB of virtual environments, marked by `.physicalai-isolate.json` / `.physicalai-engine.json`). The migration treated the old directory's mere existence as legacy Studio storage, so once the Runtime had created that cache, every later startup was blocked. The error then recommended `STORAGE_DIR=~/.cache/physicalai`, which would point Studio at an empty location and hide all of the user's data.

Changes:

- Only treat the old directory as legacy Studio storage when a Studio-owned entry (`models`, `cache`, `snapshots`, `datasets`, `robots`, `logs`, `data`) holds content; otherwise skip the migration.
- During a real migration, move only Studio-owned entries and leave Runtime-owned entries such as `isolate/` in place.
- Stop recommending `STORAGE_DIR=<old location>` when the new directory already holds data.

## Testing

`pytest tests/test_storage_migration.py` — 16 passed. New tests:

- `test_migration_ignores_runtime_isolate_cache_when_destination_contains_data`
- `test_migration_noops_when_old_storage_has_only_runtime_cache_and_empty_scaffold`
- `test_migration_leaves_runtime_isolate_cache_in_old_storage`

## Related Issues

None filed.

author: nervous-rob
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## DA-10: feedback and learning

A finding on Home and a piece of work on the Assistant page take one of seven typed answers. Each changes exactly one thing, in the system that thing belongs to, says what it changed, and can be put back where it lives. Behaviour: `documentation/delegated_feedback.md`. Reasons: ADR 0031.

| Answer | The one thing it changes | Where it is shown and undone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useful` / `already_knew` | A counter on that source of that responsibility | The responsibility's learned lines; Reset |
| `less_of_this` | That source's daily proposal cap (weight 1 → 0.5 → 0.25 → 0) | The same lines; Reset |
| `wrong` | The note the finding's run wrote is marked disputed (a revision; nothing deleted) | Changes to your notes; Undo |
| `keep_wording` | That note becomes a saved note of the person's | Changes to your notes; Undo |
| `wrong_time` | The hour it was sent is added to `attention_policies.avoidHours` | Settings → Initiative; Allow again |
| `stop_responsibility` | The ordinary `pause` or `revoke`, confirmed, with the revision shown | The responsibility's row |

### What is in it

- **`assistantFeedbackService`**: `give()` records the answer and makes its one change in one transaction; a kind is offered only where it has an effect and at most once per item; `noteDecision()` and `sweepIgnored()` count weak signals; `learned()` / `resetRate()`; `prune()`.
- **`assistant/sourceWeights`**: one row per responsibility and adapter. `capFor()` is read where the daily proposal cap is taken and nowhere else, and returns the adapter's cap or less.
- **Adapters declare `learns`**: `attention_item`, `project_plan`, `followed_source`, `job_failure`, `ci_verdict` and an implied `chat_request` learn; `conversation_request`, `project_plan_step`, a chat request by name and `process_incident` (a repair the grant names) never do.
- **Wrong time**: `attentionService.contactAllowed()` returns `WRONG_TIME` in a marked hour for every reason except `attention`; the delivery sweep holds it like quiet hours. Attention's notices, score and calibration do not read it.
- **Notes**: `knowledgeChangeSetService.recordFeedback()` records `FEEDBACK_WRONG` / `FEEDBACK_KEEP` as `direct_change` rows, so the existing Undo applies.
- **Steward**: an "ignored" pass after delivery (not during stop-all) and 180-day retention.
- **Portal**: a Feedback control on Home's findings and on work items (proposed, waiting for review, finished); learned rates with Reset on the responsibility; marked hours in Settings → Initiative; feedback changes labelled under Changes to your notes.
- **Routes**: `POST /api/app/assistant/updates/:id/feedback`, `POST /api/app/assistant/initiatives/:id/feedback`, `POST /api/app/assistant/responsibilities/:id/sources/:adapter/reset`; `learned` on the responsibilities list; `feedback` on Home's brief items and on initiatives.
- **Schema**: `assistant_feedback`, `assistant_source_weights`, `attention_policies.avoidHours` (both engines, with migrations).
- **Privacy**: both tables are in the account export, the transparency report, the privacy audit and `/forget-me`.

### Acceptance scenarios and the tests that cover them

Jest: `tests/assistantFeedbackService.test.js` (new, CI group `privacy`) and `tests/assistantDeliveryService.test.js`. Playwright: `e2e/assistantFeedback.spec.js` (person `99000000000001001`, fixture `/e2e/fixtures/assistant-feedback`).

| Scenario | Test |
| --- | --- |
| 1. "Wrong time" changes delivery timing and nothing about topic selection | "the hour it was sent is avoided for delegated work; topic selection and Attention's own notices are untouched"; delivery spec: "an hour marked as a wrong time holds delegated work until it ends, and only delegated work", "the digest waits out an hour marked as a wrong time too"; journey: "wrong time" marks the hour it was sent; Settings shows it and removes it |
| 2. "Wrong" opens a correction on the cited note and deletes no evidence | "wrong marks the note disputed through a revision, deletes nothing, and can be undone"; "neither is offered when the run wrote no note, and a note the run only confirmed is not its own"; journey: "this is wrong" disputes the note the finding wrote |
| 3. "Less of this" lowers a named adapter's rate and shows it with a reset | "each one halves what the source may propose a day, down to nothing; reset puts it back"; "it is one adapter of one responsibility: another responsibility keeps its rate"; journey: "less of this" lowers the rate of the source it came from |
| 4. "Stop this responsibility" is the ordinary confirmed pause or revoke | "it needs the confirmed choice and the revision the person saw, and then it is the ordinary action"; "revoke from a finding ends it, as revoking does"; journey: "stop this responsibility" is the ordinary pause, confirmed |
| 5. Ignoring is weak feedback and cannot silence a source alone | "ignoring alone cannot silence a source"; "dismissing lowers the rate slowly and never below one a day; starting works it back"; "a proposal left alone for a week counts once, as one dismissal"; "a finding nobody opened for a week counts once; one that was read does not" |
| 6. Feedback and derived signals are in the export, the report and erasure | "feedback and what was learned are in the export and the report"; "forgetting a person deletes both, audits to zero, and leaves everyone else's"; "feedback outlives its finding by 180 days at most; what was learned goes with an ended responsibility" |
| 7. No learned signal widens a grant, raises a budget or skips authorization | "no combination of signals yields more than the adapter's own cap"; "praise never raises a cap, and an uncapped adapter stays uncapped until something lowered it"; "every kind but "stop" leaves the grant, its budgets and its authority exactly as they were"; "work the person asked for is never slowed, whatever was learned" |
| Pilot gate (owner-only) | "until the pilot decision only the owner gives feedback; what was learned stays visible and resettable"; journey: before the pilot decision a member is offered no feedback, and the server refuses it |
| Host stop-all | "the steward runs it, and it does nothing while the host has stopped delegated work"; "giving feedback is the person's own act and works while the host has stopped delegated work" |

### Defaults chosen

- Weight steps **1, 0.5, 0.25, 0**: cap = usual cap × weight, rounded, at least 1 above zero. Only "less of this" reaches zero; only Reset raises a rate.
- Weak feedback: every **5** net dismissals take one proposal a day off, **at most two, never below one a day**; counters stop at a lead of 10.
- Ignored after **7 days**, recorded once per piece of work as `ignored` (an eighth stored kind nobody can give).
- Wrong time marks **whole hours, at most 12**, on the quiet-hours clock, and holds delegated contacts and digests only.
- "Wrong" **marks the run's own note disputed** as an undoable change rather than opening an editor; research claims are left alone.
- An adapter without a daily cap of its own gets the default cap (3) once something lowered it.
- Capability `feedback` gates giving an answer and counting weak signals. Seeing and resetting what was learned, and removing a marked hour, are never gated. Explicit feedback works during stop-all (it is the person's own act, like pausing); the ignored pass does not run then.

### Deferred

- Feedback from a notification or a Discord message; feedback by other members on a project's shared finding; ranking (a learned rate limits how many are proposed, not which). None is assigned to an increment.
- A person's edits to generated notes are not used as a signal; "keep this wording" is the explicit form.
- Neither stage follow-up candidate was taken: deciding a request from the notification itself, and project-shared findings appearing in a digest. Both are delivery work, not feedback.
- The live evaluation was not

author: jthorare
body:
Fixes #2508

## What changes
A Slack or Linear connection made through Connections (OAuth) is now indexed. Before, the Slack and Linear feeds read only the profile's token pointer (`context.sources.<preset>.token`), so a connected connection with no pointer indexed nothing. That's the same symptom #2499 fixed for GitHub alone.

- One resolver per preset, `IConnectionCredentials` / `ConnectionCredentials` (Sindri.Core): it tries the connected connection's token first, then falls back to the profile pointer. That's the order GitHub has used since #2499.
- The GitHub feed, the Slack feed and the Linear read key all use it. The GitHub-only `GitHubRecordFeeds.Token` path is gone.
- The live host registration of the Slack feed now passes the connection stores (`SlackFeedCompositionTests` pins it, since the first try missed this).
- Linear: a profile with a url and teams and no token now reads OK, because the token can come from the connection (`LinearTokenlessSettingsTests`). The old `SourcesSettingsTests` row "linear teams+url no token -> SND-CONTEXT-002" is deleted on purpose, since that's the behaviour this issue changes. The writeToken+teams-without-url row still gives SND-CONTEXT-002.
- **Order: the connection first, then the profile pointer, on purpose.** The issue asked for the pointer first. This PR reads a connected connection first and the pointer second (`ConnectionCredentials.cs`), the same as GitHub since #2499. Why: a profile can still name an old token the work org now rejects. With the pointer first, that stale token would shadow a good connection forever, and the user would see the #2499 symptom again. Please don't "fix" it back to pointer-first.
- Doctor (`context:index-github|linear|slack`, `IndexDoctorChecks`) and the setup list's sources step (`SourcesSetupReader`) ask the same `IConnectionCredentials`. So a source with no pointer but a connected connection is `ok` / `connected`, not "can't sync" / "needs token". With no connection, the warning now also says to connect it on the Connections page. `LinearDoctor` and `ContextLinearConnectionFacts` already say a tokenless Linear reads with the connection.

## Proof (bugfix-state, state gh-2508)
- Red check: `SlackRecordFeedsTokenOrderTests` + `LinearTokenOrderTests` fail at the red commit. At the final head 359a73fdbe (candidate c3, attempt 3, main merged in) they give 10 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. The judge says partial on c3; its points are answered below.
- Gate at a4fbc70f3b (the head before the main merge; that merge was clean, with an empty remerge-diff): build 0 warnings, 0 errors. ConnectionCredentialsTests 28 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. IndexDoctorChecksTests + SetupFactsTests 48 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. GitHub feeds 5 and Slack feeds 8 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. ApiGoldens 666 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Sindri unit 8769 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. Sindri integration 2553 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed. Context unit 4252 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Context integration 736 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Arch 164 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Ui GoldenContractTests 21 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. check-deps, scoped format (0 ` error ` lines) and aot-smoke are clean.
- Test changes (`--allow-test-changes`): new files `ConnectionCredentialsTests.cs`, `LinearTokenlessSettingsTests.cs`, `SlackFeedCompositionTests.cs`; new rows in `IndexDoctorChecksTests` (3, plus the no-pointer warn text now naming the Connections page), `SetupFactsTests` (1) and `ConnectionCredentialsTests` (2); `SetupFactsRig` gains the connection store; and the one deleted `SourcesSettingsTests` row above. The two frozen check files are unchanged.

## Review answers (ideas)
- A pointer that doesn't resolve gives null alone, and the connection when one is connected. A connected connection whose secret read fails falls back to the pointer. Both have rows in `ConnectionCredentialsTests`. No log line on the failed read: `ConnectionCredentials` is in Core, which has no logger. The doctor row still shows the pointer's own state then.
- Token expiry: the `connection-refresh` service (`RefreshConnectionsService`, every 5 minutes) renews any connected OAuth token that expires within 10 minutes. A key cached by the Linear read path stays good until a 401 makes it `Forget()` and read again.
- Nits (`LinearReadKey`'s `environment` is ignored when a credential is registered; the test-only public `SlackRecordFeeds` constructor): left as they are. Both are harmless and outside the fix.

## Judge: partial, answered here
1. **"SlackConnect.cs / LinearConnect.cs still read only the pointer."** They don't read an existing token at all. `sindri context connect slack|linear` asks for a NEW key, checks it against the channels or teams, stores it, then resolves the pointer it just wrote (`SlackConnect.cs:70`, `LinearConnect.cs:95` at main). There's no existing token to read, so a connection-first order has nothing to apply to. The read paths the issue names (the feeds, the Linear read key, the doctor) all go through the resolver.
2. **"The check doesn't cover the connect commands."** It follows from 1: nothing in them reads a token.
3. **"The post-fix pass is not confirmed."** The run at 359a73fdbe is recorded as passed: 10 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed (`runs/20261110T114509427Z-test-1.json`).
4. **The RS0030 blocking read (make `IExternalRecordFeeds.For` async).** The issue calls it optional ("could"). It moved into `ConnectionCredentials`, one place now instead of the GitHub feed. Making `For` async touches every feed and isn't needed for the fix.

author: zeegin
body:
Fixes #593

## Что изменилось

`tools.platform.version: sources` включает строгий выбор выпуска платформы по формату исходников основного набора. Выпуск выбирается по той же таблице, что и выбор по умолчанию (`2.17` — 8.3.24 … `2.22` — 8.5.4). Берётся новейшая сборка выпуска, и выпуск закреплён за всеми утилитами платформы. Отката на новейшую установку нет. Без ключа поведение прежнее.

- **Разбор значения.** `tools.platform.version` разбирается один раз, при загрузке настроек, в типизированное поле `Option<PlatformVersionSetting { Mask, Sources }>`; значение, которое не маска и не `sources`, — отказ загрузки. Сырой строки в коде больше нет; `platforms` эхом печатает значение через `Display`. Импорт EDT (`convert` Designer→EDT, выгрузка проекта EDT) получает в `--version` маску или, при `sources`, выпуск формата исходников (или ничего), но никогда строку `sources` — `platform::utilities::edt_import_version`. Значение `sources` отвергается проверкой настроек у проекта формата EDT и у проекта без основного набора (`SourcesNotApplicable`); проверка идёт и в путях `cluster` и `standalone`.
- **Где решается отказ.** Решает единственное место — `Locator::locate_platform` (`format_release`), до выбора кандидата и до проверки минимума. Входные данные — `SourceFormatRelease::{Unused, Preferred, Required}`, их собирает `PlatformUtilities::from_config`.
- **Когда отказ.** Выпуска нет среди установок; формата нет в таблице; формат не распознан или файл не читается. Выпуск вне таблицы не засчитывается, и текст отказа это говорит.
- **Когда не отказ.**
  - `Configuration.xml` ещё нет: выбор ничем не ограничен.
  - Выпуск есть, а компонента в нём нет: прежний `environment_unavailable` с описью.
- **С `path`.** Выпуск обязателен и под путём при любом `strict`; `strict: true` сохраняет свои гарантии (граница пути, канонические соседи, один закреплённый корень; закреплённые соседи называют `chosen_by: source_format`).
- **Опись отказа.** Опись — те же установки, по которым решён отказ. С `path` это установки под путём. Без `path` — корни по умолчанию и установки из `PATH`: `search_installations` строится на `installations()`, а утилита из `PATH` сначала канонизируется и числится той версией, куда ведёт (как её и выбирает поиск).
- **Ответ.**
  - В конверте: код `platform_release_missing`, род `environment`, выход 2. Отказ моделируется причиной `EnvironmentReason`.
  - Код шага в `data.execution.errors[]` остаётся `environment_unavailable`.
  - Новое необязательное поле `EnvelopeError.platform_release { source_format, installations }`. Оно использует `SourceFormatInfo` и `PlatformInstallation` из ответа `platforms`. Отображение `InstalledPlatform → PlatformInstallation` — одно, через `From`.
  - По MCP отказ приходит как `runtime_failure` с тем же полем.
  - Версия конверта не повышена: код и поле входят в невыпущенную версию 5.
- **Отказ доходит до ответа как есть.** Раньше его превращали в строку или глушили в нескольких местах; теперь каждое передаёт его типизированным:
  - `provider_selection::nobody_ready` и выбор исполнителя в `infobase_export` — через `ReleaseRefusal`;
  - `generation_reader` — оба чтения инструментом записи. Раньше отказ становился `NoAnswer`, и `push` отвечал `non_fast_forward`;
  - `managed_stand::locate`;
  - `reset` — чтение поколения;
  - `bootstrap` — после скрытия секретов в тексте поле сохраняется (`UseCaseError::with_message`);
  - `status --deep` — отвечает отказом, а не причиной «нет ответа» по наборам.
  - Род классифицируется через `AppError::platform_release()`; в месте классификации `debug_assert`: код `platform_release_missing` ⇔ поле заполнено.
- **`platforms`.** `requirement.version` может быть `sources`. Отказ попадает в `warnings` одной строкой, `selected` — `null`. Предупреждения о расхождении формата остаются только у режима по умолчанию.
- **Правила.**
  - Новое правило — `INV.PLATFORM.A-MISSING-RELEASE-OF-THE-SOURCES-FORMAT-IS-REFUSED`.
  - Правки в `CTR.WIRE.COMMAND-ENVELOPE` (новый код, поле, «Что изменила версия 5»), `INV.WIRE.A-MISSING-TOOL-IS-AN-ENVIRONMENT-FAILURE` (две причины, MCP), `INV.PLATFORM.PLATFORM-TOOLS-ARE-FOUND-BY-VERSION-MASK`, `CTR.WIRE.PLATFORMS-DATA`, `CTR.WIRE.FULL-PULL-PUBLICATION`.

## Summary
Stacks on PR #83. Implements the missing post-campaign founder sequence so Chronicle of Houses cannot unlock immediately after Act V.

## Changes
- Adds a pure rules system for founder reflections, epilogue completion, five-year aging passages and natural old-age death provenance.
- Adds a playable founder epilogue scene with three authored reflections: the people, the companions and the Concord.
- Requires the campaign completion, last Emperor and Empire-dissolved milestones before the epilogue can begin.
- Records the epilogue milestone only after all reflections; records the natural old-age death milestone only after the founder reaches age 70.
- Rejects premature death, non-five-year aging actions, missing founder identity and non-natural death causes.
- Adds an Act V ending handoff and a title-screen entry that loads the newest campaign save so epilogue progress can be resumed.
- Persists epilogue choices and age in the offline campaign save.
- Extends the deterministic campaign continuity test for gating, reflections, aging, save normalization and Chronicle unlock.
- Documents the flow and the current boundary: the full dynasty simulation is still a subsequent implementation.

## Validation
Static source checks passed for the gate, scene handoff, title entry, milestone order, aging threshold and test coverage. The documented test command is:
`godot --headless --path . --script res://tests/test_campaign_continuity.gd`

This environment has no Godot executable, so GDScript parsing, the headless test and in-engine playtesting have **not** been run. The character creator has no age field; the epilogue currently defaults the founder's starting age to 30 unless a saved profile explicitly contains `age`. This PR is stacked on #83 and should not be merged before #83 and its parents.

author: kiyobot
body:
When `sbx ls --json` gives the group's sandbox the status `running`, `sb` stops it with `sbx stop` and then starts it with `sbx run`. When the sandbox has any other status, or doesn't exist, `sb` works as before.

The kit's startup command, which pulls `main` of the dotfiles and runs `./setup.sh`, runs only when a sandbox starts. Docker's documentation says that `sbx run` on a running sandbox reconnects to it, so a change merged while the sandbox runs didn't reach it.

`sb` restarts a sandbox only on the exact status `running`, the one value seen in the real output of sbx v0.51. Docker's documentation doesn't give the status of a stopped sandbox, so `sb` never runs `sbx stop` on a sandbox with any other status. When `sbx stop` fails, `sb` stops with a message and doesn't go on to `sbx run`.

`sb` reads the JSON with jq. mise installs jq on each machine, and `sb` checks for it as it checks for sbx.

A failed startup command keeps the sandbox from starting, as #55 says. With this change each `sb` runs the startup command, so #55 matters more.

Closes #65

author: allixsenos
body:
## Defect

Fixes #190.

With `--node-style tagged`, `fmt` adds an argument tag on the second run. Verification of the first output fails.

## Reproduction

Input (`input.yaml`):

```yaml
Metadata:
  Value:
    Fn::Base64: !Sub |
      hello ${AWS::Region}
```

Commands:

```sh
cfnrain fmt --node-style tagged input.yaml > first.yaml
cfnrain fmt --node-style tagged first.yaml > second.yaml
cfnrain fmt --node-style tagged --verify first.yaml
```

Broken first output:

```yaml
!!str Metadata:
  !!str Value: !Base64
    !!str Fn::Sub: |
      hello ${AWS::Region}
```

Verification reports `first.yaml: would reformat` and exits with status 1.

Correct output, which also matches the second output on main:

```yaml
!!str Metadata:
  !!str Value: !Base64
    !!str Fn::Sub: !!str |
      hello ${AWS::Region}
```

## Change

Tagged style now writes the resolved tag on the first run when the parser built a node without one. Previously, the tag appeared only on the second run.

Add regression cases for multiline, plain, empty, quoted, and sequence arguments. Include default and flow style controls.

## Summary

Raw `<tool_call>…<arg_key>…</arg_value>…</tool_call>` markup was reaching the UI in research answers (screenshot from a quick-depth run). The synthesizer path already stripped it, but the **quick path** and the tool loop's **closing answer call** (after rounds run out) returned it verbatim.

- New `_sanitize_final_text` in `app/services/tools.py`: strips paired `<tool_call>` blobs, unclosed `<tool_call>` tails, and stray `<arg_key>/<arg_value>` tags; collapses degenerate 4+ repeated-line loops. Envelope JSON (`response_type`) is never altered.
- `_sanitize_result` applied to **both** `run_tool_loop` return paths (normal answer + rounds-exhausted closing call), so every tool-using path — normal chat, agents, quick research — is covered at the source.

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest tests/` — 52 passed.
- Unit checks: paired blob stripped, unclosed tail stripped, repeat loop collapses to `_(repeated 4 times)_`, envelope untouched.

## Skipped / risks

- Streaming `/v1/chat/completions` deltas are not sanitized mid-stream (only the final assembled message paths that go through `run_tool_loop`); plain non-tool calls could still theoretically leak markup, but the tool loop covers the paths where providers emit it.

author: dnikolayev
body:
## What

Adds a `same-commit-v1` execution profile to the common test result executor. An enrolled scope may reuse an original execution of the **same commit** that started under another event or ref, for example the merge-queue run of a commit that is then pushed to its branch.

Enrolled scopes: the six Healthcare Python shards and the capacity tests. They already call the wrapper and already have the evidence and upload steps, so no workflow shape changes.

## Why

A commit validated by the merge queue is tested again, unchanged, on the push that lands it. Until now every scope outside the two content profiles ran its stock command and recorded nothing, and merge-queue runs were excluded from the executor.

## How the claim holds

- The command of an enrolled scope never receives the labels a workflow starts under: event name, path and commit, ref names, pull request number and title, source branch. They are removed in every execution, original or reused, including the fallback. The event commit is a label too: for a pull request it names the merge commit, which moves with the base branch, not the commit that is checked out and tested.
- The fingerprint keeps the checkout commit, symbolic HEAD and shallow state of the source, recipe and verifier checkouts, plus the source commit and parent identities from the environment. Reachable history is fixed by the commit.
- The fingerprint leaves out three things only:
  - the list of other refs in each clone;
  - the bill-of-materials document inside an installed distribution (new serial number and timestamp on every build);
  - the installer's cache stamp for a locally built wheel (a timestamp).

  The compiled extension next to those documents stays measured.
- A different commit of the same tree, another parent, a branch checkout instead of a detached one, a changed dependency file or runner input all run in full.
- A merge-queue run may record and originate measurements for this profile only, and consumes no history. A queue candidate that never lands can never match a later commit.
- Whole-run success of the original, the one-day window, artifact and upload-step binding, recipe authentication and the separate final refresh are unchanged.

## Recipe change

The Healthcare recipe now creates its Python environment at one fixed path, falling back to a unique directory only when that path is taken. Installed launchers embed the environment path, so a random directory made 27 dependency records differ in every job.

## Selector fix

A run uploads one measurement archive per wrapped job. The selector read them in listing order and gave up on the whole run at the first archive that was another job's. It now skips an archive it cannot read for its scope and looks at the next one; verification of the selected original is unchanged.

## Measured on a caller (healthcare-mrf-api#1494, two runs of one commit)

| Job | Original run | Second run | Test phase in second run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python tests (1/6) | 586 s | 79 s | 3 s |
| Python tests (2/6) | 505 s | 63 s | 2 s |
| Python tests (3/6) | 725 s | 64 s | 3 s |
| Python tests (4/6) | 626 s | 71 s | 3 s |
| Python tests (5/6) | 517 s | 64 s | 4 s |
| Python tests (6/6) | 554 s | 63 s | 2 s |
| Capacity tests | 141 s | 61 s | 2 s |
| Total | 3,654 s | 465 s | |

- Both runs finished green, including the final job that refreshes every reused result against live reads.
- The seven coverage data files published by the two runs are byte-identical, and the second run's provenance names the first run as origin.
- Before the selector fix, the same experiment gave equal fingerprints for all seven scopes but reuse for only the one job whose archive was listed first.

## Supporting checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Same lock installed at two different paths | 65 of 12,042 files differ: 38 launchers and the 27 `RECORD` files that hash them |
| Same lock reinstalled at the same path | 0 files differ |
| Locally built wheel installed twice | only the installer cache stamp and its `RECORD` line differ |
| Two caller runs of unchanged Rust source | the four debug binaries and the extension inside the wheel are byte-identical; the wheel differs only in its bill of materials |

## Behaviour for everything else

Content scopes and stock scopes behave as before on every event. The wrapper no longer short-circuits on merge-queue events; the executor makes the same decision.

## Adoption order

A consumer that verifies caller runs with a pinned copy of this repository must move that pin first. An older verifier accepts only push, pull request and manual originals, so it would reject a pushed commit that reused its merge-queue run.

## Limits

- Covers the same commit only. A pull request head and the commit it merges as differ, so that pair still runs in full.
- An original is usable only when its whole run finished green on its first attempt.
- Wall-clock time of a run falls only when every job its final gate waits for is enrolled; this change enrolls seven.

## Tests

- same-commit reuse after a merge-queue original, with another ref added, other start labels and another event commit
- full execution for another commit of the same tree, another parent, another checkout state
- the command never sees the start labels, with or without evidence
- merge-queue runs stay outside the stock, native and content profiles
- only generated documents are ignored; a changed extension changes the fingerprint
- the broker prepares identity without history on a merge-queue run
- an original is found after other jobs' archives of the same run
- the environment path is fixed unless taken

## What
Deputy and notable-deputy chunks in the search index now describe a deputy whose mandate has ended in the past tense, with the end date.

## Why
Every deputy chunk opened with "X est député(e) de Y", including the deputies who have left the Assemblée.
A chat answer built from those chunks could present a former deputy as the current deputy for a département.
#621 closed those mandates but only touched code that already filtered on `mandate_end IS NULL`.

## Changes
- `rag/pipeline/chunker.py`: new `deputy_identity()` helper writes "X est député(e) de Y, membre du parti Z." for a sitting deputy and "X a été député(e) de Y jusqu'au JJ/MM/AAAA, membre du parti Z." for a closed mandate.
  `chunk_deputies` and `chunk_notable_deputies` select `d.mandate_end`, use the helper, and add `mandate_end` to the chunk metadata.
- `rag/pipeline/chunk_notable_deputies.py` (the builder the daily rebuild runs): both queries select `mandate_end`, `build_chunk` uses the same helper, and the metadata carries `mandate_end`. The local `dept_prep` wrapper, now unused, is removed.
- Departed deputies keep their chunks: questions about a former deputy's votes are legitimate.
- `CLAUDE.md`: one line in the RAG section recording the rule.

## Testing
- New unit tests in `tests/unit/test_chunker.py`: both wordings of `deputy_identity`, `chunk_deputies` and `chunk_notable_deputies` against a mocked cursor (SQL selects `mandate_end`, each tense, metadata), and `build_chunk` for both wordings.
- `pytest tests/ -m "not integration"`: 1276 passed, 15 skipped (the live Groq tests).
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`: clean.
- Integration tests were not run locally (Docker is down); CI runs them, and their seeded deputies are all sitting, so their expected text is unchanged.

## Risks / Notes
- The production index changes on the next daily rebuild (`ingest_prod.yml`), which re-embeds every chunk through the staging swap. No manual re-index is needed.
- Only the opening sentence changes for the ten departed deputies; sitting deputies' chunks are byte-identical.

## Breaking Changes
None

author: eraviart
body:
L'abattement spécial des personnes âgées ou invalides (CGI, art. 157 bis) n'est jamais doublé pour un couple : `foyers_eligibles` (ir.py:3660) additionne deux vecteurs booléens numpy (`True + True = True`), donc le compteur d'éligibles ne dépasse jamais 1. Depuis l'échelle 2023 (décret n° 2024-496 du 30/05/2024) : un foyer dont les deux membres ont 65 ans ou plus reçoit 2 × 1 373 € (rni entre 17 200 € et 27 670 €) ou 2 × 2 746 € (en dessous de 17 200 €) — la calculette de référence DGFiP (sources2023m_8_0, `ABTPA = NDA × NAB × 1 373`) et la doctrine (BOI-IR-BASE-40-20240618, § 60) appliquent 2 746 €, OpenFisca 1 373 €.

Reproduction (2023, retraités 14 936 € chacun, tous deux 65+) : `abat_spe` 1 373 € au lieu de 2 746 €, rni 25 511 € au lieu de 24 138 € (écart exact de 1 373 €, IRN final égal 0 € — la décote absorbe).

Correctif : convertir chaque éligibilité en entier avant la somme (`.astype(int)`), comme le fait le programme de référence (`NDA` compte les deux conjoints). Après : `abat_spe` 2 746 €, rni 24 138 € = calculette de référence ; les foyers à un seul éligible et les personnes seules sont inchangés (cas 036 du lot #151 : conforme — 2 746 € des deux moteurs et de la doctrine, l'observation associée est corrigée dans le dossier de l'étude).

`tests/formulas/abattement_spe_personnes_agees.yaml` : 6 tests, attendus issus de la calculette de référence DGFiP (millésime 2023) — 3 rouges sur master (doublement tranche 1 et tranche 2), 3 verrouillant les comportements déjà corrects. 1150/1150 sur `tests/formulas/*.yaml`, dont les 7 scénarios existants portant des couples âgés.

author: chayan-bit
body:
## fix(engine): read the node-supplied state in txpool and BAL prewarming

Fixes #10

### What was wrong

PR #6 made main block validation and per-transaction prewarming read EVM state from the node-supplied source (`OverlayStateProviderFactory::node_evm_state_provider`), because Arkiv never writes reth's database after genesis.
Three other state readers were left on `database_provider_ro()`:
- the txpool prewarming worker (`txpool_prewarm/worker.rs`), active with `--engine.txpool-prewarming`;
- the BAL account prewarm pool's provider builder (`prewarm.rs`, `bal_prewarm_pool.begin_block`);
- the BAL hashed-state account reader (`prewarm.rs`, `CachedStateProvider::new_prewarm`).

On a node with its own state source, these read reth's stale genesis database.
The txpool worker speculatively executes pooled transactions against it and publishes every read into a snapshot.
Block validation attaches that snapshot to its `CachedStateProvider`, which answers from it before the node's source is consulted.
So a sender whose real nonce is N > 0 is seen at its genesis nonce and balance (or as absent).
Valid blocks then fail the nonce check on this node (chain halt), and a transaction that overspends the real balance but not the genesis one passes here and nowhere else (chain split).
The BAL paths have the same defect and feed the same caches.

### The fix

Add `OverlayStateProviderFactory::evm_state_provider()`, which returns the node's source when one is installed and otherwise `database_provider_ro()?.into_evm_state_provider()`, boxed.
Every EVM state reader now builds its provider through it: the txpool worker, both BAL prewarm sites, and the two PR #6 call sites (validation and `evm_for_ctx`), which previously inlined the same match.
With no node source installed, every path reads exactly the database provider it read before; the only change on that path is that the txpool worker now holds it boxed, as the other paths already did.
The txpool prewarm `Handle`/`Worker` bound gains `Send + 'static` on the provider, which the concrete `OverlayStateProviderFactory` provider already satisfies.

### Testing

New test `tree::txpool_prewarm::worker::tests::warms_the_state_the_node_supplies`: the database has no account for the sender, the overlay manager's node source has it at nonce 7, one pool transaction is warmed, and the published snapshot must hold nonce 7.
Before the fix it fails with `left: None, right: Some(7)`; after the fix it passes.
`cargo test -p reth-engine-tree -p reth-storage-overlay` passes (207 + 15 + 57 tests).
`cargo clippy -p reth-engine-tree -p reth-storage-overlay --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean apart from one existing `missing_const_for_fn` hit on `overlay_manager_ref` in `storage-overlay/src/provider.rs`, which this PR does not touch.
`cargo +nightly fmt --all --check` reports no diff in the lines this PR changes; it still flags formatting that was already on the base branch (for example the `reth_storage_api` import block and two `state_frontiers` lines in `storage-overlay/src/provider.rs`).

The BAL prewarm sites are covered by the same helper but have no dedicated test here.

## Demo

The new test on the test-only commit (fails), then on the fix commit (passes).

![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chayan-bit/reth/demo-assets/reth-prewarm.gif)

Tape source: [reth-prewarm.tape](https://github.com/chayan-bit/reth/blob/demo-assets/reth-prewarm.tape)
