author: peterdsharpe
body:
Anyone who drops a consolidated tensordict in a loop keeps its buffer until Python's garbage collector runs, so the loop holds many batches at once. This is so for the result of `td.consolidate()`, of `consolidated.to(device)`, of unpickling a consolidated tensordict and of `TensorDict.from_consolidated(file)`. On a 45 GiB GPU, a loop that moves a 3 GiB consolidated tensordict to the device ends in a CUDA out-of-memory error in its 15th iteration, while the same loop on the plain tensordict peaks at 6 GiB. `td.bytes()` keeps the leaves of `td` alive through a cycle of the same kind; this PR leaves it as it is (#3644).

Each of these calls defines a nested function that calls itself (`assign`, `set_`, `from_metadata`, and `copy_dict` in `to`). Such a function is in a reference cycle with its own closure, and the closure also holds the buffer. This PR deletes the function's name once the enclosing call is done with it, which breaks the cycle, so the memory is freed when the last reference to the result is dropped.

The deletion is skipped under `torch.compile`: Dynamo in torch 2.11 has no handler for deleting a closure variable, and `consolidate()` compiles with `fullgraph=True` today. Compiled calls therefore keep the previous path.

## Behaviour changes

None in what the calls return: every result is identical to the previous path's. The only change is when memory is released: the buffer of a dropped consolidated tensordict is freed at once and not at a later garbage collection.

I compared 1,675 calls between `main` and this branch (25 kinds of tensordict, among them nested, tensorclass, lazy stack, non-tensor and jagged nested-tensor entries; `consolidate` with each keyword; `to` of a consolidated tensordict with `num_threads`, `non_blocking`, `non_blocking_pin` and `inplace`; pickling; `from_consolidated`; `bytes`). Types, batch sizes, names, devices, lock state, key order, leaf dtypes, shapes and bytes, consolidated metadata, warnings and exceptions are the same for all of them. `torch.compile` (`fullgraph=True`, `backend="eager"`, default) gives the same results, graph counts and graph breaks on torch 2.11 and 2.15.

## Measurements

Peak CUDA memory on an NVIDIA L40S (45 GiB), torch 2.15.0, Python 3.12, garbage collector at its defaults:

This PR lands together with #3640. With the buffer freed at once, `consolidate()` of padded leaves and of a slice page-faults on the temporaries that `main` builds for them, which makes a loop of such consolidates of a few MB 1.4x to 1.7x slower on its own; #3640 removes those temporaries, and its body has the timings of the two together.

| loop | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 40 x `consolidated.to("cuda")`, 3 GiB | out of memory in the 15th iteration (42 GiB allocated) | 6144 MiB |
| 40 x `plain.to("cuda")`, 3 GiB (control) | 6144 MiB | 6144 MiB |
| 200 x `consolidated.to("cuda")`, 64 MiB | 5376 MiB | 64 MiB |
| 200 x `batch.consolidate().to("cuda")`, 64 MiB | 1664 MiB | 64 MiB |

Time per call, interleaved A/B of `main` against this PR on a 32-core AMD EPYC 9R45 cloud machine, one pinned core, torch 2.15.0, Python 3.12, 10 rounds (batch 32, 7 leaves unless noted):

| call | `main` | this PR | change [range of the rounds] |
|---|---|---|---|
| `td.consolidate()` | 67.8 us | 66.0 us | -2.0% [-4.0, -0.0] |
| `pickle.loads(consolidated)` | 56.9 us | 55.1 us | -3.4% [-5.0, +0.8] |
| `TensorDict.from_consolidated(file)` | 50.7 us | 49.2 us | -1.3% [-5.3, -0.7] |
| `consolidated.to("cpu")` | 20.5 us | 20.6 us | -0.0% [-1.0, +1.8] |
| `td.to("cpu")`, not consolidated (control) | 5.19 us | 5.24 us | +0.4% [-0.3, +3.9] |

## Tests

In `test/tensordict/test_generic.py`:

- `test_consolidate_frees_buffer_without_gc` (4 cases: `consolidate`, `to`, `pickle`, `from_consolidated`): with the garbage collector disabled, the storage of the result has expired right after the last reference is dropped. All 4 fail on `main`.
- `test_consolidate_recursive_entries` (jagged nested tensor, nested tensorclass, lazy stack): `consolidate` (also with `metadata=True` and `num_threads=2`), `to`, a pickle round trip, `from_consolidated` and `bytes` return the same values and types as before.
- `test_consolidate_threads_after_closure_drop`: `consolidate(num_threads=2)`, `consolidate(num_threads=2, return_early=True)` and `to("cpu", num_threads=2)` still work, called repeatedly.

Closes #3563

body:
Replication and Gateway stay tabs (owner and dotvirt-1e, 2026-11-10). Each section's landing tab now carries their state, so the owner's rc.2 question ("why are they not visible") is answered where people land.

Storage, Library tab (above Classes when the cluster runs no VMs):
- A tile first in "Needs attention", from the Replication tab's own read.
- Operator: `protectionOf` over every copy, e.g. "4 of 7 disks survive losing a host".
- Disk owner: their disks' standings from `/api/storage/protection`; it names no host.
- One tint ladder for both, the server's standings: danger on a disk that needs an operator (split brain, majority lost, failed); warn on one exposed (a lost host takes it offline, with no copy catching up). Catching up, one copy by choice and being set up count short, untinted.
- The body speaks of the disk the link opens: what is wrong now, else which host's loss takes it offline. With nothing linked it gives the first note, or for an owner the first disk that counts short and why.
- The link lands on the Replication tab focused on that row (`focus=`): highlighted, `aria-current`, scrolled into view.

Networking, Map tab:
- A tile above the map, from the Gateway tab's own read: "3 of 4 routes live", naming the first refused route by its reason (`routeState`), never the controller's text, then how many more are refused.
- Tinted danger on a refused route; a route waiting for its Gateway is counted, untinted.
- The link opens the route: an operator on its Gateway's map (`gateway=`, `route=`), a disk owner on their routes list, highlighted.

Both:
- Same gates as the tabs: shown unless `modules.replicatedStorage` / `modules.routes` is a known no. Operator or owner follows the same capability the tab asks.
- With nothing to judge they say so ("No replicated disks", "No routes yet"), never "every".
- A failed read says so and offers Try again.
- A rail project narrows the Replication tile as it narrows the tab.

Request load:
- No new endpoint and no cluster read. The tiles reuse `state/replication.svelte.ts` and `state/gateways.svelte.ts`, re-pulled on the frame's watermark like the tabs.
- One in-memory GET per landing visit, only where the module is on: `/api/storage/replication` or `/protection` on Storage, `/api/networking/gateways` or `/routes` on Networking.

Tests:
- Unit `landing.test.ts`: each tile's count, tint, body, and the row its link lands on; a catching-up disk untinted in both views; the body names the linked disk, not an earlier one; the controller's text never shows; nothing claimed about no disk or no route.
- UI `landing.spec.ts`: operator and owner on `replicated`/`replicatedtenant` and `fronted`/`frontedtenant`: the problem state, then the click lands on the focused row. On `base`, neither tile shows.
- Removing the row focus, or either module gate, fails them.
- svelte-check, eslint + knip, prettier, vitest (493), full UI suite (185), after a rebase on #373.

author: sapphireclinicseast
body:
Front desk had exactly one way to put a second child in an hour on the spreadsheet: type `+ NAME` as free text on the notes line. Free text cannot be checked against the patient list, so a service tag or a misspelling booked **nobody at all**, silently — `+ ANDALUZ, MARCO LORENZO CBT`, `+ CABAL, RUNE EVERY OTHER WEEK`. Six real bookings were lost that way on the East OT board (#1021).

An hour can now be **declared** to hold two or three patients, on the cell itself in Decking — a small seat count that cycles 1 → 2 → 3. The sheet then draws that hour with a second and third patient line of its own, each a validated dropdown with its own payment line, ready and empty.

### How it behaves

- `DeckingSlotCapacity` holds **only the shared hours**. One is the default and is stored as the absence of a row, so the table is the list of exceptions rather than a copy of the board; setting a cell back to one deletes its row.
- The drawn count is `max(declared, patients already in the hour)` — so adding a second child in the hub opens the second line on the sheet by itself, and a cell can never hold somebody it has no line to draw. The API refuses to shrink a cell below what it holds.
- **Height is paid per hour, not per tab.** An hour is as tall as the most crowded cell on its own row, so one shared ten o'clock leaves eleven — and every other band — exactly as it was. Sized tab-wide instead, a single three-patient hour would have added four rows to all three hundred.
- Spare lines in a taller hour's neighbours carry no value, no dropdown, no editable range and no map entry, so the pull cannot read them and the extra height costs only height.

### Retired

`PAIRED_DEPARTMENTS` is gone. Sharing is a property of the **hour**, not of a department: that flag gave every SLP hour in both clinics a second patient line — a third of the board's height — for the sake of the one hour in the clinic that actually had two children in it. Those boards get their height back.

### Migration

Backfills every cell that already holds more than one patient (4 cells today: 3 East OT, 1 East SLP), so nothing has to be re-declared by hand and no second child loses its line on the first sync. Guarded throughout; the deploy replays migrations on every run.

### Verified before deploy

`buildGrid` render-checked offline on a board with one plain hour, one declared pair and one declared trio:

- plain hour → 3 rows, 3 mapped lines
- shared pair → 5 rows, both children on their own validated line with their own payments (CASH and GL)
- declared trio → 7 rows, with the empty second and third dropdowns present and the *other* cells on that row carrying blank, unmapped spare lines

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` exit 0.

body:
<!--
For Work In Progress Pull Requests, please use the Draft PR feature,
see https://github.blog/2019-02-14-introducing-draft-pull-requests/ for further details.

If you do not follow this template, the PR may be closed without review.

Please ensure all checks pass.
If you are a new contributor, the workflows will need to be manually approved before they run.
-->

## Brief summary

<!-- In one or two sentences, what does this PR change and why? -->

Adds the app shell's navigation model (P3-04 step S1): tabs and sidebar sections, typed routes, a per-scene `Router` with compact/regular normalization, library switching, identity resets, and a lossy, validated snapshot for `@SceneStorage` restoration.

## Which issue is fixed?

<!--
One issue per PR. Ex: "Fixes #1234".
If this ports upstream work, also link the upstream-port issue and the upstream
commit or PR, e.g. "Ports advplyr/audiobookshelf-app#2002" (see docs/upstream-sync.md).
-->

Fixes #176 (P3-04a, part of #44).

## Pull Request Type

<!--
Which platforms or areas does this affect? List the ones that apply:
- iOS / iPadOS
- iPhone Duo (foldable)
- macOS
- CarPlay
- Shared core package
- Repo / CI / tooling
Is it a bug fix, feature, refactor, or docs change? Does it add an SPM dependency (justify it)?
-->

- Shared core package (`ABSAppModel`)
- Feature; no new dependencies

## In-depth Description

<!--
Describe the approach and why it is the right one.
Note concurrency, persistence (SwiftData) or API changes, and any trade-offs or follow-ups.
Keep PRs to at most 20 files / 2000 hand-written lines.
-->

All new code lives in `Sources/ABSAppModel/Navigation/` and follows ADR 0004 and #44's S1 plan.

**Types**
- `AppTab`: the tabs and sections. Each library type has its own set of sections, matching the legacy nav bar.
- `LibraryKind`: book or podcast, built from ABSCore's `MediaType`.
- `Route`: Hashable, Codable and Sendable, carrying IDs only.

**`Router`**, `@MainActor @Observable`, Foundation and Observation only:
- Paths are kept per tab.
- `normalize(isCompact:)` moves a selected section into Library's path at compact width. Regular width moves nothing back.
- `selectLibrary(id:kind:supportedSections:)` resets Home, Library, Search and the section tabs, keeps Downloads and Account, and repairs the selected tab and section. It clears the paths of sections the library no longer supports.
- The first library chosen after none keeps the restored paths.
- `requestLibrary(id:)` and `pendingLibraryID` let deep links (S2) ask for a library that S7a resolves.
- `resetForIdentityChange(serverID:userID:)` resets the router for a new identity.
- The presentation flags stay per scene. The full player is never persisted.

**`Router.Snapshot`**
- `snapshotData` and `restore(from:)` give S5 a single `@SceneStorage` binding. Unreadable data falls back to defaults.
- Unknown tab keys are skipped, and each path stops at its first route that doesn't decode, so a TestFlight rollback keeps the screens it can.
- A snapshot is discarded unless both the server and user IDs match.
- The restored section is checked against the library type (the new `libraryKind` field, added to ADR 0004's field list).

**Notes for later steps**
- S5 must call `normalize` after a restore and on appear.
- S2's `pendingPlayLink` must be a stored property in `Router.swift`.

**Size:** 8 files, +962/−1. About 555 of those lines are tests.

## How have you tested this?

<!--
List the exact commands you ran and their results (e.g. `mise run lint`,
`DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer xcodebuild test …`),
plus any manual steps with the device or simulator and the server version used.
-->

- `swift test --filter Router`, twice: 40 tests in 2 suites passed. They cover:
  - compact transfer and replacement;
  - the library-switch reset matrix and book↔podcast repair;
  - permission-limited sections, including clearing unsupported section paths;
  - identity reset and partial identity mismatches;
  - a golden JSON fixture pinning the wire format;
  - lossy decoding of unknown tabs and routes;
  - pending library requests;
  - restore followed by `normalize`.
- I reverted each fix in turn and confirmed its test fails without it.
- `mise run format`, `mise run lint` and `mise run test:kit` passed before the final main merge. The merge only brings in #166's download files, which don't overlap these; CI covers the merged tree.
- A local reviewer approved it with notes, and all the notes are addressed.

## Screenshots

<!--
For UI changes, include before/after screenshots or a short video for each affected
platform and pose (iPhone, iPad, iPhone Duo folded/unfolded, Mac, CarPlay).
-->

None; there's no UI in this PR.

author: moby3012
body:
PR 8 of `.pm/spec-shell-design.md` (§4.7) + the reader items of `.pm/research-reeder.md`.

## What changes
- **Reader split** — `components/article-reader.tsx` (956 lines) → `components/reader/*`: `reader-view` (composition, sync), `reader-header` (feed line → headline → meta → hero), `reader-top-bar`, `reader-action-pill`, `reader-chrome` (lazy), `reader-body` (lazy, owns KaTeX/hljs CSS + AI card), `reader-more-menu` (lazy), `reader-typography-sheet` (lazy), `use-reader-scroll` (hide-on-scroll, progress, position, pull). `ReaderPane` uses the nav store public API only (`nav.up`, `nav.stepArticle`, `nav.goScope`); article fetching (`useArticle`, legacy adapter) untouched; `?a=` deep link still server-renders the body from the hydrated detail.
- **Instant title** — the headline path ships with the shell and paints from the list row in the tap's frame. Body and chrome are lazy chunks preloaded **and warmed** on idle (a lazy component's first mount always suspends and React throttles that reveal by up to 300 ms — that was the cause of the body landing late in an earlier iteration). Chrome renders one frame after the title (`useDeferredValue`), measured ~16–20 ms later.
- **One entrance** — compact: pane move only; wide: 140 ms content fade. Article → article fades; prev/next adds ±24 px. No animation on headline/body (asserted). Reduced motion: opacity only; the bar fades instead of sliding.
- **Top bar** — hides after 24 px continuous down-scroll past 80 px, returns on 12 px up, at top, at end, on focus inside it or while its menu/sheet is open. 2 px brand progress line under it; it stays at the top edge while the bar is hidden. Compact `[Back][feed][↑][↓][Aa]`, wide `[Back][↑][↓] … [Favorit][Später][Gelesen][Teilen][Original][Aa][…]`.
- **Bottom pill (compact)** — Favorit · Gelesen · Später · Teilen · …, toggles show state (`aria-pressed`), ≥44 px. The "previous doubles as back" button is gone. Prev/next are explicit (bar + `…` menu); `k`/`j` unchanged.
- **Aa sheet** — Sans / Serif / Rounded, size 15–24 px, leading Eng/Normal/Luftig (1.45/1.6/1.8), width Schmal/Mittel/Breit (62/68/76ch), reader theme Auto/Hell/Dunkel/Sepia **independent of the app theme**. Non-modal popover, everything applies live (CSS variables + data attributes on the reader root only) plus a preview line. Persisted per device in `localStorage` (`ff:reader-typography`); unset fields fall back to per-feed override → account `readerWidth`/`readerFontSize` → tokens. Reader themes are token scopes: `tokens.css` lists `[data-reader-theme]` next to `:root`, "Dunkel" is a nested `.dark`, and the `dark:` variant opts out inside light/sepia readers. Esc closes the sheet/menu only, not the reader.
- **Reading position** — per article, stored as a ratio (survives font-size changes), restored within 24 h (max 200 entries), re-applied while images/body grow until the user scrolls. Other articles open at the top.
- **Pull past the end → next** — touch only, resistance 0.45, trigger 64 px, tracked indicator (ring fills, "Loslassen für den nächsten Artikel" + next title), haptic tick when armed. `lib/gestures` is not on main yet → minimal implementation in `use-reader-scroll.ts` with a `TODO(gestures)` to move onto `createPull` from #235.
- **Removed** — G6 horizontal swipe-back and wheel/touch overscroll prev/next. `safe-mark-all.spec.ts` updated: a right swipe on text no longer goes back (spec: no horizontal app gestures in the reader).
- **i18n** — 27 new de/en keys (de in "du"), 2 unused removed.
- **Not touched** — `components/list/*`, nav store internals, article API, `Article.updatedAt`, Prisma schema.

## Perf (`pnpm run perf:measure -- --runs 5`, same machine, back to back, main = `e6b69d2`)
`scripts/perf-measure.mjs` now times tap → title/body **inside the page** from the tap's `pointerdown` timestamp to the first frame containing the element. The old method started a clock before `page.tap()` and polled afterwards, so ~400 ms of Playwright round trips were in the "~500 ms" baseline (old method on main: 495 ms). Both columns below use the new method.

| Metric | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Tap → reader title painted** | 79 ms | **57 ms** | −28 % (budget ≤100) |
| Tap → reader body painted | 199 ms | 202 ms | = |
| INP-proxy: open article | 56 ms | 72 ms | +16 ms ¹ |
| INP-proxy: mark read / star | 48 / 32 ms | 48 / 32 ms | = |
| LCP | 1240 ms | 1284 ms | +3.5 % |
| Time to first row | 1196 ms | 1241 ms | +3.8 % |
| First-load JS `/` route entry (gz) | 137.1 KB | 140.0 KB | +2.1 % |
| First-load JS incl. runtime (gz) | 305.5 KB | 308.4 KB | +0.9 % |
| Global CSS (gz) | 35.3 KB | 36.6 KB | +1.3 KB |
| Requests / transferred at cold start | 31 / 412 KB | 35 / 424 KB | ² |

¹ Stated regression: main's tap frame paints only a placeholder (its reader chunk mounts a frame later, title at 79 ms); here the tap's own frame contains the real headline, so that first frame costs more (still far under the 200 ms budget).
² Idle preloads of the four lazy reader chunks (body, chrome, menu, Aa) after the first row — not on the critical path.

## Tests
- `e2e/app/reader-chrome.spec.ts` (desktop + mobile): tap → title ≤100 ms via the `ff:tap-to-title` User Timing measure + no animation on headline/body; hide-on-scroll + focus pin + progress 0→1; prev/next (direction, history length unchanged, previous disabled on the first article, never back); compact pill (5 × ≥44 px, state); position restore (other article at top, restore after step back and after reload); Aa sheet (serif on body + headline + preview, size +2, leading 1.8, narrow, sepia while the app theme stays, Esc closes only the sheet, persists across reload, reset clears storage); pull-to-next (short pull tracked but no commit, long pull arms + opens next; pull mid-article does nothing).
- `tests/features/reader-chrome.test.ts`: position memory (TTL, top/end forgotten, cap 200, reload) and typography store (fallback chain, attrs, sanitizing, reset). `tokens-css.test.ts` now also guards the reader CSS (≤320 ms).

## Verification (local, sqlite)
- `tsc --noEmit` ✅ · `pnpm lint` ✅ · `vitest run` ✅ 1349 passed / 2 skipped · `translations:check` ✅ · `pnpm run build` (sqlite) ✅

- Visual check (screenshots) of light, sepia + serif, dark-reader-in-light-app, hidden bar with progress line, Aa sheet on 390 px and 1280 px.

## Notes for review
- Spec says `text-wrap: balance` for the headline; this uses `pretty` because the old reader documented a Safari bug where balanced headings stop honouring `overflow-wrap`.
- Progress uses the rAF writer only (no `animation-timeline: scroll()` branch) — one code path, deterministic in tests.
- Aa choices are device-local (no schema change); a synced variant would need additive `User` columns → [OWNER].
- Needs a real-device pass (iOS) for pull-to-next feel and the bar's safe-area behaviour.

author: nilshamerlinck
body:
## Why

A production instance should not run scheduled actions before the actual go live. Until now the production preset generated `max_cron_threads = 2`, so crons ran as soon as the instance started.

## What

- The production preset now sets `max_cron_threads = 0`.
- New `[preset_hints.<preset>]` overlay table: values to switch to by hand later. `create` / `update --preset` renders each hint as a commented line just above the active key:

  ```ini
  ; 0 disables scheduled actions. Production ships with 0 until go live, then switch to 2.
  ; max_cron_threads = 2
  max_cron_threads = 0
  ```

  At go live, the TPM swaps the two lines.
- The hint is skipped when the value already matches. Values from existing files still win over the preset, so `update --preset production` on a live config (or `create --from` an old one) keeps `max_cron_threads = 2`.
- README documents preset hints. Tests cover the hint rendering and the skip case.

## Note

`update` without `--preset` rewrites the file and drops comments, including the hint line.

author: goosterhof
body:
🎖

## What

This is the first half of the audit-retention part of the package: where a hash chain starts. It also sets up the package itself.

- `AnchorMac`: the MAC over a prune anchor. It produces the same bytes as entreezuil's `AuditChainHash::anchorMac()`.
- `AuditChainAnchor`: the anchor model, on table `audit_chain_anchors`, with a publishable migration. The provider never auto-loads that migration.
- `ChainStartResolver` and `ChainStart`: one answer to "where does this chain start", either the anchor or the seed. The anchor's MAC is checked and the result is reported, never repaired. A territory's writer, its verifier and the prune (PR B) all read the start from here, so they cannot disagree.
- Scaffolding modelled on `phpstan-warroom-rules`: Pint, PHPStan with Larastan, the test suite with a 100 % coverage gate, mutation testing at a 90 % minimum, a lowest-dependency leg, the release workflow and Dependabot. There is a `ci-passed` rollup job that requires every lane to report `success` and refuses an empty result set.

## Why

ADR-0033 Amendment 2 exempts hash-chained audit tables from erasure, but only with a retention window enforced by a prune that keeps the remaining chain verifiable. entreezuil already ships that prune (EZ-0037), and five territories owe one. This extracts it once. It is extraction only, with no new behaviour.

## Proof

- `EntreezuilFixtureTest`: entreezuil's own code wrote a fixture (anchors from a real prune, plus 8 MAC vectors) at the commit the extraction started from. Every vector and anchor verifies here, and fails under a different seed.
- Gates on this head: format and PHPStan clean; 14 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; coverage 100 % (21/21); mutation 22 killed, 0 escaped; the lowest-dependency leg (Laravel 13.39.0) passed 14, failed 0.

## Stack

PR B (the prune) is stacked on this branch. Merge this PR first, without `--delete-branch`: the repo's own auto-delete retargets PR B to `main`.

author: gsadee
body:
| Q               | A
|-----------------|-----
| Branch?         | 3.0
| Bug fix?        | no
| New feature?    | yes
| Related tickets | follow-up to #934, replaces #928 and #939

When the onboarding starts asking for more, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay, accounts connected before do not have it until the seller consents again, nothing in the admin tells which payment methods those are, and the only way to consent again was connecting a new payment method. This PR stores the scope a payment method was onboarded with, flags the ones that miss part of the current scope without asking PayPal, and lets the admin update their permissions from the edit page. It combines #939 with the commits of #928 by @rust-le, carried over onto the stored scope.

## What changes

- **Stored onboarding scope**: `OnboardingScope::current()` holds the product, the secondary products, the capabilities (`Capability` constants) and the features the onboarding asks for; the onboarding URL is built from it and the onboarding stores it in the gateway config (`onboarding_scope`).
- **Permissions state without PayPal requests**: the payment method list and edit page compare the stored scope with the current one and show "PayPal permissions out of date" (with what is missing) or "PayPal permissions unknown" (nothing stored, as for a payment method onboarded on 2.x), through `PermissionsStateChecker` and the `PermissionsStatus` of `PermissionsState`.
- **"Update PayPal permissions"** next to the credentials and in that alert: it runs the onboarding for the account of the payment method, refuses another account, keeps the credentials and the webhook, and stores the current scope.
- **Check before consent**: the modal first reads the merchant integration status. With every capability of the scope active it only stores the scope; with capabilities PayPal has not activated yet it lists them; only a missing capability or an account the configured partner does not know (404) leads to the consent, which is also offered when the status cannot be read (`MerchantIntegrationStatusUnavailableException`).
- **`OnboardingStatus`** keeps the status of every capability (`capabilityStatus()`), the same API as #940.
- **UPGRADE-3.0**: a step to update the permissions of every PayPal payment method when moving a 2.x store over.

AI-generated: Claude Code.

## Summary

Adds `docs/328-authority-temporal-safety.md`, the detailed design for **authority temporal safety**: making the lifetime of authority, not the lifetime of memory, a first-class language construct.

The document covers:

- **The axis shift**: Rust made memory lifetime a first-class type-system concept; this doc targets authority lifetime — the interval in which a `(principal, object, right)` grant is valid.
- **The Rust six-piece mapping**: old pieces, one default mechanism, an algorithmic/theorem contribution, a proof, a usability story, and one new guarantee.
- **Precedent map**: Redell/seL4/EROS/Fuchsia revocation, Verum CBGR and PICASSO for generation + per-use checking, CHERI/Cornucopia/Fil-C/MTE for sweeps and probabilistic tags, Rust/RustBelt/Stacked-Tree Borrows for the static half.
- **The model**: capability = `(D, o, g, e, r)`, three keys (domain/time law, object generation, authority epoch), events `grant/use/revoke/retire/expire/quiesce`, and properties A0–A5.
- **The guarded-subset theorem**: G1–G4 imply A0–A4 and O(1) revocation without a sweep; completeness is relative to the root set; everything outside it is a labeled floor.
- **Static/dynamic duality**: `&T` (compile-time region), `ref T` (runtime generation/epoch), `ptr` (labeled floor).
- **Default path and usability**: zero-annotation `domain` blocks, `ref` inference, diagnostics that name the failing key, migration switches.

Missing/partial JSON waits for another publication, while other read errors propagate.

Keep every real navigation, document/hook identity, replacement relay, retained capture/generation/origin, no-Stop/no-loss, native connection count and non-silent PCM assertion. The readiness probe still runs only after the replacement handshake; observation cannot repair the missing reconnect. The observer still does not read runtime.lastError. Add seven fast event-helper tests to npm test: retained publication, later publication, event during subscription, async-read event without overlapping reads, original read error, subscription-error cleanup, and virtual hang-guard expiry. Timer bounds only guard hangs; no wall-clock pass condition. Local validation PASS under the shared heavy lock: all seven helper tests (102 ms total, no skips) and the unchanged real Chromium idle BFCache case before/after (8.423→1.542 s diagnostic only, including browser startup/cache variance). Same extension and assertions; separate reports in before.json/after.json. Memory admission passed (swapouts202294 unchanged, internal26.6GBfree); private browsers closed and lock released. Exact-head CI is fully green; ready for review.

- **15 / errors:** helper preserves original reader/subscriber errors and cleans up; JSON reader tolerates only ENOENT or incomplete JSON while waiting for another file event. Watch errors propagate.

author: yegamble
body:
## Failure mode

#530 added the generic anti-adblock proxy but refused every provider path under
`/api/`. Behind the stock reverse proxy (`vidra/deploy/Caddyfile`), `/api/*` and
a fixed list of root paths are the only requests forwarded to the api; everything
else goes to the frontend. So there was no path that was both accepted by the
parser and reachable by a visitor: the example from #530 (`/f2187587a2.js`)
answers 404 from the frontend in production.

## Fix

Reserve only the REST contract namespace (`/api/v1`, exact and prefix) instead of
all of `/api/`. A provider can now be mounted at e.g. `/api/x/<opaque>.js` with no
reverse-proxy change. Root paths stay allowed for deployments that route them.

## Tests

- Parser accepts `/api/x/tag.js`; still refuses `/api/v1` and `/api/v1/...`.
- New: a provider is served through the fully wired server at an `/api/` path.
  This returned 404 before the change, and it exercises the Echo registration
  that #530 only compiled.

`go vet ./internal/httpapi/` and `go test ./internal/httpapi/` pass locally.

author: mohamedetaiw-ops
body:

_Requested by **Mohamed** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012ec1T6Q9ySrTg54FyBTigT?thread=cmsg_012ec1T6Q9ySrTg54FyBTigTVwTto2eEo3ejzGyiBTjGhV)_

## Summary
This PR adds the agent tool path of spec 017 US2 (T008 and T009), which spec 027 FR-006 also requires.

- **Declared inputs.** Connector actions now declare their inputs. For custom REST actions the inputs come from the action definition. An action with no declared inputs cannot be used as a tool.
- **Registering a tool.** The integration administrator can register an action as the tenant tool `connector.<name>`, with a description for the model and a title in each language. This uses the new `integrations.connector_tool` table (forced RLS) and lives at `/pack-connections/{id}/tools`. It needs `integration.manage`, registering needs step-up, and each change is audited as `integration.action_changed`.
- **Tenant tools in the registry.** `IAgentToolSource` in Agents.Contracts lets the registry load tenant tools next to the product tools. They load once per scope, when the policy is read.
- **Calling a tool.** A tool's parameters are exactly the action's declared inputs. The spec 027 gateway runs its checks first, and then only those inputs go through the connector runtime. Each call shows in run history with the correlation `agent-run:{id}`.
- **Write actions.** These become `write_external` tools with the default rule "confirm". They need `ai.agents.write_tools` and L3, and L3 is not built yet.
- **Pages.**
  - The connection page has a new "Agent tools" section to list, register and remove tools.
  - The agent and policy editors show a tenant tool by its title.
  - After an action is saved, the page refreshes so the new action can be registered as a tool.

## Tests
- New `tests/Integration/ConnectorToolTests.cs` with 3 tests covering:
  - registration rules and audit
  - cross-tenant denial
  - an undeclared parameter refused before any call, so only the validated, declared parameters are sent
  - the call recorded in run history
  - a disabled connection turning the tool off
  - a write tool needing L3, and the policy blocking it
- Local results:
  - Unit: 463 passed
  - Architecture: 21 passed
  - Security: 14 passed

author: ahoo-wang
body:
## What

From #5687's review: since the failure ledger keys an entry by `SubscriptionId` (D410), `ParkedOps.Scope` no longer needs to hold names and look each one's context up. It holds the ids.

- `Scope(group, ids, ledger, options, runner, covers)`: `ids: () -> Set<SubscriptionId>` replaces `names` and `contextOf`.
  - `holds(id)` is `id in ids()`; `count` and `groupedSubscriptions` read the ids; `idOf` and the old `ids()` mapping are gone.
- `Scope.of(runtime)` reads the runtime's new `subscriptionIds`.
- `Scope.of(topic, …)` builds its ids from its subscriptions.
- The timers' `Scope.of(group, timers, partitions)` takes its runner's `parkedSubscription` and drops the `context` parameter it no longer needs; its two callers (`ParkedOps.of`, `NodeAssembly`) follow.
- `SubscriptionRuntime.subscriptionIds` is new (`SubscriptionRuntime.kt` 584 → 588, under the line). The runtime's `subscriptionNames` and `contextOf` stay, since `NodeSubscriptions` and `NodeHealth` use them.
- `ParkedOps.kt`: 443 → 432 lines.

## Behaviour

Unchanged. Within one scope a name is one subscription (a runtime's group, a topic), so the id found by name in `count` is the one `idOf` gave before. Operators see the same listings, counts and actions.

## Verification

- By name:
  - `ParkedOpsTest` (each context's `wow.snapshot` apart, the grouped counts, the pages);
  - `LedgerKeyAcrossContextsTest` (two contexts on one ledger, the timers' scope);
  - `LedgerCommandsTest`, `LedgerPublisherTest`, `LedgerNodeTest`, `NodeSubscriptionsTest`;
  - `:http` `ParkedRoutesTest`, `:observability` `NodeMetricsTest`, `:spring-boot` `HostParkedOpsTest`.
- Also run: `:runtime:detekt`, `:runtime:checkKotlinAbi` (unchanged: `Scope` is `internal`, `SubscriptionRuntime` is `@InternalWowApi`), `:architecture:test`, and the integration tests of `:runtime`'s dependants: `:spring-boot`, `:migrate-data`, `:cocache`, `:spring-cloud`, `:routing-spike`, `:lease-spike`.
- **The whole build's `test`: one failure, unrelated, then green.** `ScheduledCommandsTest` "a node whose clock is ahead fires early, and the target waits for the due time" failed once: the cancel committed 1 ms before the timer's `dueAt` (…790 against ≥ …791). It passed on 5 reruns in a row. That test is the timers' and the kernel's (no `ParkedOps` on its path) and is reported separately as a possible clock-domain edge.
- Patch coverage as `ci-gate` scores it, against the merge base: 14/14 = 100%.

## Review notes

- **Cohesion / clean code:** the scope says which subscriptions it holds the way the ledger keys them, so no lookup sits between the two.
- **Coupling:** the scope no longer needs a context function from each source; the timers' scope takes the identity its runner already parks under.
- **Size:** `ParkedOps.kt` 443 → 432; `SubscriptionRuntime.kt` 584 → 588.

Follow-up to #5687.

author: wompdoo
body:
Builds on #1 (the CI workflow). Merge #1 first and this pull request shrinks to the five commits below.

## Gameplay

- **MIDI player under the navigation.** Once you learn `<TABLE>` layouts, the music player sits in the sidebar right below the links, as on 1997 homepages. The 2005 table page does the same with the podcast player. The player wraps onto two lines there so the track name isn't cut off.
- **The Flash intro can be switched off again.** Features can now be marked switchable; the Build tab shows an On/Off switch. Switched off, the intro brings no visitors and no page weight (1522 KB → 172 KB in the test) but keeps its levels. The planned 2011 scroll-jacking toggle can reuse it.

## Balance: the late-2005 snowball

Income grew ×24 within one simulated minute and 2005 was over in five minutes. Three causes:

| Cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| Most 2005 multipliers became affordable at the same time | Prices spread from $600K to $250M; late features cost and produce more |
| Hosting tiers were 10× apart, so a capacity-bound upgrade multiplied income tenfold | Six tiers about 4× apart (new: server cluster, CDN) |
| Past 200% load the site served nobody: income dropped to typing, the next tier was out of reach (a 4-minute death spiral in the simulation) | Traffic is capped at capacity instead of dropping to zero; the 503 page still shows when most visitors get it |

| Scripted player | Steepest minute before → after | 2005 length before → after |
|---|---|---|
| active | ×24 → ×8.1 | 4.6 → 11.8 min |
| relaxed | ×18 → ×4.7 | 5.6 → 15.6 min |

The simulation now prints each player's steepest minute. While fixing this, the new CI check caught a softlock: the bot never built Comments once traffic was capped, because Comments added no income. The bot now buys what the checklist requires, like a human would.

## CI hardening

- Actions are pinned to commit SHAs (checkout v6.1.0, setup-node v6.5.0, upload-artifact v6.0.0), so a moved tag can't change what CI runs.
- Dependabot opens weekly pull requests for the actions and the npm dev dependencies.

## How it was checked

- 40 unit tests, including new ones for switching the intro and for capacity capping.
- The balance simulation: both scripted players finish both eras.
- A browser check at a MacBook window size: the MIDI player is the first sidebar block, and switching the intro off removes it from the page and drops the weight.

body:
## 개요
Flutter SDK와 모바일 의존성을 최신으로 올리고, iOS를 Swift Package Manager로 전환합니다. Firebase Crashlytics의 dSYM 누락 알림 원인도 함께 해결했습니다.

> ⚠️ iOS 빌드는 아직 검증하지 못했습니다. 로컬 Mac에 iOS 26.5 플랫폼을 설치하지 못했습니다(Apple 다운로드 오류). 머지 전에 아래 체크리스트를 꼭 진행해 주세요.

## 버전
| 플랫폼 | 버전 |
|--------|------|
| iOS | 2.1.2+1 |
| Android | 2.1.2+90 |
| AppVersion.current | 2.1.2 |

## 주요 변경
| 영역 | 내용 |
|------|------|
| Flutter | 3.35.4 → 3.47.9 (Dart 3.13.7) |
| Firebase | core 5.1, messaging 17, crashlytics 6, analytics 13, remote_config 7, performance 0.12 |
| SNS 로그인 | google_sign_in 7(API 재작성), kakao 2.1, sign_in_with_apple 8.2 |
| 기타 | google_mobile_ads 9.2, flutter_local_notifications 23, permission_handler 13, location 10, flutter_secure_storage 10.3 |
| Android | AGP 9.2.1, Gradle 9.4.1, Kotlin 2.4, Java 17, compileSdk 37, minSdk 24, Jetifier 제거, Unity Ads 4.21 |
| iOS | CocoaPods → SPM, 최소 버전 15.6 통일, Unity 미디에이션 어댑터 SPM 4.21 |
| Crashlytics | dSYM 업로드 빌드 단계 추가 (Release/Profile) |

## 판단 근거
- **SPM 전환:** Firebase iOS SDK는 12.9.0(2026-02)을 끝으로 CocoaPods 배포를 중단했고, GMA SDK 13.11+도 CocoaPods에 없습니다. resolve한 결과 GoogleMobileAds는 13.12.0 한 벌만 들어갑니다.
- **flutter_secure_storage 10:** v9에서 v11로 바로 올리면 기존 데이터를 읽지 못해 Android 사용자 전원이 강제 로그아웃됩니다. 자동 마이그레이션이 있는 v10을 먼저 배포하고, v11은 다음 배포에서 올립니다.
- **FCM `getToken`:** deprecated 경고가 뜨지만 유지합니다. 서버가 FCM 등록 토큰을 사용하기 때문입니다.

## 검증
- [x] flutter analyze: 에러 0건
- [x] Android debug APK 빌드 성공
- [x] iOS SPM 패키지 resolve 성공
- [ ] iOS 빌드 (`flutter build ipa`): iOS 26.5 플랫폼 설치 후 확인 필요
- [ ] 실기기: Google, Kakao, Apple 로그인
- [ ] 실기기: 푸시 알림 수신·탭
- [ ] 실기기: 배너, 전면, 앱 오프닝, 리워드 광고

`test/widget_test.dart`는 첫 커밋부터 있던 기본 카운터 템플릿 테스트라 원래부터 실패합니다. 이번 변경과는 관계없습니다.

author: quabug
body:
Nothing in a session waits for a person's approval any more. A tool call runs at once, as the session's owner, or is refused with a reason the agent reads.

## The rules

- **Tool groups decide.** A session runs only the tools of its owner's tool group (#270); anything else is refused, whoever asks.
- **Read only** is the one access a message chooses, and it changes nothing. *Ask before acting*, *Auto-approve*, auto-merge, *Always approve* and permission requests are gone; old clients' values act.
- **The host's own machine.** Commands of unsandboxed hosts and of sessions run on their host, commands without resource limits in someone else's session, and the tunnel run only for the host's owner and members they granted host commands. Everyone else is refused.
- **Extension tools** run for those people, or for every session where the host's owner allows it. The workspace's per-extension Approval/Automatic mode is gone.
- **Content between sessions whose readers differ** (sessions tool) is refused unless the session's owner turns on the new per-session setting: Details → People → *Content from sessions other people read* (`PUT /api/sessions/:id/audience-sharing`).
- **Pushes and GitHub comments, issues and merges** run on the admission of any writer's message. Broker capabilities get `410 approvals_removed`. Where a merge should wait for a person, leave `github_merge` out of the tool group or protect the branch on GitHub.

## Old connectors

Connectors advertise `approvalFree`. The server refuses new messages to older ones with `connector_update_required`, so nothing waits on a card nobody can decide. **Host owners need to update their connector (`npx pikibun@latest connect`) after this deploys.**

## Removed

- Server: the approval and operation routes, `requester-auto-approve`, the approval reviews, `withSandboxedDefault`, `hostOwnerDecides`, and member and requester auto-approve in `authorize`.
- App: approval cards, the dock, the Approvals tab, *Operation request*, the auto-approve confirmations, *Approvals* in workspace settings, the extension tools mode and the *Needs approval* notification. The access picker is now *Act* / *Read only*, and host command grants have a single level.
- Migrations `sqlite/0063_approvals_removed.sql` and `postgres/0056_approvals_removed.sql` copy every approval review into the audit log as `approval.requested`. They then drop `approval_reviews`, `broker_capabilities`, `session_auto_approved_requesters` and `workspace_approval_settings`, and set every extension's tools mode to automatic.

## Docs and tests

- `docs/approvals.md` is now *What a session may do*; the user docs and READMEs follow it. Design docs carry a note that their approval sections describe the earlier design.
- Tests are rewritten to the new rules. Locally: `tsc` is clean, `nsh check` passes, app tests pass 126/126, and every node test passes except those this sandbox can't run (they need `/tmp`, nested bubblewrap or Unix sockets). CI runs those.

body:
Finishes audit **A-17**. #115 handled the AI servers' addresses; this does the same for the Mempool/Esplora server's address. That address is used for BTC prices, and for wallet sync when it's chosen. `docs/TODO.md` listed it as the remaining part.

**The problem:** a `user:password@` in that address (e.g. a self-hosted mempool behind nginx Basic auth) was stored as typed in `AppSettings` under `electrum_url`. That's the table Settings → Data exports whole. It was also shown as typed in the Settings field.

**The fix:**
- **One shared class:** the keychain-login logic #115 put inside `OllamaService` is now a small class, `ServerLogins`, in `lib/core/services/server_logins.dart`. `OllamaService`, `XpubService` and `BtcPriceService` all use it, and the AI servers behave exactly as before (their seven tests are unchanged and pass).
- **`XpubService`**, which saves the address:
  - the login goes to the keychain and the table keeps the address without it
  - `esploraBaseUrl` and `saveSettings` return it with the password masked
  - saving the masked text back keeps the password
  - clearing the field forgets the login
  - the wallet sync requests with the full address
- **`BtcPriceService`**, which reads the same setting, puts the login back too, so price requests to a password-protected server still authenticate.
- **Reset all data** now deletes this login along with the AI servers'.
- **When the keychain refuses:** the server still works, and "your Bitcoin server login" is named under the server field and beside Export database.

**Tests:** four new cases in `test/server_login_test.dart`:
- the table holds no password, the keychain does, the address shows masked, and after a restart the price request still carries `alice:s3cret`; saving the masked field back keeps it
- clearing the field forgets it
- Reset all data deletes it
- a refusing keychain still works and sets the flag

`icloud_backup_test` now sets up `app.xpubService`, which the Data section reads.

The PR sets A-17's status to fixed (#115 and this PR), and removes the item from `docs/TODO.md`. Format, analyze and all 807 tests pass.

Light docs slice (weekday 2026-11-10). No `.sg1` format change, no decoder code, no CLI output change.

**A. `docs/research/DAMAGE-MARKING.md`** — design note from arXiv:2611.09366 (Chvanov & Malkovsky, anchored iterative decoding of RS product codes for tape; abstract verified on arxiv.org).
- Problem: one CRC32 per whole shard (`docs/sigil-v1.txt:81`, `:186`); column repair budget 2·errors + erasures ≤ n−k (`docs/SOFT-RS.md`) → Seal 8/16 fixes 8 marked holes but only 4 hidden errors.
- Options: (1) per-4096-byte stripe checks as an optional sidecar first; (2) iterative passes with anchors, same Merkle/true-name gate (fail closed); (3) bad-holder detection (plain checks = faults F only; signed table for a lying holder, A).
- Finding: stripe flags used as pure erasures are *worse* for scattered flips (model), better for stripe-shaped damage (model) → flags must be hints. All gain numbers UNVERIFIED until the DEEP-SPACE measurement plan (M1–M6) is run.
- Perspectives (Frost/Fire Rune, servers/PCs, cloud, installed/not, Linux/Windows servers, databases, AWS, mainframe/tape, paper), threat-model lines, limitations, ADOPT / PROPOSE TO ASHLYNN (sidecar format is her pick).

**B. Unencrypted Seal pieces are readable — tested.** Plain seals fold (keyless, salt in every piece) + systematic RS, so data pieces are payload slices. New tests in `crate/sigil/src/kit.rs`:
- `unencrypted_seal_piece_on_one_frost_drive_is_readable_without_key` (usb-0 alone yields data pieces 0 and 4 exactly)
- `unencrypted_compressed_text_piece_is_readable_without_key`
- `passphrase_seal_piece_on_one_frost_drive_shows_no_plaintext`
Warnings added to README "Known limitations" and `docs/sigil-v1.txt` (Frost Rune + claim P). encrypt-to not tested (marked UNVERIFIED).

author: renesenses
body:
Closes #6103

## Ce qui change
`tune-core/src/outputs/local/empreinte_du_puits_r1.rs` : les deux `neon: None` sont remplacés par les relevés mesurés sur le Mac Studio. Le commentaire de provenance est mis à jour. Rien d'autre ne change. SSE3, scalaire et AVX+FMA n'ont pas bougé.

## Méthode (celle du 12/10, #6210)
- Machine : Mac Studio, Apple M1 Max, aarch64, macOS. Base : `origin/batch/bugs-rc12-20261108` (`c7e00884d`).
- Mêmes témoins, mêmes signaux (`pcm16(8192, 2)`, 44,1 → 48 kHz stéréo et stéréo → mono 48 kHz), même rééchantillonneur `new_streaming_resampler`. Pour 44,1 → 48 kHz, `interpolation_sinc` choisit l'interpolation Cubique.
- Instrumentation temporaire, non commitée :
  - `vendor/rubato/src/asynchro_sinc.rs` : dans `make_interpolator`, la branche NEON est sautée quand `TUNE_6103_SCALAIRE` est défini, ce qui force le noyau scalaire.
  - Dans le témoin, `noyau_de_rubato()` suit le même forçage, et chacun des deux témoins imprime son noyau, son nombre de mots et son empreinte.
- NEON : rubato sur son noyau naturel (sans forçage). Scalaire : forcé. Deux passes pour chacun.

## Valeurs brutes

| relevé | NEON passe 1 | NEON passe 2 | scalaire (Mac) passe 1 / 2 | scalaire figé (Shrek, #6210) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rééchantillonnage 44,1 → 48 kHz (17 828 mots) | 16135614424167615948 | 16135614424167615948 | 8996583943213529006 / 8996583943213529006 | 8996583943213529006 |
| adaptation puis rééchantillonnage (8 914 mots) | 7862539716852144112 | 7862539716852144112 | 3035902412451843507 / 3035902412451843507 | 3035902412451843507 |

## Recoupement
Le scalaire forcé du Mac donne au bit près les deux relevés scalaires de Shrek (x86_64), ce qui contrôle la méthode sur ce banc. Comme le 19/09, cela montre aussi que la table des sincs est portable. Sur le scalaire forcé, le message « NON remesuré » n'apparaît pas : la comparaison a bien lieu, et les 7 témoins sont verts.

## Preuve (sur le Mac, après retrait de l'instrumentation)
- Valeurs NEON en place : `7 passed`, sans message « NON remesuré ». Les deux témoins comparent donc vraiment sur NEON.
- Contre-épreuve avec chaque valeur décalée de 1 : les deux témoins sont **rouges** (`left: 16135614424167615948 / right: …949` et `left: 7862539716852144112 / right: …113`). Après restauration, ils redeviennent verts.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` : propre.

## Commandes lancées (Mac, `nice -n 15`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, target hors dépôt, un seul cargo, purgé après)
```
cargo test -p tune-core --lib empreinte_du_puits -- --nocapture                         # NEON, ×2
TUNE_6103_SCALAIRE=1 cargo test -p tune-core --lib empreinte_du_puits -- --nocapture    # scalaire forcé, ×2
cargo test -p tune-core --lib empreinte_du_puits                                        # contre-épreuve +1, puis restauré
cargo fmt --all --check
```
Aucun son : ces témoins écrivent dans un puits de capture qui hache les octets, sans aucune sortie audio.

## Portes Shrek : NON passées
La garde de Shrek a refusé la compilation : `tmpfs targets : 4.7 Gio disponibles, 16 Gio requis`, charge 40. Je ne l'ai pas contournée. Il reste à passer `clippy` (ligne CI) et les tests. Sur x86_64, la modification ne joue pas : Shrek et la CI Linux/Windows prennent AVX+FMA, et le champ `neon` n'y est jamais lu. Elle ne touche que deux constantes et un commentaire de test.

author: antaymard
body:
## What

Follow-ups to the first real run of `/v1/converse` with app events and a decision model.

**Fixes**
- An app event could silence the reply to the user: the "say it, or say nothing" instruction was written inside the event, which then sat right before the user's next words. Events are now plain context; that instruction lives only in the system prompt of a reply the assistant makes on its own.
- A pause cancelled an action the model was already deciding on mid-sentence: preparing the speculative reply at `eager_end` aborted the in-flight early look, so the action was redone only after the turn ended. The speculative reply now waits for that look. The decision gate also opens at a lower probability (a false alarm costs one LLM call).

**Defaults**
- LLM: an OpenRouter key no longer switches the conversation to Claude Haiku. Measured on the deployed server, first word after ~0.75 s with Haiku via OpenRouter vs ~0.1 s with `mistral-small-latest`. The key still enables the decision model and the `openrouter` provider.
- Voice: the Docker image sets `TTS_VOICE` to the account's custom voice, used for every language (a host variable or a per-request `voice` overrides it).

**Observability**
- `response_done` carries `speech`: `"realtime"` or `"http"`, so a client can tell when the realtime voice fails and the per-sentence fallback takes over.

## Verification

156 tests pass (`npm test`), with new regression tests for both fixes; typecheck passes. The fixes and the custom voice on the realtime speech path are to be re-checked on the deployed server after merge.

author: savinovanton
body:
## Что сделано

Причина nightly-регрессии `sim.telemetry_tick` (+10..14%) найдена bisect-ом (подробности и таблица замеров в комментарии к #217): с E7-T02 в `CharacterTable` 31 колонка вместо 6. Бенчмарк перед каждым batch делает `restore_state(base)`, и у копии `capacity == size` во всех колонках; первое рождение в batch (граница месяца) перевыделяет и копирует все ~30 колонок (~750 КБ на 5000 персонажей). Без рождений (28 тиков) разницы с reference нет.

Фикс: `World::reserve_character_headroom(extra)` резервирует место во всех колонках персонажей; `Simulation::restore_state` вызывает его с запасом `capacity/8 + 64`. Меняется только capacity: состояние, хеш, сейвы, реплеи и golden-значения прежние.

Честная оговорка: фикс не ускоряет тик, а убирает разовое перевыделение из измеряемого окна (оно переезжает в `restore_state`, вне замера бенчмарка). Реальная польза: загруженный/перемотанный мир не получает разовый затор на первых рождениях. Экспериментально (тот же код, 4 раунда по 5 повторов, интерливинг): 0a330c7 min 278 / median 291 мкс, main 330 / 367, с фиксом 260 / 285. Пороги и reference не менялись.

Closes #217

Новый тест в `tests/simulation_test.cpp`: `restore_state` сохраняет хеш, а рождения после него дают те же id и то же состояние, что и у обычной копии. `src/sim/economy/*` не затронуты.

author: mmastrac
body:
GLM-5.3-Flash at T=1 sometimes falls into a verbatim loop inside its thinking on long agent turns (DeepSeek Harness: one step repeated a 200-character stretch 72 times until the budget cut it). The sequence penalty stops loops but breaks code copying, since it matches the whole context. This adds a front-end loop guard that watches only the reply's own thinking and steps in once a loop is plain.

## What it does

- **Detector** (`frontend/g6front-rs/src/loopguard.rs`): a rolling hash over every window of `min` thinking tokens (default 64), one table entry per window. It fires when one window has occurred `copies` times without overlapping (default 3), or, with `long=` set, when the tail repeats one earlier stretch for `long` tokens (off by default). Windows the prompt also holds never fire; the prompt's windows are hashed only when a window first reaches the trigger.
- **Modes** (`mode=`): `phrase` puts a steering phrase into the reasoning; `phrase-close` puts the phrase in, and on a second trigger within `window` thinking tokens (default 4096) puts the phrase and `\n</think>\n\n` in; `close` puts both in at once; `log` only logs. `max` caps triggers per request (default 2). `text=` sets the phrase; it comes last and takes the rest of the spec, with `\n`, `\t`, `\\` escapes.
- The action uses the budget's continuation path: cancel the run, go on with prompt + reply + the guard's tokens in a new `generate`. Usage counts the guard's tokens once.
- **Options**: `--default-loop-guard SPEC` (launcher `DEFAULT_LOOP_GUARD`, validated in options.py, passed by the supervisor), and a per-request `loop_guard` (spec string, `true`, `"off"` or `false`). Off by default. With `logprobs` or a forced `tool_choice` the server default steps aside and a request's own is refused, as for `thinking_budget`.
- Each trigger logs one line: mode, trigger count, reply and thinking token index, run length, period, copies, and what went in.

## Continuation fixes (shared with the budget path)

- Inside the block, the continuation's engine budget insert (`after_tokens`) and the boost's `start` move back by the reply's length, so both still fire where they would have.
- After a close, the continuation sends no `think_end`, boost, thinking scope or insert, and a JSON grammar applies from the first token. Before, a front-end budget continuation still sent `think_end`, so the engine counted the answer as thinking.
- `cached_tokens` stays the first run's (a second continuation used to overwrite it).

## Checks

`cargo fmt`, `cargo test --release` (175 pass), `cargo clippy --all-targets` (no new warnings), `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/launch` (380, OK), `knobs gen` / `knobs check` current.

## Replays

TP=1 Flash recipe (stable-1110, this PR's g6front-rs mounted over the image's), T=1, the image's budget 28,672 and boost. The three DSH steps that looped (stable-s2 #6 at 71K, cand-s2 #14 at 104K, stable-s1 #6 at 108K), each with 4 seeds whose guard-off run looped (out of 8-12 searched), 12 runs per arm. Seeded runs do not repeat their trajectory under batching, so `ctl` (the same seeds again, guard off) is the fair comparison.

| arm | loops (window 5+) | runaway to 128,000 | good answer | write/edit | mean thinking | mean wall s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ctl (off) | 6 | 0 | 11 | 5 | 21,437 | 1,766 |
| `phrase` | 2 | 1 | 11 | 6 | 19,832 | 1,934 |
| `phrase-close,window=512` | 1 | 0 | 12 | 8 | 18,370 | 1,643 |
| `close` | 0 | 1 | 11 | 7 | 14,391 | 1,505 |
| `phrase-close,min=32,copies=4` | 2 | 1 | 10 | 6 | 18,916 | 2,079 |
| `phrase-close,window=4096` | 1 | 0 | 12 | 9 | 16,374 | 1,567 |

- A phrase alone often lets the loop come back (5 of 9 triggered runs).
- A loop came back 430 to 6,100 tokens after the phrase (most often ~1,500), so the 512 window rarely closed; the default window is now 4096.
- Every runaway was a close mid-thought (the guard's or the budget's, one with no trigger at all), after which the model went on reasoning in the answer ("let me also reconsider ... fine") until max_tokens. An answer-side guard after a forced close is the likely follow-up.
- Detector: in the guard-off seed searches (28 runs) it fired on every run with a 5+ window and on none of the 15 healthy ones. One of its 13 firings was a code block drafted three times across 25K tokens.

Suggested default: `mode=phrase-close` (min 64, copies 3, max 2, window 4096). Server default stays off.

Transcripts: harness-bench-runs `transcripts/loop-guard/`.

author: rene-langer
body:
Follow-up to #716 (#617, "Collapse merges"). Its mutation report listed untested code in `crates/git-core`. This PR adds real temp-dir repo tests in `crates/git-core/tests/` for it. I applied each mutant by hand, watched the new test fail, then restored the code. No production code changes.

## Missed mutants

| Mutant | Outcome | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `graph.rs:254:43` `\|`→`&` in `merged_commits` | Caught | `graph.rs::merged_commits_list_unrelated_commits_newest_first`: an octopus brings in three tips whose commit-time order is neither the parent order nor its reverse. `Sort::NONE` lists them in a different order. |
| `graph.rs:254:43` `\|`→`^` in `merged_commits` | **Equivalent** | `Sort::TOPOLOGICAL` (1) and `Sort::TIME` (2) are disjoint bits, so `a ^ b == a \| b`. No test can tell them apart. I applied it and the suite still passes, as it must. |
| `locate.rs:89:39` `&&`→`\|\|` in `locate_commit` | Caught | `locate.rs::a_commit_already_in_the_collapsed_graph_names_no_merge_although_a_merge_holds_it`: with "Collapse merges" on and `trunk` + `feature` selected, `feature 3` is a row of the graph. A merge on `trunk` also holds it, so the mutant reported that merge as well. |
| `locate.rs:140:33` `<`→`>` in `collapsed_merge` | Caught | `locate.rs::a_commit_hidden_behind_a_collapsed_octopus_merge_names_it_with_its_offset`: an octopus (4 parents) holding the commit is skipped by the mutant. |
| `locate.rs:144:44` `\|`→`&` in `collapsed_merge` | Caught | The same octopus test checks the offsets 0/1/2, which follow commit time. (`\|`→`^` here would be equivalent for the same reason as above.) |

`commit_at` is a new helper in `tests/common/mod.rs`. It commits an empty tree at a fixed time, so the time order in these tests does not depend on commits made in the same second.

## Timed-out mutants (binary search)

None of the four can return a wrong result. Every one of them still keeps "`line[low]` reaches the target, `line[high]` does not". Whenever the loop ends it ends with `high - low == 1`, so a mutant either gives the right answer or never stops:

- `128:26` `>`→`>=`: at `high - low == 1` the midpoint is `low`, which reaches, so the loop never ends. This happens on every search that finds a merge.
- `128:20` `-`→`+`: the same never-ending loop as soon as `low > 0`, i.e. when the merge is not the line's first commit.
- `129:30` `+`→`*`: the midpoint is always `0` while `low == 0`, so the loop never ends on any line of 2 or more commits.
- `129:45` `/`→`%`: the midpoint is `low` whenever `high - low` is even, so the loop never ends. When it does end, it went through one commit at a time and the answer is right.

So the existing tests already exercise them, and they hung until the run's time limit. The new test `locate.rs::the_merge_is_found_at_every_position_of_first_parent_lines_of_every_length` covers the bounds: first-parent lines of 2 to 7 commits (even and odd), with the merge at every index from the tip (0) to the commit next to the root. It runs under a `within(20s, …)` guard. If the search does not finish in time, the guard writes a message straight to stderr (not `eprintln!`, which the harness captures) and ends the whole test binary with `process::exit(1)`. Otherwise one hung test would keep the binary, and the mutation run, waiting until its own timeout. With each of the four mutants applied, `cargo test --test locate` now fails after about 20 s with `locate_commit ran past 20s: the search loops`.

A line of one commit never reaches the binary search with a hidden target. Such a tip has no parents, so it reaches the target only when it *is* the target. The target is then a row of the graph, and `collapsed_merge` is never called.

author: gavindu
body: Epic #807 P0 #811 / P1 #813. The prior #908 per-provider import lock did not include `DELETE /relay/.../unlink`, so an import racing revoke could write/activate credentials after an unlink reported success. Reuse the same per-provider async gate through the complete browser-worker unlink operation; concurrent imports now wait behind revocation and vice versa, while different provider operations stay independent. Bounded 45-second waiting returns explicit retryable `session_unlink_busy` (503) without pretending credentials were deleted; gate failure is distinguished as `session_unlink_unavailable`. Validate provider IDs before inserting a gate, preventing arbitrary path parameters from growing the map. Synthetic async regression verifies an in-flight import holds back unlink and another provider remains available. No local/live provider E2E. Close neither #811 nor #813 until delegated auth/restart and runtime latency acceptance. Merge only after exact-head GitHub Actions `test`, `embedded-native`, `docker-build`, and `docker-arm64-low-memory` pass.

### Summary

Related to #322.

Policy Search still carried fixture, cutover, credential-copy, Java transfer/rehearsal and qualification machinery after the Go service became the ordinary owner. This PR removes that migration-only surface and leaves a small, repeatable resource-administration path that preserves compatible state, credentials, Java repository assets and the legacy gateway contract.

### Key Changes

- **Ordinary resources and administration**
  - Uses `policy-views`, `policy-registered`, `policy-terminated` and `policy-search-service` consistently across runtime defaults, overlays, event fixtures and disposable checks.
  - Provides `resource-inspect`, `resource-ensure` and `resource-verify` targets through `scripts/resource_administration.py`, with guarded shared primitives in `scripts/administration.py`.
  - Checks the complete index, identity, credential and trust boundary before mutation; persists generated credentials before creating native users so an interrupted run can resume safely.
  - Creates new roles, users and Secrets with `policy-search` ownership while accepting compatible legacy descriptive metadata without rotating credentials.
- **Migration machinery removal**
  - Removes fixture administration, credential-copy, ownership-transfer/return rehearsals, qualification reporting and corpus assets, and retired shared dispatch entries.
  - Replaces the qualification client with a focused HTTP, gRPC, health and access smoke client.
  - Leaves Java source, build, image and legacy manifest assets unchanged.
- **Focused steady-state safeguards**
  - Covers existing Secret preservation, missing Secret creation, CA drift rejection and interrupted credential persistence with focused fake-boundary tests.
  - Makes the disposable duplicate-event check require an advancing Elasticsearch sequence number after every produced event and rechecks the final terminated document.

merge evidence or directive. The apply path now runs `linkMergedPull` inside
`transactIntentLedger`, matching against the freshest locked ledger, the same
primitive `edit.ts`/`import.ts`/`fleet-intent link` already use. Shipped
handling stays delegated to `noteShippedRelease`; dry-run preview, argument
validation, JSON shape and error codes are unchanged. No new lock and no
nested transactions.

No-match behavior: `transactIntentLedger` always persists after `mutate`, so a
`merged --apply` that matches nothing now rewrites the ledger where the old
code skipped the write. For a canonical ledger the rewrite is byte-identical
(proven below); for a non-canonical file it normalizes formatting. A missing
ledger is still never created: `ledgerFilePresent()` gates the transaction and
the legacy read path handles the absent case with zero matches and no write.

## Files changed

- `src/cli/fleet-intent-evidence.ts` (+9/-4 net): import `ledgerFilePresent` +
  `transactIntentLedger` (drop `writeLedger`); merged+apply goes through the
  transaction when the ledger file exists.
- `test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts` (new, ~330 lines): 6 tests.

Net LOC: ~+335/-4 across the two allowed files. BRIDGE_NOTES.md is the only
other changed path.

## Regression evidence

New suite `test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts` drives the real
`cmdFleetIntentEvidence` against an isolated `ASHLR_RUNS_DIR`:

- Child processes (tsx evals) released on a shared go-file barrier race
  `merged --apply` against `addIntent` + `updateIntent`: all three succeed and
  the final ledger keeps the merge evidence (status `merged`, PR association,
  evidence row) AND the concurrent add/update — the exact interleaving the old
  unlocked path could drop.
- Same-process `Promise.all` race through the in-process queue + file lock.
- Held `ledger.lock` (real `acquireLocalStoreLockWithOutcome`): `merged --apply`
  returns exit 1 with `intent-evidence: Intent ledger is busy...` (retryable),
  bytes unchanged; dry-run still answers while locked; retry after release
  applies cleanly.
- Dry-run and unmatched `--apply` leave ledger bytes byte-identical; matched
  apply persists; repeated apply replays safely (one PR association, evidence
  rows accumulate, terminal statuses kept); missing ledger is never created.

Note: the concurrent update uses an `owner` patch, not `evidence` —
`updateIntent` evidence flips `merged`->`verified`, which would make the
post-race status order-dependent. Owner edits never interact with merge status.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts`
  — 6/6 pass (~3.7s).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/intent-evidence-cli-09spc2.test.ts
  test/intent-evidence-reconcile-09spa1.test.ts
  test/intent-release-replay-preservation-09sqv1.test.ts
  test/intent-release-persistence-09spr1.test.ts
  test/intent-link-concurrent-preservation-10sry2.test.ts
  test/intent-sweep-concurrent-preservation-10sry1.test.ts
  test/intent-concurrent-writers-10srw1.test.ts` — 42/42 pass.
- `npx eslint src/cli/fleet-intent-evidence.ts
  test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts` — clean.
  (This worktree's `node_modules/eslint` was missing `lib/`; restored by copying
  the identical eslint@9.39.5 `lib/` from a sibling worktree — node_modules is
  untracked, no package files touched.)
- `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (via sibling worktree's
  `@typescript/native-preview` binary; this worktree lacks the package) —
  clean, exit 0. Equivalent to `npx --no-install tsgo`; `tsgo` is not published
  on npm under that name.

Pass/fail: all green. No commits, pushes or PRs; changes left uncommitted.

## Remaining limits

- `merged --apply` on an existing but non-canonical ledger file rewrites it in
  canonical `writeLedger` form even when nothing matches (disclosed above);
  bytes are identical for ledgers previously written by `writeLedger`.
- If the ledger file is deleted between `ledgerFilePresent()` and the
  transaction, the transaction creates a fresh empty ledger — same exposure
  any serialized writer has; no code path deletes the ledger in normal use.
- `noteShippedRelease` (release.ts) and merge-snapshot serialization are owned
  by other jobs and were not touched; `shipped --apply` keeps its existing
  semantics.
</details>

author: fueledbyredbull
body:
Powder Game wouldn't start on GPUs that offer only the OpenGL 4.3 minimum of 8 image units, which is what NVIDIA and Intel drivers usually report. It showed "GPU supports 8 image units; Powder Game requires 18" and quit.

Shaders now sample any field they don't write (texelFetch, returning zero outside the texture as imageLoad did) and use image units only for writes, all on units 0 to 7. The host binds read-only fields as textures, write-only ones as images and read-write ones as both, and image barriers also cover texture fetches. The startup limit check is gone; gpu-compile now fails any shader that goes over the 4.3 minimums.

Tested on an RX 7800 XT: ctest 103/103, POWDER_REPLAY=all passes, benchmark-realtime passes (combined GPU mean 18.5 ms). The water, sand, boundary and leakage replay signatures match v0.7.1 exactly. Gas and combined end slightly differently; I bisected that to compiler rounding in smoke_correct and gas_velocity_correct, where the values read are identical. Not tested on NVIDIA or Intel hardware.

author: maan2003
body:
Adds byte streams to `docs/gccp.md`: a clanker reaches a service that another clanker runs (a web server, git, a database). Spec only; no code.

## Protocol part (normative)

- **Stream kind 2.** After the kind: a 16-bit length and one CBOR map `{to, from, service}`. The receiving harness answers with a 16-bit length and the same result map as a message, `{success: bool}`. After `true`, bytes pass unchanged in both directions.
- **`service` is a name**, in the form of a local id. It is not a port, and only the receiving harness gives it meaning.
- **One stream for each connection** to the service.
- **Refusal** is `false` with no reason, as for a message.
- **The opener waits**: it must not write bytes after the header until it has the result `true`.
- **After the result the protocol says no more.** What the bytes mean, and when and how each side ends the stream, is between the service and whoever uses it. Nothing resumes a stream that broke.
- A harness that does not know kind 2 resets the stream with code 1, by the rule the document has already.

## "What a harness may do" (example, not normative)

- Accepting an address opens no service. A clanker opens a service by name to one accepted address.
- The harness joins a stream only to something of the clanker's own, for example a Unix socket among its files, and not a port of the machine.
- The opening side gets a local socket; each connection to it opens one stream.
- No list of services, no retry, and the owner can see and take back what is open.

The second round for a lost connection, after the design review of 0.26.1. Where the answers stopped coming, the details went on showing the last delays as if they were current, for as long as the connection was gone. Back without a connection changed the address but left the details of the page before in place, or the map alone. A question that hung looked like a live page.

**Saying how old it is:**
- From 2 minutes after the last answer (`STALE_S`) the delays are grey, and the note says "Seit 13:37 keine Verbindung · Verspätungen nicht aktuell".
- From 10 minutes (`SCHEDULE_S`) the details go by the timetable alone: no delays, departures in their planned order, and the note says "· nur nach Fahrplan". A screen reader hears each stage once.
- A line or a trip that shows no delays keeps the plain note.

**What the page holds is only part of the timetable:**
- After the last departure it holds, the list says "Weitere Abfahrten, sobald die Verbindung wieder da ist.", or says only that once all have left. This holds on stops, in "Alle Linien" and on boards.
- A vehicle whose known way has ended leaves the map and the line card, and a line card no longer counts its vehicles under way.
- The card no longer repeats "Keine Verbindung zum Server" while the details say it.

**Back, Forward and hangs:**
- Without a connection, Back and Forward open what the page held of that address in this visit (the last 12 addresses), with the note. Where it holds nothing, the details say that the address loads once the connection is back.
- With a connection, Back opens the address afresh, as before. Where the answer takes longer than a second, the details show "Lade …" under the name the page knows, without the buttons of the details being left.
- Every question to the server gives up after 20 s (`ANSWER_MS`). The search list gets 20 s to begin and 2 min to arrive.
- A button that tries again asks one question at a time, so a visit is counted once.

**A shared link (the page as the server sent it):**
- It is kept, with the note, where its first answers fail or hang. Its delays grey after 2 minutes and departures that have left go.
- The server now marks a trip's page as sent too (`server/lib/page.js`). Until its stops come, it says "Lade …", then "Gerade keine Verbindung – lädt, sobald sie wieder da ist."

**Filter:**
- A filter chosen without a connection says that the chosen lines load once it is back, instead of showing the held departures of every line under "Nur …". This holds on the board too.
- The filter sheet closes when other details take the place of those it was opened in, and it fills once the directions come.

**Trade-off:** from 10 minutes on, a departure that the last answer had as late leaves the list at its planned time, though it may still come later. That is what going by the timetable alone means.

author: suhanisharma43434343
body:
Adds the web-harness pre-build questions to Forge, so every project asks them before anything is built.

## Frozen interface change
This changes `schemas/brief.schema.json`, which `docs/interfaces.md` lists as frozen. The operator said in chat on 2026-11-10 that both owners approved adding these fields. This PR is the formal record, so it needs both owners' review approval on GitHub before it merges. (#42, the last brief change, merged without GitHub reviews.)

Every new field is **optional**. All seven sample briefs still validate. The schema diff adds 74 lines and changes 1.

| Field | Question it answers | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `audience[].arrivesFrom`, `audience[].mood` | Where does each visitor arrive from, and in what mood? | strings |
| `truths` | What is true here that nobody else can claim? | up to 6 `{ text, kind? }`; kind is place, people, material, history, method, number or other |
| `jobs` | What must a visitor do in one tap from anywhere on the site? | up to 4 strings |
| `contentRules` | What must never appear on a page, and what must always appear (legal lines such as licence numbers or consent)? | `{ rule: never \| always, text, pages: [slug \| "*"] }` |
| `access` | On day one: the domain, DNS, and what material exists and how good it is | `{ domain: { name, status }, dns, assets: [{ item, where?, quality }] }` |

Two parts of the original questions had no field. They live inside these fields rather than as extra ones:
- **Legal lines** are `always` content rules.
- **How good existing material is** is each asset's `quality` in `access`.

## What uses them
- **Intake:** new questions in every project type, rounds 2 and 3, so they don't crowd out the required fields in round 1: `q-truths`, `q-jobs`, `q-access`, `q-content-rules`, `q-languages`, `q-deadline`, `q-existing-site`.
    - The audience question also asks for `| from: ... | mood: ...`. Every prompt stays within the question bank's 300-character limit.
    - Typed answers are turned into the brief shapes: for example `never on /, /about: Smith`, `domain: example.com, client will give`, `photos: usable, in Drive`.
- **The B1 plan** shows each field:
    - It warns when there are fewer than three truths: the first deliverable is then questions for the client, not a design.
    - It lists what to ask the client for on day one: the domain, who controls it, DNS, and any material with unknown quality.
- **Contracts:**
    - Research puts the truths first in the "about" bucket and names the one the site rests on. With fewer than three, it adds questions for the client.
    - The direction's concept rests on one of the truths.
    - The section plan places every job on every page, and plans the first screen for each audience's arrival and mood.
    - The copy follows the content rules.
- **A mechanical check:** the copy check refuses copy that breaks a content rule.
    - `never` text found on a named page fails it, ignoring case and spacing.
    - A missing `always` line fails it. A line in the nav or footer counts for every page.
    - A rule naming a page with no copy is reported too.
- **Intake fix:** a date or URL answer may now be `null`, meaning there is none. A `null` recommendation (no deadline, no current site) leaves the field unset, where before it would have written `null` into the brief and made it invalid.

## Not covered
- The B2 interview questions (A or B for the first five seconds, which would embarrass you, which a competitor could copy, which needs photos we don't have, the reasons for rejections) are not in this PR. They need a new B2 format and are a separate piece.
- Whether jobs are actually reachable in one tap is a contract for the section plan, not a check. A check would need to read the built header and footer.

## Merge order

author: jakobt
body:
A disabled trigger had no representation: it compared equal to an enabled one, and a trigger Weasel created was always enabled.

Trigger.IsDisabled renders a DISABLE TRIGGER after the create when set, and FetchExistingIsDisabledAsync reads the state back. The state is compared only when the expected trigger sets it, so an existing model that leaves it unset sees no new drift.
