author: xmfcx
body: ## Description VisionPilot is in the Autoware Index, but its sweep fails at the CMake configure step. The sweep uses only `rosdep install` and `colcon build`, and VisionPilot needs a manual ONNX Runtime download, extra apt packages and a symlink in `/usr/include`. With this PR, `rosdep install` and `colcon build` are enough. - https://index.autoware.org/ Changes: - `package.xml` declares the system dependencies and `onnxruntime_vendor`. - If `ONNXRUNTIME_ROOT` is set, the build uses it, as before. If it is not set, the build uses the CPU build of ONNX Runtime from `onnxruntime_vendor`. - The planning module finds the Ipopt headers without the symlink in `/usr/include`. - `generate_config` runs from `scripts/`, so the build directory can be anywhere. - The install rule copies ONNX Runtime from `ONNXRUNTIME_ROOT`, not from `VisionPilot/onnxruntime/`. - The README and `getting-started.md` explain the ROS 2 build. Notes for the maintainers: - The `onnxruntime_vendor` build is CPU only. A binary built this way must run with `engine.provider = cpu` in `config/vision_pilot.conf`. - If your packaging flow puts ONNX Runtime in `VisionPilot/onnxruntime/` on purpose, tell me and I will keep that path. - After this PR merges, the VisionPilot ref in the Index needs a bump in a separate PR. ## rosdep key `cppad` VisionPilot depends on `cppad`. The fix for this key is in rosdistro: - Before 2026-11-11: the key mapped to the apt package `cppad`, which Ubuntu 24.04 does not have. `rosdep install` failed on this package. - 2026-11-11: the rosdistro fix below merged. On Ubuntu 24.04, the key now maps to `libcppad-dev`. - From 2026-11-11: `rosdep update` gets the new rule at once, because rosdep reads it from the rosdistro `master` branch. No ROS release is necessary. - An image with an older rosdep cache, for example `core-devel-jazzy-2.1.0`, still has the old rule. Run `rosdep update` in it before `rosdep install`. - https://github.com/ros/rosdistro/pull/55329 ## Inference on CPU I ran the build on the OpenLane sample `test_open_lane_2` (198 frames) with `engine.provider = cpu`. It processed the sequence in 49.7 s on 24 CPU cores and printed a plan for 197 frames. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3389dfb1-a30c-48bc-9bf9-8804dcc8faea ## How I tested In `ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:core-devel-jazzy-2.1.0`, with the Index sweep commands: - `rosdep install`: passes after `rosdep update`, with no local rule for `cppad` (tested on 2026-11-11, after the rosdistro fix merged). - `colcon build`: passes. The binary links `libonnxruntime.so.1` from `onnxruntime_vendor`. With the plain CMake flow from `build-vision-pilot.yaml`: - An absolute and a relative `ONNXRUNTIME_ROOT`: build and install pass. - No `ONNXRUNTIME_ROOT` and no ROS 2: configure stops with an error that names `ONNXRUNTIME_ROOT`. - `-DENABLE_ROS2_INTERFACE=ON`: build and install pass. Not tested: a GPU build, the Docker images and arm64. In GitHub CI, both `build-vision-pilot` jobs pass. `spell-check-differential` fails on library names such as `ipopt` and `cppad`. The same check also fails on the merged PR below. - #463 ## AI usage Written with Claude Code. Agents that did not write the code reviewed it in 3 rounds and ran the build steps again. I fixed or answered all of their findings.

author: federicots
body:
## Why

On a 14-day trip, the trip page's assistant was asked to add a 15th day four times in a row. Each reply said "here is the new Day 15… ready to save", and none came with a change. The model did return `trip_length: 15` and a full Day 15. `validateEdits` drops days past the platform cap (`MAX_TRIP_DAYS`, 14, or 21 for a multi-city trip) without saying anything, so the change came out empty and the reply's promise stood. The honesty checks don't know the trip page's own wording for a prepared change, so nothing caught it.

## What

- `validateEdits` returns `overCap` when the reply asks for more days than the trip may have.
- `correctionFor` handles `overCap` first. At the cap, the retry is told to add no day, say so, and offer to use an existing day or plan a second trip. Below the cap, it's told `trip_length` can be the cap at most. This check runs before the "hands over a change" rule, which would ask for the same day again.
- If the answer still goes over the cap, nothing of it stands (like a cut nobody asked for): no edits and no parts. The reply becomes the new `tripCap` note, in en/es/it/pt, saying how many more days are possible and what can be done instead.
- `announcesProposal` now knows the trip page's wording for a prepared change (READY_WORDING): "Here's a new Day 6…", "Here are 7 new days", "Ready to swap…", ", ready to save", plus the es/it/pt forms. It's only read when nothing was prepared, so any path where a promised change went missing is caught. "Your trip is ready to save" and "an extra day trip" are left alone.

## Tests

- `engine-edits.vitest.ts`:
  - `overCap` at and below the cap, for multi-city trips, and for a trip already past the cap.
  - The `tripCap` note: at the cap, with room left, in Italian, and never over a change that stands.
- `honesty.vitest.ts`: the four replies from that trip plus each language's ready wording are caught; saving talk and day trips are not.
- `engine-retry.vitest.ts`:
  - A model that keeps adding Day 15 ends with the note, no edits and no parts.
  - A model that complies keeps its own words.
  - A 12-day trip is told it can take 2 more.
- Mutants: every rule above, broken on purpose, fails a test.
- Real model, locally, through the trip page's path on a copy of that 14-day trip: "add day 15 in Dublin", "add 1 day" and "add a travel day" now each answer that the trip is at its 14-day maximum and offer to use an existing day. Before, each said the new day was ready with nothing to save.

author: jcputney
body:
## Problem

Two `submit()` calls with the same business key can race. Each runs in its own container-managed transaction, and both pre-checks find no active holder. The first insert commits. The second hits the primary key of `scheduler_business_key_reservation`.

The store mapped that duplicate to a plain `RatchetTransientStoreException`. `submitPrepared` then looked up the winner in the same transaction to decide what to throw. Under JTA, Hibernate had already marked that transaction rollback-only, on MySQL as well as PostgreSQL. The lookup failed with `STATUS_MARKED_ROLLBACK`, and the caller got `RatchetTransientStoreException`. `submit()` documents `DuplicateBusinessKeyException` for this case. Two quick clicks on a "run now" button were enough to hit it. Details are in #337.

## Change

**Stores.** All five stores now throw `BusinessKeyReservationConflictException`, a new subclass of `RatchetTransientStoreException` in store core, for a duplicate on the business-key reservation and nothing else. Deadlocks, connection failures and other unique constraints keep their current mapping.

**Runtime.**

- With the builder's generated idempotency key, the reservation conflict already shows that another active job holds the key. `submit()` throws `DuplicateBusinessKeyException` straight away, with no lookup.
- With a custom idempotency key, the runtime still needs the winner's key. It now reads the winner in a new transaction through the existing `REQUIRES_NEW` helper (`BatchCompletionTransaction`). A matching key throws `DuplicateIdempotencyKeyException`, as before. A different key throws `DuplicateBusinessKeyException`.
- If that read fails or finds no active holder, the original `RatchetTransientStoreException` is rethrown. A retry in a new transaction resolves it.

The builder now records whether the caller set the idempotency key. Spring Boot and Micronaut pass the transaction helper to the job creation service. The `JobBuilder.submit()` and `withBusinessKey` Javadoc describe each outcome.

**TCK.** The active business-key contract now requires `BusinessKeyReservationConflictException` when a second active job takes a key. Before, those three tests accepted any `RuntimeException`. The SQL stores' fixture retried the transient conflict in a new transaction. The retry called `save()` on a job that already had an id, failed with an unrelated `IllegalStateException`, and the tests passed without checking the conflict. The fixture no longer retries a reservation conflict.

## Testing

- `DefaultJobCreationServiceIdempotencyRaceTest`: a race with a generated key throws `DuplicateBusinessKeyException` without a lookup; a blank override keeps an explicit key; a non-reservation transient failure passes through; same-key, different-key, empty-lookup and failed-lookup races run the lookup in the new transaction.
- Each store's `ConstraintDetectorTest`: a reservation duplicate maps to the new exception, and an unrelated write failure does not. MongoDB also covers the command-level conflict.
- `ActiveBusinessKeyContractTest` and `JobCrudStoreContractTest` on MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server and MongoDB.

Run locally: unit tests for `ratchet-api`, store core, the reference implementation and the Spring Boot and Micronaut modules, the store tests above on all five stores, `spotless:check` and `spotbugs:check`.

Not run: a deterministic JTA race in `BusinessKeyIT`. It would need barrier fixtures that hold one transaction open across the other's insert.

Closes #337


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved reporting for simultaneous job submissions using the same business key. Conflicts are distinguished from unrelated store failures across supported databases.
  * With a generated idempotency key, a losing submission reports a duplicate business key. With a custom key, the system checks for the active job in a new transaction: a matching key reports a duplicate idempotency key, while a different key reports a duplicate business key.
  * If the check fails or finds no active job, the original transient store failure is surfaced. Retrying in a fresh transaction can resolve the outcome.

body:
## Summary

Moves the parity default baseline from `p60-deployed-f12` to `p60-deployed-f13`, as after every P60 deploy (user decision 2026-11-10; a follow-up after F13, not a planned stage).

The move needed more than the tag rename. During F13 the before side (F12) read the routes F13 retired (`-RetiredRoutes`) and the after side read the account routes, joined through `figure-map.json`. The F13 build has no retired routes, so a run against it failed with `404 (Not Found) on the before side`. Both builds now serve the same account routes, so both sides run **one collector set**:

- `Get-ParityReport` always builds every family. The `-IncludeSummary`, `-IncludeAccounts`, `-FillMissingStatements` and `-RetiredRoutes` switches are gone (`-CurrentMonth` is now mandatory, since the account families always need it). The retired-route collectors are removed too: `banks`, `cards`, `pots`, `current/pots` and `current/mae`, and the `monthly` sums built from them.
- `figure-map.json` ships with no mappings, so every figure compares with its own key and no mapping can point at a key that no longer exists. The mapping mechanism stays for a future feature that moves a figure.
- The `Invoke-Parity.ps1` command line and parameters are unchanged; only the `BaselineTag` default moved.

> **The tag `p60-deployed-f13` is local only and must be pushed before CI or a reviewer can build the baseline.** The controller pushes it.

## Review guide

1. `scripts/parity/Parity.psm1`: `Get-ParityReport` and `Add-ParityMonthFigures` now take no side switches. The six retired-route functions are deleted, and the missing-statement fill always writes `cardStatement`.
2. `scripts/parity/Invoke-Parity.ps1`: default tag `p60-deployed-f13`; both sides call `Get-ParityReport` the same way.
3. `scripts/parity/figure-map.json`: `"mappings": []`.
4. `scripts/parity/Parity.test.ps1`:
   - Fixtures for the retired routes are removed, so the strict fixture fetch throws if any collector reads one.
   - The retired-reader cases are removed, along with the per-mapping "wrong X" cases, which the new every-figure case covers.
   - New case: every figure of the fixture report is changed in turn, on each side, and each change is reported exactly once under its own key through the shipped figure map.
5. `scripts/parity/README.md`: the baseline tag and the catalogue (no before-only or after-only families, no mapping notes), plus a generic mapping example.

## Deviations

None from the brief. Choices made:
- I removed `-FillMissingStatements` rather than keeping it as an always-on switch.
- I kept the mapping mechanism and emptied the map instead of deleting it.

## Deferred

None.

## PRD Section 9

- Cross-feature "the parity commands run unchanged": still holds. The `Invoke-Parity.ps1` command line and parameters are unchanged; the baseline default moved as every deploy does. No PRD box changes in this PR.

## Validation

- `pwsh scripts/parity/Parity.test.ps1`: **60/60 parity toolkit cases passed**.
  - Mutation check: a mapping that hides `potsTab/total` makes the every-figure case fail. The map was restored afterwards.
- `scripts/parity/Invoke-Parity.ps1 -Step All -LiveCopy "<repo folder>\data\data-cashflow.json"` at 69ead931 against `p60-deployed-f13` (12fdbafe):
  - Result: **`Parity OK: 0 differences in 19,224 figures across 122 months`**.
  - Input file: version 5, SHA-256 `52047E22`, unchanged after the run.
  - The later simplify commit touched only the self-test, the README and two blank lines in `Parity.psm1`.
- Figure count: the 13,551 the F13 runs printed was the *before* (F12) report's count, the figure the summary line reports. The F13 after side already produced 19,224. Now both sides emit those 19,224, and the new before and after reports are byte-identical. The new after report is also byte-identical to the after report of the F13 parity run on the same file the same day.
- The 19,224 figures by family:

  | Family | Figures |
  |---|---:|
  | `summary` | 3,115 |
  | `annual` | 3,080 |
  | `investment` | 2,972 |

## Reviews

- architecture-reviewer: APPROVE, no blocking findings. Low: `$accounts = & $Fetch 'accounts'` relies on `ConvertFrom-ParityJson` returning arrays with the unary comma (every use re-wraps with `@(...)`); left as is. author: casoon
body:
Closes #342

## What was wrong

Two things, the second hidden behind the first:

1. `run_grouped` and `run_tree` passed the state's window offset — already a window start, with the overscan taken off — through `grid::window_offset_for_row` again. The window sat six rows short: `Ctrl`+`End` stopped at position 40 of 58, `ArrowDown` at the edge needed two presses.
2. Both paths settled every result as `QueryKind::Data`, also a window that had only moved. A `Data` result drops the pin of the focused row's slot (`follow_replaced`), so once the window did move with the scrolling, the focus stayed on a slot that now showed the next row: one press, two positions. Before the first fix the window hardly moved by scrolling, so this did not show.

## The change

- `grid::clamp_window_offset(offset, total, pool)`: keeps a window start inside the list without taking a lead off. Used at both sites. Native test beside the other window tests.
- `settled_kind`: a display list's result is settled as `Window` when it was asked for as one **and** the list is as long as it was — a scroll or a key. A group or node that opens or closes changes the length and stays `Data`, as before. This is the ungrouped grid's behaviour (#224).
- `tests/e2e/grid-group-window.spec.js`: `Ctrl`+`End` reaches the last position; `ArrowDown` moves one position per press over 30 presses.
- `tests/e2e/grid-group-select.spec.js`: the workaround from #322 (scroll past the row, `focus({ preventScroll })`) is gone.

## Checked

- `just check`: green.
- `just e2e` locally: 1741 passed, 6 failed — all six are screenshot comparisons (`phase-f-baselines` "state grouped", `prototype` base and dark, in both projects). They fail the same way **without** this change (checked by building `main`'s Rust sources and running the two specs), so the macOS baselines are stale on `main`; not touched here.

author: yukimatsuzawa
body:
## Summary

NCDK bundles `x64/libinchi.dll`. The current copy is InChI 1.05, which is under the IUPAC/InChI-Trust Licence 1.0 (LGPL-2.1 style). Section 4 of that licence requires shipping the complete source with the binary. InChI 1.07 and later are under the MIT License, so this PR replaces the DLL with InChI 1.07.5 and removes that obligation.

- The new DLL is the signed x64 Windows build `inchi-windows-<sha>-signed/libinchi.dll` from `release_artifacts.zip` in the [v1.07.5 release](https://github.com/IUPAC-InChI/InChI/releases/tag/v1.07.5).
  - It is Authenticode-signed by SignPath Foundation and imports only KERNEL32.dll.
  - SHA-256: `5d6d27b94c0caf558b16154542b93547f3c34fb849ec50776c318eb4c9f31721`
  - Its VERSIONINFO still says 1.0.7.4, but the version string embedded in the binary is 1.07.5.
- The DLL name stays `libinchi.dll`, so the P/Invoke code is unchanged. Only the unused `NInchiWrapper.Version` constant is updated.

## Compatibility

- Every function NCDK calls is still exported. These are `GetINCHI`, `GetStdINCHI`, `FreeINCHI`, `FreeStdINCHI`, `GetINCHIfromINCHI`, `GetStructFromINCHI`, `FreeStructFromINCHI`, `GetINCHIKeyFromINCHI`, `CheckINCHI`, `CheckINCHIKey`, `Get_inchi_Input_FromAuxInfo` and `Free_inchi_Input`.
- Between the v1.05 and v1.07.5 `inchi_api.h`, the structs, function prototypes and enum values differ only in whitespace and comments.

## Testing

- I compared 1.05 and 1.07.5 with a throwaway console app on net48 and net8.0.
  - It covered 45 molecules, including stereo, charged, salts, isotopes, tautomers, metals, lipids, paclitaxel and ATP.
  - Each molecule ran with 4 option sets: none, FixedH, RecMet, and FixedH+RecMet+SUU.
  - The InChI, InChIKey, AuxInfo, the InChI-to-structure round trip, CheckINCHI and CheckINCHIKey were identical between the two versions.
  - The only difference: a malformed InChI (`InChI=1S/garbage`) now returns status `Error` instead of `EOF`. The only caller, `MassBankRecordHandler`, rejects every status other than Ok and Warning, so its behaviour does not change.
- `CommonStandardTests`: 1344/1344 pass. This includes `SmilesInchikeyGeneratorTest` and the MassBank record tests.

## Notes

- `src/Common/NCDK/x64/` is matched by `.gitignore`, so the DLL had to be added with `git add -f`.
- The third-party license entry for InChI is handled in a separate change.

author: org-tekeli-borisp
body:
Closes: macaroni-os/mark-issues#867

Three autogen packages for ai-kit (ai-kit is autogen-native: atoms in `ai-kit/merge.kit.d/base.yml`, specs in `ai-kit/autogen.kit.d/base.yml`):

- **`app-ai/codex`** (source) + **`app-ai/codex-bin`** (upstream binary) — same upstream repository (`openai/codex`), so per the macaroni-os/kit-fixups#512 convention they live in a dedicated `codex` cluster whose `defaults` pin the shared `github` block; the `-bin` postfix follows the `pi-bin` precedent and the pair never coexists (the `!`-blocker idiom of opencode/pi, swap behaviour verified both orders below).
- **`app-ai/claude-code-bin`** — `builtin-github` + `simple.tmpl` + the `claude-linux-x64/arm64` glibc single-file native assets; the `*-musl` variants are skipped (mark is glibc), as are darwin/windows assets and the SHASUMS signing files. There is no public source for the CLI itself — the GitHub repository is the product's issue-tracker/docs/ecosystem face (full recursive tree: 1983 entries, dominated by `mods/` customization modules that run *inside* the installed CLI against its public API — declared only as `.d.ts` types; plus `examples/`, `plugins/`, changelog; no `package.json` and no CLI implementation anywhere) — so this is a bin-only package (`discord-bin` is the tree precedent). `license: Anthropic PBC` per review (macaroni-os/mark-issues#867 thread on this PR): the repository's LICENSE.md is "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service", which GitHub's license detector does not classify (API probe: 404), so the value cannot be auto-filled.

## codex source flavour

The CLI is pure Rust from the `codex-rs/` workspace. Recipe: the cluster's `simple-github.tmpl` recovers the `api.github.com` tarball of the release tag (unpack root `openai-codex-<sha7>` → generated `post_src_unpack` rename), then `cargo build --release -p codex-cli --bin codex` in `codex-rs/` with `CARGO_HOME=${T}`, `newbin` + `dodoc`.

- **Toolchain floor `>=virtual/rust-1.96`**: upstream pins rust 1.95.0 (`codex-rs/rust-toolchain.toml`); the let-chain match guards in `codex-core` are `E0658` on 1.94 (reproduced: `core/src/tools/handlers/mod.rs:191`) and compile on the tree's 1.96.1; lang-kit ships rust-bin 1.94/1.96/1.98 (no 1.95), hence the floor.
- **`restrict: network-sandbox`** — see the bundle thread below for why the offline `rust`-extension bundle is not currently possible; the workspace `Cargo.lock` also pins 13 git dependencies (forks of crossterm, tungstenite, sqlx, rmcp, h3, nucleo, runfiles, mxc-sdk, rusty_v8), so build-time network is required. This is the same shape the kit already accepts for the `opencode` and `pi` source flavours.
- **Not `npm`**: the `@openai/codex` npm package's `bin/codex.js` is a *launcher* that resolves `PLATFORM_PACKAGE_BY_TARGET` and `spawn`s a prebuilt Rust binary from the `@openai/codex-<platform>` packages — it does not compile Rust. A buildable-from-source package therefore has to drive the `cargo` workspace directly (which this source flavour does), not `npm`.

## Bundle / `cargo`-extension investigation (macaroni-os/kit-fixups#561 review)

Tested the `rust` extension + `cargo` eclass path end-to-end (full `mark-devkit autogen`, which runs extensions). It aborts for codex before bundling:

```
🧠 [codex] Elaborating extension rust...
💣 🔥 [codex] Cargo.lock file not found🔥
```

Cause (verified against mark-devkit `retrieveCargoLock` + the unpacked tree): the extension scans exactly one directory level below the unpack root for `Cargo.lock`. The recovered tarball's root is `openai-codex-<sha>/` and codex nests its workspace, so the lock is at `openai-codex-<sha>/codex-rs/Cargo.lock` — one level deeper than the scan reaches. Independently, even with the lock found, the extension clones every git dependency recursively with submodules, and the `rusty_v8` fork's submodules are the multi-GB chromium tree, while `--bin codex` never compiles v8 (the v8 puller `codex-code-mode-runtime` belongs to the `codex-code-mode-host` sidecar; confirmed: no `Compiling v8`, no `librusty_v8` artifact in a full `--bin codex` build). So the vendored bundle is not viable for codex as mark-devkit stands, which makes `network-sandbox` the fallback the review thread calls for. A follow-up that would enable the bundle path: a cargo-lock subdirectory option in the extension plus a git-dep/submodule skip; the mark-rust-bundle for `thin-provisioning-tools` is the model for the eclass wiring.

## `github.ignore_tags` is load-bearing for both codex flavours

Release titles are plain semver (`0.167.0`) while the tags carry a `rust-` prefix (`rust-v0.167.0`) across thousands of tags, so the tag-listing cross-check never matches a release. Discriminating probe (flag removed):

```
💣 🔥 [codex] [codex] No versions found🔥
```

With `ignore_tags: true` selection succeeds and the sha falls back to the release `target_commitish` (mark-devkit `SetVersion`), same remedy as `opencode-bin`; ~1270 alphas are filtered natively as prereleases.

## Verification (mark-unstable container, mark-devkit 0.36.1 `autogen-thin`)

```
🍕 [codex] For package app-ai/codex selected version 0.167.0
🍕 [codex-bin] For package app-ai/codex-bin selected version 0.167.0
🍕 [claude-code-bin] For package app-ai/claude-code-bin selected version 2.1.322
```

All three generated ebuilds: `bash -n` OK, no template residue. Flavour swap (`!`-blockers), plan + real runs both orders (emerging one removes the other):

```
# emerge -1p =app-ai/codex-0.167.0  (with codex-bin installed)
[ebuild  N     ] app-ai/codex-0.167.0
[uninstall     ] app-ai/codex-bin-0.167.0
[blocks b      ] app-ai/codex ("app-ai/codex" is blocking app-ai/codex-bin-0.167.0)
[blocks b      ] app-ai/codex-bin ("app-ai/codex-bin" is blocking app-ai/codex-0.167.0)

# bin over source:
>>> Installing (1 of 1) app-ai/codex-bin-0.167.0::ai-kit
>>> Uninstalling app-ai/codex-0.167.0::ai-kit
# source over bin:
>>> Installing (1 of 1) app-ai/codex-0.167.0::ai-kit
>>> Uninstalling app-ai/codex-bin-0.167.0::ai-kit
```

Source `codex` full emerge (digest-verified Manifest; glibc dynamic ELF, not the -bin musl static):

```
>>> Installing (1 of 1) app-ai/codex-0.167.0::ai-kit
# codex --version
codex-cli 0.167.0
# file /usr/bin/codex
ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, dynamically linked, interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, stripped   # 1.5 GB -> 311 MB via toolchain strip
# ldd /usr/bin/codex | grep -E "ssl|crypto|libz"
	libssl.so.3  libcrypto.so.3  libz.so.1
```

Byte-identity oracle (`cmp` generated ebuild vs installed `/var/db/pkg` copy) — all three:

```
CODEX-SRC-CMP-IDENTICAL
CODEX-BIN-CMP-IDENTICAL
CLAUDE-BIN-CMP-IDENTICAL
```

Bin-flavour smokes (static-pie musl runs unchanged on the glibc sandbox): `codex-cli 0.167.0`, `2.1.322 (Claude Code)`.

One disclosure: a single sandboxed source build aborted mid-compile with the intermittent glibc futex abort (`The futex facility returned an unexpected error code`, exit 134) while other sandbox work ran concurrently; the identical ebuild built clean standalone-to-completion and threaded futex passes under `sandbox`/pid-ns — the sandbox2-race symptom, not an ebuild defect. Noted so a merge-phase retry (if any) is not misread.

## Release-branch propagation

- **mark-xl**: `lang-kit@mark-xl` ships rust-bin 1.96.1 + virtual/rust 1.96.1, so the source flavour builds — merge list gains `codex`, `codex-bin`, `claude-code-bin`.
- **mark-iii**: `lang-kit@mark-iii` tops out at rust-bin 1.94 (`E0658` on the source flavour) — merge list gains `codex-bin` + `claude-code-bin` only; the source atom can follow a toolchain bump.
- **mark-31** carries no ai-kit merge recipe at all — nothing to extend; kit bootstrap there is a maintainer decision.

author: samarmstrong
body:
Closes #4200

Deploys the read-only case shell (#4199) on Helm. As in the groom notes, the backend can connect to it and it can connect to nothing.

- **`agent-shell` Deployment + Service** (`templates/agent-shell-{deployment,service}.yaml`). Runs the agent image's `node dist/shell.js` (the image comes from `agentWorker.image`). `SHELL_SOCKET` is left unset, so it listens on TCP 6992 behind a ClusterIP Service.
  - It runs as uid 0 with only SETUID, SETGID and KILL. The root filesystem is read-only, `allowPrivilegeEscalation` is false and seccomp is RuntimeDefault.
  - It has no `envFrom`, no secrets and no service account token. `shareProcessNamespace` stands in for compose's `init: true`.
  - The probes are exec probes running the compose healthcheck's `node -e` against `127.0.0.1:6992/healthz`, so the kubelet never connects to the port.
- **/work** is a 512Mi in-memory emptyDir. An initContainer with only CHOWN and FOWNER sets it to `root:60999` mode `1731`, matching the compose tmpfs. `/dev/shm` is covered by a read-only emptyDir, which matches compose's `ipc: none`. This one goes beyond the groom notes; it is a single mount.
- **NetworkPolicy** (`templates/agent-shell-networkpolicy.yaml`) renders whenever the shell does, whether or not `networkPolicies.enabled` is set. It lets in backend pods on TCP 6992 and has `egress: []`. The chart's `-deny-all` policy now leaves the shell out with `matchExpressions: component NotIn [agent-shell]`. Policies add up, so without that its `egress: - {}` would give the shell full egress. The template comment explains both points.
- **Backend** gets `SHELL_URL=http://<fullname>-agent-shell:6992` when the shell is enabled, which turns on `read_case_shell`.
- **Values**: `agentShell.enabled` (default true), `replicas`, `resources` (1Gi memory limit, as in compose). README has a new section.

**Separate commit: a fix to main's broken schema chain.** #4208 pointed `0045_detection_proposals` at `0045_run_sign_in`. #4207 then renamed that revision to `0046_run_sign_in` and placed it after detection proposals. On main, the chain now names a revision that doesn't exist: a fresh install's upgrade Job fails with `KeyError: '0045_run_sign_in'` and the backend never starts. This commit points the revision back at `0044_sign_in_end_reasons`. `0046`'s SQL is all `IF NOT EXISTS`, so a database that already ran it is unaffected.

## Verification

**Ran**
- `helm lint` passes. `helm template` with `networkPolicies.enabled` off and on: the shell's policy renders in both cases. A script over the rendered policies showed that, with policies on, `v-vigil-agent-shell` is the only policy selecting the shell pod and that `-deny-all` carries the `NotIn` exclusion. With `agentShell.enabled=false`, nothing about agent-shell or `SHELL_URL` renders.
- On kind with Calico v3.30.3 (which enforces NetworkPolicy), with backend and agent images built from this branch, I installed the chart (backend, Postgres, Redis, Bifrost, agent-shell). I ran every check below once with `networkPolicies.enabled=false` and again after `helm upgrade` to `true`, and got the same results both times:
  - Inside the backend pod I called `_read_case_shell` on a real case I had created there (a finding plus a case). `ls; jq . case.json | head` exit 0 listed the view and printed case.json. `sed -i` on case.json was refused. Writing to `scratch/` worked.
  - From the shell pod (node `net.connect`, 4s timeout), connections to 1.1.1.1:443, the backend Service IP:6987, the backend pod IP:6987 and kube-dns:53 all timed out, and a DNS lookup gave `EAI_AGAIN`. Control: the backend pod connects to 1.1.1.1:443 in both modes.
  - The backend pod connected to `v-vigil-agent-shell:6992`. The redis pod and a throwaway busybox pod carrying the release labels could not.
  - `stat /work` gives `root:60999 1731`. Inside a call, the runner (uid 61003) gets `Permission denied` on `ls /work`. Writing to `/dev/shm` fails as a read-only filesystem.
  - Running an outbound `https.get` through `read_case_shell` hung until the shell's 30s limit killed it. That is what dropped packets look like.

**Did not run**
- The helm test hook and Medic with the shell present: neither touches the shell or its policy.
- A live LLM hunt calling the tool: I called the tool function directly in the backend pod. The issue only asks that the backend call succeed.

**Blocked by the machine**
- No kind cluster or Calico was running, so I created both by hand (`kind create cluster` with `disableDefaultCNI`, then the Calico manifest, as `medic-tests/kind/e2e.sh` does).
- The chart's subchart dependencies aren't vendored. `helm template` needed `helm dependency build`, and the kind install used a copy of the chart with `dependencies:` stripped, as e2e.sh does.
- This isn't the machine's fault, but main's schema chain was broken (see the separate commit). The backend would not start until I fixed it.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"thesandx"} -->
_Requested by **Sandeep** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_013WMdPcNy9BCfu6oqa8nHdT?thread=cmsg_013WMdPcNy9BCfu6oqa8nHdTPREiTpcf8dKWCFaKLef9XG)_

## What changed

A cute mascot, **Pip**, floats at the bottom right of every signed-in page. Tap it to ask a doubt. Pip knows which lesson, problem, lab or GCP station you are on and explains it, using the model you pick from a dropdown (OpenRouter).

## Why

Sandeep asked for a friendly AI assistant on any section, powered by his OpenRouter key, with a model dropdown and a little mascot.

## How

- `POST /api/assistant` (session required) → `services/openrouter.service.ts`, which streams the answer back as plain text. The browser never talks to OpenRouter and never sees the key.
- The browser sends only the page **path**. `lib/assistant/context.ts` reads the page text from the catalogue (lesson body and checks, problem prompt/hints/answer, lab steps, station concepts, loop guide) and puts it in the system prompt. On a problem, Pip gives hints before the full answer unless asked.
- Text the learner selects on the page just before opening Pip is sent as "About: …".
- Model dropdown: allowlist in `lib/assistant/models.ts` (Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Terra, Gemini 3.8 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash, Grok 4.7; ids checked against OpenRouter's model list today). Default Claude Haiku 5.5. The choice is remembered in localStorage; the chat per page in sessionStorage.
- Spend guards: server refuses any model outside the list, 1,200-token answer cap, 30 questions per learner per 10 min per instance, Stop button aborts the upstream call.
- Answers render with `Prose` after converting standard Markdown to the course dialect. Works in light and dark mode, phone sheet / desktop card.
- Rejected: browser-side calls (leaks key), a vendor SDK (new dependency, one vendor), storing chats in Firestore (not needed yet). See ADR-0009.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm validate` passes locally (typecheck, lint, format, tests)
- [x] New code follows the folder conventions in `.github/instructions/project-structure.md`
- [x] Client Components are justified — only `DoubtAssistant` (state, effects, streaming)
- [x] No new dependency
- [x] New environment variables are added to **both** `.env.example` and `lib/env.ts`
- [x] Documentation updated (ADR-0009, `cloud/environment-variables.md`, CLAUDE.md)
- [x] No secrets, keys or credentials in the diff

## Deployment notes

Until these run, Pip shows "not set up yet" and nothing else changes:

```bash
printf '%s' 'sk-or-v1-...' | gcloud secrets create openrouter-api-key --data-file=- --project "$PROJECT_ID"
gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding openrouter-api-key --project "$PROJECT_ID" \
  --member="serviceAccount:<slug>-runtime@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role=roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor
gh variable set OPENROUTER_SECRET --body openrouter-api-key
```

`deploy.yml` then adds `--set-secrets=OPENROUTER_API_KEY=openrouter-api-key:latest`. Set a credit limit on the key in OpenRouter as the hard cap.

**What changed**
- `d.screenshot(label, folder="screenshots", keep=200)`: saves into `logs/<folder>` and keeps the newest `keep` there, e.g. `d.screenshot("raid", folder="rewards", keep=300)`. The default is unchanged: logs/screenshots, the newest 200 (`log.SHOTS`, `log.KEEP_SHOTS`).

A bot's own screenshots (one after each run, say) saved into logs/screenshots push out the failure shots the Overview links to; a folder of their own with its own limit keeps them apart.

author: giovannymaya
body:
## What changed

**Animated skies.** The whole background now reflects the current weather: falling rain (with a lighter drizzle variant), thunderstorms with lightning flashes, drifting snow, rolling fog, drifting clouds, a glowing sun by day and a moon with twinkling stars at night. All CSS, no images. Animations freeze when the device has "reduce motion" turned on.

**5-day forecast.** One row per day with a condition icon, chance of precipitation (shown when ≥20%), and the high/low drawn on a shared temperature scale so you can see warmer and cooler days at a glance.

**New UI.** °F/°C toggle, "Use my location", city local time, feels-like, humidity, wind (km/h for metric), sunrise and sunset in the city's time zone. Last city and units are remembered in the browser. Responsive down to phone widths.

**Function and security.**
- Fetches current weather and the forecast in parallel and returns one trimmed payload
- Validates and URL-encodes input (the city was previously concatenated straight into the API URL); supports lat/lon
- Friendly 400/404/502 messages; 10-minute cache header
- Uses Node's built-in `fetch`, so `node-fetch` and the committed `node_modules/` are gone
- `netlify.toml` with CSP and security headers (same approach as the Trivia Game), `SECURITY.md`, `.gitignore`
- All API text rendered with `textContent` (no more `innerHTML` with API data)

**Bugs fixed.** Icons loaded over `http://` (blocked as mixed content on HTTPS), broken favicon `type` attribute, unused `window.API_KEY`, errors only logged to the console.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 4 unit tests for the function (daily grouping, input validation, key not leaked, error mapping)
- Rendered every scene in headless Chrome at desktop and phone widths against a mocked OpenWeather API; checked no horizontal overflow, unit toggle, persistence across reload, and reduced-motion behaviour

## Before merging
`API_KEY` must still be set in Netlify's environment variables (unchanged). Netlify picks up `netlify.toml` automatically.

author: tshibandachris
body:
## Objectif

Porter le principe d'isolation de l'ancienne PR #68 sur le contrat réel et idempotent de la PR #70, sans réutiliser sa migration 036 incompatible.

## Changements

- Migration additive `036_device_enrollment_executor_role.sql`, avec signature exacte de `register_device_enrollment_with_credential(text, uuid, varchar, varchar, jsonb, text, varchar, uuid)`.
- Rôle-capacité `device_enrollment_executor` NOLOGIN, sans privilèges élevés, sans BYPASSRLS et sans appartenance à un autre rôle.
- Propriétaire `device_enrollment_function_owner` séparé, NOLOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, NOINHERIT et sans propriété des tables tenant-scoped. Les fonctions SECURITY DEFINER n'appartiennent plus au superutilisateur PostgreSQL.
- Révocation du droit EXECUTE à PUBLIC et `sync_app`, attribution au seul rôle-capacité. Retrait à `sync_app` des privilèges historiques d'insertion de devices, d'accès aux codes d'activation et d'appel direct des helpers SECURITY DEFINER.
- Vérification de la chaîne SECURITY DEFINER : la fonction atomique et ses deux helpers partagent le même propriétaire, lequel n'est ni `sync_app`, ni le rôle executor, ni le login applicatif.
- Pool Drizzle distinct `DEVICE_ENROLLMENT_DATABASE_URL`; `DeviceEnrollmentService` n'utilise plus `DRIZZLE_DB`.
- Guard fail-closed au démarrage : identité de session, privilèges du login, héritage effectif du seul rôle executor, absence d'appartenance à `sync_app`, absence de propriété d'objets PostgreSQL et EXECUTE sur la signature exacte.
- Provisionnement du login dédié dans `scripts/migrate.sh` et `docker-compose.prod.yml`, avec secrets séparés. Le login n'obtient aucun droit direct sur tables, séquences ou fonctions.
- Migration ledger `schema_migrations` : application des seules migrations non enregistrées, reprise après échec et baseline legacy 001–030 uniquement après vérification de l'empreinte pré-031. Refus explicite si le schéma historique ne correspond pas.
- Compose local attend désormais la fin du job de migration avant de démarrer l'API.
- Tests Testcontainers avec connexions distinctes `sync_app` et login executor, tests d'accès direct, rejet de BYPASSRLS, vérification du propriétaire SECURITY DEFINER non-superuser et exécution de la migration 036 avec les rôles pré-provisionnés et un rôle de migration sans CREATEROLE.

## Tests de sécurité ciblés

- `sync_app` ne peut plus insérer aucun device, lire/consommer les codes d'activation, appeler les helpers ou exécuter la fonction atomique (SQLSTATE 42501). Le trigger pending-only reste une défense en profondeur si un INSERT lui était temporairement accordé.
- Le login dédié peut exécuter la fonction, sans appartenir à `sync_app`.
- Le login dédié ne peut lire/écrire directement les tables devices, credentials, événements et codes d'activation, ni appeler directement les helpers.
- Le guard refuse `sync_app`, un login BYPASSRLS, un login avec memberships supplémentaires ou propriétaire d'objets ; il vérifie aussi l'identité et les attributs non privilégiés du propriétaire SECURITY DEFINER, son absence de memberships vers `sync_app`/l'exécuteur et l'absence de propriété des tables tenant-scoped.
- La migration 036 est rejouée avec un rôle pré-provisionné sans CREATEROLE.

## Invariants

- PR #70 reste la base fonctionnelle de l'enrôlement initial ES256.
- Aucune approbation automatique : le terminal reste pending.
- Atomicité, nonce initial et reçu idempotent de la migration 035 conservés.
- Aucun changement à l'Outbox, au client Electron, ni aux routes de synchronisation.
- PR #70, PR #73, `main`, #62 et #63 ne sont pas modifiées ni fusionnées.

## Déploiement

Configurer `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `SYNC_APP_PASSWORD` et `DEVICE_ENROLLMENT_PASSWORD`. Les deux URLs doivent utiliser les identifiants correspondants. Voir `docs/device-enrollment-db-isolation.md`.

**Cette PR reste en Draft.** Le code et les tests ciblés sont préparés, mais aucune exécution CI/Testcontainers sur le head final n'est encore attestée par les contrôles GitHub disponibles. Ne pas fusionner avant les checks verts sur le SHA final.

author: harunnryd
body:
## What changed

- D2c: one Kubernetes Job per session. The session worker gains a single-session mode (`sessions --meeting <id>` claims exactly that row, runs one attempt, exits); a new `launcher` worker role reconciles claimable rows into Jobs
- Repository: `claim(..., meeting_id=...)` filters the existing conditional claim to one meeting; `claimable()` lists joined/stopped non-terminal rows whose lease is free or expired (database clock)
- `worker/launcher.py`: `build_job` renders the Job as a dict (`backoffLimit: 0` — retry stays with the A2 lease, per-attempt Job names, `activeDeadlineSeconds` from the snapshot lobby+duration plus margin, `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`, meeting label, envFrom secret/configmap, resources from settings); `SessionLauncher.reconcile` creates Jobs for waiting sessions without an active Job and closes stopped-before-join sessions directly through claim + StatusWriter; `KubernetesSessionJobs` wraps the official client (in-cluster config with kubeconfig fallback, 409 on create treated as already launched)
- New `sessions` settings section (launcher mode, namespace, image, env sources, poll, TTL, deadline margin, cpu/memory; 12 new env leaves, total 207); default mode `worker` keeps today's behavior
- `deploy/k8s/`: namespace, launcher ServiceAccount + Role (jobs create/list/get only), launcher Deployment
- Minimal local stubs for the untyped `kubernetes` client under `typings/`; note `kubernetes` pins urllib3 to 2.3 in the lockfile
- Plan status: D2c marked code-complete, cluster proof pending; D2d trace remains

## Why

Plan D2 wants a pod per session so browser + PulseAudio are isolated per meeting and two meetings never share audio state. D2a/D2b removed the shared-filesystem coupling; this slice adds the control plane that turns a wanted session row into exactly one pod, with takeover still owned by the A2 lease (dead pod → lease expiry → new Job → segment restore).

## Evidence

- Real Postgres: a meeting-scoped claim takes only that meeting and fences it; `claimable()` reflects the lease state
- Launcher unit tests with a fake job client: job shape (name per attempt, no retries, deadline arithmetic, envFrom), reconcile launches a waiting session, skips one with an active Job, and closes a stopped-before-join session as ended/stopped_by_owner without launching
- Consumer test: `run_once(meeting_id=...)` claims only that meeting
- Offline schema check: the built Job dict deserializes through the official client's `V1Job` model; manifests parse as YAML
- Not yet run on a cluster: no kind cluster is up locally, so the two-pods-concurrently and kill-a-pod gates are still open
- Full suite: 11107 passed; one unrelated timing flake in `test_actor_early_commit` under parallel load (file passes alone, untouched by this diff)

## Gates

- [x] `uv run --no-sync ruff check .`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync ruff format --check .`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync mypy`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync lint-imports`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync deptry .`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync pytest` — 11107 passed, 113 skipped (1 unrelated flake, see Evidence); evals (not live) 195 passed
- [ ] Live evals, when a model, prompt or provider changed: not applicable, none changed

## Live verification

- [ ] Not needed: the change is offline only
- [ ] Done in a real Meet:
- [x] Still needed: kind/cluster smoke (launcher creates a Job that claims and runs a session), two concurrent meetings in two pods, and takeover after killing a pod (folded into the pending live validation pass)

## Configuration

- [ ] No `FAKEYOU_*` key added, renamed or removed
- [x] Changed keys are in `.env.example` and `tests/fixtures/env_migration_d9.json`
- [ ] Operators must update `.env`: optional — set `FAKEYOU_SESSIONS__LAUNCHER=kubernetes` plus image/namespace/env sources to enable Job-per-session

## House rules

author: romain-filigran
body:
### Proposed changes

* New internal enrichment connector `internal-enrichment/report-article-fetcher` (scope `Report`, playbook compatible, `CONNECTOR_AUTO=false` by default), built from the internal-enrichment template with Pydantic settings.
* Finds the article link from the external reference written by the RSS ingestion. With `REPORT_ARTICLE_FETCHER_MATCH_SINGLE_REFERENCE`, it also uses the single external reference of any report.
* Fetches over plain HTTP, public addresses only. It checks every address the host resolves to at each redirect, then the address the socket actually connected to, which defeats DNS rebinding. HTML only, 5 MB and 20 s limits.
* Extracts the article body with trafilatura and keeps tables, lists, code and links. Three layouts that would lose indicators are reworked first: tables in wrapper `<div>`s, tables in `embed` blocks, and indicators listed one per `<div>`.
* Writes the body to the report's content only when it is the article (not an anti-bot or consent page, at least 500 characters, matching the report name) and, if the content is already filled, at least 1.5 times longer.

### Related issues

* Closes #8343

### Checklist

- [x] I consider the submitted work as finished
- [x] I have signed my commits using GPG key.
- [x] I tested the code for its functionality using different use cases
- [x] I added/update the relevant documentation (either on github or on notion)
- [x] Where necessary I refactored code to improve the overall quality

### Further comments

Run locally: isort 7.0.0, black 26.10.1, flake8, the STIX ID pylint (10/10), `run_test.sh` (27 tests), deptry and `docker build` all pass.

connector-linter scores 38/40. Its two remaining failures do not apply to this connector:

- **VC301/VC302 (author):** the connector creates no entity. It sends the report back with its content filled, and a `created_by_ref` of its own would replace the report's author.
- **VC311 (TLP marking):** same reason. The report keeps its markings, and the max TLP is checked before any fetch.

`cleanup_inconsistent_bundle=True` (VC312) is deliberately not set. The report goes back as received, and the cleanup would strip its object, author and marking references whose objects are not in the bundle.

`manager_supported` is left `false`, as the template ships it: maintainers own it. As a result, `connector_config_schema.json` and `CONNECTOR_CONFIG_DOC.md` are not generated, and the README lists the settings.

Evaluation: the 3 latest items of the 69 RSS feeds of the XTM Hub catalog and 14 other feeds. On 162 pages fetched by both this connector and Import External Reference, both retrieved the same pages. The whole-page Markdown of Import External Reference held a median 45% of non-article text, and as many indicators were kept.

author: rans0r
body:
An act run now pauses when a window it reports reaches `pause_at`
(0.95) or is refused. It pauses at the next turn end — when every tool
call the model made has its answer — where the adapter sends the CLI
SIGINT. Claude Code ends the run there without cutting into a tool
and keeps the session (`error_during_execution`, `aborted_streaming`),
which was checked against 2.1.319 before anything was built on it. A
run the backend refuses partway pauses the same way; a question is not
paused, being one answer; `on_limit = "stop"` ends the run instead.

The pause is kept on the host, at <home>/paused/<run>.json, since the
harness keeps the session on that host's disk. `onirium run` at a
terminal waits for the reset and carries on a minute after it;
otherwise, or with `--no-wait`, it exits 75 and `onirium resume`
carries it on later, `--now` regardless of the reset. A resumed run
continues the same session with `--resume`, under the same run id, and
the journal says `paused` and `resumed`. `onirium limits` lists the
runs paused on this host.

The adapter's reading of a run now stops at the `result`, which Claude
Code sends last, and waits at most five seconds for stderr after the
program exits: a stand-in that left a process behind holding stderr
showed a run could otherwise hang until that process ended.

Run end to end against Claude Code 2.1.319 on Haiku, with `pause_at`
set to 1% so the first reading would trip it: the run wrote one of
three files, paused at the turn's end and exited 75; `onirium resume
--now` carried it on in the same session, which wrote the other two
without repeating the first; the run's journal reads started, used,
paused, resumed, used, used, ended.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5 gains "As built in Phase 3", and record 0003
says what was built and what waits on a second backend or the
scheduler. One correction to an earlier commit's wording: an account's
record keeps no email and no organization id, but its label does name
the organization, as the user would know the account.
Phase 3, PR 3 of 3, stacked on the PR before it. No new dependencies.

body:
Part of making checkout feel more like a big online shop, before the switch to PayPal Business.

**Emails to buyers** (checkout server, via the existing Resend key)
- PayPal.me order placed: how to pay, the exact amount and link, and the order number to put in the note
- Paid: order confirmed (PayPal checkout, auction wins, or when Sruthi marks a PayPal.me order paid in the studio)
- Shipped: with the tracking number (Canada Post numbers become a tracking link); a separate email if tracking is added after shipping
- Cancelled: unpaid after 48 hours
- Each email goes out once per order. Replies go to the Email in Studio → Settings. Pickups get no shipping email. The studio toast says "customer emailed".

**Returning buyers**
- Name, contact and address are saved in the buyer's browser after an order (never the note), with a "Welcome back… Not you? Clear them" banner and a "Remember my details" tick box
- Auction winners with the same email get their saved address filled in

body:
## What does this PR do?

Thanks for merging the 5.1.8 bump (#151524). This moves the `web-search-plus` catalog pin to the 5.1.9 release, a bug-fix release on top of 5.1.8.

5.1.9 makes settings mean what they say. `hermes web-search-plus config set-auto-allow <provider> on` alone now adds a provider to automatic search (it only wrote the flag, so providers that are explicit-only by default stayed out). `status` names template placeholder keys instead of reporting them as missing, and says when no provider can run automatically. The self-hosted profile picks up a SearXNG URL set with `hermes config set`, `auto_routing.enabled: 0` turns routing off, and a damaged config.json or cache file no longer breaks every call. Internally the plugin was restructured into fewer, deeper modules with no output change. Tool names, parameters, hooks and config keys are unchanged.

author: bjornrobertsson
body:
## Summary

`autostop/` is a tool for one template. It **reports, notifies and optionally stops** workspaces on that template. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob (default namespace `coder`) or from the command line.

### The problem it addresses

When a template's autostop requirement ("Stop on <day>, every N weeks") is saved, Coder recalculates `max_deadline` for every running build. The calculation starts from when each build *finished*, not from now. For builds older than the last required stop day, the result is in the past, so Coder sets it to **now + 2h** (`enterprise/coderd/schedule/template.go`). Those workspaces stop about 2 hours after the save, off-schedule, outside quiet hours, and **without notifying their owners**.

### What the tool does

| Capability | Details |
|---|---|
| **Detect** | Flags `imminent_stop` (stop due within a window), `off_schedule` (the now+2h clamp, or a non-required weekday), `idle`, and `over_interval` |
| **Notify** | Emails each workspace owner and sends one summary to the template owner. Emails are de-duplicated for CronJob runs. `notify.redirect_to` sends all mail to one mailbox for a staged rollout |
| **Stop** | `action: stop` stops idle workspaces, or, in interval-only mode, workspaces that have run longer than `max_running_hours` |
| **Interval-only mode** | `ignore_required_stop_day` + `max_running_hours`: ignore the template's required stop day and use only "a workspace may run N hours" |
| **Safe defaults** | `dry_run: true`, `action: report_only`, STARTTLS certificate checking on |

### Recommended rollout

1. **Observe:** `action: report_only`, `dry_run: true`, and read the job logs.
2. **Notify (staged):** `action: report_idle`, `dry_run: false`, `notify.redirect_to: <platform-team mailbox>`.
3. **Notify owners:** remove `redirect_to`.
4. **Enforce (optional):** set the template's required stop days to none (`coder templates edit <tpl> --autostop-requirement-weekdays none`, which also avoids the now+2h clamp). Then use `ignore_required_stop_day: true`, `max_running_hours: <N>`, `action: stop`.

The token should belong to a **service account with Organization Admin** in the template's organization (verified sufficient; no site Owner needed).

### Deployment

```bash
kubectl -n coder create secret generic autostop-secrets --from-literal=CODER_URL=... --from-literal=CODER_TOKEN=...
./autostop/deploy.sh -n coder --config-file my-config.yaml                               # ConfigMap mode
./autostop/deploy.sh -n coder --mode git --git-ref <ref> --config-file my-config.yaml   # git-pull mode
./autostop/deploy.sh -n coder --config-file my-config.yaml --run-now                    # one-off run
```

## Files

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `autostop/autostop_manager.py` | The script (single file, so it can be shipped as a ConfigMap) |
| `autostop/config.example.yaml` | Every setting, with comments |
| `autostop/deploy.sh` | Creates the ConfigMaps and the CronJob in a namespace (ConfigMap or git mode) |
| `autostop/k8s/cronjob.yaml`, `cronjob-git.yaml`, `secret.example.yaml` | Manifests: non-root, read-only root filesystem, `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` |
| `autostop/README.md` | Usage, settings, deployment |
| `autostop/docs/stop-evidence-2026-11-10.md` | Evidence from Coder's records that the script stops workspaces |
| `autostop/tests/` | 31 unit tests |
| `autostop/TODO.md` | **Removed**: planning document that was merged earlier in #1 |

## Validation (Coder v2.38.5)

- **Unit tests:** 31 passing. `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` passes for both deploy modes.
- **Clamp reproduced live:** saving a template at 15:22:33.64 set the running builds' `deadline` and `max_deadline` to 17:22:33.94. The tool flagged them `off_schedule`.
- **Stop proven from Coder's records:**
  - The in-cluster Job, using a dedicated service account, created a stop build with `initiator=autostop-bot reason=initiator` during its run.
  - The audit log confirms the stop.
  - A control workspace under the limit was not stopped.
  - See `autostop/docs/stop-evidence-2026-11-10.md`.
- **In-cluster runs:** both ConfigMap and git-pull modes ran successfully.
- **Real email:** the owner and template-owner emails were delivered through a Postfix relay to an inbox.

## Known limitations

- The tool cannot change Coder's `max_deadline`. When a template still has a required stop day, Coder keeps enforcing it, and the tool warns about this in interval-only mode.
- Emails are de-duplicated without stored state, so keep `run_interval_minutes` equal to the CronJob schedule.
- The exact ticket case (an *old* build clamped onto a non-required weekday) is covered by a unit test. It was not reproduced live, because that would mean leaving a workspace running across a required stop day.
- Dependencies are installed with pip when the job starts, which needs access to PyPI. For air-gapped clusters, build an image with them included.

author: ronak-dotcom
body:
## Why
On lead #123, Devaraj moved the map location and changed the survey number (40 → 725) without management approval. Both went through by design:
- `location` and `gps_coordinates` were not approval-gated at all; they were written directly on every save.
- Every gated field was freely editable for the whole calendar day the lead was created. #123 was created at 09:31 and edited at 11:37 the same day.

Agreed with the owner: the map location needs approval, and the free window shrinks to **1 hour**.

## What
- `location` and `gps_coordinates` are approval-gated and audited, like survey number, village and owner (shown as "Location" and "Map Location (GPS)").
- The free window is `LandLeadService.freeEditWindow` = 1 hour after the lead was saved (was: same calendar day). Filling in a blank field stays free.
- A GPS value **within 25 m** of the old one counts as unchanged, so re-capturing at the same spot, or the same point stored in a different format, never raises an approval request.
- Management's pending-change banner shows GPS as plain coordinates with how far it moved, plus *Old on map* / *New on map* buttons.
- After an edit, both edit entry points (Lead Detail and Land Workspace) say which fields are waiting for approval instead of a plain "Lead updated".
- **Loophole closed:** edits saved offline were synced with no previous state, which wrote every core field directly. Offline sync now fetches the server copy first (new `LandLeadService.getById`). The photo-only sync passes the lead as its own previous state.
- The decision now lives in a pure `LandLeadService.splitCoreFieldChanges` with unit tests.

Unchanged: renaming a lead keeps its own rule (first rename free, then approval).

## Testing
- New `test/lead_change_approval_rule_test.dart` covers six cases:
  - GPS move after 1h needs approval
  - location text change after 1h needs approval
  - survey 40 → 725 after 1h needs approval
  - changes within 1h apply directly
  - blank → filled is free
  - a re-capture ~10 m away in LIVE| format is not a change
- `flutter test`: same as `main` (`employee_lead_next_action_test` and `no_future_activity_test` fail to load; `add_lead_map_test` is intermittent).
- `flutter analyze` shows no new issues.

author: m1nuzz
body:
## Summary

Owner request: YouTube links must earn like TikTok. The old bypass rationale ("SDK only pays for TikTok/IG traffic", `link.rs:716` since 02a5abe) does not hold mechanically - Monetag sees only the webview, zone and Telegram user id; the source platform never reaches it. This PR makes the YT flow: **link -> quality picker -> the same ad button as TikTok -> claim -> download with the tapped quality -> delivery**.

## Changes

- `handle_yt_pick_callback`: when ads are enabled and `WEBAPP_URL` is set, builds the TikTok ad gate - `replace_pending_download` for the video URL (retired rows lose keyboards, in-flight rows answer AlreadyProcessing), mini-app + premium buttons, `set_choice_message`, then returns (no waiting in the callback - the claim spawns the download, same as TikTok singles).
- New `YT_QUALITY_BY_YMID` map carries the tapped quality to the claim path; `spawn_download_job` takes it (`take_yt_quality_for`) so the download uses the picked height instead of the stored h264/h265 preference. Entries taken once, pruned after 2 h (row lease is 30 min).
- Ads off (premium / module disabled / no `WEBAPP_URL`): direct download with the tapped quality, unchanged.

## Funnel effect

YT sessions now create real `pending_downloads` rows: they count in the S1->S2->S3 funnel, produce valued Monetag postbacks, and are covered by the expiry sweeper. Quality picker stays inline (bypasses nothing anymore).

## Verification

- Local: 149 lib tests pass.
- CI must pass before merge; post-deploy manual check: send a YT link, pick quality, expect the ad button exactly like TikTok, watch/claim, video delivers at the picked height.

author: jonathan-dejong
body:
## A question rather than a fix

The dashed placeholder next to a week's badge is as wide as `WeeklyPlannerWeek::getTentativePercentage()`. That share is measured against the **contract hours**, while the badge's own percentage (`getPlannedPercentage()`) is measured against the **capacity**, contract hours minus time off. The two are side by side in the same bar but use different denominators.

That is my doing: #30 (tentative) was written before #19 (time off) introduced capacity, and I never revisited it once both were in. The CSS comment above `.planner-summary-tentative` already says "share of capacity", so the code and the intent disagree.

It only matters in weeks with time off. Example: a 40-hour week with two days off has 24 hours of capacity, and 12 tentative hours on top of it:

| | Against contract hours (today) | Against capacity (this PR) |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Tentative share | 30% | 50% |
| Reads as | there is room for this | this fills half of what is left |

## What this PR does

`getTentativePercentage()` divides by the capacity, like `getPlannedPercentage()`, so planned plus tentative is what the week would be once the tentative work is confirmed. A week without capacity returns 0, as before. One new test covers a week with time off.

## Why it's a discussion

Measuring against contract hours is also defensible: it is the more stable figure, and a short tentative placeholder in a week of holiday does not look alarming. I lean towards capacity for consistency with everything else in the grid, but happy to close this if you prefer it as it is.

## Tests

PHPStan (level 9), php-cs-fixer and the plugin tests pass.

author: adripassanisi
body:
### Mathematical Concept Implemented
Classical limited fluctuation full credibility models:
1. `full_credibility_standard`: Computes the expected claim count threshold $n_0 = (z/k)^2$ for pure claim counts, and $n_S = n_0(1 + C_X^2)$ for compound aggregate losses accounting for severity variability.
2. `full_credibility_required_exposure`: Calculates the required exposure units $E_0 = n_S / \lambda$ given a base claim frequency rate.

### References
- Kaas, R., Goovaerts, M., Dhaene, J., and Denuit, M. (2008). *Modern Actuarial Risk Theory: Using R*. 2nd ed. Springer. Chapter 8, Section 8.1.
- Klugman, S. A., Panjer, H. H., and Willmot, G. E. (2012). *Loss Models: From Data to Decisions*. 4th ed. Wiley. Chapter 16.

### Architecture & Anti-Breakage Strategy
Core algorithms evaluate standards autonomously to ensure CI stays green without requiring upstream unmerged branches. Integration with Monticelli's partial credibility standard (PR #21) uses `pytest.importorskip`, running automatically upon merge.

### AI Assistance and Human Validation (Section 4.3)
- **AI Use:** Assisted with Google-style docstring formatting and vectorization checks.
- **Human Validation:** Manually verified the classical actuarial benchmark ($p=0.90, k=0.05 \implies n_0 = 1,082.2$ claims) and verified that severity variance scales the threshold linearly by $(1 + C_X^2)$.

author: ghywel
body:
This adds `lean/Ruliology/CellularAutomata/Rule30ZeroWallDiagonals.lean`, with its `public import` line in `lean/Ruliology.lean` after `Rule30LeftAntiPeriod` and a row in *Added in the kit* after the same module. It imports `Rule30LeftUnbounded` and `Rule30ZeroBoundary`.

**What it proves.** It shows what a counterexample to `Q01` would have to look like.
- `E_entry`, `E_tailLeft`: for a finite row with last black cell at depth `m ≥ 1`, the diagonals measured from the moving edge, `E L m j t = zrow L t (m + t - j)`, obey the left-diagonal recurrence whenever the entry guard `j + 2 ≤ m + t` holds, equality included; no converse is asserted. This is `zrow_succ`; at equality the right input is the wall.
- **The `TailLeft` package**, for every array whose coordinates 0 and 1 are eventually black and whose recurrence holds eventually at each index:
  - `tail_periodic`: eventual period `2 ^ j`;
  - `tail_profile_bound`: `M + 3 ≤ 2 ^ (2 Q)` for `Q`-periodic profiles;
  - `tail_white_unbounded`, `tail_no_two_white`, `tail_black_after_white`, `tail_black_unbounded`: eventually black coordinates at arbitrarily large index.

  `E_black_unbounded` instantiates this for the zero wall.
- `row_eq_Theta`, `rows_agree`, `freeWord_bounded_lag`, `freeWord_bounded_lag_of_finSupp`: for a finitely supported constrained row, bounded-slack repeats of the free word `freeWord L s = zrow L (2 s + 1) 1` have bounded lag.
- `le_factorCount`, `factorCount_le`, `factorCount_succ`, `rightSpecialCount_pos`, `two_run`: a core-Lean factor count, pinned as the number of distinct factors, with the binary special-factor identity, the Morse–Hedlund step, and an explicit two-run witness.
- `complexity_of_bounded_lag`, `freeWord_complexity`: such a free word has factor complexity above `n + K` eventually, for every `K`.

**Scope.** Finitely supported constrained rows exist only if `Q01` fails, so the free-word statements are conditional. The moving-edge black/white diagonal statements require a nonzero finite row with a last black cell at positive depth; `E_entry` itself needs no support or nonzero hypothesis. No rate is claimed for the complexity excess.

**Checks**, with Lean 4.35.0, at main `03a19bf`:
- `lake build Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30ZeroWallDiagonals`: no warnings.
- The kit's own `Check.lean --claim partial` passes all 20 headlines, with 324 constants and no new axioms.
- The portal form passes `Check` at the verifier's kit `5fb59158`, where `Rule30ZeroBoundary` and `Rule30LeftReset` lack only later appended declarations, none of them used here.
- The compiler rejected all six mutations tested:
  - the entry guard one step early;
  - the second diagonal black from time 0;
  - the factor count rising by exactly 1;
  - the two-run lemma with `M ≥ L + q`;
  - right-special factors of every length for every word;
  - the unchanged complexity proof with its aperiodicity parameter replaced by `True` (a structural mutation: bounded lag itself already excludes eventual periodicity, so this rejection does not show aperiodicity is an independent necessary assumption).
- The worked numbers agree in Python and Wolfram Language:
  - the edge-diagonal recurrence holds inside the guard, and the displayed single-cell run has a failure just outside it;
  - late periods divide `2 ^ j`;
  - the displayed 20,000-bit Fibonacci prefix has `n + 1` factors and one right-special factor at each tested length.
- Not run: the full catalog build (`bash build_all.sh`).

**Prior art.** The left-diagonal theory and profile bound are the kit's `Rule30Diagonals`, `Rule30LeftReset` and `Rule30LeftUnbounded`, for the single seed, ported here with entry-time guards. Morse–Hedlund's complexity bound and the binary special-factor count (Cassaigne, 1997) are classical and are reproved in core Lean; the kit's `ShiftOrbit` and `WordsAutomata` have Mathlib versions. Repetitions in low-complexity words are studied by Bugeaud and Kim (2019). No priority is claimed for the abstract word implication.

**What it does not do.** It does not decide `Q01`, gives no quantitative rate, and does not include the separate near-square claim.

Portal entry: [R30-20261110-144e6e](https://www.wolframcloud.com/obj/rule-30-prize/Agents/status/R30-20261110-144e6e).

author: nripeshn
body:
Milestone: M2 (no silently wrong translation), HLSL target.

DXC 1.9 lowers several floating-point built-ins to DXIL that does not compute their documented results (checked in the DXIL it emits):

- `fmod(x, y)` becomes `q = x / y; r = frac(abs(q)); (q >= -q ? r : -r) * y` with a fast division, so the remainder carries the quotient's rounding error. `fmod(-5.5, 2.0)` reads `-1.4999998` on WARP. A floating `%` becomes `frem fast`; a double `%` is a compile error.
- `frexp` masks the significand with `0x007fffff`: a negative value returns a positive significand, a subnormal value returns zero.
- `modf` computes `x - trunc(x)`: a positive zero for a negative integer, NaN for an infinity.

HLSL output now computes these from the operands' bits with integer arithmetic (`crosstl/translator/codegen/hlsl_exact_float_builtins.py`, new): `fmod` divides integer significands as C libraries do (exact for every operand, subnormals included), `frexp`/`modf` work on the bits; float and double (`uint64_t`, SM 6.0) and half through float. Scalar and vector operands, and output parts of other types, are covered. Hooked into `directx_codegen.generate_expression` with three small edits.

Metal output: `%` between floating-point built-in calls (`abs(x) % abs(y)`) was emitted as `%`, which the Metal compiler rejects; it now writes `fmod` (`metal_hlsl_values.metal_remainder_operand_type` types the calls from their arguments).

Measured:
- Nightly WARP divergences this targets: `m_fmod_sign`, `u_fmodf_sign`, `h_frexp_ldexp_modf`, `s_frexp_ldexp_modf` (metal/glsl/spirv -> hlsl). New conformance case `h_fmod_remainder`.
- Locally: CrossGL -> HLSL -> DXC -spirv -> MoltenVK, 9 columns x 4096 random and special inputs, bit-exact against numpy. Conformance `h_fmod_remainder`: spirv preserved 12/12 on MoltenVK and KosmicKrisp, Metal strict preserved.
- WARP confirmation comes from this PR's Windows conformance leg.

Tests: `tests/test_translator/test_hlsl_exact_float_builtins.py` (16, compiles with DXC where available); Tier 1 (`tests/test_translator`, `tests/test_backend/test_directx`, `tests/test_backend/test_metal`): 41117 passed; after merging main, DirectX/Metal codegen and backend suites 7796 passed, `tests/conformance` 278 passed (fail-closed lint clean).

author: itsfja
body:
Closes #385.

CI on main has been failing since #383 (and so #384 fails too): in `t_listen.py` the Home Assistant event listener vanished part-way through, with "Task was destroyed but it is pending!".

**Cause.** Listeners and watchers were started with `asyncio.ensure_future(...)` and nothing kept the task. asyncio only holds tasks weakly, so Python was free to collect one while it waited. When that happens depends on the garbage collector's timing, which is why it appeared on Python 3.11 after an unrelated change.

This is a real bug in exported programs: a program left listening could silently stop hearing Home Assistant events, MQTT, web requests or Telegram.

**Fix.** `_background()` starts a long-running task and holds it until it ends. The listeners, the Home Assistant watcher and the Telegram watcher use it.

**Tests.** A unit test shows a waiting task survives a garbage collection (without the fix it is destroyed). Another fails if any `ensure_future` or `create_task` in the runtime doesn't keep its result. `python tests/run_tests.py python --share 1/3`, the share that failed, passes here; CI's Python 3.11 run on this PR is the real check.

Merge this before #384; I'll then rebase #384 on main.

## Summary
`bootstrap-bucket` in `datalake-logs` gains `kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/force: enabled` and moves from `minio/mc` to `rclone/rclone`, mirroring the `cnpg-versity-gw` Job from #1698. It was the only other bare Job under `k8s/`, so the #1638 trap was latent here: the first edit to it would have stopped the whole `datalake-logs` pass, Loki included. The image moves with it because a replaced Job has to pull: `minio/mc` is gone from Docker Hub (Hub API 404, manifest 401, the same answers a repository that never existed gets). The annotations reference now names both Jobs.
## Evidence
- **Before:** this pod template without the annotation, `flux diff kustomization datalake-logs -n datalake-logs --path …` → `Job/datalake-logs/bootstrap-bucket dry-run failed (Invalid)`, exit 2.
  **After:** same command on this branch → `Job/datalake-logs/bootstrap-bucket created`, nothing else differs. `make validate`, `docs-lint`, `docs-reference-check`, `docs-build` clean.
## Merge Danger
**Door:** two-way, though a revert lands back on an image that no longer pulls. **Merging makes Flux delete `bootstrap-bucket` and run it again, once**, because the pod template changes. `rclone mkdir vgw:loki` on the existing bucket does nothing; the same image and command completed against the same versitygw (v1.7.0) in `platform-storage` after #1698. It has not been run against this gateway.
**Blast Radius:** datalake-logs. A failing Job would retry and sit failed; the Kustomization does not wait on it, and Loki and its bucket are not touched.

author: andrebras
body:
## Summary

Turning the page's terminal off now says what it ends, and `tempo config terminal off` from the command line now also ends the tmux sessions Tempo started. tmux is a terminal multiplexer: a program that keeps shells running in named "sessions". With tmux installed, each project's terminal shell runs in a session named `tempo-<folder>-<6 hex characters>`.

- **Command line:** after turning the terminal off, the command ends every tmux session with Tempo's naming pattern, and no other, and says which:
  - `Terminal is off. Ended 2 tmux sessions Tempo started (tempo-app-3f9a1c, tempo-web-91be02); anything running in them was stopped.`
  - `Terminal is off. No terminal sessions were running.`
  - Without tmux: `Terminal is off. Shells kept alive by a running page server stop when that server stops, or when you turn the terminal off in the page's Settings.`
- **Settings:** with terminals running, Off first asks, inline under the switch, the way Merge does (no browser dialog): "Turning the terminal off ends 2 running terminals; anything running in them stops.", with **Turn off** and **Cancel** (Esc also cancels). With none running, it turns off at once. Afterwards a line says "Terminal is off. Ended 2 terminals."

## Why

Turning the terminal off in Settings already ended every Tempo shell and tmux session, but without a warning. `tempo config terminal off` only refused new shells, because the command can't reach a running page server, so tmux sessions kept running. The decision for #140's open question was that the command also ends Tempo's tmux sessions, and that the user is clearly told what was stopped, both on the command line and in Settings.

## What changed

- `tempo/terminal.py`: `sessions()` lists the tmux sessions with Tempo's naming pattern (the existing matcher), and `end_sessions()` now returns the names it ended. `Shells.running()` counts the running terminals: the shells the page server keeps itself (without tmux) and every Tempo tmux session, shown or hidden, including one an earlier server left. `Shells.end_all()` returns how many it ended.
- `tempo/server.py`: a new `GET /api/terminal/running` answers `{"running": N}`. Like every terminal route it needs the terminal secret, and it never opens the database. Turning the terminal off in Settings answers `ended: N`.
- `tempo/cli.py`: `tempo config terminal off` ends Tempo's tmux sessions and prints one of the three messages above instead of the usual setting line.
- `tempo/page.js`, `tempo/terminal.js`, `tempo/page.html`: the inline warning before Off, the notice after it, and one CSS line so the warning takes the row's full width.
- Tests: `tests/test_cli.py` checks the three messages. `tests/test_server.py` checks the running count, the secret check on it, and `ended`, with and without tmux. `tests/page.test.js` checks the warning's and notice's wording. `tests/test_page.py` has a browser flow: Off shows the warning, Esc cancels and the shell keeps running, Turn off ends it and shows the notice.
- Docs: `docs/reference.md` (what turning off ends, from Settings and from the command) and a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## How it was tested

`bin/ci` passes on this branch, based on `feat/page-terminal`: 409 Python tests and 40 Node tests, plus every lint, type and security check. No test was skipped, so the tmux tests ran (tmux on macOS). The tmux tests, the new CLI ones included, run their own tmux server on a socket in a temporary folder (`-S <tmp>/tmux -f /dev/null`) with the session prefix `tempo-test-`, and each checks that a session with another name is left alone. I compared my own tmux sessions before and after the full run: they were the same.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **A test fix on its own commit:** `test_turns_the_terminal_on_and_off` in `tests/test_server.py` turned the terminal off with tmux found on `PATH`. Since #140, that ends every `tempo-*` session on the default tmux server, so running the tests could end the sessions of terminals open on the real page. It now runs without tmux.
- **The command ends sessions for every Tempo database:** tmux sessions are named for folders, not databases. So `tempo config terminal off` run against a scratch database (`TEMPO_DB`, or a worktree's `.tempo-dev` database) still ends the sessions the real page started. The same is true of Settings off on a scratch page.
- **Shells kept by a page server without tmux** are not reached by the command. It says so, and they stop with that server or with Settings off.
- **How tests reach tmux:** the session-ending code uses the module's `TMUX` command, which the tests replace with one pointing at their private socket (as the existing tmux tests do), rather than taking a socket argument that production would never pass.
- **If the count can't be read** (for example, the page was loaded before a server restart, so its terminal secret is stale), Off shows the error instead of turning off without a warning. Reloading the page fixes it.
- **No notice when nothing ran:** with no terminals running, Off turns off at once and shows no line, as the switch itself shows Off.
- Size: about 130 changed lines of real code in `tempo/`.

- [x] `bin/ci` passes
- [x] A line under "Unreleased" in `CHANGELOG.md`
- [x] The version changes only in a release PR

No effectiveness hypothesis or identification of distinct arrow labels is used.

Advance [Orbifolds/README.md, O2.3, “Prove the kernel-order function is locally constant on each connected orbifold component”](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/Orbifolds/README.md#o2-retained-arrow-charts-averaging-and-effective-reduction), delivered by `TauCeti.isLocallyConstant_card_ineffectiveKernel` and `TauCeti.isLocallyConstant_coarseCardIneffectiveKernel`. After this PR, O2.3 still needs the topological/smooth effective quotient presentation, the general-groupoid dense principal-open comparison, and the ambient/labelled-face kernel comparison.

Roadmap: Orbifolds

<!--tauceti-target:v1 {"focus":"Orbifolds","id":"islocallyconstant-card-ineffectivekernel"}-->
