<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"NixoSM"} -->
_Requested by **Nicola** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01N7Gvj2Xbbtp3gNRf1i9ZiE?thread=cmsg_01N7Gvj2Xbbtp3gNRf1i9ZiEG5VnhqwnCaeHVENw2PcMmR)_

Every step (A to K) of the health check of 2026-11-09, then the two bug checks the project asks for, with their fixes.

## This is a draft on purpose: no Mac build yet

A draft pull request now runs only the free checks on Linux. **To build `Kotoba.ipa`, press "Ready for review" at the bottom of this page.** That starts a new run which builds the app on a Mac (roughly 50 allowance minutes, judging by earlier runs, and only once: merging afterwards reuses the same build). "Run workflow" in the Actions tab, with this branch selected, does the same without changing the draft.

**Nothing here has been compiled by Xcode or tried on a phone.** The engine and the app's logic are compiled and tested on Linux. The screens are only type-checked against hand-written stand-ins for SwiftUI (`tools/screen-check`), and a few files are not checked by any compiler at all (`KotobaApp`, `AudioPlayer`, `LongWork`, `AppModel+Device`, `Palette`, `ResultsWebView`, the camera screens, the share extension). Expect the first Mac build to find compile errors in those. I will fix what it reports.

## What changed

**Builds (A)**
- Engine tests, app logic tests and a compiler's look at the screens run on Linux. The Mac is used only to build the app, and for the camera tests when camera code changed.
- A merged pull request is not built a second time on `main`.

**Search (B, C, G)**
- Verb stems are understood: 食べながら, 見やすい, 起きそう, 食べ方, 食べ始める, and older negatives such as 書かぬ, 書かねば, 書かされた.
- Romaji with long vowels (tōkyō, kōhī) and shimbun, sampo.
- A "words that start with" list: しんぶ offers 新聞.
- Searching by meaning no longer comes back empty because a large switched-off dictionary filled the candidate list.

**Dictionaries (B, E, K)**
- Importing pictures no longer slows down with every file (8,000 pictures took over two minutes).
- Several files can be imported in one go, with a count and a way to stop. The screen stays on. If the app is left long enough for iOS to suspend it, the import stops cleanly and says so.
- Deleting asks first, runs in the background, and reports errors.
- Kanji dictionaries are read, and the kanji of the first word appear under the results.
- Each dictionary has a detail page. Dizionari now lives inside Impostazioni.

**Results page (D, H, I)**
- Grey text and accents of the light themes reach a 4.5:1 contrast. Audio and Anki buttons are 44 pt.
- Dictionary-supplied names and stylesheets cannot inject markup. The page forbids network loads and foreign scripts.
- Changing theme repaints instead of rebuilding every screen.
- The page is photographed in every theme by the pipeline (artifact `results-pages`).

**Screens (E, F, J, K)**
- First run: download, import, Yomitan settings, in three steps on the search tab.
- A Parole tab: the words sent to Anki, by kana row with a thumb index, or by date.
- Anki fields can be added, renamed, removed and reordered. The tick appears when AnkiMobile reports the note saved, not on the tap.
- A diagnostics page: a diary of imports, deletes and errors, and a report to copy. Impostazioni shows the version and when the signature expires.
- Word audio lowers other audio instead of stopping it.

**Version** 0.16.0 (16), now set in one place (`project.yml`).

## Bug checks

- **bug-echo** on the fixes: 3 bugs fixed, 8 weaker spots (5 fixed, 1 partly, 2 left with reasons). Report: `.agents/research/2026-11-10-bug-echo-health-check-fixes.md`
- **bug-prospector** (quick) on the changed files: 8 bugs fixed. Report: `.agents/research/2026-11-10-bug-prospector-health-check-branch.md`

The one that matters most: **tapping ＋ closed the app when an Anki field name had a space or a Japanese character** ("Word Reading" in the Kaishi deck, 単語). This was reproduced on Linux, which runs the same Foundation code as iOS 17 and later. Whether AnkiMobile accepts the encoded names as intended can only be confirmed on the phone.

Left for later, with reasons in the reports: the two `try?` writes in the texthooker (that work belongs to another thread), the index builder at launch racing an import, the `kotoba://mined` link that another app could forge, and how iOS behaves when background time runs out during an import (needs a phone).

## How it was checked

- Engine: 81 tests on Linux.
- App logic: 61 tests on Linux (1 runs only in the pipeline).
- Translations: 368 texts, English and Japanese complete.
- Screens: 20 files type-checked against stand-ins.
- Not checked: anything on a device, and the real SwiftUI/UIKit compile.

## Not included

- Frequency lists for kanji (`kanji_meta_bank`) are still ignored.
- Screenshots of the native screens (only the results page is photographed).
- The private or public repository decision, and replacing the `back-cover.png` test picture.

author: simonholmes
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Merge with "Rebase and merge" (or a merge commit), not squash.** The first commit is a pure `git mv`, which is what lets `git log --follow` carry the ledger's 91-commit history to its new name. A squash folds the rename and the rewrite into one commit, and git then sees a deleted file and a new one.

Moves the divergence ledger to where the Hub looks for it, in the shape it counts. Hub task t-190.

## Why

Sunrise #1062 (0.17.0, reached us with Daybreak 0.10.0) set where a leaf's ledger lives, `.context/app/platform-divergences.md`, and what a row holds. The Hub reads it from `main` and counts the rows whose Upstream cell starts with `sunrise#N` or `daybreak#N`. Ours was `.context/app/divergences.md`, one section per row with the issue partway through a cell, so the Hub found no ledger.

## What changed

- **The ledger** is one table in Sunrise's columns, row numbers kept, `Next row: 35`. Every original cell is kept word for word in a notes section per row, so nothing a sync relies on is lost. Retired rows 4, 17 and 23 keep one line each, because comments still cite them. "On a sync" points at `CUSTOMIZATION.md`'s procedure rather than copying it, and keeps the leaf's caveat: a `sunrise#N` fix counts only once Daybreak has taken that Sunrise release.
- **One ledger, both tiers.** Our edits to Sunrise's and to Daybreak's files are both here; Daybreak's own ledger is named and left alone.
- **References**: about 60, across docs, code comments, tests and `CLAUDE.md`. All of them sit on lines we added. One is left: a comment in an applied migration's SQL, which is never edited. The ledger says it was formerly `divergences.md`.

## Every row with an upstream trigger now has its ask filed

Owner ruling: a row whose deletion trigger is an upstream change is an ask, filed now with the tier that owns the file. "Raise it if a second leaf needs it" is a dead end, because one leaf can't see the others. Each file was checked three ways, and each target repo searched first.

- **New on Sunrise:** #1205 (`metadataBase`), #1206 (title check for a `generateMetadata` page), #1207 (theme: third state and the Safari failed write), #1208 (public header action and footer notice slots), #1209 (sitemap), #1210 (icons), #1211 (Prettier ignore).
- **New on Daybreak:** #330 (keep its Hub block out of leaves' `CLAUDE.md`), #331 (version-parity case).
- **Our case added to existing Sunrise issues:** #1200 (fonts), #1197 (surface swap), #636 (protected-nav test, and the Prisma stub half of row 12).
- **Rows still `none`, each with its reason:** 7 (no support page of our own yet), 9 (our terms page; permanent), 10 (our privacy policy isn't written yet), 30 (Sunrise declined #984; t-175 moves us off it), 32 (the home page's thin shim is ours: t-191).

## Found on the way

- **Three edits with no row**, now ledgered: rows 32 (`app/(public)/page.tsx`, replaced whole), 33 (`.prettierignore`) and 34 (`daybreak-version.test.ts`).
- **One edit removed instead:** the planning-folder ignore in the root `eslint.config.mjs` is a global-ignore block in our `lib/app/eslint.config.mjs` now, and Sunrise's file is the release's again. `defaults.test.ts` pins the new block exactly, since any extra key would stop it being global.
- **`CLAUDE.md`'s banner** said we were on Daybreak 0.9.0; it now says 0.11.0 (Sunrise 0.18.0).
- **Coverage:** the comment-only rename made the per-file gate check `lib/app/memory/delete-conversation.ts`, at 77% branches. Three tests now cover failures that aren't `Error`s and a call that names no person, bringing it to 85.7%.

## Gates

- **`/pre-pr`:** `validate` passed, re-run after the ESLint change. The scoped run selected 2,190 files and every test passed; the first run's one failure was a stale Prisma client, from a comment edit in a schema file.
- **`/security-review`:** no findings. Every non-markdown change is the path rename, almost all in comments.
- **`/code-review`:** three rounds, findings fixed as new commits. Declined:
  - Rows 1, 13 and 31 are edits Sunrise's §2 already documents. They stay, because they carry merge actions our syncs use and now cite real asks.
  - "The rename widens the diff on upstream files": every renamed line is ours.
- **`npm run format`:** clean.

author: yasyf
body:
## Summary

When the LTX Behavioral Gate (short) runs (LTX is the transaction file format Litestream writes), CI now keeps Litestream's own log from each of its three load profiles and uploads them as one build artifact, `ltx-behavioral-gate-litestream-logs`, whether the gate passes or fails. Until now the log went into a Go test temp directory that was deleted when the test ended. A red gate showed only the summary counts the test prints, such as `L1: 16 compactions`, and never which compactions they were or what ran around them.

This is a CI-only change: two additions to `.github/workflows/commit.yml`, with no Go code touched.

## Refresher

The gate runs `TestLTXBehavior` from `tests/integration/ltx_behavior_test.go`. For each of three two-minute load profiles (low, high and burst volume), it starts a real `litestream replicate` against a local file replica and writes its output to `litestream.log`. It then parses that log to count syncs, snapshots and compactions per level and checks how often they happen. `SetupTestDB` (`tests/integration/helpers.go:82`) already keeps its directory as `/tmp/litestream-<profile>-<random>/` when `SOAK_KEEP_TEMP` is set. Otherwise, it uses `t.TempDir()`, which Go deletes when the test ends.

## Biggest surprise

The test code needed no change. The switch that keeps the directory was written for local soak runs, and CI never set it.

## What you will hate most

Each gate run now stores about 40 KB of zipped logs. That is three logs of 170 to 315 KB of DEBUG-level text, kept for the repository's default artifact retention. A rerun of the gate in the same workflow run uploads a second artifact under the same name, and `gh run download -n` returns the first one. To read a rerun's logs, download by artifact id from the run page or `gh api repos/Forge-AI/litestream/actions/artifacts/<id>/zip`.

## Show me

The change:

```yaml
      - name: Run LTX behavioral tests (short mode)
        env:
          LOG_LEVEL: DEBUG
          SOAK_KEEP_TEMP: "1"
        ...

      - name: Upload Litestream logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ltx-behavioral-gate-litestream-logs
          path: /tmp/litestream-*/litestream.log
```

Before, a failing gate's only trace was the test summary:

```
ltx_behavior_test.go:44:     L2: 9 compactions
ltx_behavior_test.go:44:   [compaction-timing-L2] FAIL: 4/8 intervals outside [12s, 48s] (expected ~30s)
```

After, the artifact from [a run of this exact workflow change](https://github.com/Forge-AI/litestream/actions/runs/42839117545/attempts/2) shows the two level-2 compactions inside one 30-second window. The second one runs 2.7 s after the first and holds one transaction:

```
time=2026-11-10T15:20:01.670Z level=INFO msg="compaction complete" ... level=2 txid.min=0000000000000001 txid.max=0000000000000013 size=10641871
time=2026-11-10T15:20:04.400Z level=INFO msg="compaction complete" ... level=2 txid.min=0000000000000014 txid.max=0000000000000014 size=15287
```

The artifact holds one directory per profile:

```
litestream-ltx-behavior-low-volume-732182687/litestream.log
litestream-ltx-behavior-high-volume-816492368/litestream.log
litestream-ltx-behavior-burst-volume-558439268/litestream.log
```

## His words

- "figure out how it got into a bad state": `.github/workflows/commit.yml:237` keeps each profile's directory, and `.github/workflows/commit.yml:244` uploads every profile's `litestream.log`, so a red gate can be traced from Litestream's own lines instead of from the test's summary counts.

body:
Fixes #2902. This is the separate follow-up chosen after #3048: an Advisory commit decision must answer the review feedback that actually reached its author, not whatever the host stored later.

**What changes**
- `review_reference` gains an optional `shown_outcomes`: the identity of the review outcomes that a handback actually rendered. It is built from the existing `outcome_states` and does not prove anyone read it.
- An outcome that settles after that reference was returned refuses the old decision twice: before staging, and again just before `git commit`. The free collection then returns it under a fresh reference; no new paid wave is sent.
- These cases keep a decision usable:
  - accounting and custody revisions of the record;
  - a recorded Continue, which keeps the original reference and `decided_by_task`;
  - a reference whose record is missing, settled with nothing to read, or `NOT_DISPATCHED`.
- Blocking keeps its own refusal. Cyber Pro still lands, with `unread_outcomes` recorded beside the decision.
- A refused landing is recorded and returned as a typed refusal even when restoring the index fails. A managed merge keeps its index and `MERGE_HEAD`.
- The `#112` comment in `run_delegated_review_session` moves onto the line it explains, which keeps that function at its 300-line ceiling.

**Checks**
- Independent Astra review of tree `c5ca6927` on this base: the core contract holds, and Astra found no path where a later outcome lands under an older decision. It reran the 213 commit-review consumer tests.
- Two follow-ups came from that review and are in this PR without being re-reviewed: the cleanup-failure refusal (with a new real-Git test) and keeping the `#112` comment.
- After those edits, the five commit-review consumer modules and `test_update_merge_assisted.py` pass locally, with a clean safe_test release.
- The real ledger writers settle the late outcomes; the reviewers are simulated.

**Not checked**
- The managed-merge test mocks the phase-restore helper.
- The full battery, cost contract, and the doc-size and inventory suites were not run locally; CI covers them.
- No native, packaged or live-provider run.

author: manikantadhulipala
body:
## Summary

Lesson 23 (Security Review: APIs and Config), `apps/web`, transactions route:

- `api/transactions/route.ts`: `POST` checks in this order:
  1. Rate limit by IP (10 requests per minute, `429` with `Retry-After`).
  2. Zod validation with `safeParse` (`userId` must be a UUID, `amount` positive and at most 10000). Returns `400 Invalid input`.
  3. Authentication via `verifyAuth` (`401 Unauthorized`).
  4. Authorization: the user can only create transactions for their own `userId` (`403 Forbidden`).
  5. Mock processing.
- Errors are logged on the server with a request ID. Clients get only generic messages.
- `lib/auth.ts`: demo `verifyAuth` that accepts any Bearer token. It needs a real verifier before production.
- `lib/rate-limit.ts`: fixed-window in-memory limiter (`server-only`).

Validation runs before authentication, so malformed requests get `400` even without an auth header. This matches the lesson's Done-When checks.

## Testing

- `pnpm check-types`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm build --filter=@repo/web` pass.
- Production server:
  - Invalid `amount` → `400 {"error":"Invalid input"}`
  - Invalid `userId` and negative `amount` → `400`
  - Valid body without auth → `401`
  - Valid body with auth → `200`
  - Other user's ID with auth → `403`
  - Requests past the 10th within the window → `429 {"error":"Too many requests"}` with `Retry-After: 60`
- Client bundles: no `server-only-value` (the `INTERNAL_CONFIG` value) appears. The `INTERNAL_CONFIG` name appears once as code reference, without its value.

## Notes

- The rate limiter and `verifyAuth` are demos. Counts are per server instance, and `verifyAuth` accepts any Bearer token. Use a shared store (for example Redis from the Vercel Marketplace) and a real token check before production.
- Requests with no `x-forwarded-for` header share the `unknown` bucket.

body: Leo, 2026-11-10: > "our app is still like embarrassing in various places ... the lags, the crashes ... it's not acceptable ... to put that out there, have my name on it. Like the slow animations, ugly, incoherent UI ... we need to be holding ourselves to high standards." > "WE DO NOT STAND FOR BAD CI AND LOW QUALITY STUFF EVER ... you're playing whack-a-mole like you're kids ... amateur hour." The `cmux-next CI guard group` job has been red on feat-cmux-next pushes since about 13:06Z (10 of 44 pushes to 14:34Z; 17 red steps at c33502fb). Every red came from a PR merged with no CI while the Mac runners were down. This PR fixes each one at the tip, except the `ios-reliability-matrix.yml` reds, which #40463 already fixes (runner labels, job class, fork routing, path-filter parity, its three artifact retentions). ## What changed - **Send-path caps** (#37736, #40053): the guard newly scans two Messages files. `maxReadBytes` (3 MiB) is the chunk size of a ranged read, and the page loops over the whole file. `maxFileBytes`/`maxTotalBytes` are the disk budget for staged draft bytes kept across launches. A file over the budget still sends; only its bytes aren't kept on disk. Both go in the allowlist as `safe:`. `claude_peers.rs`'s `size > 1 << 20` is macOS kern.argmax for `KERN_PROCARGS2` (reading another process's launch arguments), listed as `platform:`. None of these refuses a message, prompt or file. - **Short timeouts** (#40395, #40360, #40242, #40364, #40147): two kinds of finding. - Real short gates became 30 s hang breakers, so a slow answer gets waited for and isn't reported as failed. These are the Cloud Codex DNS reachability probe (2 s; a slow resolver on a fresh machine flipped Codex to own mode) and `cmux ext dev`'s reload pickup, load check and request deadlines (10 s and 15 s). - The rest were false positives. The ratchet looked 3 lines around each Duration, so a poll interval, a progress note or a backoff step declared next to a TIMEOUT constant counted as a timeout. Now a `const` whose own name says it spaces tries (backoff, retry, reconnect, restart, first wait, poll, interval, note) is judged by that name. A name that also says TIMEOUT, BUDGET or DEADLINE still counts. This changed exactly 9 hits across the tree, all pace constants. Their allowlist entries shrink, and a regression test covers it. - **Short fixed gates** (`turns.rs`): `Pace { pause: 2 s, deadline }` is the pause between retries inside the deadline next to it. The lint now skips a duration bound to `pause`/`interval`/`spacing`, with self-test cases for both sides. - **Test determinism**: - One false-positive class fixed: a one-line JS/TS helper (`const settle = () => act(... setTimeout(r, 0))`) declares a sleep but runs nothing where it's written. That cleared #37777's new finding and 4 old allowlist entries of the same shape, now removed. Self-test cases cover both sides. - Nine fixed sleeps from three no-CI Swift PRs (#40052, #40278, #40314) need a Mac to change and verify. They're listed as owned debt pointing at cmuxterm-hq#8911, which has the per-site fix. - **Outbound hosts**: `cursor.com`, `accounts.x.ai` and `auth.x.ai` (sign-in pages) get their `opens` rows in docs/privacy.md. - **Gallery health routing** (#40240, #40314): `schemas/theme/slots.json` and two string catalogs the gallery build reads now trigger the workflow, on both events. - **Upload retention** (#40385, #40353): the Cloud matrix artifacts keep 3 days, not 7. Their tables already go to the run summary. - **Test registry**: `tests/test-execution.d/ci.toml` re-sorted with the registry's own `fix`. ## Why a workflow with forbidden runner labels landed The guard group runs on every pull request (no path filter). #40289's own run was red on `cmux-next CI guard group`, but the outage policy (cmuxterm-hq#8734) let a `leo-named-fix` PR merge without CI. That skip is already gone: leo-workspace#4152 made merge_hold refuse any merge without its CI, outage or not. So this PR adds no new gate. ## Numbers (one harness: the guard scripts, run on the tip in this checkout) | | before (tip c33502fb / cfd1ff8c) | after | |---|---|---| | guard-group red steps | 17 | 6, all from `ios-reliability-matrix.yml` (#40463) | | send-path caps | 5 new caps | OK | | short timeout ratchet | 9 new hits in 7 files | OK (253 retained hits, 3 entries shrunk) | | short fixed gates | 1 | OK | | test determinism | 10 active | 0 active | | outbound hosts | 3 unlisted | OK | | gallery routing | 3 unrouted | OK | | upload retention | 6 | 3 (all #40463's) | Checked locally with each guard's own test or lint, plus the full guard profile on Linux (`cmux-ci test -- scripts/ci/guards-local.sh ...`). ## Changelog - No user-facing change: CI guard fixes. `cmux ext dev` waits up to 30 s for a reload before it reports one as failed. Agent session: [agent session](https://cmux.com/deeplink/agent?id=aid-fb75b7af9902231028aa) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the `cmux-next CI guard group`'s 17 red steps on `feat-cmux-next`, all from PRs merged without CI while Mac runners were down. - The Cloud Codex DNS reachability probe and `cmux ext dev`'s reload, load-check and request deadlines become 30 s hang breakers, so a slow answer is waited for rather than reported as failed. Everything else passing are false positives in the guard scripts, not behavior changes. - The short-timeout ratchet now judges a `const` whose own name says it spaces tries (backoff, retry, reconnect, poll, note) by that name, unless it also says TIMEOUT, BUDGET or DEADLINE. - The lint skips a duration bound to `pause`/`interval`/`spacing`, which is the pause between retries inside the deadline beside it. - The determinism guard no longer flags one-line JS/TS helpers that declare a sleep but run nothing where written; three Swift test files from no-CI PRs are listed as owned debt (tracked in cmuxterm-hq#8911). - Adds send-path cap allowlist entries for the Messages page's ranged-read chunk, its draft-bytes disk budget (including the one-time native-composer draft handoff), and macOS kern.argmax; none of these refuses a message, prompt or file. - Adds privacy rows for three sign-in hosts, routes the gallery health workflow for the theme slots schema and two string catalogs it reads, drops Cloud matrix artifact retention from 7 to 3 days, and re-sorts the test registry. author: hrl20
body:
I come across loom artifacts that are linked from a PR that are broken showing "session not found". For example https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8210 links [FineStore transactions](https://loom.oa.dev/s/qyinm7he/artifacts/finestore-transactions) which is broken, but the artifact actually exists just under a different session: https://loom.oa.dev/s/1a34lh68/artifacts/finestore-transactions . This PR implements a session redirect when resolving the session from a branch.

🤖 Agents mint artifact links with their branch id (`$WEAVER_BRANCH`), as in `/s/<branch>/artifacts/<name>`. `sessions.get` resolved a branch key only to its live session, so once that session was done, errored or archived the page showed "session not found", although the artifact was still served.

- `sessions.get` falls back to the branch's newest session in any state when a branch key has no live session (new store query `latest_for_branch`, next to `active_for_branch`). `resolve_key` and `require_session` are unchanged, so every verb that acts on a session still needs a live one.
- The session page moves to the session's own id when it was opened under a branch key, keeping the rest of the path, query and hash. This applies to live branch links too, not only ended ones: the channel read receipt, the events stream and the other calls on the page are keyed by the session id, so every `/s/<branch id>` link now ends on `/s/<session id>`.
- A session token's scope check still resolves live-only, so an agent reading an ended session by branch id with its own token gets 403. A parent reading an ended child should use the session id. Human and admin callers are not affected.
- The page instance opened under the branch key stays in the keep-alive cache, rendering nothing, until it is evicted. It takes one of the four slots. Resolving the key in a route guard instead would avoid that, and is left as a follow-up.

The new Playwright case in `e2e/tests/artifacts.spec.ts` has not been run: CI has no Playwright job (despite AGENTS.md saying it runs `e2e/`), and no machine available to this change could build loom for it.

## What changes

- **FG-A "Tim finds the resort"** plays on One Island's Kindle Road, just below Ember Spa: once Bill's first Sevii trip is over, while the Friends are still in Kanto (at FG11, or FG12 after the League), Tim, Brian, Ham and Nick are on the sand with Tim's Spearow, Brian's Slowpoke and a local woman. Talk to any of them: Tim wants a night market, the local says most people go to bed, Spearow tugs at the return tickets, Tim reads the ferry board and pays for the rooms. A choice ("Sounds like a vacation" / "You sound like a tour guide"), then the four go into the spa and aren't on the road again. Optional, no battle, nothing given.
- They stand clear of the spa door and of the road north to Mt. Ember and south to One Island. #117's traveller is in One Island's town (10,14), another map.
- The draft's lines as written, except two given to other speakers to keep the voices the owner set (Nick says the simple thing, never explains the scene; non-leads get one line):
  - Nick's "He's telling you to keep track of them." (explains the Spearow) is Ham's **"He's checking."**
  - Nick's "You know the ferry times for an island nobody's heard of." is **Brian's**. Nick keeps "To Thailand?" and, on the tour-guide branch, "Like a friend."

- **Shared machinery for the handoff's new scenes (FG-A–FG-G)**, the first commit, identical in the FG-B (#122) and FG-C (#124) pull requests, so it merges cleanly whichever goes first. The allocation audit (10 November): the new scenes are scenes 23–29 with the handoff's receipts `0x956`–`0x95C` (scene 23 + n, receipt `0x956` + n). Nothing else used those bits when I checked (every branch on origin had them required-zero; FG-D/E/F's branches since take `0x959`–`0x95B`, as the allocation says); they're saved Kanto flags with the Friends' others, after the stage `0x94B`–`0x94F`, invitation `0x950`, loss `0x951`–`0x954` and reunion `0x955`; `0x95D`–`0x95F` stay required-zero. They can't just follow scene 22's receipts (`0x935` + scene − 1 for scene 23 is a stage bit), so they have their own range. The stage keeps its 0–22 placements and never holds 23–29: an extra scene's gate names the placements it plays at, its map never moves the stage, it stays for the rest of the visit it's seen on, and a later placement retires it. The handoff's 29-placement order table isn't used: it would renumber every existing save's stage.
- Code: `FriendsStory_IsHere` (the old check for the 22 scenes, plus the extra ones), `SeenAny`, a camp row that also says who is in front, which visitor slots the scene uses and whether the group leaves; shared beats 80/81 (the home reflection) and 90 (the group leaves). FG-A is scene 23 on `MAP_ONE_ISLAND_KINDLE_ROAD`; menus use `dynmultichoice`, so no new `MULTI_` numbers. The stage's five bits have names (`FLAG_FRIENDS_STAGE_1`…`_16`) so a test can start the Friends at a placement.
- Docs: KR-124 in `kanto-rebuild.md`; the campaign guide's Sevii chapter, the handoff section's audit and FG-A's row.

## Tested

- `make -j4` after `make clean`: exit 0, `pokefirered.gba` 33,554,432 bytes, sha1 `424a99bf43ff3212ec62e093bc2b09861890e880` (the tested ROM).
- `pae test run -p engine --no-build`: 651 tests (644 existing + 7 new), all pass with the timing screens below accepted.

  - `kindle road tim finds the resort` (stage 11): talk to Nick; ends on Tim's "Fine. We're staying one night. Rooms are on me."
  - `kindle road tim finds the resort after the league` (Champion, stage 12): the same, after the League.
  - `kindle road tim finds the resort like a friend`: the whole scene, "You sound like a tour guide"; ends on Tim's "Same thing in this group." after Nick's "Like a friend."; receipt `0x956` set.

They start by Nick's spot and only turn and press A (a held direction walks one or two tiles depending on the build's timing).
  - On the v2-main ROM (`1d5968a3…`) the scene tests fail (nobody there) and the closed-gate tests pass, as they should.
- 29 existing screens changed and were accepted after looking at each (own commit): all are on or next to a camp map (Cerulean, Vermilion, Celadon, Lavender, Fuchsia, Saffron, Pallet, the routes into them, Dragon's Den), where the shared machinery adds a little work at map load and the frame the map finishes on moves. A wandering person or walker is a step elsewhere, the sea's animation is a frame on, a map-name sign or a box's text is a few pixels further on; nothing else differs. #122 and #124 carry this commit too: their ROMs show the same 29 screens pixel for pixel, so those files don't conflict. author: spankyed
body:
Four defects a review of #91 found in what it changed, each with a test that fails without the fix.

- **`renameType` told no reader of another type.** It rewrote other types' edges and `ref` fields past the events a write makes, so `changedSince(["Task"])` answered complete with no ids while a Task named an id that was gone. It now emits an event for each row it rewrites.
- **A change set read destroy-then-create as create-then-destroy.** An entity destroyed and made again under its id in one commit is now `created` alone; one made and destroyed is still both.
- **Four writes reached an entity of a removed type**: `grantExclusive`'s `among`, `unlink` by target, and `removeRelation` and `updateRelation` on a relation it is an end of. Each is refused as the others are.
- **A close that gave up left the database open with no builder.** What is left to build is queued again.

Not in this PR, from the same review:

- `Builder::stop` joins its own thread when a listener delivered by a builder's commit changes the schema.
- `waitForIndexBuilds` answers `Ok` when a schema change stops the builder it waits on.
- A multi-field write is held to the key limit on a pair of values it only passes through.
- The Rust write path stores a non-finite `now`, `createdAt` or `updatedAt`.

Run locally: the engine's suite (612 tests) and clippy over the workspace. Not run: the binding's tests, the mutation gate, Loom and Shuttle.

body:
## What - Bump `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-http`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-appender-tracing` and `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions` to 0.33.1, and `tracing-opentelemetry` to 0.34.0. - Add `[opentelemetry] max_retries` (env `SOCKUDO_OTEL_MAX_RETRIES`), default `3`, `0` disables, so the new upstream retry default is operator-controllable. - Remove the stale zstd advisory ignores from `deny.toml`. - Fix the changelog: the retry bullet names the real setting, and the zstd bullet no longer describes the 0.32 pin and the removed ignores. ## Why The crates must move together: 0.33 changes the `LoggerProvider` trait consumed by the tracing bridge, so the Dependabot PRs #489, #550 and #551 fail to compile on their own. The lock also collapses to a single otel tree (0.33.1 was already present via `google-cloud-gax-internal`), dropping the duplicate 0.32 copies. The zstd ignores are obsolete: `zstd 0.13.4` / `zstd-safe 7.4.0` include the fixes for RUSTSEC-2026-0391/0398/0403. `cargo-deny` now reports them as not encountered. ## Behavior changes - OTLP exports retry failed batches by default (3 retries, upstream exponential backoff). Set `[opentelemetry] max_retries = 0` or `SOCKUDO_OTEL_MAX_RETRIES=0` to disable. - Schemeless gRPC endpoints now default to `https://`; set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_INSECURE=true` for plaintext. ## Verification - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` - `cargo fmt --all --check` - `cargo deny check advisories` → `advisories ok` - `cargo audit` → no vulnerabilities - `cargo test -p sockudo-core --lib opentelemetry` → 4 passed - `cargo test -p sockudo --bin sockudo --features "opentelemetry,push,push-fcm,push-apns,push-webpush,ai-transport,mysql,postgres" telemetry` → 6 passed `cargo test --workspace` was not run locally (needs the service containers from `docker-compose.test.yml`). Docs `astro check` was not run (astro not installed in the local `node_modules`); the docs change is a Markdown table row and a TOML example line. ## Review feedback - Greptile: `RetryPolicy::disabled()` was unreachable for operators → added `max_retries`. - Greptile: the new otel note contradicted the older zstd entry → rewritten to the shipped state.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; both previous findings are fixed and no new actionable issues were found.

Summary

Updates the OpenTelemetry crates together and removes stale advisory ignores. - OTLP exports retry failed sends under a configurable limit. - Schemeless gRPC telemetry endpoints now default to HTTPS. - The zstd advisory exceptions are removed after patched releases arrive. Both previous findings are addressed. No new actionable issues were found. This review checked source code; it did not run builds or tests. body:
## What

Meeting minutes outlive their transcript (#3780), with the owner's decisions recorded in #3862.

- **Retention**
  - Minutes are kept **forever by default**. `minutes_days` is 0 (forever), or 1–3650 days and never shorter than `recording_days`.
  - Transcripts keep `recording_days`, 14 days by default.
  - Both are in `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/assistant` and in `persona_settings` (`assistant.minutes_days`, which also takes "forever").
- **Trim**: a recording past `recording_days` that has minutes keeps only `meta.json` (with `trimmed_at`), `minutes.json` and `minutes.md`. The transcript, summary, live log and undo journal are removed. A recording without minutes is deleted as before; a trimmed one is deleted at `minutes_days`, or never when it is 0. A user delete still removes everything.
- **Trimmed recordings**
  - never re-filled by a late upload (always `expired`);
  - never summarized, calendar-matched or regenerated: `POST …/minutes` returns `409 transcript_expired`;
  - attendance is turned off;
  - the live log can't be written back;
  - the minutes are still read, searched and used to confirm to-dos;
  - `kb_get` / `kb_list` say the transcript expired;
  - reconciliation still lists them, with `trimmed_at`, and `days` is unchanged for the phone.
- **Earlier minutes in meeting answers**: they are not used until a meeting can be marked private (owner decision, #3862). One switch, `EarlierMeetingsInAnswers`, is off. The answer prompts then say only this meeting's material is available, and neither claims nor promises earlier minutes.
- **Web**
  - Settings › Persona › Recordings sets both retentions, minutes as Forever or a number of days.
  - Switching from Forever opens a draft and saves only the number you commit, never an intermediate value that would already delete minutes.
  - A trimmed recording's detail says how long its minutes stay.
- **Mock hub and docs**: `meeting-minutes.md`, `protocol.md`, `knowledge.md`, `recording.md`, `web.md`, and the kb tool descriptions with their goldens.

## Verification

- **Go**: gofmt and `go vet ./...` pass. The kb, assistant, hub and prompts tests pass against an isolated Postgres 18.
- **Web**: lint and `tsc -b` pass; 8,241 tests pass and 1 is skipped; the build passes. The retention browser e2e (`web/e2e/recording-retention.mjs`) took 30 screenshots (light and dark, large text, en, zh-Hans, ja), and I looked at them.

- **Docs and privacy**: the doc path, Go-path, wire and section checks and the privacy scan pass.
- **Reviews**: two rounds (data safety, contract, privacy), each finding verified, all fixed with a test that fails without the fix. The worst finding: moving from Forever to days saved 365 first, which could delete older minutes. That is fixed.
- **After merging current main**: re-checked the settings, i18n and knowledge web tests (767), the mock tests, and the kb and prompts Go tests.

Known failures that come from main, not this PR:
- `TestHardcodedChineseBaseline` on `assistant/direction_progress.go`.
- The sleep ratchet on test files from #3928 and #3903.

**Green:** guards (the sleep ratchet passes after #3921), server build, web, runtimes, scripts shard 0, Android lint-build-test-0, Mac.

**Red, none from this change** (it touches only `docs/`, `scripts/mock`, `server/` and `web/`):

author: brianm-di4u
body:
The nightly Firefox job failed every test at boot on ubuntu-26.04, even with Mesa installed. With no display, Firefox can't create a WebGL context through GLX. Refs #48.

## Change

- `playwright.firefox.config.js` launches Firefox with `MOZ_WEBGL_FORCE_EGL=1` and the `webgl.force-enabled` pref. That gives WebGL2 on Mesa llvmpipe through EGL, so the job keeps the latest runner and the workflow doesn't change.
- Two tests run into software GL itself. They now allow for it, but only on Firefox with software GL:
  - AT-11.1's 30 fps check skips itself there (llvmpipe manages about 9 fps).
  - The kernel check expects bilinear, which is what software GL uses by design (REQ-IMG-33).
- Chrome keeps both checks as they were.

## Testing

- `verify full`: PASS (evidence `1327dc8d05d4`).
- Firefox with no display (WSL Ubuntu 26.04.1, `DISPLAY` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset) on a886838, running the imaging, compare and Firefox boot specs:

  | Firefox config | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | This one | 11 | 1 (AT-11.1) | 0 |
  | Same, with the EGL env and pref removed | 0 | 0 | 8 (every boot and imaging test) |

body:
## 问题与根因
ZCode 桌面 3.18.0 将宿主凭据从 `enc:v1` 信封（派生密钥）迁移到 `enc:v2:{os|env}:{keyId24}:{seal}`：密钥改为 32 字节随机值存入 OS 凭据库（service `ZCode Credential Encryption`，account=sha256(credentials.json 路径).hex）。插件此前只认 v1 → 解密失败 → 额度链 fail-closed，套餐额度 chip 显示「查询失败/未配置」。宿主刷新凭据即完成迁移，旧 v1 值不复存在。

## 改动
- `src/quota/00-constants-and-crypto.cjs`：v1/v2 双信封按宿主语义重写解码。v2 密钥按源分派生（`os`=OS 凭据库，经宿主自带 `@napi-rs/keyring` 读取；`env`=sha256(受管 secret)，文件限 32–4096 字节）；信封内 keyId 指纹比对——换钥作废缓存重读自愈、伪造/损坏信封 fail-closed，绝不跨钥强解；异步预热密钥缓存 + 同步解密；keychain 真失败 60 秒冷却（防每秒风暴）、缓存未热 1 秒短重试；未知 `enc:` 版本拒绝（对齐宿主 throw 语义）；keyring 负缓存按 resourcesDir 分桶；Linux 透传宿主同款 secret-service 选项。
- `src/quota/05-scheduler-and-exports.cjs`：绑定上下文与预热接线；缓存未热的解密失败走 1 秒短重试。
- spec/docs：`.zcode/rules/quota.md` 信封契约、`docs/quota-support-audit.md` 版本中立表述、`AGENTS.md` 代码地图行。
- 测试：v2 用例 4→10（换钥自愈、SECRET_FILE 三态、双 env 同设、keychain 寻址与分桶、截短 tag、畸形 secret、未知 enc:、上界 4096）。

## 验证
- 独立审查两轮（第①轮 3 路：正确性/变异测试/文档面；修复后第②轮 2 路全新实例：调度级假时钟实证 + 变异抽杀）：9 项修复全部验证落地，无 BLOCKER/MAJOR；4 条有界 MINOR 已在下方如实披露。
- `quota-client.test.cjs` 115/103（10 个 v2 用例全绿；12 红与基线 72af87d 失败集合同名，均为本机既有环境性 reset-client 失败）；`model-puller.test.cjs` 68/67+1 skip 全绿；`overlay-quota-chip` 54/54 绿；`build_quota.py --check`、`sync_plugin.py --check`、`node --check` 通过；根产物与插件副本字节一致。
- 构建产物在本机真环境端到端验证：keychain 读钥 → keyId 指纹匹配 → 真实凭据解密成功（v2:os 主路径）。
- 基线对照（pristine 72af87d 全树对跑）：失败集合逐名相同或为子集，零新增失败。

## 未验证项
- macOS / Linux 的 OS 凭据库读取未实机验证（Linux 已透传宿主同款 secret-service 选项）。
- v2:env（受管 secret）以合成测试 + 宿主语义对照验证，无真账号配置该场景。
- 4 条已知 MINOR（有界、fail-closed）：持久 keyId 失配（如跨机复制凭据）无冷却但频率有界；keychain 模块缺失时冷却内存在内存级空转；换钥重读实际发生在下一 tick（自愈时延 ~2–3 秒）；插件 base64url 解码接受集略宽于宿主（GCM 认证兜底）。

### 发版说明素材
- 类型：修复
- 用户可见条目：
  - 修复：升级 ZCode 3.18.0 后套餐额度 chip 显示「查询失败/未配置」的问题——适配宿主新凭据信封（enc:v2，密钥迁入操作系统凭据库），旧 enc:v1 凭据照常兼容，无需配置迁移或用户操作。

author: scolastico
body:
## About The Pull Request

> [!WARNING]
> **Before merging, the GitHub Pages deploy method has to be changed in the repository settings:** Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source must be set to **GitHub Actions** instead of "Deploy from a branch". With this PR both the code documentation and the map diffs are deployed by their workflows. If the source stays on the `gh-pages` branch, GitHub keeps running its own branch build on every push, and that build times out after ten minutes once the site holds many map files.

Adds a map diff viewer for pull requests. When a PR changes a station map, CI renders that station before and after the change with the [splurt-atlas](https://github.com/scolastico/splurt-atlas) generator and publishes a side by side comparison on GitHub Pages, next to the existing code documentation. A bot comment on the PR links to it. The main atlas stays hosted on the splurt-atlas repository; only the diffs live here.

**New workflow: `.github/workflows/atlas_map_diff.yml`**

- **Find changed stations:** reads the `_maps/*.json` station configurations and the PR's changed files, and selects only the stations whose map files changed. A PR that touches no station map stops after this job, which takes about ten seconds.
- **Render:** renders the selected stations at the merge base and at the PR head, in parallel on two runners. Both use the same generator image digest so generator changes cannot show up as map changes.
- **Publish:** writes the result to `atlas-diff/pr-<number>/` on the `gh-pages` branch and deploys the complete branch to Pages. The folder is removed again when the PR is closed or no longer changes a station map.
- **Comment:** waits until the diff is live, then creates or updates one comment with a link per changed station.

At most 6 stations are rendered for one PR; any further changed stations are listed in the comment as not rendered. Only station map changes trigger a render, so icon or code changes that alter how a map looks do not.

**Changed workflow: `.github/workflows/generate_documentation.yml`**

- The documentation deploy replaced the whole `gh-pages` branch every six hours. It now keeps the `atlas-diff/` folder.
- It deploys Pages from a workflow artifact after updating the branch, the same way the map diff workflow does.
- It shares a queued concurrency group with the map diff publish job, so the two never update the branch at the same time and deployments stay in order.

**Security**

The workflow runs on `pull_request_target` so that PRs from forks get a diff too. Files from the PR are only ever read as data: by `jq` in the first job, and by the generator, which runs in a container without network access, without credentials and with a read-only checkout. No script from the PR is executed. The write permissions are limited to the publish and comment jobs.

The generator is my own code and the workflow pulls it by the `latest` tag, so it runs here without having been reviewed by SPLURT maintainers. That is safe with regard to tokens and secrets because it only ever runs inside the Docker container described above: no token or secret is passed into it, it has no network access, all capabilities are dropped, and the only thing it can write is its output folder. It cannot read or leak anything from the repository's CI, and it cannot push anywhere. What it does control is the content of its output, the viewer and map data that the publish job then puts under `atlas-diff/` on Pages. If you want to rule out unreviewed updates entirely, pin `ATLAS_IMAGE` to a digest.

**Notes for maintainers**

- The generator image is `ghcr.io/scolastico/splurt-atlas:latest`, which is public. It can be pinned to a digest in the `ATLAS_IMAGE` variable at the top of the workflow.
- The concurrency groups use `queue: max`. actionlint does not know this key yet; GitHub accepts it.
- The `github-pages` environment must allow deployments from the default branch, which is the default setting.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Map PRs are hard to review from a `.dmm` text diff. With this, reviewers and mappers get a link in the PR that shows the old and the new station next to each other, with every changed tile ringed and the tile contents of both revisions in the inspector. Nobody has to check out the branch or open a map editor to see what a PR does to a station.

It is cheap to run: only the changed stations are rendered, both revisions render in parallel, and PRs without map changes cost one short job. The test run below took about six and a half minutes from push to comment for one station.

## Proof Of Testing

Tested end to end on my fork, with Actions enabled and the Pages source set to GitHub Actions:

- **Map diff on a PR:** [test PR](https://github.com/scolastico/babylon13/pull/1) swapping a stool and a table on Box Station. The [workflow run](https://github.com/scolastico/babylon13/actions/runs/42873994978) selected Box Station only, rendered both revisions, published and deployed them and posted the comment. The [live diff](https://scolastico.github.io/babylon13/atlas-diff/pr-1/#m=boxstation&old=./base/) shows both revisions with 4 changed tiles and no failed requests.
- **Removal on close:** a [second test PR](https://github.com/scolastico/babylon13/pull/2) changing Runtime Station got its diff published and was then closed. The [removal run](https://github.com/scolastico/babylon13/actions/runs/42876777513) deleted `atlas-diff/pr-2/` from `gh-pages`, redeployed the site (the folder now returns 404, the first PR's diff is still live) and updated the comment.
- **Documentation deploy keeps the diffs:** [Generate documentation](https://github.com/scolastico/babylon13/actions/runs/42876157725) was run while a diff was published. `atlas-diff/` was kept and the [code documentation](https://scolastico.github.io/babylon13/) and the diff were both live afterwards.

Before that, the station selection, the publish and removal step and the comment step were each run locally against the real station configurations, and the published generator container was run locally with the exact flags the workflow uses.

Not tested: a PR from a fork of the repository (both test PRs came from branches of the same repository), and a PR that changes more than 6 stations on GitHub (the cap was only exercised in the local run of the selection step).

<details>
<summary>Screenshots/Videos</summary>

Live diff of the first test PR: https://scolastico.github.io/babylon13/atlas-diff/pr-1/#m=boxstation&old=./base/

</details>

author: andylynch
body:
## What

A password-gated page (port 8100, compose profile `demo`) for showing aeronfire to people and letting them break it:

- **Cluster:** crash, stop, freeze, restart a member; add delay/jitter/loss (`tc netem`); wipe a member's state so it rejoins from nothing.
- **Risk controls:** credit breach, halt a loan, sanctions hit, kill switch (four-eyes release), throttle, tight price collar. Done through the control plane API as named users, so entitlements and approvals apply.
- **Load and latency:** RFQ rate 0-200/s at runtime, live RFQ-to-quote p50/p99/p99.9/max.
- **Timeline:** times the election, trading resuming and each control biting, from the monitor feed.

Run it: `DEMO_PASSWORD=... docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/demo-lockdown.yml --profile demo up -d --build`, then http://localhost:8100 (user `demo`). README has a new "Demo panel" section.

## Changes outside the new `io.aeronfire.demo` package

- `VenueControl` + `VenueSimulator`: optional control port (`VENUE_CONTROL_PORT`) to change the rate and read latency; stats are published from the loop thread, so the histograms stay single-threaded.
- `ClusterNode`: if `/tmp/aeronfire-wipe` exists at start-up, delete local Aeron/archive/cluster state first.
- `Dockerfile`: `iproute2` for `tc`. `docker-compose.yml`: `NET_ADMIN` on the members, `venue-live` and `demo` services under the `demo` profile. `deploy/demo-lockdown.yml` rebinds every other published port to loopback.

## Security

The panel mounts the Docker socket, which is root on the host if the panel is compromised. Mitigations: password (constant-time), 1 change/s rate limit, required `X-Demo-Request` header (CSRF), allowlisted member services and operations, range-checked numbers, fixed command templates, no general exec. Auto-heal (60s) and auto-revert (120s) put things back. For a public host, put Cloudflare Access in front too and consider a socket proxy. The demo-lockdown file matters: the base compose publishes the control plane (password = user name) and Jolokia (`jolokia/jolokia`) on all interfaces.

## How it was checked

The sandbox has Java 21, no Gradle distribution and no Docker daemon, so **I could not run the Gradle build, the JUnit tests, or a real cluster.** What I did run:

- Compiled the whole demo package with `javac -Xlint:all` (clean) and ran it against a fake Docker daemon (Unix socket, chunked responses), monitor, venue and control plane: auth, CSRF, rate limit, every fault op, all six scenarios incl. four-eyes approve and throttle/collar interaction, auto-revert, reset, and the measured-recovery timeline.

author: blegat
body:
`cvp` now builds its critical point equations with `PolyJuMP.lagrangian_kkt`, so it also accepts a semialgebraic set: `cvp(p, set, maxdegree)` computes a polynomial whose roots contain the critical values of `p` on `set`. `cvp(p, maxdegree)` is unchanged. Since `lagrangian_kkt` builds a DynamicPolynomials system, the cvp tests now use DynamicPolynomials.

Update to MultivariatePolynomials v0.6, MultivariateBases v0.4, MultivariateMoments v0.5 and SumOfSquares v0.8:
* `MB.MonomialBasis` is replaced by `MB.SubBasis{MB.Monomial}`.
* The rows and columns of `LazyMatrix` are now sorted monomial vectors since `MB.keys_as_monomials` allocates a new vector at each call. They are converted to a `SubBasis` in `nullspace`.

SumOfSquares v0.8 requires DataStructures v0.19 which requires recent versions of Manopt and ManifoldsBase:
* `retract_project!` no longer takes the step length.
* The Levenberg-Marquardt Jacobian is now expected in the default orthonormal basis without receiving it as keyword argument.
* The initial point is passed as keyword argument to the solver state and must be on the manifold, otherwise Levenberg-Marquardt does not converge anymore.
* `ArrayPartition` comes from RecursiveArrayTools.

The dependencies are not released yet so they are taken from `[sources]` and CI now tests Julia v1.10 instead of v1.6.

author: 4thlabs
body:
## What

Closes #138: Quoll against third-party clients and servers, for HTTP, server-sent events and WebSocket, each way, before step 6, as the maintainer asked. The gate that closes the protocol layer: afterwards, only what touches security or stability. Nothing broke.

- `tests/interop/server.cpp`, `quoll_interop_server`: the routes the runs use, `/hello`, `/echo`, a chunked body `/pieces/{n}`, server-sent events `/events/{n}`, `/close`, and a WebSocket echo `/ws`, on 0.0.0.0.
- `tests/interop/client.cpp`, `quoll_interop_client`: `http`, `sse`, `ws` checks against a third-party server serving the same routes, and `autobahn`, the client Autobahn's fuzzing server drives.
- `tests/interop/peers/`: the third-party ends, each run in a container: curl; Python's requests, httpx, http.client and websockets, and an aiohttp server; Node's fetch, node:http and WebSocket, and a node:http and ws server; nginx as a reverse proxy in front of Quoll's server; Autobahn's configurations.
- `tests/interop/run.sh`: runs them on a Docker network, Quoll's programs in the container `QUOLL_CONTAINER` (quoll-work by default), which it joins to the network as `quoll`.
- `QUOLL_INTEROP` builds the two programs; the PRs' CI compiles them, as it does the load. `interop.yml` runs everything every night, and on a PR touching it, in Debug for the library's assertions, keeping Autobahn's reports.
- Docs: `docs/development.md`, `AGENTS.md`.

## Results

| Way | Peers | |
|---|---|---|
| third-party clients → Quoll's server | curl (keep-alive, a POST of 2 MiB after its 100, chunked upload, SSE, HTTP/1.0, HEAD, 404) | 10/10 |
| | Python: requests, httpx, a raw 100-continue, http.client on one kept connection and HTTP/1.0, websockets (echo, 1 MiB, ping and pong) | 7/7 |
| | Node: fetch (POST streamed chunked, SSE), node:http on one kept connection, WebSocket | 8/8 |
| Quoll's client → third-party servers | Node (node:http, ws), aiohttp, nginx in front of Quoll's server: one kept connection for GETs and a POST, 1 MiB, chunked, a close, a GET and a POST after 6 s idle past the servers' idle time, SSE, WebSocket with its close | 30/30 |
| Autobahn, WebSocket | Quoll's server, Quoll's client: 301 cases each way | 296 OK, 2 NON-STRICT, 3 INFORMATIONAL, 0 failed |

The two non-strict cases (6.4.3, 6.4.4): an invalid UTF-8 sequence across fragments, which Quoll finds at the end of the message rather than at the fragment. The informational ones (7.1.6, 7.13.1, 7.13.2) carry no verdict. Sections 12 and 13, `permessage-deflate`, are left out: Quoll offers no extension.

A POST after 6 s idle against Node, which closes idle connections after 5 s, and nginx and aiohttp, set to 3 s: the check from #130 finds the connection closed and opens another.

Left for later, in #149 with the maintainer: HTTP/1.1 has no conformance suite as Autobahn is, so differential parsing (HTTP Garden), request smuggling scanners, and HTTP/2 at a proxy in front of HTTP/1.1 pods.

## Review

Three rounds of `/code-review high`. None found a bug of the library; what they found in the harness, fixed:
- a local run that never joined Quoll's container to the network; Autobahn runs that ignored their program's failure and could read a former report, which its root-owned files kept; a server started again before the former had gone, and waited for a fixed second; nothing bounding a peer, then a bound that killed the Docker client but not the program; a Python wait for the 100 that spun at a close;
- checks that did not check what they said: a kept connection that compared bodies (now the connection, numbered by the servers, or the clients' socket), an `Expect: 100-continue` through http.client, which sends the body at once (now by hand), and curl, which gives up waiting after a second (now waited for and checked), a ping whose pong was not awaited, a close whose answer was not read, aiohttp's connection ids that memory reuses and a `/close` that did not close, an idle time below the servers' but Node's, Autobahn's close verdict not counted;
- `QUOLL_HOST`, which nginx and Autobahn hard-coded; a WebSocket echo written three times (now `quoll::test::websocket_echo`); the PRs' CI not compiling the programs; RelWithDebInfo dropping the library's assertions; includes; names.

Codex's four points, fixed in 5528fc9: http.client's socket taken before a closing response clears it; curl's five URLs each answered 200 on one connection; the 1 MiB echo compared byte for byte; an Autobahn case that cannot start failing the run. Four more rounds of `/code-review high` on that fix, what they found fixed too: the bodies on the kept connection; a report that must hold the 301 cases of the image, now pinned by digest, read whatever the program's end, and a report missing or cut short failing; three cases in a row not started ending the run at once with every case left counted, each exchange bounded at 60 s, tried by killing Autobahn mid-run and by freezing it; Autobahn's logs when it never answers; messages.

Codex's next point, fixed in 322a037: curl's status lost in a pipe or a `$(...)`, so that a response cut short passed. Each check now reads curl's body once curl has succeeded, compares it byte for byte, shows it on a failure, and bounds curl at 30 s. Each was tried against a server answering slightly wrong, and a body without its last chunk; the review of that fix found no bug beyond what it fixed.

Not taken: the count of 301 written in `run.sh` rather than derived from the configurations, as it goes with the image's digest beside it; an `std::optional` around a case's connection, which a helper would return as well.

## Borrow check

No library code changes. In the two programs: the lambdas given to `check()` are awaited at once within it, their captures (`client`, `url`) in the caller's frame, which outlives them; `running.socket` is moved into `websocket_echo`, which owns it until it ends.

body:
Closes #1486. Serves #1329 (`mission_webgl`).

## What changes
- Problem: opening Jetson's board shows columns of text running off the top and bottom edges, and dense text over the parts. It reads like a rendering bug, but the board file carries that text on its fab layers, and kicad-cli draws the same thing from F.Fab and B.Fab.
- Every one of those texts is also a DOM node in WebGL's text layer, so it costs every pan.
- Change: a board with no stored choice opens with its fab rows hidden, on the canvas and in a board view beside it. The layer list and the All preset still show them.
- Change: storage now keeps "show every layer" as `[]` rather than deleting the key. Otherwise a reader who turned fab back on would lose that choice on reload.
- Problem: zoomed in, WebGL draws courtyard and silkscreen outlines as 1px hairlines, while SVG and KiCad draw them at their width. GL lines are always 1px wide.
- Change: each packed record carries its line's width in micrometres in its two spare bytes. WebGL draws the line as triangles once that width spans a canvas pixel, and as a GL line below that. The lines stay line primitives, so a click still passes through them to the part.

Minimal example:
```
/designs/jetson/designs/jetson/view?mode=webgl&sheet=board
```
- Today: every layer shows, fab included, and text covers the board and runs past its edges.
- Expected: F.Fab and B.Fab start unticked in the layer list, and the board shows its copper and silkscreen.

## Before / after
Jetson's board in WebGL, headed on an M5 Pro. "Before" is the board after clicking All, which is how main opens it. "After" is how this branch opens it.

| Before (main) | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/55e5091a37bb5ce5b0e31eccde90786072aba7ad/1486-before.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/55e5091a37bb5ce5b0e31eccde90786072aba7ad/1486-after.png?raw=true) |

kicad-cli's export of F.Cu, B.Cu, the edge, both silkscreens, Dwgs.User, Eco1.User, Eco2.User and both courtyards, with F.Fab and B.Fab left out. The parts, copper and text sit where ours puts them, the 1 mm `+12V` track along the bottom edge and the 1 mm `VCC` track on B.Cu at the top included. KiCad fills a pour solid where we wash it, and uses its own palette. The frame leaves the inner layers out because KiCad's single-file plot paints their pours over F.Cu, and a plane then covers the front copper. Its export of F.Fab and B.Fab draws the same columns of text as "before".

![kicad-cli, outer layers](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/f44e05a38eb8851d6b6393a0dceef467b0696dd0/1486-kicad-outer.png?raw=true)

Zoomed into the USB-C corner. On main WebGL draws the cyan courtyards and the magenta and yellow outlines as hairlines. On this branch they match the width SVG gives them. The two zooms aren't pixel-aligned, since each renderer measures its wheel zoom on its own.

| WebGL on main | WebGL on this branch | SVG |
|---|---|---|
| ![webgl before](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/3ec3abf5eb5b0ce51efb2245701398d2e27114e0/1486-zoom-webgl-before.png?raw=true) | ![webgl after](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/3ec3abf5eb5b0ce51efb2245701398d2e27114e0/1486-zoom-webgl-after.png?raw=true) | ![svg](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/3ec3abf5eb5b0ce51efb2245701398d2e27114e0/1486-zoom-svg-after.png?raw=true) |

## Prerequisite knowledge
- [The web client](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/viewer/fab-hidden-1486/docsite/content/architecture/web-client.md), the board-layer bullets, covers how the canvas and each board view keep their own hidden set. The new bullet sits right after them.
- [Geometry and rendering](https://github.com/panyam/agni/blob/viewer/fab-hidden-1486/docsite/content/architecture/geometry-and-rendering.md), the copper-width paragraph, explains why copper already packs as triangles. The new paragraph on outlines sits right after it.

## Reviewer's guide
- A road atlas can print every contour line, but it opens on roads and towns, with terrain as an overlay you turn on.
- The fab layers are the terrain. They're useful when you go looking, and they bury the page when you didn't ask.
- An atlas that forgot whether you turned the terrain on would be worse than one that never offered it, so "everything on" has to be remembered as a choice. Storage used to treat an empty hidden set as no choice at all.
- So the PR adds one default, uses it only where no choice exists, and stores the empty choice.
- The outlines are the atlas's road edges. Zoomed into one town, a road prints at its real width. On the whole-country page it prints as a fine line, since the real width would vanish.

Read in this order:
1. [web/src/boardlayers.ts](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-8e654e0a1bd1808302b5eec40a193d9ae7bb3a0a815c20711e1f829e97750283): start here. `defaultHidden`, and the `save` that keeps `[]`.

6. [core/render/collector.go](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-a0235700614399e1f0ba73be1038b63f0690e45d06cec4733d624143865592ee) and [core/render/packboard.go](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-0a0d89540f7ac83d4893ced71489120c9d087d27ae6b6f4dc2e49a74332b5144): a board graphic packs with its width, and [core/render/board_stroke_test.go](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-7ff959cadc38e6d32583b929cf6e311aa8c299464f879cb451bab66e87523caf) checks the bytes.

[web/src/packed.ts](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-6902b84d2506db6ba7b3ace2082d447110812c2ae6f89459da8e91781fbf393f) and [web/src/packed.test.ts](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-4f521aadee0de2958d95221ddb20359c557d37823376765489121e41361800e1): the decoder reads the width.

[web/src/webgl.ts](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-bddb4e7fa359fbef2a938de22ebec37719bc1b92fbe0ee4b0475b924d094bdd2) and [web/src/webgl.test.ts](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-ab8784a7f55f7babdb78157590b116eadcad3c93346fdad54b3d70fbcf89d029): `strokeQuads`, and the per-frame choice between the triangles and the line.

Skim or skip: [docsite/content/architecture/web-client.md](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-21554a1f63663ebba49f6fe50c08125719be21cf405c0b4d32a248dbcd5300c6), [docsite/content/architecture/geometry-and-rendering.md](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-c0edf6af31200e3c578f492b447bc91ad2456cc94593f4a71b38c4eba99bc025), the generated `geom_packed` files, and [web/src/fakegl.ts](https://github.com/panyam/agni/pull/1487/files#diff-328e94e4ff4a2e2bed44595c20f3d42c959a006a42b18aeec4ee472011b02a64). author: boesing
body:
## Summary

Until now `/oauth2/idpresponse` dropped every ID token claim that is not a scalar. A claim like `roles: ["A", "B"]` therefore never reached the user, even when it was mapped explicitly.

Such claims are now kept as described in the [attribute mapping documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-specifying-attribute-mapping.html):

> When IdP attributes contain multiple values, Amazon Cognito flattens all values into a single comma-delimited string enclosed in the square-bracket characters `[` and `]`. Amazon Cognito URL form-encodes the values containing non-alphanumeric characters except for `.`, `-`, `*`, and `_`.

Example: `roles: ["FOO_BAR", "Document.Read"]` mapped to `custom:roles` becomes `custom:roles = "[FOO_BAR, Document.Read]"`.

Only OIDC federation is changed. SAML still takes the first `AttributeValue` per attribute.

## ⚠️ Potential breaking change

Multi-valued claims were silently dropped before and are now stored as user attributes.

This also applies to claims **without** a mapping rule. MiniStack currently stores unmapped claims under their original name, which this PR does not change. AWS ignores them.

For example, Entra ID's `amr: ["pwd", "mfa"]` becomes the user attribute `amr = "[pwd, mfa]"`. It then shows up in `AdminGetUser`/`ListUsers`, in ID tokens and in `/oauth2/userInfo`.

The follow-up PR that writes mapped federation attributes only resolves this: unmapped claims, multi-valued or not, are no longer written.

## Evidence

- AWS documentation, quoted above.
- **Not yet validated against a real AWS account.** The documentation does not specify:
  - whether there is a space after the comma; this PR assumes there is one, `[a, b]`, like Java's `List.toString()`
  - how `~` and spaces are encoded; this PR assumes `%7E` and `+`

## Tests

`tests/test_cognito.py`:

- `test_cognito_oidc_federation_flattens_multi_valued_claims`

Omit absent options, request bodies and response-decoding fields. Preserve operation-body precedence for inferred mutators and keep success-only validation/date hooks out of error decoding. Add strict generated-code regression coverage and regenerate the affected shared-runtime fixtures and snapshots.

author: lazbutton
body:
## Le défaut

Le conducteur date une coupure molle (« Attend la fin ») de la fin du titre à cheval sur sa minute : une coupure de :20 est prévue à 10:22:16. `_planned_anchor_item` ne reconnaissait une ligne qu'à l'heure et à la minute de la coupure. La ligne glissée n'était pas trouvée : l'antenne tirait de son côté un son du bac, et la ligne prévue restait « prévu ». Deux lignes au conducteur pour une coupure, et un bac en Aléatoire de plusieurs sons jouait un autre son que celui annoncé.

## Le correctif

Dans `engine/radiotomate/scheduler/clock.py`, une ligne est celle de l'occurrence quand elle porte la minute de la coupure, par son heure ou par `details.minute`, et tombe dans l'heure qui suit cette occurrence, date comprise. Le reste de `tick()` ne change pas.

## Les tests

14 cas dans `engine/tests/scheduler/test_execution.py`. Avec le code de `main`, 9 échouent. Chaque clause de la condition est tenue par un cas. `./scripts/verifier.sh moteur version donnees` : vert, 537 tests passés.

## À relire en particulier

- **Coupure dure, deux cas changent.** Une ligne restée « prévu » un autre jour à la même heure, après un direct qui l'avait retenue par exemple, passait devant celle du jour : elle n'est plus reprise. Et une coupure passée de molle à dure après la prévision reprend sa ligne glissée.
- **Une coupure molle joue la ligne prévue telle quelle**, comme une dure : un son désactivé après la prévision passe encore, jusqu'à « Reconstruire le conducteur ». Avant, l'antenne tirait un son prêt.
- **Ce que le correctif ne fait pas** : une coupure molle dont le titre finit après le changement d'heure ne passe toujours pas. La branche `moteur/coupure-molle-apres-l-heure`, bâtie sur celle-ci, le corrige et suivra.

## Les commits

Le correctif (`d19165c`), une fusion de `main`, puis les retouches d'une relecture indépendante (tests et textes, rien dans `clock.py`). `d19165c` n'est pas réécrit : l'autre branche est bâtie dessus.

author: stuartharris
body:
Closes #658. #657 added `notify_every` to `crux_time` on `master` after this stack was written, so the shipped time protocol and handlers did not know the operation. This PR adds it on top of the stack. I tried to fold the work into #651, #605 and #606, where the files come from, but the generator change conflicts through about 30 later commits.

There are two commits, and I suggest that you read them in order.

**`fix(typegen): emit EffectSink when a shell protocol is emitted`**

`notifyEvery` is the first shipped protocol method for a stream, so it is the first to name `EffectSink`. The handler API emitted the sink, which means that `without_effect_handlers()` removed it, and the protocol then did not compile. The sink is the same generic type for every app, so type generation now emits it once when the handler API is on, or when it emits a shell protocol. With the handler API on, the generated code does not change.

Two things here are not ideal:

- With a protocol and no effect, `build` now rejects every reserved generated name for an app type, not only `EffectSink`.
- An `Effect` in a namespace with the handler API on would get two sink types. That configuration does not compile today for other reasons, so I left it.

**`feat(time): handle notify_every in the shipped protocol and handlers`**

Each handler calculates every tick from a monotonic start time, so the timer does not drift, and a late wake sends one tick instead of a burst.

The handlers stop only when a `ClearTimer` request arrives. If the app aborts the command, the shell is not told, and the timer continues for the life of the app. #662 proposes how to tell the shell. I think this is good enough for now, but it is the part most open to argument.

A tick that is already under way can reach the core after the clear. The handlers do not lock against that, because the generated Swift and Kotlin `Core` queue each resolve, so a lock in the handler cannot prevent it. The docs say that the core ignores that tick, and that is true only with #663 under the stack.

All four language harnesses ran locally. Swift ran on macOS only, so Linux is not yet checked. I did not build the weather shells against this.

author: skyfuller1303
body:
**Merge after #57 (P1-1).** The diff of this PR alone: [team-1-schema...team-2-space-layer](https://github.com/Skyfuller1303/craft-cloud/compare/team-1-schema...team-2-space-layer).

P1-1 added the tables and the store functions for team spaces. This adds the server side that uses them: a request can name a space, the server decides what the account may do there, and every route says which role it needs. No client sends the header yet, so a server running this answers an agent or app exactly as before. I kept it separate from the member and admin routes (P1-3) because this is the permission code, and I wanted it reviewable without the routes around it.

## What

- **The `craft-space` request header** (`SPACE_HEADER` in `craft-cloud-proto`): one hyphenated space UUID, on every space-scoped route. Without it the space is the device's personal space, and nothing more is looked up. A malformed header (not a UUID, not the hyphenated form, two headers) is `400 invalid`. A space that does not exist and a space the account has no access to are the same `404 not_found`.
- **The echo:** every answer of a space-scoped route carries `craft-space` with the space the server worked on, also without a request header (the personal space's ID) and also on the layer's own `404` and `403`. A new agent will refuse an answer whose echo is missing or different, which closes the hole where an older server would ignore the header and answer about the personal space. `craft-epoch` on those routes is now the working space's epoch; the account routes keep the personal one.
- **`require_space`** (new `apps/craft-cloud-server/src/space.rs`), a layer after `require_device`: reads the account's role with `Meta::space_access` on every request (nothing is cached), refuses a role below the route's minimum, and puts a `SpaceAccess { space, role, personal, required }` in the request. Every space-scoped handler now takes its space from it. The roles per route are in one place, `space_routes` in `api.rs`, as in the spec's table: viewer reads (`/space`, `/tree`, `/changes`, `GET /chunks`, `GET /manifests`, history, trash list), editor writes (`/chunks/missing`, `PUT /chunks`, `PUT /manifests`, `/commit`, `/saves`, restore, restore from the trash), owner removes from the trash.
- **`403 read_only`** (new code `read_only` in `craft-cloud-api`) for a member whose role is too low, and for the owners and editors of an archived space (archived caps a role at viewer). Never 401, which the agent reads as "this device was signed out".
- **The role is checked again inside the write transaction**, in the same transaction that locks the space's row, so a role lowered, a member removed or a space archived between the layer and the write is respected. New: `Meta::guarded(WriteGuard { user, min })` returns a handle whose `commit`, `restore_from_trash`, `restore_version`, `attach_save`, `request_purge`, `add_chunk(s)` and `add_manifest` read the role again after taking the lock (Postgres: `FOR UPDATE` for commits and restores, `FOR SHARE` for uploads, which therefore don't wait for each other but do wait for a member change). The handlers get that handle from `SpaceAccess::meta`; in a personal space it is the plain handle, since its owner is its only member. Refused: `read_only`, or `not_found` if the access is gone.
- **Long-polls:** a `GET /changes` waiting on a team space is woken by `Notifier::members_changed(space)` and reads the access again; if it is gone, the answer is `404`. The member routes of P1-3 will call it; a waiter in another process notices at the end of its wait (at most 60 s).
- **Live:** the WebSocket upgrade goes through the layer too. Until live protocol 3 exists (a role per frame), a team space's upgrade answers `404` to everyone, so a viewer can never write through a protocol that has no role in it. The personal space is unchanged, with or without the header.
- **Protocol version:** `PROTOCOL_MAX` is 2, `PROTOCOL_MIN` stays 1; `/api/info` says so. The live protocol stays 2.
- **Meta, small:** `MetaError::ReadOnly`; `DeviceAuth::personal_space()` for the account routes that are about the account (`GET /account/usage`, the device layer's epoch, `Session::new`); `Notifier::subscribe_members` and `members_changed`.
- `AGENTS.md`: the workspace map names the space layer.

## Checks

On Windows, through a memory-limited runner:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p craft-cloud-meta -p craft-cloud-api -p craft-cloud-server -p craft-cloud-proto -p craft-cloud-sync -p craft-cloud-agent -p craft-cloud-app --locked` against Postgres 17 and SeaweedFS 4.48, with `CRAFT_CLOUD_REQUIRE_BACKENDS=1`
- `cargo test -p craft-cloud-store -p craft-cloud-meta -p craft-cloud-server --locked`, the same backends (the CI backends job)
- `cargo +1.95 check --workspace --all-targets --locked` (MSRV)

The listed commands passed. No dependency changed, so `cargo xtask licenses` did not need to run. The existing server, sync and agent suites run unchanged apart from two lines: the server's info test expects protocol `1..=2`, and the agent's "incompatible server" test now builds a range above its own maximum instead of hard-coding `2..=3`.

New tests (`apps/craft-cloud-server/tests/spaces.rs`, SQLite and Postgres, plus two in `crates/meta/tests/team_spaces.rs`):

- Every space-scoped route (15) as owner, editor, viewer, an invitation not yet accepted, a stranger, a removed account, a disabled account and a signed-out device, in a team space, and as owner, editor and stranger in an archived one; plus the personal space with no header, with the header, and named by someone else.
- No header is the personal space: the `GET /space` body has exactly the old five fields, the echo is the personal space's ID, and a commit by a client that knows nothing of spaces lands in its own feed and not in the team space's. `/api/info` says `1..=2`.
- The echo and the epoch of the working space; bad and doubled headers; account routes ignore the header.
- A viewer reads a chunk and is refused an upload with `read_only`; an editor is refused removal from the trash and an owner is not; a role lowered or a member removed takes effect with the next request.
- A chunk of the personal space that the store has is `not found` through the team space's header, and `chunks/missing` is answered per space.
- A long-poll on a team space ends with `404` within a second of a member's removal.
- The live upgrade: personal works, a team space is `404` for owner, editor and viewer alike.
- Meta: a write through a guarded handle is refused after the role was lowered (`read_only`), the member removed (`not_found`) or the space archived, takes no sequence number and records nothing, and the plain handle still goes through.
- A test greps the server's source for `auth.space` and `device.space` and pins the files that may call `personal_space()`.

## Latest check of this head

Checked on Windows with Postgres 17, SeaweedFS 4.48 (S3) and `CRAFT_CLOUD_REQUIRE_BACKENDS=1` under a 16 GiB memory limit at `6bfffca`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` pass; `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`: 1793 passed, 1 failed, 2 ignored. The one failure is the desktop test `audit::tests::filters_are_the_closed_list_and_start_the_list_over`, which expects 36 filter choices while this stack adds audit actions (49 now). It counts from `AUDIT_ACTIONS` in the P1-5 PR (#61), so merge P1-1 to P1-5 together.

## Not in this PR

- The member, invitation, usage and admin routes, the audit events for archive and rename, and the CLI: P1-3.
- `GET /space` gaining `kind`, `name` and `role`: P1-3, with the other new fields.
- Live protocol 3 (the space and the role in the welcome, a role per frame): P2.
- The agent sending the header, checking the echo and switching a space to read-only: P1-4 and P1-5.
- The commit-racing-a-downgrade ca
