author: rogeriojorge
body:
`BiotSavart.B` and `BiotSavart_from_gamma.B` repeated the same dense formula, which builds a (coils x quadrature x 3) temporary for every evaluation point, and again for its Jacobian under `jacfwd`. Both now call one `_biot_savart` kernel that sums the same expression over coils with `lax.scan`, 8 coils per step (the last step is padded with zero-current copies), with `jax.checkpoint` on the step so reverse mode keeps no per-coil residuals. Constructors and public API are unchanged.

**Why this form.** The first version of this PR used a different einsum inside the scan and cost 10-30% in warm time. Using the previous kernel's exact expression inside each chunk, with 8 instead of 4 coils per step, removes that cost for everything except a bare `B` call.

**Accuracy.** x64, 4096 random points, 16 and 64 coils, versus the previous kernel: B, dB/dx, kappa from `gc_quantities` and `jax.grad` with respect to the coil dofs agree to 4e-16 .. 1e-15 relative. A traced guiding-centre run differs by 6e-9 relative (adaptive stepping amplifies round-off).

**Numbers (CPU).** Laptop with other jobs running (load about 10-14), median of 3 fresh processes, `examples/input_files/ESSOS_biot_savart_LandremanPaulQA.json` (16 coils) and the same curves with nfp=8 (64 coils), 75 quadrature points. 4096 points for B, dB, gc; grad is of sum |B|^2 over 256 points with respect to all dofs; trace is 1000 guiding-centre particles for 2e-6 s. Times are good to about 10%.

| | warm time old -> new | peak RSS (MiB) old -> new |
|---|---|---|
| 16 coils, B | 13.4 -> 14.0 ms | 462 -> 445 |
| 16 coils, dB | 33.7 -> 23.9 ms | 894 -> 434 |
| 16 coils, gc | 43.9 -> 35.1 ms | 1209 -> 542 |
| 16 coils, grad | 6.1 -> 5.8 ms | 428 -> 406 |
| 16 coils, trace | 2.42 -> 2.17 s | 760 -> 624 |
| 64 coils, B | 50.3 -> 61.7 ms | 939 -> 478 |
| 64 coils, dB | 118 -> 112 ms | 2611 -> 461 |
| 64 coils, gc | 171 -> 142 ms | 3832 -> 574 |
| 64 coils, grad | 19.7 -> 22.7 ms | 716 -> 503 |
| 64 coils, trace | 7.09 -> 4.99 s | 1437 -> 751 |

Small cases are within 5% of the old speed or faster; the only slower entries are a bare `B` on 64 coils (+23%) and `grad` on 64 coils (+15%). Compile time is unchanged within noise.

**Scaling.** Extra peak memory and warm time of the Jacobian of `B` at 1024 points, 16 to 256 coils (`python docs/biot_savart_scaling.py`): the dense sum goes from 207 to 2445 MiB, the scan from 98 to 217 MiB, with the same warm time (8.7 -> 6.7 ms at 16 coils, 141 -> 143 ms at 256 coils).

![Peak memory and warm time versus number of coils](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/uwplasma/ESSOS/01366faf32cedf348040e182c2fd7921883c42b9/docs/_static/biot_savart_scaling.png)

**Tests.** `tests/test_fields.py` now checks, against analytic results independent of the kernel: the scan against a direct sum for chunks that pad, fit exactly and are mostly padding; geometric convergence of the quadrature of a circular loop at an off-axis point (Jackson, ch. 5); div B = 0 and curl B = 0 off the filament through `jax.jacfwd`; and Ampere's law, the circulation of B around a loop linking the coil being mu0 I (and 0 for a loop that does not link it). The on-axis B_z and its derivatives of a loop were already tested.

**Reviewer commands.**
```
JAX_ENABLE_X64=1 python -m pytest -q -n 2 tests          # 394 passed, 1 xfailed; Python 3.10 + JAX 0.6.2: 389 passed, 5 skipped, 1 xfailed
JAX_ENABLE_X64=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_fields.py -k "scan or off_axis or divergence or ampere"
python docs/biot_savart_scaling.py                       # regenerates the figure, prints the numbers
```

**Limits.** No GPU numbers for this version: both workstation GPUs were in use by other jobs. The earlier version of this PR, measured on an idle A4000, cut device peak memory 4-15x; the temporaries are the same size here. Bare `B` on many coils is up to 25% slower than the dense sum. Memory still grows slowly with the coil count (the inputs and the padded copies), about 2x from 16 to 256 coils.

**Overlap.** #152 removes `sqrtg`/`to_xyz` from `BiotSavart` a few lines from the `B` body changed here, so at most a trivial context shift. #190 touches `coils.py`, not `fields.py`.

author: shawnowen
body:
## Problem

Codex threads that use Ollama's own compaction can break for good. `Complete()` closes call/output pairs only through `p.groups`, and synthetic `ollama_compaction_summary` pairs are deliberately left out of those groups. When the summarizer lists a prior summary's output in `retain_item_ids` without its call, the output is saved alone in `retained`.

From then on, every compaction fails in `analyzeCompactionToolState` with `function output has no matching call "call_ollama_compaction_…"` (400, `invalid_request_error`). That happens on both entry points:

1. **Triggered:** `compaction_trigger` on `POST /v1/responses`.
2. **Standalone:** `POST /v1/responses/compact`.

The history stays above the client's auto-compact limit, so every turn compacts first and fails. Two local threads were observed bricked this way, on v0.40.13 and v0.40.15. Upstream `main` had the same file byte-for-byte.

## Fix

- `Complete()` never retains prior summary calls or outputs. The new summary supersedes them, matching the existing `TestRepeatedCompactionReplacesRatherThanNestsPayload` intent.
- `analyzeCompactionToolState` tolerates an orphaned `call_ollama_compaction_*` output, so histories saved by earlier releases compact again. Its text still reaches the summarizer. Any other orphaned tool result is still rejected.

## Tests

- `TestCompactionDoesNotRetainPriorSummaryOutputWithoutCall` covers the malformed write and a round trip through both entry points.
- `TestCompactionRecoversHistoryWithOrphanedPriorSummary/{triggered,standalone}` covers both stalls at the package level.
- `TestResponsesCompactionRecoversOrphanedPriorSummary/{triggered,standalone}` covers both stalls over HTTP and expects 200.
- `TestCompactionStillRejectsOrdinaryOrphanedToolOutputs` is a guard: ordinary orphaned tool results must still be rejected.

Without the source change, every new test except the guard fails with the production error. With it, `go test ./openai/` passes and `go vet ./openai/ ./server/` is clean. In `go test ./server/`, three tests fail (`TestModelOptionsNumCtxPriority`, `TestSchedRequestsSameModelSameRequest`, `TestSchedRequestsMultipleLoadedModels`). They fail the same way on unmodified `main` on this machine, so this change didn't cause them.

## Scope

This PR is in Shawn's fork only and was not opened against `ollama/ollama`. No session stores were edited. Threads that are already bricked recover only once a daemon built with this change is running.

> Changes compaction payload validation and retention logic on a critical Codex code path, though behavior is narrowly scoped to synthetic summary items with backward-compatible recovery.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **Codex threads that permanently failed compaction** when a prior `ollama_compaction_summary` output was kept without its synthetic call, which triggered `function output has no matching call` on every later compaction.
> 
> `Complete()` now **drops all prior summary call/output refs** (`summaryRefs`) from `retain_item_ids`, so each compaction supersedes the previous summary instead of nesting or leaving orphan tool results. `analyzeCompactionToolState` **tolerates orphaned** `call_ollama_compaction_*` outputs from older releases while still rejecting ordinary unmatched tool outputs.
> 
> New package and HTTP tests cover malformed retain behavior, recovery on both `POST /v1/responses` (trigger) and `POST /v1/responses/compact`, and guards for summary-like client `call_id`s.

author: pawellisowski
body:
Refs #806 (regression of #211)

## Root cause

Trimble Identity public clients (PKCE, no client secret) refresh by **serial PKCE**
([Trimble docs](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/authentication/guides/authorization-code-pkce/)).
Every token request registers a new `code_challenge`, and the next refresh must present
its `code_verifier`. AWARE sent neither, so Trimble answered every refresh with 401 and
each sign-in died when its first access token did. #211 added `offline_access`, which gets
a refresh token issued, but that refresh token could never be used.

A second bug hid the first one. `aware connect --refresh` went through the lazy refresh,
which hands back a still-fresh token untouched. So it printed "refreshed" over an expiry
that never moved (issue step 2), and the 401 only showed up after the token had already
expired.

## Fix

- `StoredToken.pkce_verifier` (serde default, left out of storage when absent). The code
  exchange registers the first challenge; each refresh presents the stored verifier and
  registers the next one. Only `trimble-connect` does this (`IntegrationConfig::serial_pkce_refresh`).
  A credential without a verifier refreshes the same way as before.
- `aware connect --refresh` now forces a refresh (`refresh::refresh_now`), as cli-spec says.
  Behaviour change: on a pasted token with no refresh token, it now errors "no refresh_token;
  re-run aware connect" instead of printing "refreshed".
- Trimble refresh tokens are single-use, so two processes refreshing one slot at once leave
  the second one rejected. That loser now returns the fresh token the winner stored, instead
  of failing.
- A Trimble sign-in made before this fix has no verifier. Its rejected refresh now says to
  run `aware connect trimble-connect` again, instead of showing a bare 401. **Existing Trimble
  connections need one new sign-in after upgrading.**
- `--from-file` import keeps a blob's `pkce_verifier`.
- Spec: `10-core/oauth-registration.md`.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` pass. Auth tests: 159 pass.
  New tests cover the two-step verifier chain, the exchange registering the first challenge,
  no PKCE parameters for other providers or for verifier-less credentials, forced refresh,
  concurrent-rotation recovery, the reconnect message, and the import. I disabled
  `serial_pkce_refresh` as a negative control and the chain tests failed.
- Full `cargo test --bins`: 2525 passed, 1 failed:
  `provider_store::tests::a_package_root_must_be_an_absolute_real_directory`. It fails because
  this machine's `TEMP` is an 8.3 short path (`ADMINI~1`) and the test compares it with the
  canonical long path. That file is not touched here.
- **Real CLI end to end** in a throwaway `AWARE_HOME`, against a local stand-in for Trimble's
  token endpoint. The stand-in enforces serial PKCE and single-use refresh tokens as documented,
  and answers 401 otherwise. The run is `aware connect trimble-connect --oauth`, then `--refresh` twice:
  - AWARE 0.175.0 reproduces the issue: the exchange sends no challenge, and `--refresh` prints
    "refreshed" twice with the same `expires_at` and sends no request.
  - This branch: the exchange registers a challenge, both refreshes get 200, each one presents the
    verifier for the previous challenge plus the rotated refresh token, and `expires_at` moves
    each time.
  - Not verified: a live Trimble sign-in. That needs the owner's own sign-in.

Review rounds: 3 (self-feeding: 0) — rounds: Codex r1 clean + code-reviewer (concurrent-refresh loser, exchange untested, legacy message), Codex r2 (import dropped verifier), Codex r3 clean; outcome: all fixed

author: felipedefensor
body:
For TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#157 (WP12, T017). Stacked on #872, which is on #871 (WP3's reader).

## What

`open_corpus`'s default `time_map_of` is now WP9's `tilia_core.timemap.time_map_of`, called with the roles the index resolved, for the documents WP3's reader gives (`corpus.tla_reader.time_map_of`; any other document gets none, so tests with their own reader are unchanged). `build.py` and `scan.py` already stored what a time map gives, so nothing else changes:

- `measures` from `measure_rows()`, and `positions` for every unit whose start lies on the map;
- `files.time_map` from `TimeMap.timeline_id`, and `files.time_map_guessed` from `TimeMap.guessed`;
- the time map kept for `Corpus.time_map(file_id)`, which TQL uses for bars.

## Tests

- New `tests/corpus/test_corpus_positions.py` (written first; 4 of its 5 tests fail without the change): a tapped file with a pickup and a repeat; its `measures` rows and every unit's `positions` equal WP9's own, computed from the file as `tla` reads it (passes, a fractional beat, units off the map); the timeline and `guessed` recorded, with and without a timeline whose role is `time_map`; the time map kept for queries; a file without a beat timeline has neither.
- `test_corpus_examples.py` now runs TQL's 90 examples with WP9's time maps instead of WP13's fake: all pass. Without the new default, the 7 examples that need bars fail.

## How WP9's time map differs from WP12's `contracts/time-map.md`

The issue asks for these to be recorded, so that the contract can follow WP9:

1. `time_map_of(document, roles)` takes a `tla.Document`, not the index's `Document`; the index passes the one its reader read (`TlaDocument.source`). `roles` may hold lists.
2. WP9's measure rows (`MeasureRow`) have no `beat_unit: int`: the beat unit is in `meter` (with `time_signature` and `assumed` computed from it). `pass_` is None for a cadenza bar, and there are `cadenza`, `movement` and `folded`. The `measures` table stores `time_signature`, `cadenza` and `movement` as before, and no beat unit.
3. `Positions.end_bar` is `int | None`, and `pass_` is None in a cadenza; `cadenza` and `movement` are added. The columns are nullable.
4. `position`, `length` and `unit_seconds` take `unit` with no default; the corpus's `TimeMap` protocol gives `"bar"`.
5. WP9's `time_map_of` logs its warnings (several timelines claiming the role, beats past the media, misplaced closing taps) at each call, so the index logs them each time it reads such a file.

## Left open: the time map's reason and warnings

A comment on TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#157 suggests calling `find_time_map` instead, so that the index reports why a file has no time map, and the warnings (several timelines claiming `time_map`, beats past the media) with the file. WP12's data model and contracts have no column or report field for them yet, so this PR follows `contracts/corpus.md` (`time_map_of`, WP9's by default) and doesn't add one. `find_time_map` logs every warning it finds, so they are in the log. Where they should be stored is a question for the contract.

author: arman-jalili
body:
## Two kinds of pin that were not pins

The two wasm engines are pinned exactly and `check-pins.py` refuses a range with a
sentence. The workflows were held to a different standard: every action ran a tag
or a branch, **including the one holding the PyPI token** — and the secret scanner
was pinned to a tag under a comment claiming that a moved image could not happen.

| what | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| actions | `@v4`, `@v5`, `@stable`, `@release/v1` | 40-hex commit + `# vX.Y.Z` on the line |
| `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` | `@release/v1` | `@7245906f…  # v1.14.3` |
| secret scanner | `gitleaks:v8.30.1` | `gitleaks@sha256:c00b6bd0…  # v8.30.1` |
| scanner output | the image name | `▶ scanner: <digest>  (v8.30.1)` |

**Recorded exception:** `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` has no version tag following its
`stable` branch, so it is pinned to the commit behind the moving `v1` tag —
`683b588c…  # v1`. The comment says what was resolved rather than a version number
that does not exist. Every other SHA came from `gh api repos/<action>/commits/<tag>`.

## The guard, and both defects reported together

```
$ # planted: actions/checkout@v4  and  gitleaks:v8.30.1
❌ .github/workflows/ci.yml:24: uses: actions/checkout@v4 is not a commit SHA — a tag or branch can move; pin the 40-hex commit and put the version in a comment
❌ scripts/check-secrets.sh: GITLEAKS_IMAGE is zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.30.1 — a tag can be moved, and then the same command runs a different scanner (pin @sha256:<digest>, tag in the comment)
→ exit 1
```

A SHA *without* the version comment is a third defect with its own wording: the SHA
says what runs, the comment says what it is. `--self-test` covers the action tag,
the uncommented SHA, the tag-pinned scanner and the minor Go floor; the check runs
in `audit.yml` and in `local-ci`.

```
✅ check-pins self-test: a minor floor, an action tag, an uncommented SHA and a tag-pinned scanner are each refused; the pinned shapes are accepted
```

## The seed found two defects in my own work

The `local-ci` seed plants the new surface in a **clean second fixture** (a range
error from the first would otherwise be all the guard had to report). Writing it
went wrong twice, and both times the seed caught it because it asserts the *reason*
each plant is refused:

1. BSD `sed` has no `0,/re/` address — the plant silently did nothing, and the guard
   "passed" on an unplanted file.
2. The plant used single quotes **inside** a single-quoted step string, truncating
   the command: `sed: 1: "s#uses: …": unterminated substitute pattern`.

```
✅ a planted range, a tag-pinned action and a tag-pinned scanner are refused, each by name
```

## Acceptance

- `git grep -nE 'uses: [^ ]+@(v[0-9]|stable|release/)' -- .github/workflows` → nothing
- `git grep -n 'zricethezav/gitleaks:' scripts` → `@sha256:` with the tag only in a comment
- `python3 scripts/check-pins.py --self-test` → planted action and image refused, each named
- `bash scripts/check-secrets.sh` → prints the digest, still clean

## Gate

`bash .ci/local-ci.sh` → **GREEN — 43 step(s) executed**, exit 0.

Closes #105.

author: todd-uams
body:
ShortPixel Image Optimizer's background processor asks `admin-ajax.php` to optimize the next image in the site's shared queue every few seconds on Media and editor screens. The request guard refuses `shortpixel_image_processing` in an Auditor session, and ShortPixel reports each refusal as a fatal error. This turns the processor off for the role and hides the two ShortPixel screens that would still trigger or expose it.

## Approach

- New `includes/ShortPixel.php` returns `true` from ShortPixel's own `shortpixel/processorjs/disable` filter in an Auditor session, and leaves the answer alone for every other role. Media and editor screens still show each image's ShortPixel status.
- `Screens::defaults()` hides `page:wp-shortpixel-settings` (the screen shows the API key, and the role holds `manage_options`) and `page:wp-short-pixel-bulk` (ShortPixel runs the processor there even with the filter set).
- `shortpixel_image_processing` stays off the AJAX allowlist: it writes files and rows.
- Decision recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; the case added to `docs/WRITES-ON-LOAD.md`.

Read against ShortPixel Image Optimizer 6.6.1 (`shortpixel-plugin.php` and `res/js/shortpixel-processor.js`).

## Test plan

- [x] CI passes (Pest, PHPStan, Rector, Pint, mutation, integration, screen walk)
- [ ] As an Auditor on `uamshealth.test`, the Media Library shows no ShortPixel fatal error and still shows the ShortPixel status column

- [ ] As an administrator, ShortPixel's processor still runs on the Media Library

body:
Implements #8187 (broker side, incl. Drews amendments 6776133945 / 6776183066 / 6776188930): no task is assigned to opencode or a specific lane by default and without a specific recorded reason; platform/lane/pool/model/task/session are MARKS — recorded, never a filter or a requirement.

## Changes (Turso backend, pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue)
- **Default = direct.** verb_lane: the hard-coded 1:1 opencode/direct balancing is removed. Fresh assignment = direct, reason=default_direct on lane_assigned. Opencode ONLY via the new `fleet queue lane --opencode-reason <text>`, recorded on the new ledger column `opencode_reason` (schema + additive migration). --exclusion-reason forces direct and wins over --opencode-reason. Platform is NEVER a routing reason (no platform door).
- **Reassignment:** an existing opencode ledger row flips to direct on --exclusion-reason unless a session is bound; flip updates the row, re-syncs progress.lane, emits lane_assigned reason=exclusion reassignment=true.
- **Sink drain:** default_pick_predicate gains a third branch admitting parked handoff sink rows with NO not_before gate and no new placeholders; lanes claim the stranded sink tasks (+0 attempts) and work them direct. Claimant parked_handoff pick + by-id claim unchanged in shape.
- **Platform demoted to a mark (amendment 2):** platform_allows deleted; pick SELECT, claim_update_sql and by_id_claimable no longer filter on platform — a mismatched-platform claim claims the item, a no-platform claim works identically (the claimant `claim --platform openchamber --handoff` path included). The declared platform is stamped on the claimed row via `platform = COALESCE(?, platform)` in both claim UPDATEs and carried on the claimed event. New client flag `claim --session-id` records the claiming sessions id as a mark.
- **Audit marks (amendments 2+3):** events are the append-only audit log. audit_marks/with_marks fill task_id, queue, pool (=queue), platform, lane_id, model (claim_provider/model/variant) and session_id into payloads. Extended events: claimed (pick + by-id), lane_assigned (fresh + flip), lane_session_bound, parked, woken, completed, failed. No update/delete path added for events. A future bulk reset can write a queue_reset event through the EXISTING /events-append verb (kind is a free non-empty string; worker/task optional) — no backend op needed.

## Audit (per #8187 sharpening)
- Enqueue stamps NO lane/assignment (progress={}, no ledger row, platform defaults NULL). The opencode claimant (poll.py/claimant.py) only READS progress.lane to discover candidates; it never assigns and has no lane default. verb_lane was the only assignment producer.

## Tests
7 #8187 regression tests (default direct; opencode-reason door + recording; flip matrix incl. session-bound never flips; sink branch + placeholder count; platform-not-a-lane-input; platform-not-a-claim-filter: mismatch claims / no-platform claims / mark stamped; claim event carries lane/pool/model/session marks). `cargo test -p fleet-queue --all-features`: **149 lib + 2 integration passed, 0 failed** (laptop-verified).

## Review disposition
Codex review hit its usage limit with zero findings (verified: no inline comments, no reviews on the PR). CodeRabbit likewise rate-limited. Basic checks queue for hours and required checks are disabled; merging on laptop-verified targeted tests per the standing #8185 pattern.

Refs #8187

Ordinary exact Python integer/rational arithmetic independently checked the same identities. Neither a computational check nor the AI review is a formal proof certificate.

## Base, provenance and direct dependency

The benchmark checkout is pinned to cdb1ebff130d861e2c61e9cf517ab66c0a56ca7a from Layr-Labs/dcp, track main, required dcp-joint-bounds-v7 policy. Only submission/ is edited in the benchmark checkout.

The material direct source is PSG4-THIRDBASE-REFINED by mpjunior92, submission 53921d7e-f55c-4ca7-b9cd-5b6f1c2d88a0, published archive commit 3335bc78b723613b2424a7fb2f693384537fda86. Its complete submission/proof.md is included unmodified as family-source.md. SHA-256 da756264b856999eee099efbee811a04f8e6e754df5a243e25d2c8086535f008 matches its recorded official evidence. The dependency declaration explicitly selects both the source family/caps and their use in this snapshot. Historical upstream credits are retained inside the unmodified file; no prior acceptance or attribution decision is used as a theorem premise.

The direct source's Section 11 already states and proves the rational q, alpha family. Our selected rational program is q=49/100, alpha=7/16. The source's selected third-base theorem is a different program; proof.md expressly limits its use to the family source and constituent algorithm. Every dependent profile, source confidence, decoder parameter and literal cap is recomputed. A smaller sample coefficient here is not represented as a faster time bound than that source.

## Joint theorem and changes

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, set n=ceil(log2 N), L=log2 n for n>=2,
F=sqrt(nL), G=sqrt(n)L^(-7/16). Define the fixed rational constants

    q=49/100, c=7401/9800, f=2599/7401.

The single algorithm PSG49-F7, specified in Section 2, recovers the entire secret
with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal mixed
coset states. On EVERY execution branch, including failed attempts, incorrect
label extraction, discarded copies and aborts, it has the simultaneous bounds

    T=O(2^(c F+(3/4)G)), S_C=O(n^2), S_Q=O(n),
    Q=O(2^((49/100)F+(3/8)G)).                         (1)

Constants are absolute, independent of N,s and outcomes. n=1 belongs to the
explicit finite algorithm branch and is covered by the same big-O guarantee.
The four growth indices are exactly (1/2,0,0,1/2). Fractional tolerance is 0 in
Section 7's exact clean error model. No cube-root work or optimality is claimed.


The primary new proof is proof.md. It specifies all parameter substitutions, restates the relevant correctness hypotheses, and gives an explicit capacity/gap argument for the exact selected full envelopes. family-source.md retains the complete underlying exact gates, low-bit instrument, decoder and cutoff proofs so that a reviewer need not fetch any paper or prior submission. submission.json supplies four ordered supported dcp-bounds-v4 objects and exact rational indices, followed by one unscored dcp-fractional-error-tolerance-v1 declaration with expression 0. No claim mixes two configurations.

The fixed base fraction is f=2599/7401, not one third. The source's first-feasible profile search uses u=max(1,floor(fR)). The retained widths, q0, hmax, K, Sodd, H0, Qcap, Wcap and extraction precision all follow from that actual integer program. The algorithm never computes real radicals, F, G or the enormous analytical threshold; those are proof tools only. The n<256 branch is the source's bounded exhaustive shift tester and meets the same success guarantee.

## Capacity and positive-gap proof

Exact identities, verified by integer arithmetic, are

    c=q/2+1/(4q), f=(1-2q^2)/(1+2q^2),
    c(1-f)=49/100, (1-f^2)c^2=1/2.                 (2)

For sufficiently large R, u=floor(fR)<=fR and the retained decrement intervals
cover [u,R]. With D_R=max delta(v)<=log2 R+4, integration (the decreasing-step
profile argument in source Sections 9 and 11) gives

    2 S_u(R) >= (R^2-u^2)/D_R >= (1-f^2)R^2/D_R. (3)

Let Rtest=ceil(cF+G/2). Eventually Rtest<=F since c<1 and
G/F=L^(-15/16) tends to 0; the rounding adds at most 1/F. Thus
D_Rtest<=L/2+(log2 L)/2+4. Expanding its numerator with (2) gives

    (1-f^2) Rtest^2 >= nL/2 + (4900/7401)n L^(1/16). (4)

An explicit certificate for the comparison of (4) to nD_Rtest starts at
L0=2^128. There

    (4900/7401)*256 - 64 - 4 = 751132/7401 > 0.

For H(L)=(4900/7401)L^(1/16)-(log2 L)/2-4,

    L H'(L)=(4900/(16*7401))L^(1/16)-1/(2 ln2)>0

for L>=L0, using ln2>1/2 and L^(1/16)>=256. Hence H stays positive.
The additional eventual inequality Rtest<=F is immediate from the displayed
ratio and rounding; taking the maximum of its fixed threshold and L0 suffices.
No special-case branch or preloaded table uses this enormous threshold.
Thus Rtest is eventually feasible, and the literal first-feasible search obeys

    R <= cF+G/2+1.                                  (5)

Also n<=2S_u(R)<=2R^2, so R>=sqrt(n/2). Since f>1/3,
u(R)>=max(1,floor(R/3)); in particular u>=R/8 on the main branch. For large R,
u>=fR/2 and all retained heights are Theta(R) up to constants. Decrements are
Theta(log R), whence mstar=O(R/log R)=O(R/L). The fixed positive f gives
hmax=Theta(R). Source Section 6's stage count is therefore O(1+n/R), K=O(R),
and H0=O(n). All constants here depend only on the displayed absolute rationals.

## 5. Every-branch resources and positive absorption gaps

The exact branchwise ledger of source Sections 4.2, 8-9 now yields

    Q <= Qcap = O(n(2u+6)2^(R-u)),
    T = O(n^(5/2)L^(5/2)2^R),
    S_C=O(n^2), S_Q=O(n).                            (6)

For clarity its applicability is checked explicitly. Each complete combiner
costs O(R^2 L2^v_i) core operations; the used inequality n<=128v_i^2 remains
valid because u>=R/8. Wcap=O(nR2^R/L), so all combiner core work is
O(nR^3 2^R)=O(n^(5/2)L^(3/2)2^R

body:
## Why
The view-only password (`VIEWER_PASSWORD`) worked under any name, so anyone who had it could sign in. It now only works for players on the roster.

## What changed
- **`apps-script/Code.gs`**
  - A view-only sign-in is accepted only if the name is in the **Full Name** column of the **Players** tab in the stats spreadsheet.
    - Capital letters and extra spaces don't matter, but the full name does.
    - Rows whose Player ID starts with `EX` (example rows) and the legend lines above the header are ignored.
  - A name that isn't on the list gets `reason: 'not_on_roster'`, is logged as `failed:roster`, and counts toward the existing lockout (5 failures a minute).
  - Removing a player from the tab also ends their current sign-in: `handlePlays` and `handleCheck` refuse a viewer token whose name is no longer on the roster.
  - The roster is cached for 5 minutes. A missing tab or Full Name column means nobody signs in as view-only.
  - `checkSetup` reports how many names the view-only password accepts.
  - Team and admin passwords are unchanged and work under any name.
- **`assets/js/gate.js`**: the sign-in popup shows "That name isn't on the team list. Use your full name as your coach entered it.", puts the cursor back in the name field, and leaves the password filled in.
- **`assets/js/admin.js`**: the admin list labels these attempts "Failed: name not on team list".
- **`README.md`**: a new "Who can use the view-only password" section.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 342/342 pass.
- New tests in `tests/roster.test.mjs`:
  - listed names sign in, ignoring capital letters and extra spaces;
  - an unlisted name is refused;
  - example rows, the legend and the header aren't accepted as names;
  - unlisted names count toward the lockout;
  - a missing tab or a tab with no name column lets nobody in;
  - coach and admin passwords are unaffected;
  - removing a player ends their sign-in;
  - the popup message and the admin label.
- The shared test helper now sets up a Players tab holding the names the existing viewer tests sign in under.

## After merging
The script lives in Google, so merging doesn't change it. Paste the new `apps-script/Code.gs` into the script editor, then **Deploy → Manage deployments → Edit → Version: New version → Deploy**. Run `checkSetup` to confirm the roster count.

author: moinakmalkhan
body:
## Why the deploy failed

Hostinger's build of `main` (3ea4c1d) crashed in Turbopack before it reached any page code:

```
Failed to write app endpoint /page
Caused by:
- [project]/src/app/globals.css [app-client] (css)
- creating new process
- node process exited before we could connect to it with exit status: 0
```

Turbopack runs PostCSS (Tailwind) on `globals.css` in a separate Node process. On Hostinger's build server that process exits before Turbopack can connect to it. This isn't caused by the code: the same commit builds with Turbopack on macOS and in a clean `node:22` Linux container.

## Changes

- **`npm run build` is now `next build --webpack`.** Webpack runs PostCSS inside the build process, so the step that failed isn't used. Local `npm run dev` still uses Turbopack. The README explains why, so nobody switches it back while the site is on Hostinger.
- **A second phone number.** `contact.phone` is now `contact.phones`, holding `+92 339 4924171` and `+92 304 7884449`. Both numbers show on the contact page and in the footer (so on every page), and each gets its own `ContactPoint` in the Organization JSON-LD. A shared `telHref()` helper builds the `tel:` links. The WhatsApp button still uses `+92 339 4924171`.

## Checks

- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` pass (one existing warning in `opengraph-image.tsx`).
- `npm run build` (webpack) passes on Node 22 on macOS and in a `node:22` Linux container using `npm install`, as Hostinger does.
- Checked in the browser:
  - both numbers on `/contact` and in the footer;
  - `tel:+923047884449` links;
  - the JSON-LD has both numbers;
  - no horizontal scroll at 375 px;
  - `/policy/chess` still renders.

I couldn't run a build on Hostinger itself. Merging starts a new Hostinger build, and that build is the real test.

author: jonringer
body:
## Problem

e801cac synced `default.nix`'s export list with nixpkgs, but didn't sync the sub-libraries those exports come from. Accessing any of 16 top-level names throws `attribute '<name>' missing`:

| Sub-library | Missing names |
|---|---|
| `filesystem` | `baseNameOf`, `dirOf`, `isPath`, `readDir`, `readFileType`, `hashFile` |
| `trivial` | `mul`, `div`, `ceil`, `floor` |
| `derivations` | `addDrvOutputDependencies`, `unsafeDiscardOutputDependency` |
| `strings` | `appendContext` |
| `versions` | `compareVersions` |
| `sources` | `filterSource` |
| `lists` | `replaceElemAt` |

corepkgs works around the `filesystem` names in its `lib.nix`.

## Fix

- Re-export each builtin from the same sub-library that nixpkgs uses.
- Port `lists.replaceElemAt` from nixpkgs. It's the only missing name that isn't a builtin.

## Verification

- **Every top-level attribute:** I evaluated each one separately. On master 20 fail; with this change all of them evaluate except the four release-info names (`version`, `nixpkgsVersion`, `isInOldestRelease`, `oldestSupportedReleaseIsAtLeast`). A follow-up PR handles those.
- **The restored names:** each one, called on real inputs, returns the expected result.
- **`tests/modules.sh`:** failures drop from 55 to 29. None of the remaining failures is new.
- **`filesystem.sh`, `sources.sh`, `network.sh`:** pass, the same as on master.
- **`tests/check-eval.nix`:** already broken on master, because `misc.nix` references an undefined `versions`. This PR doesn't change that.

## Notes

- **Nix versions:** `readFileType` stays a plain builtin, as in nixpkgs, so it's still missing on Nix < 2.14. Use `lib.filesystem.pathType` there, which gets a fallback in #16.
- **Merging:** this PR and #16 edit different hunks of `filesystem.nix`, so they should merge cleanly in either order.

author: maxbernstetter
body:
## Why

- Local and prod authenticate differently: Terraform and six scripts hard-code `test` keys for local, and the Go config falls back to them.
- Secrets are picked up in several ways, so local and CI cannot be compared like for like.

## Target

- The same `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` are read from the environment on both sides: the local environment file (copied from `env.example`) and the CI environment.
- A missing variable fails at once with the names of the missing variables.

## Solution

- `scripts/lib/require-env.sh` (new): `require_env` names the missing variables and points to `env.example`.
- `scripts/infra-apply.sh`, `backfill-start.sh`, `db-migrate.sh`, `frontend-deploy.sh`: call `require_env`, no longer export `test` keys. Local keeps unsetting profile and role variables, so a dev shell cannot route to AWS.
- `infra/terraform/providers.tf`: no `access_key` or `secret_key` override.
- `src/internal/awsenv/awsenv.go`: `Load` uses the default credential chain; the static `test` fallback is gone.
- `Taskfile.yml` (`lake:upload`): passes the variables through instead of literals.
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: the same names in the workflow `env:` (`AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`).
- `env.example`, `README.md`, `infra/terraform/README.md`: document the contract.

## Caveats

- Breaking for existing local setups: an existing environment file without the three `AWS_*` lines now makes `task up` fail. Add them from `env.example`.
- Lambdas do not get `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, so their behaviour is unchanged by the removed fallback. Whether Floci injects credentials into Lambda runtimes is not verified here; CI's end-to-end run is the check.
- Prod is not changed in this PR. There is no deploy workflow and no GitHub `prod` environment yet; the prod side of the contract is documented, not wired.
- Not covered: sourcing the variables through devbox so they are not tied to the dotenv file. Follow-up.

## Testing

- Verified:
  - `scripts/infra-apply.sh local` with the `env.example` values: Terraform applied 3 + 2 + 81 resources on Floci, and `scripts/frontend-deploy.sh local` uploaded the web app. Run from this branch; log kept locally.
  - Guards: `infra-apply.sh local` and `db-migrate.sh local` with the variables unset exit 1 and name the missing variables; `infra-apply.sh prod` without `CI=true` refuses.
  - `go vet ./src/internal/awsenv/` passes; `bash -n` passes on all touched scripts.
- Not run:
  - `task up`, `task test:system` and `task e2e` locally. CI's `floci` job will run them on this PR.
  - Prod apply (not possible outside CI).
  - The unit-test packages: `awsenv` has no tests.
- CI: pending on this PR.

Closes #232

author: roshangbd
body:
## Pourquoi

L'accueil reçoit environ trois visites sur quatre (76 % des visiteurs sur 30 jours dans PostHog, chiffre approximatif, non refait depuis) et parlait à tous les médecins à la fois. La nouvelle page parle d'abord au remplaçant (et à l'interne, au vacataire, à l'activité mixte), dans la nouvelle direction artistique validée : le ciel, l'eau, la mascotte, le jaune réservé à « ce qu'il te reste ».

## Ce qui change

**L'accueil, entièrement.** Dans l'ordre : premier écran « Sors la tête de l'eau » ; « Sous la surface » (aperçu à trois onglets, puis trois grandes cases) ; « Pour qui » (remplaçant, interne, vacataire, mixte) ; Ryan et le film ; syndicats d'internes, partenaires et soutiens ; quatre témoignages, mot pour mot ; tarifs ; dix questions ; six guides ; scène finale.

**Détails visibles** : le logo est le mot « Hippodoc » seul dans le menu et le pied de l'accueil ; un petit bouton met le décor animé en pause ; sur ordinateur, la bannière cookies se range en bas à gauche.

**À savoir** : entre cette mise en ligne et l'étape suivante (sept jours au plus), l'accueil et les autres pages n'ont pas le même menu ni le même pied.

**Ce qui disparaît de l'accueil** : « En chiffres », les 12 fonctionnalités, le bandeau du milieu de page, les parcours « collaborateur » et « installé », onze témoignages sur quinze, la question sur la collaboration libérale.

**Quatre faits corrigés partout où ils étaient dits :**

- la carte bancaire est demandée à l'inscription, rien n'est débité pendant l'essai ;
- internes et docteurs juniors paient 10 € par mois jusqu'à la fin de l'internat ;
- les adhérents des syndicats d'internes partenaires ont 6 mois d'essai au lieu de 30 jours, grâce à un code fourni par leur syndicat ;
- les données sont hébergées dans l'Union européenne (« hébergées en France » restait sur `/tarifs` et `/guide-declarations`).

**Ce qui ne change pas, volontairement** : le titre de la page dans Google, sa description et l'image de partage (étape à part, plus tard). Les données structurées ne changent pas, sauf la FAQ déclarée à Google, qui suit le texte visible (10 questions au lieu de 11, deux réponses corrigées).

**Ce qui change quand même** : le grand titre (H1). « Ton activité médicale, sous contrôle. » devient « Logiciel de gestion pour médecin remplaçant : Sors la tête de l'eau ». D'ici l'étape suivante, le titre et la description dans Google parlent encore de « cockpit financier » : à surveiller dans la Search Console.

**Chiffres du bloc fondateur, relevés en base le 10 novembre** : 24 200 journées enregistrées (24 252 exactement) et 2 714 lieux d'exercice, à la place des chiffres du 15 août. « 900+ médecins » reste (908 comptes).

**Sous le capot** : aucun script ajouté (onglets, profils et plis fonctionnent sans JavaScript), une police auto-hébergée de 42 Ko, les onze anciens composants de l'accueil et 21 images inutiles supprimés. `CLAUDE.md` et `MIGRATION.md` décrivent la nouvelle page ; `MIGRATION.md` liste tous les textes nouveaux, retouchés et retirés, mot pour mot.

## Mesures avant / après

Mesures locales (pas sur le site en ligne), téléphone simulé, médiane de cinq passages.

| | Avant (`main`) | Après |
|---|---|---|
| Performance de l'accueil (Lighthouse, sur 100) | 96 | **98** |
| Affichage du plus grand élément (LCP) | 2,72 s | **2,26 s** |
| Poids de l'accueil au chargement | 445 Ko | **223 Ko** |
| Accessibilité, bonnes pratiques, SEO | 100, 96, 100 | 100, 96, 100 |
| Longueur sur un téléphone de 390 px | 16 494 px | 15 797 px |
| Mots de texte dans la page | 4 134 | 3 215 |

- L'accueil charge deux feuilles de style au lieu d'une : 41,7 Ko compressés contre 28,2 Ko. Le plan en espérait 33.
- `/simulateur` : 93 avant, 92 après (bruit de mesure, la page n'a pas changé ; elle était déjà sous l'objectif de 95). Un article de blog : 99 avant, 99 après.

## Pages touchées hors accueil

- **`/faq`** : deux réponses disent maintenant les 6 mois des syndicats et le tarif des docteurs juniors.
- **`/tarifs`** : une réponse dit que l'offre se choisit à l'inscription et que la carte est demandée sans être débitée ; « hébergées en France » devient « hébergées dans l'Union européenne ».
- **`/guide-declarations`** : même correction d'hébergement.
- **Les 66 autres pages** : aucun texte ne change ; seuls deux noms de fichiers à empreinte changent (feuille de style commune, script de mesure). Rendu comparé en images à 390 et 1 440 px : identique au pixel.

## Mesure d'audience (PostHog)

- **Séries qui s'arrêtent** : sections `social-proof` et `mid-page-cta`, bouton `cta_signup_cta_banner`, profils `collaborateur` et `installe`, `landing_faq_collaboration`, et sur l'accueil `landing_nav_decouvrir`.
- **Séries qui commencent** : sections `founder`, `guides`, `final-cta`, bouton `cta_signup_final`, rendez-vous `fondateur`, profil `vacataire`, `landing_apercu_*`, `landing_guide_*`.
- **Séries qui ne se lisent plus pareil** (à annoter le jour J) : `features` est maintenant le deuxième bloc (taux de vue en hausse), le film est plus bas (vues en baisse), les clics sur un profil ou un onglet sont comptés deux fois par l'autocapture, la profondeur de défilement n'est plus comparable.

## Vérifié

- `npm run build` (70 pages) et `node scripts/verify-site.mjs` : 0 erreur à chaque commit. Le script contrôle aussi la nouvelle page et refuse le retour de « hébergées en France ».
- Événements rejoués dans un navigateur sans rien envoyer à PostHog.
- Textes repris de l'ancienne page comparés par script : identiques mot pour mot.
- Rien n'est inventé : témoignages et attributions sont ceux déjà publiés (seul « Dr » est retiré devant Anaïs V., interne), les chiffres viennent de la base.

## Ce qui n'est PAS testé

Tout a été vérifié dans un seul navigateur, Chromium, sur ordinateur.

- **Safari** (iPhone et Mac) : jamais ouvert. À regarder : onglets, choix du profil, pastille du menu au-dessus de l'eau, scène finale.
- **Firefox** : jamais ouvert. Deux finitions n'y existent pas (indice de défilement des témoignages, mascotte des tarifs qui s'efface sous le menu) ; la page reste lisible.
- **Android**, **lecteur d'écran**, **vrai téléphone** : aucun essai.
- **Site en ligne** : les mesures de performance sont locales, l'aperçu Vercel n'a pas été mesuré.

## À faire avant et le jour de la mise en ligne

1. Ouvrir l'aperçu Vercel du dernier commit sur un iPhone (Safari), un Android et Firefox.
2. `git fetch origin` : si `origin/main` a avancé, mettre la branche à jour puis relancer build et contrôle.
3. Donner sa lettre à l'entrée de `MIGRATION.md` (« 9.?? »).
4. Dater `/`, `/faq` et `/tarifs` dans `src/lib/pages-lastmod.ts` à la date du jour ; si ce n'est pas le 10 novembre, refaire le relevé des journées et des lieux.
5. Fusionner.
6. Annoter PostHog (« nouvelle accueil ») et noter les chiffres Search Console de l'accueil sur trois mois.
7. Dans les sept jours : étendre menu, pied et police aux autres pages. Puis trois à quatre semaines sans toucher aux titres ni aux textes des pages indexées.

## Retour arrière

- **Le plus rapide** : dans Vercel, remettre en production le déploiement précédent. Aucune adresse ne change.
- **Pour que le dépôt suive** : annuler la fusion par une nouvelle demande de fusion.
- Un retour arrière emporte aussi les quatre faits corrigés : l'ancienne accueil redirait « sans carte bancaire » et « hébergées en France », à recorriger tout de suite.
- La suppression des 21 images est un commit à part (« DA 2026, phase 4a : 21 images de l'ancienne accueil supprimées ») qui s'annule seul.

## Reste ouvert

- **Le H1 change dès la mise en ligne**, avant le titre et la description : à confirmer avant de fusionner.
- « Sans engagement » reste sous le bouton d'essai du bloc « Pour qui » et d'autres pages, alors que l'offre annuelle engage 12 mois.
- Les 21 images supprimées répondent « page introuvable » : à remettre si une adresse sert ailleurs.
- Témoignages : statut, ville et accord des quatre personnes.
- À confirmer

author: frankiedeane
body:
## Qué es
Tangent Study v1 en `/study/`, para probar todo el recorrido sin cuentas todavía. Los datos quedan en el navegador.

- **Study**: es obligatorio citar la fuente primero. Después se graba 5 o 10 min, el audio se manda en partes de 60 s y no se guarda. También se puede sacar foto de la hoja o escribir el texto. El resultado trae una explicación fácil en ES y EN, ideas clave, preguntas para probarse, "revisá en tu fuente", imágenes y lectura en voz alta.
- **Carpeta**: guarda los resúmenes y los imprime o guarda como PDF en A4, Carta, Oficio o A5, en ES, EN o los dos.
- **Tablero**: columnas con nombre y color que se pueden reordenar. Las tareas tienen fecha y color, se mueven arrastrando (también con el dedo) o con flechas, se editan con doble toque y se pueden borrar.
- **Agenda**: link a Google Calendar, archivo .ics con aviso, avisos en el dispositivo y semana para imprimir.
- **Otras pantallas**:
  - Escala diaria del 1 al 5.
  - Mini test basado en ASRS, con aviso de que no es un diagnóstico, más fortalezas con fuentes.
  - Kit de papel.
  - Ideas (usa `/api/suggest`).
  - Cuenta (vista previa: código de acceso, plan con botón de Mercado Pago desactivado, perfil con opt-in).
  - Términos y cookies, con descarga y borrado de datos.
- Interruptor ES/EN en toda la app, diseño para celular y para escritorio, y el logo del skater.

## Servidor
- `POST /api/study-chunk`: transcribe con Gemini y, si falla, con Groq Whisper.
- `POST /api/study`: arma la explicación en ES y EN. Acepta foto. Si no hay fuente, no hay resumen.
- `POST /api/study-code`: valida códigos de acceso.
- Acceso: el env `TANGENT_ACCESS_CODES` (lista separada por comas) o `STATS_TOKEN` dan uso libre. Sin código hay 1 estudio gratis por dispositivo. Ningún código está escrito en el repo.
- Seguridad de Study (`checkStudyText`): los temas escolares como historia o biología están permitidos. Se bloquea solo autolesión (en ese caso muestra ayuda), contenido sexual con menores, odio e insultos, sin strikes.

## Cómo se probó
Probé con Playwright y APIs simuladas, en celular (390 px) y escritorio (1280 px). Funcionaron la grabación con micrófono falso, la transcripción, el resumen, las fotos, la carpeta y el PDF, el tablero (flechas, edición, arrastre), la descarga .ics, la escala, el test, el kit, las ideas y el código. No hubo errores de JS ni scroll horizontal.

Lo que **no** se probó todavía: la IA real (Gemini o Groq) en Netlify.

## Pendiente
- Supabase con cuentas reales, sincronización y redacción del texto guardado.
- Mercado Pago.

body:
## Status

**Merged by an agent with the owner's approval, 11-10:** merge commit **`505e6bd8`** on `main` (19:53:55Z), after #378 (`a6599fd2`), tree `61d17c0d` = this PR's head `781c3820` (Fork Tests 42882853010: success, all 10 shards), after the independent review (`review-stream-tail.md`: approve, merge after #378 as a merge commit). Consumer: Layr-Labs/d-inference#1971, re-pinned to `505e6bd8`; #1965, #1969 and candidate (c) move to the same commit.

**Opened by an agent with the owner's approval, 11-10** (the owner lifted the forks' rule that agents may not open or merge PRs: "You have approval to merge any of our mlx forks", 11-10 ~03:10Z). Draft until the independent refactor review passes; not to be merged before that.

**Merge order: #378 (Nemotron 3.5 Lightning) → this.** This branch already contains `main` `ef028fbe` (#398). `git merge-tree` of this head with #378's head `746e504880` is clean, and the files are disjoint (#378: `PagedKVQuantizationPolicy.swift`, Nemotron decode command buffers, two tests; this PR: two `Prefix/` files, two tests). Consumer: Layr-Labs/d-inference#1971 (draft; it moves to the SDK `main` commit that contains #378 and this PR, together with every other provider PR that pins the SDK).

## Proposed changes

### Why: a stream stays open while its checkpoint is coded one row at a time

By default a donor's terminal waits for its complete checkpoint's publication (`EngineLoopV2.finishAfterCompletePrefixPublication`). At a lossy checkpoint precision (`balanced`, the provider's default) the export runs `CBv2NativeQuantizedCheckpointTensorSource.readSegment`, which:

- read its native source **once per row** (`maximumBytes: role.nativeRowBytes`). Under a native completion profile every such read revalidates the publication's native binding twice (`retainForNativeExport` → `requireNativePagedSources` → `validateCompletePrefix`; `work.retain` and `captureCurrentStreams` → `validateBinding` → `CBv2NativeExecutionContract.validateCompletePrefix`), each pass rebuilding the model's layer kinds and recurrent spec;
- then coded the row on **one core**, with a scalar Hadamard rotation, on the store's single writer.

Measured effect (GLM-5.3-Flash, single M5 Ultra, Darkbloom 0.10.12 candidate): the stream stayed open **63.0 s** after a 200k-token prompt's last token and **17.3 s** after a 57k-token one, 100 % of one core, GPU idle, slot charged throughout — **~28 µs per coded latent row** (63.0 s / (11 DSA layers × 200,013); 17.3 s / (11 × 56,737)). Coding alone was ~3 µs per row (standalone copy of the encoder, `-O`); the rest is the per-row read. In production (0.10.11, 12 h) the same path costs Gemma 4 26B a median 1.24 s (4–8k prompts) and 1.62 s (8–32k), GPT-OSS 20B 1.65 s (8–32k), GLM p90 49 s (≥ 32k); on OpenRouter requests with prompts ≥ 4k it is 28 % of Gemma's generation time.

### Fix

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `afe380af` test (red) | `NativeQuantizedContiguousCheckpointTests.testNativeBoundExportReadsCodedRowsInBatches`: a hand-built publication `CBv2NativeCompletePrefixWork` whose `validateBinding` counts calls; every coded tensor read in one segment may check the binding at most 4 × heads times. `testCodedExportMatchesRowByRowReferenceAtEverySegmentSize`: the exactness oracle (every coded row = the reference codec's bytes for its native row, every recent row its native bytes, segment sizes 1, 3, 17, 257, 1021, 20000 and whole; BF16 and FP32). |
| `2eb747f3` fix | One source read per batch of a head's consecutive rows of one band, up to 256 KiB (`CBv2NativeCheckpointRowCodec.exportBatchBytes`), charged with the segment's scratch. Same rows, same encoder, same order. |
| `bca3aa05` perf | `CBv2NativeCheckpointBatchCoding` codes a batch on up to `exportCodingWorkers` = min(4, max(1, active cores / 4)) cores, one prepared encoder per worker writing only its rows (≥ 16 rows per worker); the lowest worker's refusal is the first row-by-row refusal. The encoder rotates eight lanes at a time with the scalar butterflies' additions in the same order (the decoder's in-register first three stages), computes `lo / scale` once per group and skips zero-scale groups; `encode(_:into:)` codes into the caller's buffer, `encode(_:)` keeps its contract. Unit test `NativeCheckpointBatchCodingTests` (no arrays). |
| `67cf895d` | Merge `main` (`ef028fbe`, #398). No file in common. |

### Bytes identical

The checkpoint's bytes do not change: the same rows reach an encoder that performs the same IEEE operations per element in the same order, so restores, and the answers after them, are exactly today's. No live-path arithmetic changes. Evidence:

- `testCodedExportMatchesRowByRowReferenceAtEverySegmentSize` (Metal) and the existing `NativeCheckpointRowCodecTests.testPreparedEncoderMatchesCheckpointRowsAndRefusesWhatTheyRefuse` (every profile, width 64–512, dtype, role) pass;
- `NativeCheckpointBatchCodingTests`: 1, 2, 4 and 7 workers write the reference codec's bytes for BF16/FP16/FP32 × widths 64/256/512 × keys/values, and a refused row refuses the batch. Mutants: a swapped butterfly → red at every worker count; a worker range off by one row → red at 2/4/7 workers (54 issues);
- a standalone copy of the scalar and the eight-lane encoder gave identical bytes on **3,000,000 rows** (signed zeros, constant groups, subnormals, ±1e30, random bit patterns; 0 mismatches).

### Per-row timing

| | Per coded row |
|---|---|
| Before, end to end on the M5 Ultra (GLM latent, 512 wide) | **~28 µs** (read ~25 µs inferred + coding ~3 µs measured) |
| After, coding, release build, CPU only (Mac A, 36 cores) | **1.99 µs on one core → 0.56 µs on four** (512-wide keys); 256-wide keys 1.00 → 0.29 µs; 256-wide values 0.63 → 0.19 µs |
| After, read | one read (two binding checks) per batch of up to 256 KiB: ≤ ~0.1 µs per row |

Expected end-to-end: GLM 200k ~3–4 s (from 63 s; the remaining time is the file's AES-GCM and write), 57k ~1 s (from 17.3 s), Gemma 4–8k ~0.3 s (from ~1.2 s). To be measured on a real Mac in the next window.

### What it does not change

- Checkpoints stored **native** (no coding): Qwen 3.5/3.6 with the MTP head (their history forces native storage), and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning after #378. Their end-of-stream wait is the native file write; #398's new Qwen donors are not shortened by this PR. Nemotron 3.5 Super's coded rows are.
- The cluster's own SSD prefix records (`CBv2CheckpointRowCodec`, reference codec): unchanged.

### Red, then green

| Run | Head | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Red** (branch `test/checkpoint-export-batched-row-reads-red`, not for merge) | `afe380af` (tests on `093563be`) | Fork Tests [42867182443](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlx-swift-lm/actions/runs/42867182443): **failure in exactly one test**, shard 4: `testNativeBoundExportReadsCodedRowsInBatches`, binding checks per coded tensor 256 > 8 (full layer: 2 heads × 64 rows × 2) and 74 > 4 (window layer: 37 rows × 2). The oracle passed; every other shard passed |
| **Green** | `bca3aa05` | Fork Tests [42867187553](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlx-swift-lm/actions/runs/42867187553): **success**, all 10 shards, coverage and "each test ran once". The batched test passes (0.129 s against 14.1 s), the oracle, the prepared-encoder parity test, `NativeCheckpointBatchCodingTests` (unit shard) and GLM's `realTargetRoundTripsLossyLatentRowsBesideExactState` (paged coded latents, 333-byte segments) pass |
| This head | `67cf895d` (+ `main` `ef028fbe`) | Fork Tests [42873676459](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlx-swift-lm/actions/runs/42873676459) (workflow_dispatch) and this PR's checks |

Downstream: Layr-Labs/d-inference#1971 pinned at `67cf895d`: CI **success** (run 42873758971: provider and cluster builds and tests).

author: davidmckayv
body:
## Why

OpenBot Desktop sends `setup_failed` for every failed install, start or update. A hang isn't a failure, so it sent nothing. A Windows setup window froze for minutes: the native side kept working and sending progress, and the page took none of it until a click or Alt+Tab. We only knew because a tester said so.

## What changes

Two new usage-data events, with the same rules as `setup_failed`: closed values and numbers only, sent by the desktop itself (the window can't send them), queued and retried the same way, and nothing at all when usage data is off. Platform rides on both, as on every event (`openbot_platform`).

**`setup_stalled`: a step running far past its usual time.**
- Covers the back end's first setup (`local setup`, each CLI step), its update (`local update`, each CLI step), OpenBot's own start (its setup rows), and OpenBot updating itself (the release row's steps).
- Typical times are the journeys' measured ones from #1390 (`journey.ts`, `StartJourney.tsx`). `desktop/src/journeyTimings.json` mirrors them for the native side, and `journeyTimings.test.ts` fails if the two drift.
- Fires once per step at **3x typical and at least 2 minutes over**. A step that then finishes sends nothing more. One that fails is a `setup_failed`.
- Payload: `part` (`setup`, `update`, `start`, `release`), `step` (e.g. `dependencies_wait`, `services`, `backing_up`), `typical_seconds`, `elapsed_seconds`.
- Downloads aren't timed as steps, because the journeys measure them by their bytes and a stuck download fails on its own. A download that's still moving restarts the clock of the step it holds up, so a slow connection doesn't read as a stall.
- The CLI only logs a step when it ends, so the running step is the one after the furthest step it logged.

**`ui_stalled`: the setup window stops answering.**
- `setup:progress` now carries a number (`seq`). While the setup, start or update screens show, the page invokes `setup_heartbeat` every 5 s, and again as soon as progress reaches it, with the highest number it has taken. The invoke is async on the native side, never awaited by the page, and limited to one a second when it's sent because progress arrived.
- Progress left untaken for **over 30 s**, while the window is shown, not minimised and (on macOS) not covered, is a stall. Acknowledging the progress number, rather than just checking for any heartbeat, also catches a page whose timers still run but which isn't receiving updates.
- The Desktop log says `[ui] the window has not answered for 31s during start_machine` when the stall is noticed and `[ui] the window stopped answering for 42s during start_machine` when it ends. The end sends one `ui_stalled` with `step` (by the same names as `failing_step`) and `stalled_seconds`.
- A stall ends when the page catches up, the window leaves the screen, the window loads another page, or OpenBot quits. It's recorded before the quit flush.
- Window state is read without asking the window's own thread. On Windows that's `IsWindowVisible` and `IsIconic` on its handle. On macOS it's `occlusionState` on the main thread, with a 2 s limit and one look at a time. WebKit slows timers in covered windows, so on macOS a covered window doesn't count.

No UI changes beyond the heartbeat. `desktop/TELEMETRY.md` has the event table and privacy text, and the CHANGELOG has a line.

## Tests (red, then green)

Red runs: the detection rules stubbed out (`tick` returning nothing), then the on-screen rule ignored.

- `stall.rs`: `a_step_running_three_times_over_is_said_once` (dependencies-wait: quiet at 147 s, said at 148, never again; a retry is a new step), `short_steps_get_two_minutes_and_downloads_are_not_timed` (a moving download holds the clock), `progress_untaken_while_on_screen_is_one_stall_of_its_length` (42 s), `no_heartbeat_at_all_is_a_stall_said_at_quit`, `a_window_off_screen_is_never_a_stall`, `a_fresh_page_and_a_replaced_page_are_not_stalls`. Red: 4 failed with detection stubbed; `a_window_off_screen_is_never_a_stall` failed with the on-screen rule ignored.
- `desktop_stall.rs`, through the real emitter to a loopback ingest: `a_step_running_three_times_over_is_recorded_once`, `a_window_that_stops_taking_progress_is_recorded_with_its_length`, `a_minimised_or_hidden_window_records_nothing`, `opted_out_nothing_is_sent`. Red: the first two failed with detection stubbed, and the hidden-window test failed with the on-screen rule ignored. The opt-out test can only fail if something bypasses the emitter, so it passes on both stubs.
- `telemetry.rs`: `stall_events_round_trip_and_refuse_anything_open`, plus the schema test, which now includes the new events.
- `heartbeat.test.ts`: the first heartbeat is fresh, later ones go on even when the native side never answers, it sends the highest number at once (at most once a second), a failed invoke is dropped, and stopping ends it. Red against a no-op heartbeat.
- `journeyTimings.test.ts`: the mirror equals `SETUP`, `UPDATE`, `OPEN` and `RELEASE`. Red when one number is changed.
- All tests pass: desktop Rust (950 lib, 286 bin), desktop frontend (375), `plain-setup-words`, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt on macOS.

## Still needs a live check on Windows

- Reproduce a stall: with the window on screen during install, freeze the page (e.g. the lone-Alt menu mode), wait over 30 s, then click. Expect the two `[ui]` log lines and one `ui_stalled`.
- Minimise it, and separately close it to the tray, during install. Expect nothing.
- Run a normal first install and an update on a typical connection, and confirm no `setup_stalled` and no `ui_stalled` (no false positive).
- The Windows and Linux on-screen readers are compiled and linted only in CI. They didn't run on a Mac.

body:
The overnight non-GPU batch (Chirag, 2026-11-10: "Whatever the non-gpu work we should do batch it and run it overnight"). Record: `plan/2026-11-10-autopilot.md`.

**What changes**
- **Anvil, compaction cost.** The summary call's token usage goes on the run record (`run.compacted` output `usage`, an added field), and the run's token total counts it. The simple battery reports compactions and summary tokens.
- **Host, storage prompt.** One storage prompt per app: file calls that arrive while it is open wait on the same answer. Each waiting call hears `naklios:rpc:waiting`, and the SDK stops that call's 30 s timer. Covers the fs, file and system fs routes.
- **Pi.** Waits for your storage answer instead of falling back to browser storage, and says so in its status line. Replies stream into the window. Each tool call gets a card that fills with its result. A thinking line counts the wait.
- **Anvil, AI slots.** The host refuses an app's 4th pending AI request, so a 4-way dispatch lost a child. Every Anvil host call now holds one of 3 slots (`sys/ai/slots.mjs`). When Anvil's deadline gives up on a call, it now cancels that call at the host.
- **TeX browser test.** A failed first compile now prints the end of its TeX log. The intermittent CI failure was a failed compile, not an OPFS bug; the next occurrence will name its cause.
- **Mirrors.** The SDK change is reinstalled into the 7 managed SDK copies, at their existing upstream pins.

author: gallagit
body:
Closes #1405

Read-only adapter for **Claris FileMaker Server** through the FileMaker Data API, following the plan approved in #1405.

**Auth**
- `LOGIN_TOKEN` with `loginBasicAuth: true` (from #1460): `POST /fmi/data/vLatest/databases/{db}/sessions` with HTTP Basic and an empty JSON body, token read from `response.token` and sent as `Bearer`.
- `tokenTTLSeconds: 900` with proactive refresh, plus `refreshOn401: true`, so an expired session (15 min of inactivity) triggers a fresh login.

**Tools (all read-only)**
- `filemaker_list_layouts`
- `filemaker_get_layout_metadata`
- `filemaker_find_records` (POST `_find`)
- `filemaker_get_record`

The `filemaker_find_records` description and the instructions say that FileMaker code `"401"` in `messages[]` means an empty result, not a failure, and is not the same as HTTP 401.

**Tests**
- Static spec: login flow, every tool's method/URL/body through the real `RestEngine`, response transforms, env var metadata, and the 401 wording.
- Live spec (skipped unless `RUN_FILEMAKER_LIVE=1`): ran against FileMaker Server 26.0.3 (trial, self-hosted in Docker) with a read-only file account that has the `fmrest` privilege. 21/21 passing: sign-in, wrong password refused without echoing credentials, list layouts, metadata, find, get record.
- Manual checks on the same server:
  - a matching find returns the record;
  - an empty find returns code `401` "No records match the request". On FileMaker Server 26 this came back with **HTTP 200**, not 500, so the wording now covers both;
  - a closed/invalid token returns HTTP 401 with code `952`, which is what triggers the re-login.

Opening as draft for early feedback. I will sign the CLA.

author: ikarys
body:
## What

- **Security agent** (`agents/claude-code`, `agents/fennec`): hunts each threat-model class sink by sink, runs the declared static analyser first, says how every finding was confirmed (`Confirmed by:`), uses only the convention's severities and verdicts, writes the A2 report itself. Threat model coverage table added to `templates/audit/report-security.md`.
- **New `skills/code-audit`**: measures size and duplication (or reads the T8 evidence), runs the security and architecture agents in parallel, writes the A1 report with per-axis scores and the index rows. Listed in `CONVENTION.md` tooling and `agents/README.md`.
- **Convention loosened** (a convention, not a format):
  - severities judged from the person affected: user, maintainer or operator (`CONVENTION.md`, `docs/requirements.md`);
  - A2 data exposure check only when the software holds or serves user data; a library says so and skips it;
  - report format is a minimum: extra sections and finding fields allowed, bare `key: value` header accepted;
  - A4 index may carry more columns in any order;
  - `agents/README.md`: start a new session after copying or editing an agent.
- **vibecheck**: index parsing moved to `src/audit_index.rs` (the pre-commit T8 hook caught `audit.rs` going past 400 lines), columns located by header name with the template order as fallback, bare header parsed, kind compared only when the index has that column. Three new unit tests.
- All eight agent header blocks fenced with `---`, matching what vibecheck parses.

## Verified

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` (18 suites) pass in `vibecheck/`; the repo's own pre-commit vibecheck passes.
- The skill ran twice on rango-orm (develop `f8cb0ec`) to check report stability; the per-axis scoring rule came out of that.

author: zarbopiero963-droid
body:
[TASK: p0_emergency_stop]

Autorizzata da **OWNER DIRECTIVE `PF-OWNER-P0-EMERGENCY-STOP-20261110`**. Il difetto è il FINDING P0 `AUD-BF-016` di Claude D (#627 c.6775355046), riprodotto in modo indipendente due volte.

**Il merge è riservato all'owner.** La PR è safety-critical: tocca `core/runtime_controller.py`, `betfair_client.py`, `headless_main.py` e `mini_gui.py`.

**Precedenza:** BB-1G non aveva ancora una PR aperta, quindi, secondo la direttiva, il P0 passa prima.
- BB-1G è sospesa in modo ordinato: il codice è su un branch locale con bundle di backup (Gate A/B, 23 test, 10/10 mutanti eliminati).
- Riprende con una PR dedicata dopo questa.

## Il difetto
`RuntimeController.emergency_stop()` sceglieva gli ordini da cancellare **solo** dalla tabella `order_saga`.
- Quella tabella la scrive `OrderManager`, che in produzione non viene mai costruito.
- Il motore, il cashout e il Microstake scrivono invece nella tabella `orders`.
- L'exchange non veniva interrogato.

Risultato: **zero cancellazioni**, arresto riportato come riuscito (rc 0, RESULT `VERIFIED`) e ordini ancora aperti sull'exchange.

## Cosa cambia per chi usa Pickfair
L'arresto d'emergenza segue il contratto dei requisiti 1–8 della direttiva. Dettaglio in `docs/emergency_stop.md`.

1. **Fonti affidabili:**
   - tabella `orders`, con una denylist dei soli stati che non possono avere un ordine aperto, quindi anche `INFLIGHT`, `AMBIGUOUS`, `HEDGE_*` e stati futuri;
   - `order_saga`;
   - **fotografia dell'exchange** prima e dopo il cancel, sulla sede in cui il runtime operava (LIVE o SIM).
2. **Blocco immediato** dei nuovi ingressi (invariato).
   - Cancel per mercato degli ordini del bot, compresi quelli noti solo sull'exchange per `betId` o `customerOrderRef`.
   - L'autorità del runtime (#536) viene riverificata prima di ogni mercato.
   - Gli ordini aperti **non attribuibili** al bot non vengono cancellati alla cieca: sono elencati e richiedono l'operatore.
3. **Mai successo senza verifica:** `verification = VERIFIED` solo se la lettura finale dell'exchange riesce e non resta nulla di aperto. Altrimenti l'esito è `OPEN_ORDERS_REMAIN`, `CANCEL_INCOMPLETE` o `UNVERIFIED`.
4. **Esito per ordine:** `CANCELLED`, `PARTIALLY_MATCHED`, `ALREADY_MATCHED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `STILL_OPEN`, `UNKNOWN`. Per gli ordini senza `betId`: `NO_OPEN_ORDER_ON_MARKET`.
5. **Posizioni reali** abbinate prima dell'arresto: elencate in `matched_positions`. La fonte dei settlement precedente all'arresto resta invariata.
6. **Circuit breaker:** in emergenza la cancellazione e la lettura di verifica del client LIVE lo attraversano (AUD-BF-010). Fuori dall'emergenza resta rispettato.
   - Una cancellazione singola, mai ripetuta.
   - Un timeout del cancel produce un esito ignoto, che la verifica successiva risolve.
   - L'operazione è idempotente: ripeterla, anche dopo un riavvio, non duplica nulla.
7. **Audit:** il risultato completo va nell'evento `EMERGENCY_STOP_TRIGGERED` e, per `--emergency-stop`, nel RESULT della scatola nera. Il ledger non viene riscritto: settlement e contabilità restano alla riconciliazione.
8. **Notifica:** in caso di intervento manuale:
   - log CRITICAL;
   - evento `EMERGENCY_STOP_MANUAL_ACTION_REQUIRED`;
   - dialogo GUI `EMERGENCY STOP: intervento manuale richiesto`;
   - `--emergency-stop` esce con **rc 3**.

## Prove (eseguite)
- **RED su main** (`36bf242e`): `test_emergency_stop_cancels_an_open_engine_order_and_verifies_it_on_the_exchange` fallisce con `markets_attempted 0` e l'ordine ancora aperto sull'exchange.
- **GREEN:** 17 test nuovi, con HeadlessApp e SQLite reali, `SimulationBroker` come exchange LIVE e un exchange a comportamento controllato. Coprono:
  - cancellazione verificata;
  - ordine parzialmente abbinato, già abbinato, non trovato;
  - cancel fallito, eccezione o nessun effetto;
  - exchange illeggibile prima o dopo;
  - ordine `AMBIGUOUS` senza `betId`;
  - ordine noto solo per `customerOrderRef`;
  - ordini non attribuibili;
  - idempotenza e bypass del breaker;
  - sede SIM;
  - avviso GUI.
- Aggiornati i test dell'esito CLI (`tests/blackbox/test_blackbox_runtime.py`): rc 0 solo con `VERIFIED`, più 5 casi nuovi.
- **Suite completa: 12942 passed, 0 failed.** Su Python 3.11 i test toccati danno 152 passed.
- **Mutanti** `p0_estop_*`: 8/8 KILLED, più `i536_emergency_cancel_not_rechecked_per_market` KILLED. Sui moduli toccati: 146 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED.
- **Scope:** 12 file, coincidenti con il diff (`p0_emergency_stop`, verificato con `guardrail_check.py`).

## Cosa NON copre (dichiarato)
- **AUD-BF-020:** dopo l'arresto il runtime è in SIM e il cashout delle posizioni reali rimaste non passa da qui. Le posizioni sono comunque elencate e notificate. Rilievo separato.
- **#622:** il caso in cui l'arresto non parte affatto (DB corrotto). Difetto distinto, non toccato.
- **GUI-006:** non incluso.
- **Prova visiva GUI (Xvfb):** non eseguita. La modifica alla GUI è un dialogo d'errore esistente (`_safe_show_error`) con un testo nuovo, documentato in `docs/design/design_handoff.md` e coperto da un test.

## Cosa peggiora (dichiarato)
- `--emergency-stop` esce con **3** quando la cancellazione non è verificata. Prima usciva sempre con 0: chi automatizzava su rc 0 ora vede l'errore. È voluto.
- L'arresto fa due letture in più dell'exchange (prima e dopo).

PR safety-critical: sì (`core/runtime_controller.py`, `betfair_client.py`). Nessun ordine reale, nessun accesso LIVE. LIVE OFF, certificazione OFF, kill switch ON.
