author: gitchrisqueen
body:
## What changed

Take attendance now shows the Docker browser live, lets you pause and resume the run, and keeps your chosen view when the page refreshes.

- **Live browser view.** The container's noVNC screen is embedded in an iframe (no sign-in, nothing to type; the noVNC client is asked to be view-only, which is a client setting and not a lock, see Known limits). It is drawn outside the 1.5 s polled fragments, so the refresh timer does not reload it. It appears only when the run really uses the Docker browser (`BROWSER_TYPE=DOCKER_CHROME`, `HEADLESS_BROWSER=false`) and the viewer port answers; otherwise the page keeps showing screenshots as before. While the Live browser view is open, event screenshots narrow to tab changes; in any other view every event refreshes the snapshots (the page tells the job which view is open). New `live_viewer_url()` in `selenium_util.py`; the logged VNC URL and the embedded one come from one builder (`vnc_viewer_url`).
- **Views.** The page opens on **Tab snapshots**; the live viewer loads only when the instructor chooses **Live browser**. `Live browser | Tab snapshots | Log` and the per-tab picker are keyed `st.segmented_control`s. Tabs are named "Tab N" with the page title in a caption, so a page retitling while it loads no longer resets your choice (the old tab labels carried the title).
- **Pause / Resume.** New `PauseGate` (`src/cqc_cpcc/pause_gate.py`). The `ScreenshotListener` `before_*` hooks wait at the gate, so the worker holds before its next browser command. While held, a keepalive (`raw_driver.current_url`, every 60 s, on the worker thread) stops the grid deleting the idle session (`SE_NODE_SESSION_TIMEOUT=600`). Cancel still frees a paused run, and a pause ends by itself after 30 minutes (warning logged) so a closed tab cannot hold the browser slot forever. The button is hidden on the plan form, on the EVA form, and while an MFA number waits. After 15 min paused the page warns that MyColleges may sign you out. A caption says other pages cannot use the browser while paused (`SE_NODE_MAX_SESSIONS=1`).
- **docker-compose.yml.** noVNC is published on `127.0.0.1` by default (`SELENIUM_VNC_BIND`); the container password now follows `SELENIUM_VNC_PASSWORD` (default `secret`, as before). No `SE_VNC_VIEW_ONLY`, port 14444, session timeout and max sessions are unchanged. New `.env.example` entries: `SELENIUM_VNC_BIND`, `SELENIUM_VNC_PASSWORD`, `VNC_PUBLIC_URL`.
- **Proof tooling (not in CI):** `scripts/verify_pause_keepalive.py`, `scripts/docker-compose.keepalive-test.yml`, `scripts/dev_attendance_viewer_harness.py`, `scripts/verify_viewer_ui.py`.

Deviation from the written plan: the plan named `st.components.v1.iframe`. The locked Streamlit (1.67) marks it deprecated in favour of `st.iframe`, so the page uses `st.iframe` and falls back to the old call on a Streamlit without it.

Other pages that share the grid (BrightSpace fetch and write-back, find student, withdrawals, project feedback, the Selenium MCP) use port 14444 only, which this PR does not touch.

## How to test on your machine

1. `.env` needs `BROWSER_TYPE=DOCKER_CHROME`, `DOCKER_TYPE=LOCAL`, `HEADLESS_BROWSER=false` (with the default `HEADLESS_BROWSER=true` the app uses local headless Chrome and the page shows screenshots).
2. Recreate the container so it picks up the new port binding: `docker compose -p cpcc_task_automation -f docker-compose.yml up -d --force-recreate selenium-chrome`
3. `poetry run streamlit run src/cqc_streamlit_app/Home.py`, open Take attendance, **Start attendance**, approve the sign-in as usual.
4. Expect: the page opens on Tab snapshots; choose **Live browser** to watch the browser live; Pause freezes the run at its next browser command and shows "Paused since H:MM ET"; Resume carries on; switching between Live browser, Tab snapshots and Log does not stop the run; a rerun (press R) keeps your view.
5. If Streamlit and Docker are on different machines, or Streamlit is served over https, set `VNC_PUBLIC_URL` (see `.env.example`).

Not tested by me: a real MyColleges attendance run (needs your credentials and MFA approval). Everything below ran against the real Docker grid with a synthetic page.

## Evidence (Docker grid on a Linux VPS, 2026-11-10)

Files: branch `evidence/take-attendance-vnc-viewer` at `c0416f9` (kept off master).

**Port binding** (configuration, `docker-compose.yml` at the head: line 31 `"${SELENIUM_VNC_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${SELENIUM_VNC_PORT:-17900}:7900"`; line 27 `"${SELENIUM_HOST_PORT:-14444}:4444"` is unchanged and, like before, published on all interfaces without authentication, a pre-existing exposure outside this PR).

**Unit tests:** CI at head `e0b1cd1` (run [42934829761](https://github.com/christopherqueenconsulting/cpcc_task_automation/actions/runs/42934829761)): Unit shard 1/2 `3145 passed, 1 skipped, 11 xfailed`, Unit shard 2/2 `2948 passed, 1 xfailed`, every check green including GitGuardian. Student PII guard run [42934829678](https://github.com/christopherqueenconsulting/cpcc_task_automation/actions/runs/42934829678): `pii-guard: OK (1296 files, 23 denylist entries)`.

**Keepalive** (`scripts/verify_pause_keepalive.py`; the real listener gate, a worker clicking through it, no commands of our own during the hold):

| Run | Grid timeout | Hold | Keepalive | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Control | 60 s (test override) | 90 s | off | session deleted: `InvalidSessionIdException` ([log](https://github.com/christopherqueenconsulting/cpcc_task_automation/blob/c0416f96743b7344d4ec041b4d7e76363fba335d/take-attendance-vnc-viewer/control-no-keepalive.log)) |
| Scaled | 60 s | 150 s | every 20 s | 7 keepalives; page timer advanced 150 s; worker clicks frozen at 6; after Resume clicks 6 → 15 and `document.title` read OK ([log](https://github.com/christopherqueenconsulting/cpcc_task_automation/blob/c0416f96743b7344d4ec041b4d7e76363fba335d/take-attendance-vnc-viewer/keepalive-150s.log)) |

Kevin approved retiring these on Nov 10 after the model deep dive (`docs/review-2026-11-10-models-deep-dive.md`, added here).

**Retired (57 registry rows):** daily WTI, Brent, natural gas and gasoline; weather highs and lows (every version); ERCOT peak; sports spreads, totals and every `+cal` row; every hourly-WTI line except the live-feed v4. Market and baseline rows go with a family when the whole family is retired.

Journal history is untouched. Health reads `FORECASTERS`, so retired families raise no "froze nothing" alarm. The gap tracker builds its own forecaster instances and is unaffected.

**Known effect:** the Weather page's highs, lows and ERCOT panels stop getting new rows after the last frozen day settles. Rain continues.

body:
## Why

Phase 8g: the gate run of phase 8's budgets, with the pool (#38, #39) and the start-up work (#40) in place. The result goes on the roadmap's phase 8 row.

## Testing

All on **Battery Power** (Low Power Mode, the phase 8 reference), commit `b98ff4e` (same tree as this branch's base), median of 5, `scripts/benchmark_search.py` at `--jobs 8` (the default) and `--jobs 1`. Every query's solution count matched its golden.

| Workload | `--jobs 1` | Pool of 8 | Budget | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1a, warm: Blademaster, Attack Up [Med] + Sharp Sword, default charm list, data already loaded | 1.45 s | 0.66 s | ≤ 0.5 s | **miss** by 0.16 s |
| 1a, cold: `mhp3ass search` in a new process | 2.49 s | 1.90 s | ≤ 2.0 s | pass |
| g18: six-skill search, no charms, 1.17M combinations, none match | 26.39 s | 3.87 s | ≤ 3.6 s | **miss** by 0.27 s |
| f305: largest random query with two-skill charms, 1.84M combinations, 20 match | 36.83 s | 5.53 s | ≤ 5 s | **miss** by 0.53 s |
| f058: random six-skill query, two-skill charms, 1.47M combinations, none match | 36.75 s | 5.59 s | ≤ 5 s | **miss** by 0.59 s |
| f081: random six-skill query, two-skill charms, 1.71M combinations, none match | 34.99 s | 5.47 s | ≤ 5 s | **miss** by 0.47 s |
| f362: largest random query with one-skill charms, 1.94M combinations, none match | 25.21 s | 5.05 s | ≤ 5 s | **miss** by 0.05 s |
| f099: random query where almost everything matches, 96,723 of 96,768 | 3.00 s | 0.96 s | ≤ 1.0 s | pass |
| Full fuzz gate, `pytest -m fuzz` (500 queries in the pool + serial L3) | | 204.5 s (3.4 min), 5 passed | ≤ 3.7 min | pass |
| Default `pytest` suite | | 78.2 s, 776 passed | ≤ 45 s | **miss** by 33 s |

Start-up steps (pool run): imports 99 ms, data 28 ms, charm tables 267 ms, charm checks 90 ms.

The budgets were set from mains-power measurements. On mains the pool timings barely move (8e: g18 3.95 s on mains against 3.90 s on battery), so the misses aren't a power-source artefact.

**Outcome:** the budgets are revised to these measurements plus about 15 % headroom (warm 1a ≤ 0.75 s, g18 ≤ 4.5 s, the largest fuzz queries ≤ 6.5 s, default suite ≤ 75 s), rather than adding hot-path tweaks or pruning. Phase 8 is done; the roadmap row says so.

author: gusthavosouza
body:
Closes #314. Follow-up to #313: its rules name folders some teams commit (`Pods/`, `Carthage/Build/`, `bin/`, `build/`, even `node_modules/`).

**What**
- Before the sweep removes a planned folder inside a clone or worktree, it asks git whether it tracks any file there: `git ls-files -z -- :(literal)<folder>/`. If git does, the folder is kept and logged as skipped, "tracked by git".
- Git runs only through #298's runner (`git_check::tracks`, which reuses `plain_config` and `git`): the config allowlist, fixed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`, no lazy fetch, no optional locks, hooks and fsmonitor off, a 10 s timeout and capped output. There is no new way of running git. When git can't answer (a refused config, a git folder outside the workspace, an error, a timeout, more than 4 MB of output), the folder is kept: "git can't say whether it tracks it".
- `.venv` is swept only beside `pyproject.toml`, `requirements*.txt`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg` or `Pipfile`. Markers now take one `*` anywhere in the name, which is needed for `requirements*.txt`.
- `docs/sweep-rules.md` explains the tracked-folder rule and the `.venv` markers. The `git_check.rs` module doc now says the sweep asks git too.

**Worth knowing**
- On this Mac, 5 of 102 agent clones have a config key outside the allowlist (4 × `credential.https://github.com.helper`, 1 × `merge.conflictstyle`). The sweep keeps those clones' build output and logs it as skipped. That's the fail-safe the ticket asks for; widening the allowlist would be a Security call.
- Clean's preview lists a workspace's top-level items and the folders inside a main clone, and the user ticks them. It never offers rule-matched build folders, so it needed no change.
- The sweep runs in `spawn_blocking` and waits on each git call with `Handle::block_on` on Loft's multi-thread runtime. The tests' `sweep()` helper does the same through `untracked`, so every sweep test now goes through the git check. Their fake `.git/HEAD` clones are real `git init` repos now, as is the one in `updater::an_update_sweeps_before_restarting`.

**Tests**
- `a_folder_git_tracks_is_kept_and_logged_and_the_same_folder_untracked_goes`: a tracked `Pods/` stays and is skipped as "tracked by git"; the same `Pods/` untracked is swept.
- `a_folder_in_a_clone_git_can_t_be_asked_about_is_kept`: `filter.x.clean` in the config means git isn't run, and `Pods/` stays.
- `.venv` has a case per Python marker in `CASES`. `every_rule_is_swept_beside_its_marker_and_kept_without_it` checks that it's swept beside each marker and kept with none.

```
$ cargo test -q --bin loft sweep::
test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 576 filtered out; finished in 1.90s
$ cargo test -q
test result: ok. 611 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 13.34s
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.20s
$ cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings      # clean
$ find $TMPDIR -maxdepth 1 -name 'loft-*' | wc -l   # before → after the full run
73281 → 73281
```

**Try it**
In an agent's clone, commit a `Pods/` beside a `Podfile` and backdate it 4 days. Then wait for the next daily sweep (or restart Loft: the first sweep runs at start). `Pods/` stays, and Settings › Disk shows it in the sweep log under skipped as "tracked by git".

author: groussac
body:
## Summary

Add opt-in head-template compilation to `rangular-aot`. The generated view
contains direct HTML elements from the template.

## Changes

- Add `compile_head`, `compile_head_named`, `compile_head_tokens`, and
  `compile_head_tokens_named`.
- Emit direct `<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`, and `<script>` elements.
- Preserve the existing behavior of ordinary AOT compilation.
- Preserve unrelated head markup, including stylesheets and non-JSON-LD scripts.
- Report unsupported head-template content as `RANG403` diagnostics.
- For JSON-LD, accept static text or one interpolation containing the complete,
  already-serialized JSON value. Replace `<` with `\u003c` so `</script>` cannot
  close the element. JSON validation and serialization remain the caller’s
  responsibility.
- Document the compiler’s output and input requirements.

## Scope

The generated view is a fragment; the host application must include it in the
document `<head>`. It does not move or remove elements when pages change, or
automatically remove repeated elements. This change does not claim behavior
across every application rendering mode.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p rangular-aot`
- `cargo clippy -p rangular-aot --all-targets`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

## Incident réel
Après activation de l’API, l’ajout Xtream/M3U retourne `Enregistrement impossible. Vérifie la migration source_owners.`. Ce message est renvoyé par un `catch (Throwable)` générique : il accuse à tort la migration même lorsque le vrai problème est le chiffrement, une autre table ou l’insertion du job.

## Commits
- `AccountSourceCreator` : transaction de création atomique (limite, chiffrement, source, propriétaire, grant, job) avec gestion contrôlée des rollbacks.
- `AccountSourceWriteFailure` : indication de l’étape exacte où l’enregistrement échoue, sans transmettre aucun secret fournisseur ou texte d’exception SQL.
- Contrôleur : réponses sûres, code diagnostic, journaux limités à l’étape/classe/code ; la création réussie conserve son contrat HTTP 201.
- `bin/doctor-account-storage.php` : diagnostic **read-only** des tables/colonnes MariaDB et du chiffrement en mémoire ; ne modifie aucune donnée ni n’expose la clé.
- `tests/account_source_creation_smoke.php` : test réel de création sur SQLite temporaire, chiffrement/déchiffrement, compte autorisé, job `queued`, rollback forcé si insertion échoue, erreur de clé invalide.
- CI PHP étendue, tests contrôleur réajustés et documentation d’exploitation.

## Validation / déploiement
La CI PHP/Node doit être verte avant fusion. Aucune migration ou configuration n’est modifiée automatiquement ; après synchronisation `main` sur o2switch, exécuter `php bin/doctor-account-storage.php`, puis traiter uniquement la cause identifiée. Ne pas modifier la clé de chiffrement déjà utilisée sans migration sécurisée des données. Aucun accès fournisseur ni modification de la base de production lors de cette PR.

## Summary

- Production host, secret provisioning, administrator onboarding, and real-user/cross-authority authorization tests are still release blockers.
- API response security headers/HSTS and subject-partitioned API rate limiting were added with integration tests. The first rate-limit test run exposed interference from a shared anonymous bucket; this was corrected by limiting authenticated subjects globally and applying a separate readiness-only anonymous policy. The correction passed Backend build run 42924648212 (Success); subsequent Backend and Client CI runs 42924701188 and 42924701234 also passed on the documentation commit. author: lucaredaelli
body:
## Skip card-reveal animations after special mission claims

### Problem

Special events that grant a card, e.g. the Immersive Pikachu card on day 10 of the PikaPika event, play a pack-style card reveal during/after the reward claim. The reveal ignores ESC and shows no caption:

- Inside `ClaimVisibleEventRewards` the claim loop sees the event needle covered by the reveal, counts it as `changedWindow > 3` and returns while the reveal is still playing.
- `GoToMain` then spams ESC on the reveal until the animation ends on its own, wasting several seconds per run.

### Changes

- **`Scripts/Needles/SkipEvent.png`** + `Mission_SkipEventReveal` registration in `Coords.ahk`: the Skip button shown by event card reveals, which differs from the pack-opening Skip.
- **`Scripts/Include/BotMissions.ahk`**:
  - inside the claim loop, the claim clicks double as probe taps; `Mission_SkipEventReveal`/`Skip`/`Skip2`/`Next`/`Next2` are then clicked through, consuming the reveal before the loop can exit early;
  - new `SkipCardReveal()` on both claim-exit paths (`Mission_CompleteGotAllClaims` and `changedWindow > 3`): dismisses the toast, then probe-taps until the `List` tab is back (the tab stays visible under the toast, so it is only checked afterwards);
  - `GoToMain` unchanged: no blind taps outside the claim flow.

author: rtkelly13
body:
The large specs' hour (#2) was Roslyn binding two methods in the generated fake.

## Cause

`SampleJson` and `TryAnswer` switched on the pair `(operation, status)`, one arm per documented response. Roslyn checks such a switch's patterns for redundancy (`DecisionDagBuilder.CheckOrAndAndReachability`, under `Binder.BindSwitchExpression`) in time roughly cubic in its arms:

| Arms | `(string, int)` switch | nested switch |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 100 | 1.2 s | 0.07 s |
| 600 | 13.0 s | 0.04 s |
| 1,200 | 112.7 s (157.7 s in a second run) | 0.14 s |

- **Stripe:** the two methods have 1,193 and 1,222 arms. They took 3:39 of a 3:49 compile: `TryAnswer` 2:02 and `SampleJson` 1:37.
- **GitHub:** the two methods have 3,119 and 3,724 arms.
- **Ruled out:**
  - GC, at about 6% of the run (dotnet-counters on CI).
  - The 20,000-line endpoints method, which binds in 2 to 5 s.
  - Overload resolution, flow analysis and nullable analysis: a trace of the 1,200-arm switch expression (the shape of `SampleJson`) spends all of its CPU in pattern-redundancy checking. `TryAnswer`, a switch statement, is shown by timing only.

## Change

Each method now switches on the operation and, within it, on the status. The arm order is kept: specific statuses, then ranges, then the default. An operation without a default response still answers nothing for an undocumented status; `FakeTests.Only_documented_outcomes_can_be_scripted` covers this.

## Evidence

- **Compile time.** This is compiling the generated code with `GetDiagnostics`, as `LargeSpecTests` times it. The runs were local, with the test project's references, so the generator emits what it does on CI.

  | Spec | Before | After |
  |:--|--:|--:|
  | Stripe | 3:49 | 0:41 |
  | GitHub | about an hour on CI | 1:13 |

  Binding Stripe's fake went from 3:09 to 7.4 s.
- **Derived evidence.** Of the 33 files, only the 11 `.g.cs` files change. Each is byte-identical outside `SampleJson` and `TryAnswer`.
- **Tests:**
  - `EmittedCodeTests` passes, 31 of 31: every sample in all three outcome styles, with no warnings.
  - `DerivedEvidenceTests` passes, 12 of 12.
  - `Matchmark.Sample.Tests` passes, 121 of 121.
- **New check.** `EmittedCodeTests.No_generated_switch_dispatches_on_a_tuple` examined 409 switches across 13 fakes. With `SampleJson`'s tuple switch restored, it fails: `bookings: Bookings.Fake.g.cs: switch ((operation, status))`.
- **`LargeSpecTests`, locally, with the fix:** both specs in 2:26.

  | Spec | Time | Generated | Compile errors |
  |:--|--:|--:|--:|
  | GitHub | 1:26 | 98.7% | 0 |
  | Stripe | 0:54 | 99.8% | 0 |

  On CI, this PR's `test` job ran both large specs in 1:54 ([run 42922952977](https://github.com/rtkelly-labs/matchmark/actions/runs/42922952977)). The same step without the fix has run for more than 90 minutes on #3.
- **The new check catches both switches.** It also fails with only `TryAnswer`'s statement switch restored.
- **The full suite** passed on CI. Generator: 282 passed, 1 skipped; main has 281 and 1.

## Conflicts

`AGENTS.md`'s Checks row (Generator 280 → 281) will conflict with #3, which also changes that count.

author: evanfeenstra
body:
Games as apps need browser features the app frame used to block. Ruled 2026-11-10: what a game needs goes in the frame **every** app gets, and `app.yaml`'s `permissions:` stays only for the three features with a real privacy argument.

## Every app's frame

```
sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads allow-forms allow-pointer-lock allow-orientation-lock"
allow="microphone; clipboard-write; fullscreen; gamepad; screen-wake-lock"
```

So with no declaration, every app gets fullscreen (plus orientation lock, which needs it), pointer lock, the gamepad and the screen wake lock, the way the microphone and clipboard already worked. None of these lets the page get anything out:
- each needs a click or a visible page;
- the browser shows its own way out of fullscreen and pointer lock;
- the page still sends nothing except through its bridge.

## Declared: `permissions: [motion, camera, geolocation]`

| name | added to `allow` | why it's declared |
|---|---|---|
| `motion` | `accelerometer; gyroscope` (no compass) | Chrome hands it to a frame without asking, and motion can be read to guess keystrokes |
| `camera` | `camera` | the browser prompts, but the prompt names the host, not the app |
| `geolocation` | `geolocation` | same |

`camera` and `geolocation` are MCP Apps' own names, mapped as ext-apps' `buildAllowAttribute` maps them. `fullscreen`, `pointer-lock`, `gamepad`, `wake-lock`, `microphone` and `clipboard-write` are accepted and dropped, so a manifest written to those names still builds. Any other name is a build error naming the allowed set; `vibrate` gets its own message, since browsers block it in cross-origin frames and no attribute turns it on.

## What changed

- **Manifest** (`src/apps/manifest.ts`): `DECLARED_PERMISSIONS` and `EVERY_APP_PERMISSIONS`.
- **Build**: `dist/build.json` carries `permissions`, the declared three only.
- **Host** (`web/src/frame-permissions.ts`, pure and tested; `AppHost.tsx`):
  - `BASE_SANDBOX` / `BASE_ALLOW` hold the fixed string.
  - AppHost reads build.json beside the document and adds the declared features to `allow` before the srcdoc, then resets to every app's when the page goes.
  - The camera, microphone, geolocation and clipboard grants are reported to the page in `ui/initialize` as `hostCapabilities.sandbox.permissions`.
- **Visitor and peer**:
  - `GET /public/apps[/:name]` carries `permissions`.
  - A peer's build.json comes through the read-through like its document.
  - The store's live preview adds the game features and the declared ones to its own frame of the publisher's page, because a nested frame only gets what every frame above it has. That frame also gains `allow-forms`, so a form in an app previewed there can fire its submit handler.
- **Docs**: App.md's manifest section (nothing else on that page), plans/apps.md §9, specs/API.md.

## Does the frame need re-creating when the version changes?

No. The browser reads the attributes when the frame loads a document, so setting them before the srcdoc is enough. The main view and the side panel key AppHost by app@version anyway. JobAppPanel and ArtifactViewer reuse one element; that path was checked directly, below.

## Verified

- `npm test`: 4068 tests, 0 failures, 52 skipped. Engine `tsc` clean; `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vite build` clean.
- New tests: manifest parsing (declared, dropped, errors), build.json, the public listing, and the attribute mapping (`web/src/frame-permissions.test.ts`, which holds its names equal to the manifest's).
- **In real Chrome** (Playwright, local Chrome, against a scratch strut serving this branch). The test apps call `requestFullscreen()` / `requestPointerLock()` and report the frame's policy:
  - **An app that declares nothing:** fullscreen resolves and pointer lock locks; gamepad and wake lock are allowed; accelerometer, gyroscope and camera are not.
  - **An app declaring `[motion]`:** accelerometer and gyroscope are allowed as well.
  - **One frame element across two documents:** setting the attributes before the srcdoc grants and revokes as expected (checked while features were still declared).
- **Not exercised:** real motion events (headless desktop Chrome has no sensors; checked at the policy level only), and the store's live-preview frame, which needs an index with a live listing (it type-checks and uses the same constants).

## Other hosts

**Hive** and **Peel** frame apps too. They should:
- copy the fixed `sandbox` / `allow` string above, so games work there with no declaration;
- read `permissions` from `dist/build.json` for motion, camera and geolocation.

Until they do, an app shown there gets only the microphone and clipboard.

author: voho
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"voho"} -->
_Requested by **voho proton** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Kv5CAWgmwWfvGrT4H2sw9m?thread=cmsg_01Kv5CAWgmwWfvGrT4H2sw9mQijnLqoY5F2w3cqRQtDM6b)_

## Summary

Point 7 of the UI feedback: spectral analysis must always match the audio after any edit.

The spectrogram is analysed once per source file. Edits are non-destructive: trim, split, stretch, reverse, transpose and warp only change how a clip maps onto that source. The underlay already followed linear edits (trim, cut, `source_rate` stretch, reverse). It was wrong for **warped** clips, though. It drew one linear span across the whole visible clip, so once warp markers were added, dragged or stretched, frequency content showed up at the wrong time.

- `spectrogram::paint` now splits the visible clip at its warp markers (mirrored for reversed clips) and maps each segment separately. Segments narrower than a pixel merge into their neighbour. Unwarped clips still paint as a single span, so their behaviour is unchanged.
- Destructive results (join, recording, reimport) already get a fresh analysis through a new path, a new PCM identity or the on-disk stamp check, so they need no change.

## Tests

- New E2E test `warping_stretching_and_cutting_keep_the_spectrum_aligned_with_the_audio`. It runs warp markers, stretch, split and undo through the running app. For each one it checks that every painted spectral segment matches the clip's playback source mapping at its edges, and that the cached analysis is reused rather than recomputed. Without the fix it fails.
- Passing: `spectrum_e2e`, `spectrum_view_e2e`, `audio_warp_e2e`, `waveform_refinement_e2e`, `signal_analysis_e2e`, the `spectrogram::` unit tests and `cargo clippy -p daw-app --all-targets`.

author: t09tanaka
body:
## Why

With routing a mutant runs only the tests that reach it (usually milliseconds to a few seconds), but every run of it had `max(20 s, 5 x the whole baseline)`. With two or more jobs a mutant in an endless loop held a job for that whole limit, and then had it again in the run alone that follows a time-out. In a crate with about 900 mutants and a slow test suite that is minutes per hung mutant.

The rule this PR keeps: **a faster run must not weaken the check.** What is reported as caught, missed or `timeout` is what 0.2.0 reports.

## What changes

1. **`fix(proc)`: a process group id of 1 or less is never signalled.** `killpg(1)` is `kill(-1)`. The id is always the pid of a child today; `kill_group` and `group_gone_within` now check it. The test covers the predicate only and never calls `kill_group` with such an id.
2. **With routing and two or more jobs, the first run of a mutant is given up sooner.**
   - Tracing records what each test takes alone; the baseline records what each binary takes.
   - `first run = min(whole-suite limit, max(10 s, ceil(5 x the time of the steps of its plan)))`. Listed tests count with the sum of their alone times; a binary that runs whole counts with its baseline time. The estimate is computed in the same function that makes the plan.
   - A first run that reaches it is **not a result**: the mutant is run again alone with the whole-suite limit (or `--timeout`), and only that run decides. A mutant that is slow but ends is caught or missed as before.
   - Not used with one job (there is no second run, so the only run gets the whole limit), with `--timeout`, with `--no-routing`, when tracing was given up, for the mutants built on their own, and for a mutant that no single test reaches.
3. **Release 0.3.0**: version, CHANGELOG, README, `--help`.

The history also holds a change of the `--jobs` default and its revert, and a first version of (2) in which the sooner limit decided the status; the last two commits are the state described here.

## Decisions

- **The sooner limit never decides.** In the first version a mutant that made its tests more than five times slower (and longer than 10 s) without hanging became a `timeout`, which does not fail the run, where 0.2.0 reports it as missed. That is a weaker check, so the second run now uses the old limit.
- **What this costs.** A hung mutant cannot be told from a slow one before the old limit has passed, so it still costs the old limit once. The gain is the first run: about 10 s plus the old limit, instead of twice the old limit, with two or more jobs. With one job a hang costs the old limit once, as in 0.2.0; nothing is gained there, and nothing is lost.
- **`--jobs` default unchanged (a quarter of the processors, at most 4).** What the code guarantees per job: a process group and a `TMPDIR` of its own. What it does not: the jobs share the working directory of the package and the network, so tests that write files there or bind a fixed port can fail under concurrent jobs, and a failed test is a mutant reported as caught. That isolation cannot be shown, so a higher default would weaken the check for such packages. More jobs stay an explicit choice (`--jobs`).

## Measured

On the `run_kit` fixture of this repository (`--re count_to -j 2`, one mutant in an endless loop, baseline about 1 s, whole-suite limit 20 s): the first run is given up after 10 s, the run alone ends after 20 s as `timeout` (`did not end within 20s`), and the mutants take about 30 s. With 0.2.0 it is 2 x 20 s by its rule (derived, not measured again).

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` (all suites pass), `cargo check --all-targets` on 1.89
- New tests:
  - `routed_timeout`, the estimate per plan and per binary, and which run gets which limit (first run of several jobs, run alone, single job, `--timeout`, no routing);
  - `a_mutant_slower_than_the_limit_of_its_own_tests_is_not_a_timeout`: with two jobs, mutants that end after longer than the sooner limit are reported as missed and as caught, the one that never ends is a time-out after the whole limit, and with one job there is no second run. It drives `run_embedded` with a shell script as the test binary and a small floor; a cargo fixture would need a mutant that takes more than the real floor of 10 s;
  - an integration test on the fixture: first run 10 s, run alone with 20 s, `statusReason`, the note, the total;
  - the process group check.

## Not done

- `--timeout 2.5` is still printed as `2s` in the reason and the progress.
- The cost of tracing (one process per test) is unchanged.
- Running the second runs of several hung mutants at the same time would save more, but they would no longer be alone, which is what the second run is for.

author: williamwmarx
body:
This is the last file of track P3b-lp (`native/design/prover.md`). It ports `src/prover/smt/solver/lp/nra-solver.ts`, nla's bridge to nlsat, to `prove-smt`'s `lp/nra_solver.rs`, on top of the nlsat port (#234). It replaces the stub #233 left. That stub declined every check that reached nlsat; now those checks are answered as the TypeScript answers them.

## Port
- **Entry points:**
  - `NraSolver::check(nla, max_conflicts, budget)` (`None` stands for the TypeScript's `Infinity`)
  - `check_assignment(nla)`
  - `value(nla, lp_var)`, which `theory-lra-model.ts` uses
  - `am()`, for the theory's `am.add/mul/compare`
- **Step points:** nlsat steps on the same `ResourceLimit` as in the TypeScript, `nla.limit`, so the step count is the same.
- **Errors:**
  - `NlsatUnsupported` becomes `undef` only where the TypeScript catches it.
  - `Canceled` and the other errors propagate.
- **Iteration order:** the cone's constraint set is iterated, so it is an `OrderedSet`. The other sets and maps are only looked up.
- `nla_core.rs`: `check`'s limits are `Option<u64>`.
  - The test of a check that once declined at the stub now expects the TypeScript's result on the same setup: a Grobner conflict, `[] {0,1,2,3}`.

## Tests
- **The six `nra …` cases of `smt-nlsat.test.ts`** are ported case for case:
  - `check_assignment` refutes x*y ≤ 1, x*x ≤ 1 and x*x = 2;
  - `check` refutes x*x < 1;
  - `check` finds the model x = √2 and makes it nla's;
  - a budget of 1 cancels.

  They also check the exact lemmas and nlsat step counts the TypeScript gives on the same setups.
- **`tests/lp_trace.rs`** now replays `nra` too:
  - `nra.value`, with algebraic numbers encoded as the recorder encodes them;
  - `nra.am.add`, `mul` and `compare`;
  - nlsat's resource-limit callbacks, checked by count on each call: `limit.count()` must equal the recorded `inc` callbacks.
- **Trace results:** on the 45 `tests/fixtures/smt` inputs and 27 nonlinear inputs, all 72 traces are the same; none differ, decline or crash. That includes a trace with 9.9M `inc` callbacks and traces with `nra.value` on irrational roots.
- **Tampering:** I tampered with traces five ways (a dropped `inc` callback, a flipped `inc` answer, a changed `nra.value` interval, a changed `compare` argument, an early `false` answer). The replayer reported the flipped answer as declined and the other four as `differs`.
- **Known gaps:** the order of `inc` calls among a call's other callbacks is not checked, only their count. No recorded trace calls `am.add` or `am.mul`.

## Checks
These were run from main (335d7e5) with the three commits applied:
- `bun install`, `bun run build` and `bun scripts/platform-packages.ts build`.
- In `native`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` (and for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` on `prove-it-wasm`) and `cargo test --locked`.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint` and `bun run format:check`.
- `bun run test`: 3,246 pass, 0 fail.

body:
## What

One branch on today's `main` (`9a76574`) that replaces #13 and #22. #13 and #22 branched before #8, #9, #10, #15, #16, #17, #18 and #21 merged. This branch resolves the conflicts with all of them in one tree, verified on the A100, and rebuilt as linear commits by area:

| commit | what it carries |
|---|---|
| `perf(exec)` | #13/#22's executor (dependency path, static path, fused MLP step), with five of your ports: bf16 storage (#10/#17), the Hopper hook (#17), the version-wait check, `submit_stream`'s window de-dup, and your two litmus controls (`KVM_BREAK_CHUNK_RELEASE`, `KVM_BREAK_CONT`) |
| `perf(ops)` | #13's tiles dispatch, with #16's tile set beside them as `kvmgpt::j16` for one A/B; #16's staged epilogue on the default bf16 geometry; #17's Hopper hook guarded to plain 1xTF32; #21's bf16 attention storage |
| `perf(frontend)` | our lowering (it extends #16's `mm_tile` code); #21's storage pass in full |
| `fix(runtime)` | `OP_WRITES` lists the merged ops, measured with `test_op_writes`'s own recorder (47 ops, 0 differ) |
| `fix(runtime)` | `runtime/abi.py` reads the registry files from `include/kvm_ops_list.inc`, so the fused MLP step's `kvm_ops_fmlp.def` is no longer invisible to Python's task and trace readers |
| `test(litmus)` | your `popticket` mutant and parallel builds, on our claim code |
| `bench` | `bench_mm` times ours, #16 at 144 and 96 KiB, and cuBLAS in one binary |
| `results(a100)` x2 | `results/2026-11-10-a100-merged/`: the panel below, the bench as run, raw JSON, stage logs, every suite's log with its GPU, the GPT rows on main, Phase B's PyTorch side |

## Why

Two bugs on `main` don't exist in the merged tree:

- `kvm_exec.cu:285`: `CK(cudaMemset(S_.trace, ...))` sits inside the `//` comment of the `indeg` memset on the same line (from `fddc183`), so the trace buffer is never zeroed.
- `kvm_exec.cu:1039`: window sizing checks the task count only (`nt > cfg.live_cap && nt <= (1 << 20)`). The merged tree sizes by records (`fits_one_record`).

## Results (A100 SXM4 40 GB, PyTorch 2.15)

| workload | PyTorch's fastest (variant) | ours | ratio | #13/#22 alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MLP h72 d2, 1 run | 72.6 us (`compile_graph_whole`) | 32.6 us | **2.234** | 2.292 |
| MLP h72 d2, 8 runs | 78.8 us (`batched_compile_whole`) | 32.3 us | **2.440** | 2.452 |
| MLP h72 d2, 32 runs | 104.0 us (`batched_compile_whole`) | 46.3 us | **2.246** | 2.288 |
| MLP h48-h104 d2, 8 runs | 137.8 us (`multi_compile_graph_whole`) | 35.8 us | **3.847** | 3.419 |
| MLP h256 d4 | 125.2 us (`compile_graph_whole`) | 250.2 us | **0.501** | 0.525 |
| MLP h1024 d2 | 103.8 us (`compile_graph_whole`) | 309.5 us | **0.335** | 0.343 |
| GPT tiny | 185.1 us (`compile_graph`) | 263.8 us | **0.701** | 0.716 |
| GPT small | 417.3 us (`compile_graph`) | 571.9 us | **0.730** | 0.738 |
| GPT 162M | 63.1 ms (`compile_graph`) | 118.0 ms | **0.537** | 0.543 |
| **geomean** | | | **1.090** | **1.095** |

A ratio is PyTorch's best conventional mode over ours (above 1, ours wins), each row against its own PyTorch run on the same host. Time per training step, median of 7 repetitions. The merge costs the executor about 1% (its own times are x0.991 of #13/#22's, 8 of 9 rows slower by up to 2.4%, against 0.5% between repeated reads of one binary). PyTorch's hetero-row bar is bimodal (137.8 us here, 121.9 us in #13/#22's read); at its fast mode the headline is 1.076x. Every row passed its correctness gates. Method, bench as run, raw JSON and logs: `results/2026-11-10-a100-merged/`.

**Against main, same host and session** (#18's rows, main `9a76574` as it is; PyTorch's bars of the two reads within 0.2%): GPT tiny 641.4 -> 263.8 us (**x2.43**), GPT small 1,549.1 -> 571.9 us (**x2.71**), GPT 162M 135.0 -> 118.0 ms (**x1.15**).

## Roadmap Phase A, on the merged executor (nvcc 12.8)

- **Litmus-mutant suite hang:** it runs to its end in 3 of 3 passes, none hanging, every mutant detected. Each pass still exits 1 on consumer Ampere: the relaxed-CAS `mp` control does not show on that GPU, and the harness counts an undetected control as a failure (`litmus.cu:136-140`). On the A100 every control is detected (below). Three e2e controls stay silent in this harness; #24 makes them bite.
- **`recycle` flake (2 of 3 on your admitter):** 0 failures in 10 (3,000,000 tasks in 100,000 bundles, 16,666 ring wraps). Yours came from `window_done`'s wrap; ours is wrap-safe (`kvm_exec.cu:682`).
- **`test_ops` T=1 attention-backward bound:** on the A100's production build the T=1 backward noise sweep (64 seeds x hd 16/32/64/128) reads a worst |noise|/bound of 0.089, an 11x margin, and its largest |dq|, |dk| is 2.77e-5, under the README's 1e-4; the single T=1 cases read 0.004-0.053 of their bounds (`results/2026-11-10-a100-merged/tests/test_ops_a100.log`). The README item itself is your `fix/readme-t1-attn-bwd`.
- **Litmus on the A100:** `litmus_prod mp` 0 violations in 2,000,000 rounds, every control detected; `litmus_weakpub` 63 violations (the mutant is caught).

## Op ids

New ids stay below 128: `sgd_range` 123, `fmlp_slice`/`fmlp_sgd` 124/125, `round_tf32` 126, `softmax_ce_fused` 127. Id 119 (`matmul_tile_dgelu`) is retired: `matmul_tile`'s flag 512 does its work in the epilogue.

- `softmax_ce_fused` was 134 on #13. #19's split tick assigns `doom_sim` = 134, and `runtime/abi.py` raises on a duplicate id, so the frontend would stop the day both land. We moved ours.
- Future fused-step ops take 176..199, between #19's control ops (160..175) and the test pack (200+). Tell us if you want another range.
- #19 merges onto this branch with 3 text conflicts (`frontend/kvmfe/fuse.py`, `include/kvm_exec.cuh`, `kvm_exec.cu`). It adds no new use of 119.

## QA

Tested tree for the GPU results: this branch's tree before two later changes, both CPU-checked (end of this section).

- **CPU:** `tests` 154 OK; `tests/frontend` 133 OK; `tests/dist` 74 OK; `examples/models` 7 OK; `bash -n` on 75 scripts; `test_fuse_pass` on h72-d2, h128-d4, h256-d2, h576-d1.
- **RTX 3090-class build (sm_86, `-DKVM_GPT_BIG_BK=16 -DKVM_GPT_MMA_SMEM=90112`):** `test_exec` 8,609 checks, 0 failed; `test_ops` 4,999 passed, 0 failed, 67 skipped (cases this build cannot compile: hd=128 attention, the T=1 sweep); static path `run_check.sh` PASS at 1, 4, 16 and 107 workers; `gptdiff` 8/8 on the static path; memcheck, racecheck and synccheck clean.
- **A100 (production build):** `test_ops` 5,403 passed, 0 failed (every case, hd=128 included); `test_e2e` 7/7; memcheck on the attention cases clean; static path `run_check.sh` PASS; litmus as above. `test_exec` with sanitizers did not run on the A100 (its full-pack build outlasted the session's GPU time); its coverage is the RTX 3090 run above, 8,609 checks with 0 failed. The roadmap's Phase B row (162M bf16s) did not run on the executor's side: its build, with every op pack, was still compiling when the GPU time ended. PyTorch's side is measured on the same A100 (eager 51.2-51.7 ms a step), so the executor's gate is 67.1 ms.

Two changes came after the GPU builds, both CPU-checked on this branch's tree: `softmax_ce_fused`'s id (one registry line; every use is by name) and `runtime/abi.py` reading the registry list from `include/kvm_ops_list.inc`, so `kvm_ops_fmlp.def`'s ops are no longer invisible to Python (Python only).

Supersedes #13 and #22.

author: danieljoppi
body:
Part of #179. Merge after #180 (the link targets its "Outside contributions" section).

## What

`templates/README.md.in`, org-sync's README seed, gets a three-line `## Contributing` section before `## Licence`. The natural place, since the seed is only a title, the badges, a description and the licence pointer. It links CONTRIBUTING "Outside contributions" (#180) and names `git commit -s`.

The link is absolute (`swarm-routing/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#outside-contributions`), so it works from any repository, including one that has its own `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Reach

`README.md` is a **seed**: it is written once and then belongs to the repository. So this reaches **new** repositories only (`org_sync.py init`). `org_sync.py seeds` will list existing READMEs as `differs`, which is information only (exit 0). `reseed README.md` would overwrite a whole hand-written README, so it is not a way to add the line there. In existing repositories, a contributor finds CONTRIBUTING through GitHub's own "Contributing" link: the org default is served to every repository without its own. A per-repository README line, if wanted, is a hand edit or a future managed section. I have not made it one, to keep this short.

## Verification

- org-sync, docs-review and org-bot self-tests: pass
- a fresh `org_sync.py init --kind python` repo through `check_docs.py`: same warnings with and without this change (none about the new section)

Follow-up to #536 / #537.

`.retention.yaml`'s rules sections (`intents`, `runs`, `logs`) only took a list of rules, so a hand-written map such as

```yaml
logs:
  keep: 7
  since: 30 days
```

was rejected (and the builder quietly skipped log pruning). Now every rules section, and every `protected:` list, reads a bare map as a single rule, so all three sections take the same two shapes. An empty map counts as an empty section (keep everything), like an empty list. The shipped defaults are unchanged.

ADR-004 §10 says so, with an amendment bullet.

## Verification

- New test: each of the three sections parses a map (with a map `protected:`) the same as the list form; `{}` is an empty section.
- Local gates: full pytest (incl. slow) 4057 passed, ruff, ty, cspell, markdownlint clean.

author: andrewdakers
body:
**Task:** the stage's half of ground textures and picture skies (spec 17 §2, #348, agreed with S4; WP3b, 3.7). S4's #350 makes the assets. This works without them, and with no Backstage at all.

## Ground textures
- When Backstage has an item under a ground's own id (`storystage/Ground/<name>`), `load()` reads its one tile and its picture. `preload` fetches it too.
- The picture goes on the stage's own ground material, not the glTF's, so Alice's lights colour it as they colour a flat ground.
  - It's shaded by `TEXTURE_SHADE`, so a picture of the ground's on-screen colour looks exactly like the flat ground (tested).
  - It tiles across the 600 m ground or the room's floor, ground size ÷ tile size, with mipmaps and up to 8× anisotropic filtering.
  - The ground's opacity, the walls and the ceiling stay as they were. `paint` keeps using the colours.
- **Pictures as they are:** a backdrop's item is read without sRGB buffers. With them, Babylon.js hands the plain material linear values, and a texture of the grass colour showed at (29, 87, 11) instead of (95, 158, 58).

## Picture skies (the owner's choice, 10 Nov)
- `PICTURE_SKY_TYPES`: `storystage/Sky/clearDay`, `cloudy`, `sunset` and `night`, each with `storystage/Lighting/<same name>`. Their atmosphere and lighting colours are **provisional** until S4's build reports each picture's horizon and a lighting to suit.
- The dome uses the item's mesh with the stage's own material. It's unlit and without fog, kept on the camera, and scaled to just inside the 256 m far clip, so it's behind everything there is to see. It's in pictures, crossfades and fades.
- Fog and the background follow the atmosphere colour. Setting the atmosphere colour tints the picture by new ÷ own, at most 1 (the owner's choice).

## What's missing
- A ground with no item is drawn in its colour, as before, and isn't reported.
- A picture sky with no item, or any backdrop item that can't be read, is drawn in its colour, the scene plays on, and it's reported as `{ kind: 'backdrop', id }`.
- FakeStage does the same for a picture sky that `knownModels` doesn't list.

## Checked
- **Two new browser tests**, using test files made in code to the layout of S4's makers (`tinyGroundTileUrl`, `tinySkyDomeUrl`):
  - A texture of grass's own colour gives the same pixels as the flat ground. A black and white check tiles near the camera. An item that can't be read falls back and is reported.
  - The dome's middle (u = 0.5) is straight ahead, with +X on the picture's left and −X on its right, bright above the horizon and dim below. Half its own atmosphere colour halves it. With no item, the sky is its atmosphere colour, reported.
- **Looked at:** a textured ground tiling to the horizon without shimmer, and a sunset dome with its grid the right way round. Both are attached to "keeps pictures of the scenes" for reviewers.
- **Unit tests:** the picture skies and their lighting, and FakeStage's reporting.
- **Locally:** all 26 browser tests with software rendering, as in CI, and all 26 on the owner's RTX 2060. Also 3813 tests, typecheck, ESLint, the boundary check and Prettier.

**One thing noticed, not changed here:** models' own pictures go onto the stage's plain materials the same way, so textured models (KayKit, the MakeHuman people) are drawn darker than their files mean. Fixing that changes how every textured model looks, so it's a separate decision.

body: Four contained fixes to sprint 001 catalog code. ## What changed and why **Resource cards open detail pages in-app.** `ResourceCard` linked with a plain ``, so opening a resource from `/resources` or a type page reloaded the whole page. It now uses an Inertia ``, as AGENTS.md asks for links between new pages. Cards are only rendered by `catalog/CatalogPage` and `catalog/TypePage` (the home page has none), and those pages only exist while the `catalog` page group is on, which is also what serves the detail page, so the target is always a new page. The comparison table's resource and font links on type pages were plain `` to the same detail pages and now use `` too. Download links are unchanged. **Comparison table at phone width.** The table already scrolled sideways inside its container, but the name column scrolled away with it, so at 360 to 412 px you saw a few numbers with no name. The name column is now sticky (`left-0`, card background, an inset shadow as its edge, since a border on a sticky cell scrolls away under `border-collapse`), and its minimum width drops to 9rem below `sm` so more of the other columns fit. The page itself still never scrolls sideways. **Format docs button on type pages.** The type page header now has an outline button " format docs" (for example "Mushaf layout format docs"), as in the prototype. The URL comes from `Catalog::Taxonomy.guide_path`, which the detail page's Data tab now uses too, sent as the nullable `guidePath` prop of `Catalog::TypesShowResource`; the button is only shown when the type has a guide. author: harahu
body:
Proof-only change to `TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Finsupp/Coderivation.lean`, which was added in #17378. No statement, name, attribute, docstring or import changes.

`LinearMap.eq_zero_of_finsupp_comul_comp_eq` was proved with `Finsupp.lhom_ext` and closed with a six-rule `rw` chain (`← mul_one r, ← smul_eq_mul, ← Finsupp.smul_single, map_smul, hzero, smul_zero`) and then a bare `rfl`. That `rfl` relied on undocumented definitional unfolding: it proves `0 = (0 : _ →ₗ[R] _) (single i r)`. Both are proof-quality rubric issues: a brittle named-lemma `rw` chain, and reliance on accidental definitional equality.

The new proof reduces to the basis vector `single i 1` with `Finsupp.lhom_ext'` and `LinearMap.ext_ring`. It then closes the goal with `simpa`, using `Finsupp.eq_zero_of_comul_eq_tmul_add_tmul` as before. The `simpa` uses only rewrite lemmas (`simpa?` reports `coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, Finsupp.lsingle_apply, zero_comp, LinearMap.zero_apply`). The `rw` chain, the `rfl` and the intermediate `hzero` are removed, so the proof is 4 lines shorter.

There is no call-site cost: no statement changes, and no module in the repository imports this file.

I also considered dropping the `p`/`q` lets in `Finsupp.eq_zero_of_comul_eq_tmul_add_tmul` in favour of `congr(...)` with `map (lapply i) (lapply i)` directly. I left it unchanged. That version has to repeat `TensorProduct.lid R R (map (lapply i) (lapply i) ...)` three times and wrap past 100 columns. It saves almost nothing and is no clearer than the named `q`.

author: vitoramaral10
body:
## What and why

The app grows from a firmware updater into a preset editor, and is renamed **Pocket AMP Tools**. It merges what the private pocket-amp-editor prototype measured on hardware. Closes #11.

- **Backups v2:** every preset as named fields (models and knobs by name), restored from those fields, so a file edited by hand or by an AI goes back to the pedal. v1 files still restore.
- **Editor:** list and detail of the 80 presets, the chain, each block's model and knobs, and the EQ. It writes only what changed, and refuses if the pedal changed since it was read.
- **Live on pedal:** edits play on the active preset's RAM as they are made.
- **Cabinets:** a user IR can be put in any of the 20 CAB slots.
- **AI assistant:** optional, on an OpenAI-compatible service the user sets up.
- **Bluetooth on Linux:** a paired pedal through BlueZ, presets only.
- **Write guard:** every packet to the pedal is checked against the shapes measured on hardware before it is sent.

## How it was checked

- [x] `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` pass (84 tests, including the adversarial review's findings)
- [x] Changes to the update path have a test against the simulated pedal
- [ ] Safety checks are unchanged. They are **stricter**:
  - a clone vendor's own package is refused;
  - the update checks the exact identity it confirmed;
  - a second pedal is never taken for the one coming back;
  - a package other than the known official V1.05 needs an extra confirmation.

Tested on: Linux, Pocket AMP V1.05 over USB.
- **Detection:** works.
- **Full bank read:** all 80 stored presets pass the guard, and the v2 file reopens byte for byte.
- **Live edits:** on/off, a knob and the chain, undone by reloading the preset.
- **Preset write round trip:** checked through a power cycle; the value survived it.
- **Not tested on hardware:** firmware update, IR upload, Bluetooth, Windows and macOS.

Measured on the pedal along the way: a V1.05 pedal acknowledges but ignores a Change Routing unless FX and AMP are the first two blocks (14 of 14 orders), so the editor keeps them there.

author: joeldacruz
body:
## O que muda
- `ArenaGate` passa a aceitar sessão **completa de plataforma** (`global_admin` + MFA) em qualquer arena ativa, sem `Membership` (nenhum vínculo artificial). Jogador → 403; token preliminar de MFA → 401; arena suspensa → 403; arena do caminho ≠ do recurso → 404.
- Portal DEV: botão **Abrir Gestão da arena**. Handoff por `postMessage` same-origin + ticket de uso único (60 s) trocado por sessão de app `arena` limitada a **uma** arena (1 h). **Nenhum token/ticket em URL.** A sessão é reavaliada a cada requisição (conta inativa, sem `global_admin` ou sem MFA ⇒ cai).
- Auditoria `platform.arena_act` em toda requisição mutante em contexto global (sem corpo/segredos).
- O global gerencia replays de qualquer arena, mas não reproduz conteúdo privado; não cria `global_admin`; guarda de último gestor preservada.
- Sem migração. Docs: `docs/ACESSO-GLOBAL-ADMIN-GESTAO.md`.

## Base / reconciliação
A `main` não contém `deps.py`/`routers/arena.py`; a base é `feat/gestao-usuarios-arena` (`936e2b6`, informada como em produção). Os arquivos candidatos aplicados manualmente no `cmtb-srv01` devem ser substituídos pelos desta branch via `git checkout` (não `cp -a`). Ver PR #9.

## Testes (evidências reais)
- Suíte completa (commit anterior ao ajuste de testes): 438 passed, 2 failed — as 2 falhas eram testes antigos de RBAC que afirmavam o contrário da regra nova; foram atualizados e o arquivo `test_rbac_separation.py` foi reexecutado e passou. **A suíte completa não foi reexecutada depois disso.**
- `test_global_admin_arena.py` (9 testes) passa.
- E2E de navegador no commit atual: 54/54 passos.
- Não houve validação com token real de plataforma/MFA no servidor.

## Atenção
**Não fazer merge nem deploy automaticamente.** Pendente: validar sessão real com MFA no `cmtb-srv01` e confirmar rollback.

body:
Closes #95
Closes #123

## 概要
Issue #95（工房: スマホ幅 390px で文字7px・マス約12px・押せない/見切れる）への対応。minori の「指定値」どおりに縦持ち用レイアウトを実装。**横向き誘導オーバーレイ（暫定策）ではなく本実装**（B案）。

## 変更
- 縦持ち判定（幅 ≤ 600px かつ縦長）のとき、canvas を画面の CSS ピクセルと同じ大きさにして縮小しない（Phaser FIT 起因の 7.3px 縮小をやめる）。工房を出るとき 320×180 に戻す
- 盤面: 幅 360px（左右 15px）・1マス 30px × 12列・y=56 から上詰め
- ヒント: y=8・高さ 40px・16px・タッチ版の文言（タップ=置く／消すボタン=消す／向きボタン=向き）
- 操作列（向き・音高・消す・音・全消し）: 各 44×44px 以上・gap 8px。長押し/右クリックの代わりに **「消す」モード**（ON の間マスのタップで消す）を追加
- 機械の棚: 横スクロール（高さ 64px・ボタン 64×56px 以上・scroll-snap・左右 16px のフェード）
- 注文票: 本文 16px 以上。内容が多いときは内部スクロール
- 実行ボタン: 画面下固定・358×52px・safe-area 対応
- 横持ち・PC の見た目は変更なし（棚の入れ物は `display: contents`）
- `createSceneFx` に任意の幅・高さ引数を追加（既定は 320×180）

## minori 指定値との差分（正直に）
- **「元に戻す」ボタンは未実装**（元に戻す機能がコードに無いため。別 Issue 推奨）

- 盤面セルは 30px（44px 例外）

## 他 PR との関係
- **PR #133（AE#123 A案: 縦持ちは「横にしてください」オーバーレイ）と競合する**: #133 が先にマージされると縦持ちではオーバーレイが全面に出て、この縦レイアウトは見えない。B案（縦対応）を採るなら #133 は不要、A案なら本 PR は保留。採否は daichi 判断
- **AE#123 について**: 縦持ちの扱い（A案/B案）は kotoha の方針を未受領のまま進めた。回答が違えば再修正する。kotoha の回答が届き次第共有する。
- PR #115（#94 棚の 2 列化）と `workshop.css` / `WorkshopScene.ts` が重なる。本 PR は main 基点。後からマージする側で rebase が必要（棚を palette/actions に分けたため #115 の 2 列化とは衝突しうる）

author: micaelarp
body:
## Qué cambia
La barra de secciones pasa a dos niveles: arriba **Hoy**, **Hacer** y **Guardados**; dentro de Hacer están Tareas y Hábitos y dentro de Guardados, Leer, Ver y Probar. Las URLs no cambian (`/tareas`, `/habitos`, `/leer`, `/ver`, `/probar`); solo cambia cómo se llega.

## Por qué
Con seis enlaces planos la barra ya se desplazaba en pantallas de 360 px, y la pantalla de Objetivos (siguiente PR) sería el séptimo. El prototipo de Mica usaba pestañas principales con subpestañas en el celular; esto sigue esa lógica.

## Cómo se verificó
- 126 tests y build de producción en verde; test-first (4 tests en rojo antes de implementar).
- Build servido en navegador a 320, 360 y 390 px en `/hoy`, `/tareas` y `/ver`: todos los enlaces miden al menos 91×44 px, sin texto cortado ni desborde; la navegación entre grupos y subsecciones funciona y deja el grupo marcado.
- Pendiente: probarlo en el iPhone.

## Alternativas descartadas
- Seguir con una barra plana que se desplaza: esconde secciones en un iPhone normal.
- Una barra inferior de pestañas (como en apps nativas): cambia el diseño visual del prototipo y no hace falta para resolver esto.
- Un menú desplegable ("hamburguesa"): oculta todo detrás de un toque; tres grupos siempre visibles son más directos.
- Deuda asumida: los nombres "Hacer" y "Guardados" son una propuesta mía; se cambian en un solo lugar (`GRUPOS`).

author: matias-ceau
body:
## Why

The fictional dossiers were four pages long and had no intake observation. Real records run to 20-30 pages, open with an observation that retraces the whole trajectory, and reveal some elements only years later. That is the case the tool exists for, so it is now the case it is measured on.

## What

- **Six long fictional dossiers** (`data/anonymized/dossiers-longs/`): 21 to 26 pages, 74 to 76 observations, six to nine years of follow-up. Each expected event carries its origin (intake, follow-up, revealed late). `scripts/check_long_dossier.py` checks size, intake observation and origins.
- **Segmentation by rules**: known exports are split into observations locally, without a model call (`segment-rules.ts`); the model is only asked when the layout is unknown.
- **Regrouping of duplicates**: a dossier read in several lots gets one more request, without any observation text, saying which events are the same thing. The merge is done and checked by code; every regrouped mention stays visible and discordant dates are flagged (`consolidate.ts`).
- **Runs without a paid call**: each request is written to a file and answered from a file (`file-transport.ts`). The 33 requests and answers of the long dossiers are kept in `data/processed/frise/answers/longs-regroupe1/`, so the run replays identically.
- **Scoring**: recall by origin, estimated cost of file-answered runs, `rapport-longs.md` and its JSON summary.
- **Demonstration and library**: one long dossier replayed end to end, regrouping included; the library lists the six long dossiers, then the fourteen short ones.
- An event without a start is placed at its first mention; recordings made before that rule replay as their own run went.

## Results (long dossiers)

- 468 of 532 expected events found (88 %): intake 87 %, follow-up 88 %, revealed late 87 %.
- Start date right for 94 % of found events, compatible end for 67 %.
- Regrouping: 725 → 553 tracks for 404 expected; lower-bound precision 40 % → 55 %, recall 90 % → 88 %.
- Cost is **estimated** from the characters exchanged (the answers were written from files, outside the API): about 0.57 $ per dossier.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 670 passed; `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `PW_PORT=4319 npm run e2e`: 8 passed
- `uv run pytest`: 30 passed; `ruff` clean on the changed files
- Replay from the saved answers: 0 request left to answer, same report

## Note

Merging publishes the application (GitHub Pages) with the new demonstration and library.

author: lamontaes
body:
Touches pool item: laws-work-requirement-pays-households-more (cause and fix written in; nothing built, so the item stays open).

## What changed for the player

Nothing.

## What I found

The money is one extra month of food aid paid to the town's counted households. The work requirement does not cause it. The cause is how a changed payment is reopened.

- **Cause.** `reconcileObligations` in `src/core2/law-reach/group-b-money.ts` (line 366) ends a standing payment when its amount changes and opens a new one due tomorrow (line 392 and line 427), whatever day the old one was next due. The monthly close runs food aid on the 1st, so payments fall due on the 2nd. The law's change-day rerun (`src/core2/law-reach/group-b.ts`, the `assistance-time-limit` case, line 526) runs food aid again on the law's effective date. The counted households' amount has drifted since the 1st, so their payment is reopened and paid again the next day.
- **Place and seed.** Marion, Mississippi, bench seed 7df73e53cd67, place key 2845160. The seed alone draws Trilla, Illinois. County law row `law:county:28075:county:us-policy-positions:health-human-services.work-requirement-for-assistance:general:2025-02-19:2025-1`, enacted with no added section.
- **Record ids.** Obligation `reach-b:benefit:snap-maximum:US|residents:jurisdiction_7fa9e484fb9a8bc7` paid $113,002 on 2025-02-02 in both worlds. In the law world it paid again on 2025-02-20. Its due day moved to the 20th, so the 2025-04-01 reopen paid again on 2025-04-02. That is six payments against the twin's five. After 120 days the federal `reach-b` lines were $111,294 lower and counted households $80,666 higher.
- **State version.** Paid 2025-03-02, then again 2025-03-22 at $118,485. After 180 days the federal treasury was $116,166 lower and counted households $93,525 higher.
- **Why the requirement changes nobody's limit here.** The federal starting row is in force from 2024-07-01, and it is the first yes level. Both worlds read the same limit and stopped the same 78 heads on 2025-04-01.
- **Probe.** In my working copy only, I made `reconcileObligations` keep the old obligation's next due date. The county result moved to federal +$5,315 and counted households −$2,480, which is drift between the twins. I undid the probe; it is not in this pull request.
- **Ruled out.** A month counted twice against the time limit: `recordDraws` skips a month already recorded.
- **Fix written into the item.** Keep the due date when only the amount changes. This covers every group B benefit that goes through `reconcileObligations`. The item also asks for a test that fails if anyone is paid twice in a month. Model: Sonnet, medium effort, 3 hours.

## Still unknown

- Why LaGrange, Wyoming moved almost nothing.
- How many of the audit's other wrong-way law results are this same reopening.
- `law-run.ts` hashes its seed again, so it cannot replay Marion. The item's Done when now says so.

## Removed

Nothing.

author: junioryono
body:
Closes #845.

## What changed and why

Every removal of the Ceph store's advisory locks blocklisted a client that no longer existed. Each blocklist entry is a new OSD map epoch, which every OSD and the host's kernel client have to take.

**Where the entries came from.** Measured on ubuntu-01 on 2026-11-10 with bpftrace over 150 s:
- `rbd lock rm` on `billet-cache/.cache-index` ran 54 times.
- The monitor recorded 56 `osd blocklist add` entries in the same window, each from a short-lived `client.billet` session.
- That is about 35 epochs a minute, with about 1,060 entries listed.
- No other `rbd` command lined up with the entries: the kernel client all 114 mapped devices share never issued one, and the publish lock (golden images only) ran no removal in that window.

**Why the blocklist fenced nothing.**
- The locker an advisory lock records is the client of the `rbd lock add` that took it. That CLI exits the moment it has.
- The holder is a billet process or the build script, not a Ceph client. Every command it runs after the add is a new client the entry doesn't name.
- So exclusion was already resting on the cookie, its age and the heartbeat alone. The guest-image build script's comment had said "breaking it fences nothing" all along.

**Proof the option works.** On a throwaway 1 MiB image the same day (Ceph 20.2.0):
- A default `lock rm` added a blocklist entry naming the locker's address.
- `--rbd_blocklist_on_break_lock false lock rm` removed the lock and added none.

**The change.**
- The three removals pass the option: `Release`, the stale holder's break, and `removeAbandoned`.
- The build script's two removals do too, and so does the hint it prints for an operator.
- `keepKernelClient` becomes `noBlocklist`, since it now covers both reasons; its doc comment states both.
- The skill text and the rule test that held the opposite ("its `lock rm` keeps the blocklist that is its fence") are turned round. The dropped skill sentence is recorded in `skills-dropped.txt`.
- A new measured fact records the trace.

## How it was verified

- The `internal/store/ceph` tests, and the skills tests, on the shared Linux host.
- `requireLockRemovalsBlocklistNobody` requires at least one removal and the option on every one. It's called from the tests of the release, stale-holder break, abandoned-cookie and golden-import paths; the flipped rule in `requireCacheImageRules` judges the cache-index releases in the lifecycle flow.
- Mutations: reverting each of the three Go sites alone fails its test. Dropping the option from either build-script line fails `TestTheBuildRemovesItsPublishLockWithoutABlocklist`, which runs both shell functions against a recording `rbd`.
- Codex review: no P0–P2. Its one P3, that the shell removals had no test, is addressed by that test.

## Not covered

The fleet's epoch rate after this ships isn't measured yet. I'll read `ceph osd dump` before and after the next release reaches ubuntu-01. The entries already listed expire on Ceph's own schedule.

author: jasondk11
body:
**Bug:** recruiting didn't work on J's realm. WoW Forever shows a surname after a character's name: `/who`, the guild roster, raid roster, chat lines and system messages say "Be Fachada" or "Gorm Tshabalala". But `UnitName`, whispers and every shared record use the first word ("Gorm"; that's what J's own records are written as).

- **Recruiting:** queued names like "Be Fachada". A shared record key can't hold a space, so **Message** failed for everyone ("Couldn't note that for the guild"). `/w Be Fachada …` would also have whispered "Be" the wrong text.
- **The app had every guildmate twice:** "Gorm" from the addon and "Gorm Tshabalala" from the roster scan. That affected the roster, leveling matches, the instance helper and nearby (which compared roster names with `UnitName`), boss-kill raiders, celebrations' buddy and joined lines, and donation credit (bank log names).
- **Chat-log sender check (from #44):** it would have read "Tshabalala" as the sender, refusing J's own celebrations and calls to arms for Discord.

**Fix:** the character is the first word of the name.
- **Addon:** every name taken from the game uses `^([^%-%s]+)`, which drops both the realm and the surname. Roster scans store first names. The recruiting queue drops entries saved with a surname.
- **App:** `shared/names.js` `baseName` is applied to roster uploads, bank log lines and the chat-log sender (which may now contain a space).
- **Migration 32:** merges the roster's surname copies into the real characters (level, rank, online, first seen and so on carry over), renames lone ones, and fixes bank log and donation names.
- Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md ("Character names").

**Tests**
- New: `surnames.test.js` (baseName, the migration merge, uploads and bank log), the recruit surname flow, and the sender with a surname.
- Updated: the tests that expected "Grommash Hellscream" as its own character.
- Full suite: 991 pass. The 2 failures were those old expectations, now updated and passing.

body:
## What's new

- **? blocks on the path**: one at the start and one between every pair of pipes. Each is its own stop, and left/right now walk stop to stop, all the way back to the start.
- **Up = jump**, and only when standing under a block (or on the way to one). Enter and click also work on blocks. Down no longer does anything.
- **New sprite frame** (`hit`, fist raised) and a short hop whose peak meets the block; the block bumps and turns used.
- **Chest screen** (`js/chest.js`): shows everything at once instead of cards. The chest drops in and opens with a burst, then every skill tile pops out with its icon, `NEW SKILL` or `LV a >> LV b`, a level bar whose new pips flash in, and a one-line detail. Everything is on screen in under a second, and any key or click closes it. With reduced motion it appears instantly with no animation.

body:
Marco M3 do Cursor (meta de 100%): as duas dependências de sistema que faltavam.

## O que muda
- **`/usr/bin/security`** vira Mach-O (`userland/cli-macos/security.c`, compilado pelo `tools/build.sh`). O `@vscode/proxy-agent` do Cursor e do VS Code roda `cp.spawn('/usr/bin/security', ['find-certificate','-a','-p'])` e rejeita saída ≠ 0. Agora sai o PEM das 118 raízes da Mozilla que o kernel embute (`SecTrustSettingsCopyCertificates`). `find/add/delete-generic-password` usam o Keychain do mOS. Keychain de usuário sem certificado sai 44, como no macOS.
- **git na imagem**: `tools/stage-git.sh` põe o git 2.55.0 (bottle Intel, sha256 do ghcr conferido pelo `fetch-bottles.sh`) em `/usr/local/opt/git`, com `libpcre2-8.0.dylib` e `libintl.8.dylib`. Os ~150 hardlinks de `libexec/git-core` viram `#mOS-link:`: **27 MiB em vez de 619 MiB**. `stage-apps-oficiais.sh` baixa `git gettext` e passa `--bottles` ao Cursor.
- Saem os shims falsos `tools/brew-shims/git` e `security` (certificado vazio, `git init` de mentira). Sem bottle, `--cursor-extras` agora falha com mensagem.
- `machotest`: `SYS_NET`/`MOS_NET_TLS_ROOTS` (lê `assets/certs/cacert.pem`), `SYS_CHMOD` e o `mode` do stat (o Keychain exige pasta 0700 e chave 0600).
- CI Linux roda os dois testes novos.

## Só se prova na VM / no PC

author: yenhenglaitt
body:
## Summary

Five Key Manager behaviours that the specification states had no grade or coverage in any open-tree test. This PR extends two existing leaves: `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` (shred fill, second revoke, warm reload) and `sep_km_sram_scrambler_key_rand_test` (S-box input coverage). It adds no test module and no testlist entry, and it does not edit the TB, RTL, RDL or specification. Return codes that no text fixes are logged as `OBS-` lines and not graded.

Below, "KF" is `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/firmware.adoc`, "KA" is `hw/ip/key_manager/doc/architecture.adoc` and "SA" is `hw/ip/scrambler/doc/architecture.adoc`.

Checks, before -> after:

- `CHK-SHRED-FILL` (`sep_km_command_set_rand_test`, both AES shreds of the leaf: AES holding KAT_KEY_A, then KAT_KEY_B). Before, CHK-SHRED graded the return code, the destination echo and that AES re-keys afterwards, and CHK-GONE graded that a shredded AES does not start. The shredded key material itself was not observed. After, the leaf captures the AW/W beats on the AES port of the `KM-BUS` key-path tap between the CMD_ENGINE_SHRED send and its response, pairs them in order, and decodes the share offsets from the generated register header. Five terms:
  - (a) every byte lane of all 16 share words (KEY_SHARE0[0..7], KEY_SHARE1[0..7]) is written at least once, so an empty capture fails;
  - (b) the `CHK5_km` EDN-to-KM beat count of the DRBG scoreboard rises during the shred;
  - (c) the final share-0 vector, the final share-1 vector and their XOR each differ from the key the engine held;
  - (d) share-0 data and share-1 data are each not one repeated value;
  - (e) the share data of the second shred differs from the first.

  Golden: KF:1803-1805 ("Clear `key_valid`, then overwrite both shares with PRNG data in shuffled order for `SHRED_ITER + 1` passes. Normal calls reseed from the DRBG before each pass"), KF:1447-1453 (a 128-bit PRNG state seeded from four DRBG words), KA:292-294 (8-word shares whose XOR is the key). Terms (c) to (e) compare whole vectors only. A correct KM fails one of them with probability at most 2^-128, the PRNG state width, and every failure replays from its seed. The pass count stays unstated, so the per-offset beat count and the strobes are logged only (`INFO-SHRED-FILL`). The docstring "not observed" bullet is replaced by this record.
- `CHK-REVOKE-TWICE` (`sep_km_command_set_rand_test`, two sites). Before, the revoked handle was revoked again only with a reserved bit set, and that frame was logged, not graded. After, CMD_KEY_REVOKE of the already-revoked handle, with the reserved bits 0, is sent right after CHK-CLOSED (site `revoked`) and again on the full vault after CHK-VAULT-FULL (site `full-vault`). At each site the revoke is refused with _invalid_arg_ and RETURN_ARG 0, or with _failure_ and no RETURN_ARG, and CHK-ALIVE follows. On the full vault, the single-slot CMD_KEY_LOAD that follows still fails with no argument, so the refused revoke freed no slot. Golden: KF:433-439 (the argument each code carries), KF:1909 ("Destroy handle. Reject an invalid handle"), KF:680-682 (resource exhaustion returns _failure_ with no argument). Which of the two codes applies is not stated, so the code is logged as `OBS-REVOKE-TWICE`.
- `CHK-VAULT-WARM-LOAD` (`sep_km_command_set_rand_test`, a new last leg after CHK-OTP-CHG-DORMANT, so no existing check sees a changed pre-state). Before, the vault was filled and the refused GENERATE and LOAD were graded, and no warm reset followed. After, with the vault still full, the KM bit of `SW_RESET_N` is written low and then high, each write read back, and the KM announces `RESP_KM_READY`. Then three things are graded:
  - the single-slot CMD_KEY_LOAD that the full vault refused returns _success_ with handle 1 and its size and destination echoed;
  - a CMD_KEY_TRANSFER to AES of a handle issued before the reset, which the registry initialization cleared, is refused with _failure_ and no RETURN_ARG, and CHK-ALIVE follows;
  - a CMD_KEY_TRANSFER of the new handle 1 to AES returns _success_ with the handle and destination echoed, so a dead KM-to-AES path after the warm reset fails.

  Golden: KF:1382 (the boot initializes the key registry), KF:1889-1895 (handles from 1; Initialize clears every entry and sets the next handle to 1), KF:1763-1764 and KA:441 (a warm reset clears the slot locks), KF:690-691 and KF:504-513 (the success arguments), KF:1069-1070 (an unavailable handle gets _failure_). The refused load of CHK-VAULT-FULL in the same seed is the control of the load term, and the transfer of handle 1 is the control of the refusal. The stale-handle code is also logged as `OBS-WARM-STALE-HANDLE`.
- `CTRL-SSCR-SBOX-STORES` (`sep_km_sram_scrambler_key_rand_test`), new. A test-local watcher on `km_sram_scr_wr_count_o` must see each of the 64 stores of the 64-store run as exactly one rise of the count. SCRAMBLER_KEY (`km_csr_scrambler_key_o`, `KM-CSR` tap) must read the plan key kA at the ready and at the done message. This line gates the coverage below: a leaf whose store run or key read fails samples nothing. The existing `CHK-SSCR-*` checks are unchanged.

Coverage, new group `sep_km_sram_sbox_in_cg` (owner `sep_km_sram_scrambler_key_rand_test`, 168 bins):

- `cp_data_lane0` to `cp_data_lane7`: the S-box input `(W ^ Rkey)[4j+3:4j]` of data nibble lane j, values 0x0 to 0xF (128 bins). SA:76, :115-116, :132, :136, :183, :222, :247.
- `cp_addr_lane0` (word-index bits [12:9], 16 bins) and `cp_addr_lane1` to `cp_addr_lane3` ([8:6], [5:3], [2:0], 8 bins each). SA:192-196, :217. The specification does not state which key bits the address path XORs in. All 64 stores use the one key kA, and under one key the XOR is one-to-one on each lane, so the plaintext lane values cover every S-box input value of the lane, whatever the slice.
- The group is model-side and samples no DUT net. After CHK-SSCR-ROWS, CHK-SSCR-ALIAS and CTRL-SSCR-SBOX-STORES pass, the leaf computes each store's values from its plan word and the specification round key (`scr_round_key` in `sep_km_img_param.py`). It writes them through one new setter, `set_km_sbox_in` in `sep_fcov_gate.py`, and `u_sep_fcov` samples inside the owner's window. A bin hit therefore does not show the S-box input inside the DUT, because the KM SRAM has no cipher golden. What it shows is that the graded store stream, taken by the DUT under the key it reported, presents each value. `SEP_FCOV.adoc` says the same.
- The plan makes the first 16 of the 64 stores a sweep, so every seed closes all 168 bins: store i puts i in every data nibble of `W ^ Rkey` and in bits [12:9], and steps each 3-bit lane from a drawn offset. The parameter-block layout and the committed image are unchanged. `ScrPlanTest.test_sbox_in_closure` checks the closure for seeds 1 to 500 and 0xFFFF_FFFF, and `test_round_key_rows` pins `scr_round_key` to rows worked by hand from SA:132 and :183.

## Doc changes

- `hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/SEP_VPLAN.adoc`: summary and detail rows of both leaves. The open-question bullet on KM handle return codes now names `OBS-REVOKE-TWICE` and `OBS-WARM-STALE-HANDLE`, and a new open-question bullet asks which key bits the KM SRAM scrambler XORs into the 13-bit word address. That question gets no `OBS-` line: the address path reaches no observation point except the physical row, which the untabulated perm13 also sets.
- `hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/test_contracts/key_manager.adoc`: checker rows, procedure steps and CHK-ALIVE probe list of `sep_km_command_set_rand_test`; checker rows of `sep_km_sram_scrambler_key_rand_test`.
- `hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/SEP_TB_ARCH.adoc`: the KM-BUS key-path tap user list gains `sep_km_command_set_rand_test` (CHK-SHRED-FILL).
- `hw/sys/sep/dv/docs/SEP_FCOV.adoc`: the `sep_km_sram_sbox_in_cg` section (point, bins, owner, sampling, seeds) and the model-side exception in the sampling rules.

## Test plan

Commits: f5f3ff432 (tests, plan draws, setter, covergroup, docs), ad5f94588 (per-share term (d), the transfer of hand
